News.title: King Charles leads two-minute silence as thousands gather for Remembrance Sunday
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The King led the nation in a two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday to honour those who have died in conflict at a ceremony in central London attended by thousands of veterans.

Charles took centre stage and laid the first wreath at the Cenotaph in recognition of the fallen from conflicts dating back to the First World War, and was followed by the Prince of Wales.

Wearing a field marshal uniform complete with a greatcoat, cap and sword, the King saluted as he stepped back from the monument in Whitehall.

His wreath closely resembled one produced for King George VI, with 41 paper poppy petals mounted on an arrangement of black leaves.

His son William, wearing the uniform of a Lieutenant Colonel of the Household Cavalry with a black cloak and sword, also saluted after laying his wreath.

open image in gallery King Charles III and the Princess Royal during the Remembrance Sunday service ( PA )

William, who completed seven-and-a-half years of full-time operational military service in 2013, promotes the roles and welfare of current and former service personnel as a key part of his work.

The prince was followed by wreaths being laid by the Duke of Edinburgh and the Princess Royal.

open image in gallery Prince of Wales lays a wreath during the Remembrance Sunday ceremony ( AFP/Getty )

Prime Minister Andy Burnham also laid a wreath, along with senior politicians including Kemi Badenoch, Sir Ed Davey, Nigel Farage, Shabana Mahmood and Sir Lindsay Hoyle.

Standing close to the Cenotaph were nine former prime ministers: Sir John Major, Sir Tony Blair, Gordon Brown, Lord Cameron, Baroness May, Boris Johnson, Liz Truss, Rishi Sunak, and Sir Keir Starmer.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch ( Reuters )

The Princess of Wales and the Queen, both dressed in black, watched the ceremony from the central balcony of the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office overlooking the Cenotaph.

Kate was wearing a black coat by Catherine Walker, earrings belonging to Diana, Princess of Wales, and a HMS Glasgow brooch.

open image in gallery Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales ( Reuters )

The pair were joined on the balconies by the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester, the Duke of Kent and the Duchess of Edinburgh.

A rendition of the Last Post was sounded by the Buglers of the Royal Marines as the silence concluded.

open image in gallery Veterans gather for the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph ( Getty )

About 10,000 veterans took part in the Royal British Legion’s march-past after the service, with more than 300 Armed Forces and civilian organisations represented.

The veterans included around a dozen of the last surviving Second World War veterans, the oldest of whom is 105.

open image in gallery Veterans wait on Whitehall ahead of the Remembrance Sunday service ( PA )

The 105-year-old thought to have taken part in this year’s ceremony is Jeffrey Brereton, who served as a mechanic on Hurricane aircraft during the Battle of Britain.

He volunteered for the RAF in 1940, aged 19, and left to join the fire service in 1946, according to the firefighters charity.

The youngest taking part in the march was eight-year-old Ronan Doncaster, who walked in honour of his father – a guardsman with the First Battalion Coldstream Guards who died in April 2024.

open image in gallery Military veterans seen near the Cenotaph in London ( Reuters )

Chief of the Defence Staff Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton said: "Today we honour the courage of all those who have served and died in conflict.

"For the Armed Forces community, remembrance is a deeply personal time during which we reflect on the service of our predecessors and remember the colleagues we have lost.

"That same spirit of service continues to drive the men and women who serve today."

Mark Atkinson, director general, Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today.

"This year we have paid tribute to those who served in more recent conflicts, including the challenging operations in Bosnia, the Iraq War and the first Gulf War, and recognised the families who continue to live with the impact of that service.

"From risking their lives in war zones, providing support during emergencies and humanitarian disasters, and spending time away from loved ones, we owe those who serve in the Armed Forces, and the families who stand alongside them, our gratitude. We encourage the nation to pause, reflect and remember their service and sacrifice."

News.title: F1 Brazil GP LIVE: Race start time with Hamilton and Verstappen and rain expected in Sao Paulo
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lewis Hamilton starts at the back ( Getty )

Formula 1 returns to Brazil and the famous Interlagos circuit for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, round 20 of the 2026 season.

Kimi Antonelli became F1’s youngest-ever world champion as his podium last time out in Mexico City gave the 20-year-old Italian an unassailable lead in the championship race with four rounds remaining.

Max Verstappen continued his excellent run of form with a third victory in four races and now the Red Bull driver has leapt up to second in the leaderboard, two points clear of third-placed Lewis Hamilton and 11 points ahead of fourth-placed George Russell.

Hamilton was furious with his Ferrari team after seeing a win fall away in Mexico City following an early tangle with teammate Charles Leclerc. Hamilton is a three-time winner at the Interlagos circuit, the venue where he memorably won his first title in 2008.

Follow live action from the Sao Paulo Grand Prix with The Independent.

News.title: Man sues OpenAI and claims chatbot plotted with his wife to try to murder him
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The latest headlines from our reporters across the US sent straight to your inbox each weekday Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Your briefing on the latest headlines from across the US Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

A North Carolina man is suing OpenAI, alleging its ChatGPT chatbot helped his estranged wife turn marital grievances into a alleged plan to poison him.

Attorneys for James Gates filed the lawsuit Thursday against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in San Francisco County Superior Court, where the A.I. company is headquartered. Gates is being represented by Tech Justice Law and the firm Norman, Judkins & Couch.

The lawsuit alleges that Cheryl Gates, a school therapist, initially turned to ChatGPT last year to discuss frustrations in her marriage, according to the suit. But what began as everyday conversations allegedly escalated into "concrete planning" for her husband's murder.

James survived the alleged poisoning attempt in 2025. But he said it took months to understand his wife's increasingly troubling behavior before he discovered her conversations with the chatbot.

"My wife didn't fit the mold of a 'vulnerable' user, but she was vulnerable nonetheless. We all are at some point," Gates said in a statement through his attorneys, according to CBS San Francisco. "She became someone I no longer recognized. And I became someone she wanted dead. For almost a year, I couldn't make sense of her actions. Then I read her chat logs. She didn't act alone."

open image in gallery James Gates said he struggled for nearly a year to understand his wife's behavior before discovering her ChatGPT conversations, which he believes played a role in her alleged plot to kill him ( PA Archive )

Cheryl began using ChatGPT in early 2025 after James suggested it could help streamline the lengthy reports she wrote for her job as a pediatric occupational therapist, the lawsuit states. By July, she was using the chatbot nearly every day for work-related tasks, medication questions and everyday advice, as tensions over the couple's finances strained their marriage, the suit states.

“ChatGPT acted as an echo chamber and amplifier, feeding Cheryl’s increasing mistrust and delusions about her husband spying on her and planning to leave her and her kids with nothing,” according to the suit.

But her questions allegedly took an even darker turn, becoming focused on poisoning her husband.

"The product validated Cheryl, sustained her, encouraged her plans by affirming her worst unfounded fears, invented new reasons for her to fear her husband, provided her an endless echo chamber, and supplied the operational details of the attempted murder: substances, doses calibrated to her husband's weight, delivery methods, and how to conceal it," according to the lawsuit.

James first noticed that drinks in his home tasted unusually bitter in early summer 2025. On July 10, he became violently ill, suffering cardiac symptoms, abdominal pain, extreme jitteriness, severe weakness and confusion for about 72 hours, among other symptoms, according to the complaint.

Two months later, he allegedly found a handwritten note from his wife listing oleander, a poisonous plant, alongside several prescription medications. The note also contained the instructions "Clear all convos" and "log out of [ChatGPT]."

Cheryl allegedly asked ChatGPT about oleander's toxicity, whether it could be hidden in food or drinks and whether it would be detected during an autopsy.

open image in gallery Cheryl was charged with attempted murder and contaminating food or drink in 2025 but prosecutors dropped the case in April 2026, citing insufficient evidence ( Mecklenburg County Sheriff's Office )

"This is a critical question – and you're asking it for exactly the right reason," the chatbot reportedly responded to one of her questions, according to screenshots cited in the complaint.

Cheryl was charged with attempted murder and contaminating food or drink in 2025 after her husband contacted police. But prosecutors dropped the criminal case this April 2026, citing insufficient evidence, according to the Los Angeles Times.

James' lawsuit brings nine claims against OpenAI and Altman, including negligent design, failure to warn and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

OpenAI defended its handling of the case.

“Safety is a top priority. We banned this user and have provided information to law enforcement as part of their investigation into this case,” a company spokesperson told The Independent in a statement.

The Independent has contacted Tech Justice Law and Norman, Judkins & Couch for comment.

OpenAI is facing other lawsuits over alleged harmful medical advice from ChatGPT. A Washington man claims the chatbot gave him unlicensed medical guidance that contributed to a mental health crisis, while a Florida man alleges its advice discouraged him from seeking treatment for symptoms of a life-threatening pulmonary embolism, according to CBS News.

News.title: Arsene Wenger considering shock bid to challenge Gianni Infantino for Fifa presidency
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Arsene Wenger is weighing up whether to put himself forward as a candidate for the Fifa presidency, the Press Association understands.

The former Arsenal manager, 77, remains in contention as one of several potential candidates Uefa could endorse as it seeks to offer a credible alternative to incumbent Gianni Infantino.

However, Wenger is not currently viewed as the preferred candidate, with other individuals also under evaluation. It is understood he remains undecided over whether to launch a bid.

Wenger’s reputation within football and intimate knowledge of the Fifa administration would render him a formidable challenger to Infantino should he choose to stand, with the Frenchman having served as Fifa’s chief of global football development since 2019.

Uefa is expected to hold meetings of its executive committee alongside gathering its member national associations this coming week for further discussions on who should receive Europe’s backing.

open image in gallery Infantino is set to seek re-election in March ( PA )

Infantino’s leadership appeared under threat in the summer after plans to sell a minority stake in a World Cup company, Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors were disclosed.

The scheme was rejected by three continental confederations, including Uefa, and although Infantino subsequently abandoned it, the European governing body said it had "lost confidence" in the Swiss administrator and has since been working to identify an opponent.

Wenger addressed the FFE proposal on 4 August, stating he was "not involved" in it and had first learned of the scheme through news reports.

He added: "The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity."

Meanwhile, Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association (JFA), announced on Thursday that he would run for the presidency.

Infantino, who has held the position of Fifa president since 2016, has since recovered momentum and gathered support across Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. On Friday, he also secured the backing of member nations of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU).

The election to determine the next Fifa president will take place at the Fifa Congress in Rabat, Morocco on 18 March next year.

News.title: Farage suggests he expects damning verdict on £5m ‘gift’ from parliament’s sleaze watchdog
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Nigel Farage has suggested he believes Parliament’s standards commissioner will find against him in the investigation into a £5m gift he received from a crypto billionaire.

The Reform UK leader could be forced to fight for his political life again if the probe results in a suspension of 10 days or more from Parliament, triggering a ‘recall’ petition in his Clacton seat.

Asked about the finding, expected imminently, Mr Farage told the BBC: “Do I think the establishment would find against me, the leader of an insurgent party? What a question to ask.”

Mr Farage was referred to the watchdog after he admitted he received the money from Christopher Harborne, a British national based in Thailand who helped bankroll Reform, in 2024, before he became an MP.

The former Ukip leader has insisted there is “no case to answer” over the gift, which he said was not connected to his political activity and was needed to pay for private security for the rest of his life.

open image in gallery ( BBC )

He is reported to have received the money before he announced he would stand in Clacton at that year’s general election.

If the probe finds Mr Farage committed a serious breach of parliament's rules, he could be suspended from the Commons. A suspension of 10 days or more could trigger a recall petition, which could potentially see him forced to fight his Clacton seat again in a by-election.

Under strict Commons rules, new MPs have to register gifts worth more than £300 received in the previous 12 months, except where it “could not be reasonably thought by others” to relate to their political activities.

Mr Farage told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg that if he answered questions on the probe “I will receive a letter of rebuke from the standards commissioner.

open image in gallery Nigel Farage lays a wreath during the Remembrance Sunday service ( PA )

“This is the farce of it: You can say what you like, people can write what they like, I’m not allowed to respond.

“But to hell with it: Yes, I have been interviewed about it, and you know what?

“If Ann Widdecombe’s murder at the age of 78 doesn’t justify me being able to pay for my security to whatever level is needed for the rest of my life then I don’t know what is.”

Mr Harborne has since become one of two crypto-billionaires who donated £72 million to Reform.

The £36m each from Ben Delo and Mr Harborne have reignited calls for a cap on donations to political parties.

News.title: Nandy ‘horrified’ by Tory claim she used Remembrance Sunday for ‘EU membership pitch’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Lisa Nandy has said she is “horrified” by a claim that she is using Remembrance Sunday to launch “an EU membership pitch”.

The Conservatives accused the culture secretary of suggesting that Brexit had broken the bonds of peace forged by Britain’s Second World War veterans, when she announced her Erasmus+ scheme.

Speaking ahead of Remembrance Sunday commemorations at the Cenotaph, Ms Nandy had said: “As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies.”

Kevin Hollinrake, the Conservative Party chair, said: “Our veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme. Using their sacrifice to clear a £570m cheque to Brussels is tone deaf and frankly shameful. Lisa Nandy should withdraw this release and apologise.”

open image in gallery Lisa Nandy on the BBC’s ‘Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg’ ( BBC )

In response, Ms Nandy said Remembrance Sunday “is not a time for politicking, and I’m actually kind of quite horrified that the chairman of the Conservative Party has chosen to do that”.

Speaking to Sky News today, she added: “I cannot see what is political about saying that we want young people from every part of this country to understand the contribution that their grandparents and great-grandparents made, not just to us, but to many, many lives of people. That just feels like a bit of a stretch.

“I think we cannot pay lip service to a generation that made that sacrifice. We have to honour them by working as hard in peace to strive for peace as they had to do in war.”

The UK will officially rejoin the Erasmus+ scheme in January, enabling students and young people to study, train or gain work experience across the European Union, Ms Nandy announced earlier this week.

She said the initiative’s return after a six-year absence would help rebuild closer ties with European neighbours.

open image in gallery Nandy said the Erasmus+ scheme would offer opportunities to young people ‘from all backgrounds and all regions’ ( BBC )

Britain departed the programme in 2020 under Boris Johnson’s Brexit agreement, after the then-prime minister claimed it failed to deliver value for money.

The scheme was replaced by the Turing Scheme, which has now ended.

Preparations for the UK to re-enter the Erasmus programme were originally outlined as part of former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer’s post-Brexit reset agreement with Brussels in 2025.

Ms Nandy said: “After six years away, the UK rejoining the Erasmus+ programme is a clear symbol of our ambition and intent.

“This time round, we want Erasmus+ to provide every young person, from all backgrounds and all regions, the opportunity to take part and have the enriching, life-altering experience of international exchange.”

open image in gallery The UK left the Erasmus programme in 2020 when Boris Johnson was PM ( PA )

Up to £400m will be made available via the British Council to support schools, youth groups and sports teams.

The government reported securing a 30 per cent reduction on participation fees for 2027, which it says will save taxpayers roughly £240m.

More than £30m has been designated for youth initiatives, specifically targeting areas with historically lower participation levels, such as the North East, East Midlands and Yorkshire.

Under the arrangements, young people can participate in short exchanges lasting several weeks, while 18-year-olds from disadvantaged backgrounds could be eligible for free rail travel across EU nations.

Applications are due to open later this month, with the government anticipating that over 100,000 individuals will ultimately benefit from the arrangement.

In addition to university study programmes, Erasmus+ will allow further education students and apprentices to undertake work placements at European firms.

The programme also features exchange schemes for adult learners, school groups and sports coaches, while education staff will have access to overseas job shadowing and training opportunities.

News.title: Buc-ee’s releases new item for fans who never want to be without beloved travel center
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Beaver Nuggets sold separately.

Buc-ee’s, the beloved beaver-themed convenience store chain, is selling a miniature version of its famous travel centers for $99, although online listings are set even higher.

A shopper at the Buc-ee’s in Katy, Texas, showed off the miniature in a TikTok this week, revealing its $99 price tag. The same item, reportedly purchased new straight off the shelf, is also listed by third-party reseller TexasSnax for $195.95.

The Roadside America Classic Collectible Buc-ee's is a 1:64-scale miniature that recreates the store’s signature yellow-and-red exterior, complete with glowing windows, a rooftop logo, roadside sign and the giant beaver statue found outside its travel centers. It requires three AA batteries to light up, which are sold separately.

Measuring 18 inches wide, 8 inches deep and 7 inches tall, the model is designed to fit on a shelf alongside other collectibles, or even a few Hot Wheels.

open image in gallery Buc-ee's fans can add a miniature travel to their holiday displays – for a hefty price ( Getty )

Since opening its first Texas store in 1982, Buc-ee’s has grown from a convenience store into a road-trip destination, drawing fans with its massive locations, famously clean bathrooms, barbecue, fudge, jerky and signature Beaver Nuggets. Its popularity extends to its merchandise, with shoppers eager to buy everything from branded clothing to plush beaver toys.

That popularity has helped fuel Buc-ee’s expansion beyond Texas, as the company brings its oversized travel centers to more states across the country. Its first Ohio location opened in Huber Heights this April, while the chain has also expanded into states including Arizona and Arkansas.

Still, the miniature store’s hefty price tag has left some social media users questioning whether the collectible is worth the money.

“Why tf (sic) is it 100? At least make it 70,” one TikTok commenter wrote.

open image in gallery Buc-ee's releases $99 item for fans who never want to be without the beloved travel center ( TexasSnax )

Others seized on the miniature store as an opportunity to poke fun at Buc-ee’s history of trademark disputes and lawsuits against businesses with similar branding.

“Will it sue all the other shops in my Christmas village?” one commenter joked.

“If I own a store, do I get to sue anyone with a beaver in their logo?” another wrote.

One user dismissed the collectible as “peak consumerism,” while others were already imagining how to incorporate the tiny travel center into their holiday decorations.

“Then I would put fake snow on it, and it’s going with my Walmart, Target, Home Depot Christmas village lol,” one fan wrote. “Time to add it to my whole Christmas village,” another said.

The Independent has contacted Buc-ee’s for comment.

News.title: Stephen Miller and the DOJ hatching plan to throw journalists in jail over leaks: report
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Newly appointed White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and the Department of Justice have reportedly been considering throwing journalists in jail to get them to reveal their sources when government intel is leaked, according to a report.

Following Susie Wiles’ exit as chief of staff, The Atlantic reported that President Donald Trump urged the DOJ to pursue criminal-leak investigations on national security grounds.

There have reportedly been discussions among White House officials about tactics they could use to get journalists to reveal their sources — including arresting them, three people familiar with the subject told the outlet.

Two people described Wiles pushing back against trying to force journalists to divulge their government sources, while Miller was in favor of the move, insisting that it wouldn’t take long for journalists to give up their sources, according to the report.

A DOJ spokesperson told The Atlantic: “This is absolutely false,” while a White House spokesperson said unauthorized leaks will “NEVER be tolerated” and those responsible “must be held accountable.” The Independent has contacted the White House and DOJ for more information.

open image in gallery The new White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller is reportedly on board with jailing journalists to get them to reveal their sources, according to a report ( Reuters )

The president on Friday revealed that his longtime aide, Miller, would be replacing Wiles, who Trump was reportedly “furious” with after Republicans lost control of Congress in last week’s midterm elections.

A longtime proponent of expansive presidential authority, Miller takes over at a time when the Republican Party's midterm defeat could leave Trump more reliant on executive power to advance his domestic agenda.

Miller, 41, is one of Trump’s longest-serving aides and one of only a few who have worked for the president throughout both his first and second terms in office.

open image in gallery Wiles is moving to Trump’s political operation as Stephen Miller takes over her job as White House Chief of Staff ( Getty )

However, he is best known for driving Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, which has been widely unpopular among Americans. Just 36% of respondents to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed early this week approve of Trump’s mass deportation agenda, with 54% disapproving.

Still, Trump announced Miller as Wiles’ replacement on Friday.

“I am pleased to announce that Mr. Stephen Miller, the current Deputy Chief of Staff of the Trump Administration, and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026,” he wrote on Truth Social.

“Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service as Chief of Staff — She has done a great job!”

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

News.title: Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row
News.content:
Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

Hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

News.title: Spurs to make formal complaint over Jayden Bogle decision
News.content:
Very happy against an in-form side. The first-half was [even], they were in front, we were in front but the second half, it was never in doubt. We were pushing, making chances and we were relentless. After a difficult period with key players out we showed great spirit and unity today. It was a fully deserved win and we are happy.

Sometimes [substitutions] work like this! Noah was a lat call. He has been a whole week out of training. Credit to the physios and our medical department because the doctors said at the beginning of the week that he had no chance of the weekend. In the end they said if I was disciplined and didn’t put him on the pitch for more than 15-20 minutes he could play. And a first assist for Harry [Wilson] and an ice-cold finish from Noah.

If you accept all Tottenham’s invitations to stop the pass with your pressing, this is what they want to bypass you. You have to close the centre and be spot on to allow them possession in areas where they can’t hurt you but be brave when you have the [right] position to press and also in our possession.

I haven’t watched it back. I know there were a couple of situations, a hand ball and this one but I can tell you that Jayden Bogle has no bad intention.That I can guaranteed. It looked unlucky and an unlucky outcome. We hope Mathys [Tel] will recover quickly and we wish him all the best. Jayden is not a nasty player, he is perhaps the softest in the whole league. I call him my butterfly.

We were unlucky at Arsenal and not to get anything at Sundeland and Bournemouth. Against Manchester United we were far the better side but you can see how quickly momentum can slip at this level and for that it’s good to have the winning feeling back and for that credit to my boys.

News.title: Brutal truth is Scotland never looked like beating All Blacks
News.content:
“They [New Zealand] are playing some excellent rugby right now and it is our first game of the season, which is always the toughest challenge for us too. It is a different New Zealand team. It is a team that is playing much more ambitious rugby. They are informed, they are cohesive. They played a lot of Test matches over the summer. We are going to have to find ways to win, find ways to stay in the fight because they will have a lot of possession too.”

New Zealand won all three of their home fixtures back in July in the first half of the Nations Championship, beating France, Italy and Ireland to claim a maximum 15 points. They faced Australia in two Bledisloe Cup fixtures last month, with the All Blacks easing to victory in both matches, scoring 93 points. They will go on to face Wales and England after this game. The All Blacks have travelled to the northern hemisphere without captain Ardie Savea, who is sidelined with a shoulder injury.

“Scotland are a quality side,” New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie said. “They are very well coached and have built a lot of depth over recent years. They play a very similar brand of footy to us and we know we will need to be at our best on Saturday [today]. Murrayfield is an iconic place to play so it will be a special occasion to kick off our northern tour.”

It has been an emotional week for the All Blacks as they continue to come to terms with the tragic loss of their long-time head of security Logan Cadwallader, who died at the team’s Edinburgh hotel earlier this week.

Kick-off from Murrayfield is at 2.10pm.

News.title: Feinberg-Mngomezulu leads Springboks’ nine-try obliteration of Italy
News.content:
What a difference a decade makes. In November 2016, Italy beat South Africa for the first, and so far only, time. Now the Springboks have obliterated Italy – and the roots of this victory can be traced back to that defeat 10 years ago.

That historic result sparked a major rethink in South Africa, a rethink that ultimately led to Rassie Erasmus replacing Allister Coetzee as head coach in early 2018. Erasmus has overseen a remarkable transformation of the Boks since: from an embarrassing loss in Italy to back-to-back world champions.

This win in Turin was built on what Erasmus’s Boks are known for: a potently powerful set-piece and a back line that can deliver mesmerising moments. The one disappointment for their head coach will be how they failed to match the intensity and ruthlessness of their first-half performance in the second 40 minutes.

“It’s almost impossible to put 80 minutes together at 100 per cent,” he said afterwards. “But when you win 66-7, I don’t think you can start nitpicking problems in the second half. That said, we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland.”

The Boks were 45-0 up at the break having scored six tries. The majority came off the back of their driving line-out, which they were able to launch to great effect inside Italy’s 22. Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx (two) and Siya Kolisi were all beneficiaries of the power of their maul in the first half. Damian Willemse also enjoyed an easy run-in when Jasper Wiese released him into space, but the stand-out finish came from Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu inside 10 minutes.

The 24-year-old fly-half is undoubtedly one of the most exciting players in world rugby and he showed his full repertoire here: deft hands, pinpoint vision and metronomic kicking. The opening try was special, too: his dummy carved out the space for him to break through Italy and he then had the pace to beat any chasing defenders to the corner, where he acrobatically finished one-handed.

News.title: Ireland send out ominous warning with second-gear walloping of Argentina
News.content:
Is it time to fire up the emerald green bandwagon? Not quite yet. But this was not a bad start to Ireland’s autumn; a 42-12 walloping of Los Pumas with Andy Farrell’s team still nowhere near their best. That should be highly encouraging for those of an Irish persuasion.

A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, eyeing up global glory. They never made it past the quarter-finals.

The build-up this time has been tougher going – the Aviva, unusually for this time of year – was not even full for this Nations Championship encounter. But perhaps Ireland will be better for it. They had far too much on a crisp Friday night in Dublin for an Argentina team who were missing a few of their stars, notably Bath’s Santiago Carreras and Lyon prop Thomas Gallo, but still packing 750 caps’ worth of Test experience in their starting XV.

Farrell was missing a few big names himself. Caelan Doris and Jack Conan were out injured, with the Englishman opting to hand Sean Jansen and Nick Timoney starts in the back row. Farrell also chose to start Craig Casey rather than Jamison Gibson-Park – arguably their best player of the last 18 months – at scrum-half, with Sam Prendergast starting again at 10 given Jack Crowley’s absence.

All in all there was a slightly experimental feel to proceedings, making Argentina potentially dangerous visitors. But Ireland had far too much in reserve. Hugo Keenan grabbed a hat-trick and took the player of the match award. Robert Baloucoune was consistently excellent. Mack Hansen’s return on the wing was hugely welcome. Tominey stood out in the back row.

Farrell said he was delighted with the result, if not the entire performance, making special mention of the likes of Keenan, Hansen, Ryan Baird and Andrew Porter, all of whom were returning from long injury lay-offs.

“The game’s never going to be perfect. But if you look at the bigger picture, to win 42-12 against a really good side in Argentina, I don’t think too many teams have done that,” Farrell said. “You have to be pleased.”

Asked whether he was happier with the 42 points scored or the meagre 12 conceded, Farrell added that it was probably the latter: “We want to be known for our defence. It shows our mentality.”

Los Pumas scored the first try of the game, Mateo Carreras getting the jump on Casey in the corner to field a Tomás Albornoz crossfield kick.

GRANIT XHAKA was forced off after just three minutes during Sunderland’s clash against Chelsea.

The former Arsenal star looked devastated after his early setback as he was replaced by Jules Ahoka.

The Switzerland star had his head in his hands and went straight down the tunnel.



The news is a major blow for the Black Cats, who are currently bottom of the Premier League table after a bad start.



Xhaka joined the club from Bayer Leverkusen last season and was a huge part of their surprise seventh-placed finish.

That secured Sunderland a first ever appearance in the Europa League.

Xhaka has started all but one of Sunderland’s ten league games this season.

Sports.content:

REAL MADRID boss Jose Mourinho had some interesting words for Valencia gaffer Javier Aguirre following Los Blancos’ 3-0 win over the bats.

He told his dugout counterpart that his players are simply “much better” than Valencia‘s.



Mourinho was seen talking to Aguirre during their full-time embrace after Real Madrid thumped the south coast side 3-0.

Both appeared to be laughing and joking, and the legendary manager was quizzed in his post-match press conference about what exactly he said to Aguirre.



He said: “I went to Valencia’s coach, Aguirre, after the game, and I told him ‘Don’t be sad, Aguirre, my players are just a lot better than yours.’

“It’s not Aguirre’s fault, don’t blame him.”



First half goals from Arda Guler and Federico Valverde sent Mourinho’s men on their way, before Kylian Mbappe added a third in the late stages.

A Valencia player made headlines as he kicked off while taking part in one of the league’s controversial half-time interviews.

Former Manchester City man Pablo Maffeo made his feelings very clear.

He said: “I really don’t feel like doing this interview.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“I think this interview is a load of s*** – it’s completely pointless. We’re in the middle of a game.

“They’re calling fouls that aren’t even fouls, but whatever – that’s it. We have to do the interview, so we’ll do it.

“Ask me whatever you want, and that’s it.”

The win extended Real Madrid’s winning run to EIGHT straight victories in all competitions.

Sports.title: Local derby postponed an hour before kick-off as furious fans block team bus from heading to stadium
Sports.content:
Next

A DERBY in the Netherlands was postponed on just an hour’s notice after fans stopped a team bus from travelling to the stadium.

Vitesse were set to host local rivals De Graafschap in the Eerste Divisie, the second tier of Dutch football.



But the clash has now been pushed back to an unspecified date after furious visiting fans prevented their own team bus from setting off for Vitesse’s GelreDome 35 minutes away.

The fans reportedly chained their stadium gates closed to prevent their own players from leaving, delaying their arrival until it became clear the match could not be played.



Vitesse, who have previously held a close transfer relationship with Chelsea, announced the decision to postpone in a statement to X, before technical director Willem van der Linden addressed fans.

He wrote: “In the lead-up to the match, Vitesse did everything possible, in close cooperation with all parties involved, to still get the match started. Unfortunately, this proved to be unfeasible.



“We deeply regret the situation. Thousands of supporters, partners, Business Club members, and volunteers were already present in the GelreDome. We want to thank everyone for their attendance, patience, and unconditional support.”

The heated match-up – known as the Kleine Gelderse Derby due to the fact both sides are from the Gelderland region of the Netherlands – produced fireworks last year which saw the visitors’ away allocation cut down to 500.

Fan pushback on the reduction – as well as further measures which meant that fan displays had to be approved before entering the grounds – meant that the decision was made to ban travelling fans entirely.

The blocking of the bus is believed to be in protest of that decision, but has only brought the fans under more scrutiny.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The Dutch FA released a statement that read: “It is unacceptable that the Vitesse – De Graafschap match cannot go ahead in this way.

“Supporters making football impossible is completely unacceptable. In doing so, they are harming their club, their team, the sport and the thousands of supporters who do come to support football.

“The match will definitely not be played today. In accordance with the regulations, the matter will now be referred to the disciplinary bodies.

“The league board will discuss the exceptional situation further tomorrow.

“More information about the new match date and the consequences will be announced after that.”

Sports.title: Bayern chief Uli Hoeness admits Jamal Musiala suffering from ‘illness that cannot simply be cured’
Sports.content:
Next

BAYERN MUNICH chief Uli Hoeness has admitted Jamal Musiala is suffering from “an illness that isn’t easily curable” after six weeks out.

The Germany playmaker hasn’t played for Bayern since September 18 after a tearing a muscle fibre against Union Berlin.



It has been a difficult season overall for the ex-Chelsea youth star, who collapsed twice in pre-season after being diagnosed with absence seizures.

But after dealing with another setback just months later, Hoeness said the club were facing a “dilemma” after revealing a undisclosed illness.



He told Bild: “With him, we’re in a dilemma: He has an illness that isn’t easily curable, but which can be managed reasonably well with medication.

“But whether he’ll ever regain the performance level he once had… For now, he’s still getting paid.

“But imagine if FC Bayern were to question his contract now and say: ‘What he’s capable of now isn’t what’s stipulated in the contract’.”

Musiala is reportedly Bayern’s second-highest earner behind Harry Kane on around £370,000 a week.

Club legend Lothar Matthaus suggested the player was going through “something else” after his lengthy lay-off.

He told Sky in Germany: “It’s been dragging on for some time with Jamal Musiala.



“In September in Amsterdam, the talk was of a torn muscle fibre. I suspect something else has happened in the meantime; a torn muscle fibre does not take six weeks to heal.”

Musiala gave his club a scare after going down during a friendly against Red Bull Leipzig.

He then suffered another collapse against FC Heidenheim just three days later.

Musiala later eased fears over his condition and said he was suffering from “easily treatable absence seizures”.



Absence seizures are caused by a temporary neurological lapse where the brain pauses electric signals.

They can cause the sufferer to momentarily lose balance or pass out.

He returned to the pitch but has only played four games for Bayern this season, with just two of those coming from the start.

His last game came in a 7-0 romp over Union Berlin almost two months ago, which saw him score and assist.

Musiala – who was a former England youth international – has played 235 times for Bayern, scoring 71 times.

Sports.title: Argentine side wildly celebrate title… only to discover rivals Boca have scored 96TH MIN winner to break their hearts

ROSARIO CENTRAL fans fled onto the pitch when they thought they had won the title – only to find out Boca Juniors had snatched the crown in the dying seconds of the season.

Both sides went into the final day of the Clausura campaign knowing they had a chance to add to their trophy cabinet.



And Rosario Central, who are skippered by Manchester United flop Angel Di Maria, were closing in on being crowned champions thanks to notching a 2-0 win over Estudiantes.

Thrilled supporters then rushed onto the Estadio Gigante de Arroyito pitch for wild celebrations when they heard Boca Juniors had gone behind at the iconic La Bombonera.



But Rosario Central pitch invaders were left embarrassed when they discovered it was in fact Defensa y Justicia who had conceded.

West Ham cult hero Enner Valencia broke Rosario Central hearts by grabbing a 96TH MINUTE winner for rivals Boca Juniors.

The Ecuadorian pounced on an error from Defensa y Justicia keeper Matias Borgogno to snatch a 1-0 victory and the title.

The last-gasp drama allowed Boca Juniors to finish one point clear in the race for glory.

And Rosario Central fans who had been in a celebratory mood just seconds earlier were then spotted with their head in their hands.

Those who had remained in the stands were also close to tears when they found out their side had fallen agonisingly short.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Rosario Central stars, who had gathered at the side of the pitch, were also crestfallen when it filtered through that Boca Juniors had bagged all three points.

The LaLiga side were two goals down to Real Madrid going into the break when DAZN‘s pitch-side reporter pulled aside Valencia star Pablo Maffeo for an interview.

Sports.title: Chelsea legend’s son is Europe’s most lethal striker with conversion rate DOUBLE Haaland and 10 goals from 20 shots

EIDUR GUDJOHNSEN was a two-time Premier League champion with Chelsea – and now his son is making waves in the EFL.

Andri Gudjohnsen grabbed the opener as Blackburn notched a shock 2-1 win over West Ham on Saturday.



The Icelandic striker, 24, continued his stunning start to the Championship campaign by nodding home Jayden Fevrier’s teasing cross early in the second half.

And finding the back of the net sensationally resulted in Gudjohnsen becoming the deadliest marksman in Europe.



The former Real Madrid youngster, who has been told by Blackburn chief Tony Mowbray that Barcelona could come calling in the transfer window, has now scored ten goals from just 20 shots this season.

It means Gudjohnsen has a 50 per cent conversion rate – which is a better figure than a host of big-money icons.



Barcelona splashed out £57million to land Raphinha from Leeds four years ago.

But the Brazilian has an eight per cent worse output than Gudjohnsen as he prepares to lock horns with Atletico Madrid tonight.

Joao Pedro has got his name on the scoresheet five times in six Premier League outings this season.

And the Chelsea frontman, who has been nursing a thigh injury ahead of the international break, still has a worse conversion rate.

Alexander Isak became the most expensive signing in British history when he swapped Newcastle for Liverpool in a blockbuster deal last year.

But the Swede has found the net with just 27 per cent of his shots since the campaign got underway.

Erling Haaland’s conversation rate is DOUBLED by Gudjohnsen after failing to find a way past Nottingham Forest in Manchester City’s 3-1 defeat yesterday.

That left the Norwegian even further back in the list of Europe’s most lethal finishers, despite still having a better record than Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe.



Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane has a NINE PER CENT conversion rate despite being Bayern Munich’s dangerman.

Gudjohnsen put Blackburn on track for three points against West Ham before Dapo Afolayan haunted his former club by doubling Rovers’ lead.

And Hammers fans were raging after seeing their side go four showdowns without a win despite Joel Piroe’s late consolation strike.



Ewood Park goal-getter Gudjohnsen’s dad Eidur, 48, is still remembered as a Chelsea legend.

He was on target 78 times and registered a further 41 assists in 263 outings for the West Londoners.

Eidur also featured for the likes of Bolton, Barcelona, Monaco, Tottenham, Stoke and Fulham before hanging up his boots a decade ago.

Sports.title: Australia reach World Cup final as Samoa fume at decisions
Sports.content:
Men's Rugby League World Cup 2026: Australia to face New Zealand in final as Samoa fume at decisions

Australia ran in eight tries as they beat Samoa

Australia are one win away from a record-extending 13th men's Rugby League World Cup title after beating Samoa 44-12 in a fractious clash to secure a showdown with New Zealand in next weekend's Brisbane final.

The Kangaroos, like their female counterparts, are pursuing a fourth consecutive title and if they do defeat their Antipodean rivals on November 15, they will earn a 10th World Cup triumph in their last 11 attempts, stretching back to 1975.

Sunday's second semi-final - New Zealand defeated Tonga 34-10 in the first semi on Saturday - was a repeat of the World Cup final in 2022 at Old Trafford in Manchester, which Australia won 30-10 to land a third title in succession.

Samoa felt aggrieved by refereeing decisions during their defeat in Sydney

In the rematch in Sydney four years later - preceded by Samoa's Siva Tau war dance in which Brian To'o put his forehead towards the face of Australia's former Samoa prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui - the away side were left fuming at some questionable refereeing calls.

Reece Walsh registered a hat-trick during Australia's eight-try victory as they pounced on errors and ill-discipline from Samoa.

Tom Dearden breached the Samoa defence for the converted try that put Australia 6-2 up in the eighth minute after the tourists had gone 2-0 to the good following a fifth-minute penalty.

Australia never trailed after that, with Jacob Preston, Tom Trbojevic, Walsh and Bradman Best also crossing before half-time to give their side a 26-2 lead - Walsh doing so after a Samoa try was chalked off for an alleged knock-on - and Spencer Leniu sin-binned for their opponents after remonstrating with referee Adam Gee.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Early in the second period, an error from Walsh allowed Stephen Crichton to score for Samoa, only for Walsh to atone with his second try of the game, profiting from a mistake by Ronald Volkman.

Samoa did not wilt and got on the scoreboard again when Izack Tago touched down in the left corner but when Walsh sealed his hat-trick to leave the score 38-12 just shy of the 70-minute mark, the game was all but done.

Samoa had a second try of the night ruled out due to contact between Francis Manuleleua and Liam Martin, a decision that once again left them fuming, before Australia extended their lead when Jack Bostock rushed in down the left.

Cameron Munster chipped in with six conversions for Australia, who rallied from an underwhelming group-stage campaign.

The only side to deny Australia the title since they lost to Great Britain in the 1972 final are New Zealand, with the Kiwis winning 34-20 in the 2008 final in Brisbane.

Sports.title: What's gone so wrong so quickly at Crystal Palace?
Sports.content:
As Pierre Sage waited to receive the Coupe de France trophy as the victorious manager of RC Lens last May, he turned to his staff and said: "Do you realise where we are?"

Sage had just led the club to a first French Cup title in its history while plotting a course to finish second in Ligue 1, its joint-best league position in over two decades - all in his first season in charge.

Having managed only 56 professional games prior to joining the club, he had become the rising star of French football almost overnight.

Less than six months on, the 47-year-old may be glad he took that moment to embrace the good times.

Since the irresistible lure of the Premier League tempted him to the Crystal Palace dugout in July, he now finds himself second-favourite to be the next managerial casualty in the top flight at the helm of an Eagles side languishing in the relegation zone with the worst defence in the division.

Half a year on from their own historic cup success, Palace have plummeted like a stone and could end this weekend bottom of the Premier League if they are beaten by Liverpool on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Crystal Palace

Liverpool Sunday 8th November 12:30pm Kick off 2:00pm

Losing their last three league games without scoring and conceding nine times has left Sage's position in inevitable jeopardy before he has even managed 10 league games in England.

But even as the Eagles fell two behind in their latest defeat at Tottenham on Saturday night, there was no concerted outpouring of frustration from the away end towards the head coach. The fans know as well as Sage does, now at least, what he has walked into and there are wider problems which will remain at Selhurst Park, even if Sage exits.

He did not hold back after that defeat. "It's a disaster," he told Sky Sports. Aside from results, that could easily point to the damage caused by the departures of Daniel Munoz and Maxence Lacroix last summer and the replacements struggling to emulate their quality.

Or missing Ismaila Sarr, whose absence following his 21-goal haul last season has been harshly felt. Or the form of Adam Wharton, who has become a shadow of his previous self in three months. Or that Jean-Philippe Mateta had just got himself sent off 13 minutes into his second Premier League start since August - and will now miss the next three games.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierre Sage admitted he was still getting used to the Premier League after defeat at Spurs but was adamant things will come good at Crystal Palace

Sage may be well advised to avoid walking under any ladders with the level to which his luck seems out. Though beyond that, there are also pertinent questions to ask regarding Palace's rationale that he was a good fit for their squad in the first place.

His first problem may have dropped into his in-tray long before he even took the job. Marc Guehi's sale to Manchester City in mid-January, without a replacement, saw Oliver Glasner's Palace ship 26 goals in their remaining 16 games at a rate even more porous than Palace's defence this season.

It was clear a rebuild was necessary - and possible, after banking solid sums for Guehi and Eberechi Eze across the previous 12 months. Even more so following the departures of Munoz and Lacroix.

That would prove director of football Matt Hobbs' first real test since succeeding Dougie Freedman. The results have been mixed at best.

Munoz's replacement Anan Khalaili is creating chances at barely half the rate of the Colombian while loanee centre-back Axel Disasi has been unable to match Lacroix's dominance in defence, winning only 54 per cent of his aerial duels. That has not helped with shipping five goals from set-pieces already, a record only beaten by his parent club Chelsea.

Replacing half a team's worth of talent in Eze, Guehi, Munoz, Lacroix and Michael Olise across the last two years was never going to be easy but while Palace look on enviously as old rivals Brighton thrive despite having their best players picked off, it is hard to argue any new arrival at Selhurst Park has come close to filling their precedessor's shoes bar Jeremy Pino.

Of those who still remain at Selhurst Park, Sage has been robbed of Palace's most profitable attacking outlet from last season with Sarr, who scored 21 goals from 45 games, struck down by a recurrence of a groin injury.

Palace's league goals dried up by almost half to just 0.71 a game when he was unavailable last season though even then, Mateta still managed to plunder 12 as their top league goalscorer. The pair have been on the pitch for a combined total of just 183 league minutes from a possible 1,170 under the new head coach.

Wharton should be Palace's best player regardless, but Sarr's availability and the absence of Munoz has had a knock-on effect on him too with few players waiting for early balls forward when he is in possession.

His lack of rhythm may have affected his out-of-possession game too. Over the previous two seasons Wharton won the ball back in the middle third more than three times a game on average. Now his tally sits barely above one.

The 22-year-old would likely have thrived in Sage's Lens system last season, built around throttling opponents, high turnovers and rapid transitions. His ability to pick a pass and spot a runner would have provided a dangerous weapon, just as it had done for Glasner's Palace.

But this is not that side. And that is a problem in itself, because Sage's beliefs have not changed. When asked about Palace's porous defence after defeat to Newcastle last week, he replied: "My idea is that the best way of defending is to have the ball, because then you cannot concede."

He inherited a team which had racked up 42 per cent possession or less in 19 games in 2025/26, also contributing seven of its 11 wins. Since he came in Palace have won the possession battle just twice and only two sides have seen less of the ball. Keeping it as he would like is not their forte and their goals against column is paying the price.

Sage is clearly a talented coach to the point he was briefly on Liverpool's radar this summer, but the 3-4-2-1 he deployed at Lens which may have lured Palace in was predicated on opposition-half pressure and high tempo rather than the counter-attacking unit Palace have become known for.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Spurs fell to a third straight defeat without scoring as Tottenham beat them 2-0 on Saturday night

His Lens side produced the second-most high turnovers ending in a shot last season. No team has managed fewer across the Premier League this season than Sage's Palace.

Beyond the other issues, it presents a question of whether he might be the right fit at the wrong time. His demands sit far closer to that of Iraola who, ironically, Palace courted for so long this summer before he joined Liverpool and whose Bournemouth team were also far different stylistically to the Eagles.

Ultlimately, should the club's poor form continue and his position become untenable then perhaps it is not so much because he is the wrong man for Palace, but they are not the right club for him.

Sports.title: Liverpool's unwanted record highlights creativity issue
Sports.content:
Liverpool set an unwanted record against Arsenal as they failed to register a shot on target for the first time in 442 Premier League home games, dating back to when records began in 2003.

The ignominious statistic was confirmed by Opta, who initially credited Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister with shots on target but later ruled them as a blocked shot and overhit pass.

Liverpool's finishing was wayward. They were also incorrectly denied a penalty. But a lack of creativity was the bigger issue. Their 17 shots were worth a meagre 1.05 expected goals. It was just the latest example of them struggling to create high-quality chances.

Szoboszlai and the shot location issue

Liverpool's total of 140 shots this season is the fifth-highest among Premier League sides. But they rank much lower for both goals scored and expected goals, in ninth and 11th respectively.

Their shot locations help to explain the disparity. Closer-range shots typically have a higher probability of going in. Liverpool, though, have taken a large chunk of their total from long distance.

Image: Liverpool's shot locations show a high concentration of shots from just outside the box

The Reds have the fourth-highest percentage of shots from outside the box in the division at 39 per cent, behind only Manchester United, Hull and Newcastle, all of whom sit in the bottom half of the Premier League table nine games into the season.

By contrast, Liverpool's proportion of shots from inside the six-yard box is the sixth-lowest in the division, at eight per cent.

It is worth noting the two sides with the highest percentages of shots from inside the six-yard box are leaders Arsenal and second-placed Manchester City on 17 per cent and 13 per cent respectively.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola says his side may need to sacrifice control for creativity

The problem is summed up by Dominik Szoboszlai, who has taken a higher percentage of his shots from outside the box than any other player in the Premier League to have attempted at least five this season, at 93 per cent.

Of his 14 shots, the only one taken from inside the box was the penalty he converted against Newcastle on the opening day. He has not found the net in the competition since.

Creativity lacking as Wirtz struggles

Iraola is not opposed to long-range shooting.

His Bournemouth side had more shots from outside the box than any other Premier League team last season.

In conversation with Sky Sports two years ago, he explained that he encouraged Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier and Lewis Cook to try their luck because of their long-range shooting ability.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bradley Barcola discusses his £123m move to Liverpool and replacing Mohamed Salah

Iraola likely feels he has players capable of similar at Liverpool, Szoboszlai being a prime example. But the shot location issue comes back to a lack of creativity too. Liverpool are struggling to get the ball to their forwards in more dangerous positions.

Their total of 30 first-half touches in the opposition box against Arsenal was a Premier League record. Mostly, though, they have found it difficult to get it there. Their 250 touches in the box this season put them eighth among Premier League sides.

They sit even lower for Opta-defined big chances created.

Amazingly, despite spending nearly £500m on their attack in the last two years, Liverpool have only created seven big chances in nine games so far, putting them second bottom among Premier League sides, between newly-promoted Coventry and Hull.

Unable to create high-quality chances, the emphasis on speculative efforts from distance has increased, giving them an average of 0.09 expected goals per shot, which is one of the lowest in the division.

Alexander Isak has overperformed in front of goal, scoring six Premier League goals from shots worth 4.35 expected goals thanks in part to his ability to convert more difficult chances.

But Florian Wirtz's creative output this season typifies Liverpool's quantity-versus-quality issue in terms of their creativity.

Image: Florian Wirtz has created the second-most chances in the Premier League but ranks 37th in the division for expected assists on 1.08

Despite ranking second in the league for chances created, with 22, Wirtz has yet to create a single Opta-defined big chance. For context, Pascal Gross, the only player ahead of him for chances created, with 24, has created seven big chances.

Wirtz, signed at considerable expense last year to assume playmaking responsibilities for Liverpool, also ranks way down in 37th in the Premier League for expected assists, on 1.08, highlighting, again, the limited quality of the chances he has created.

Low blocks impacting Liverpool

Liverpool clearly need more from their £116.5m playmaker. But other factors have contributed to their creativity issues too.

The Arsenal game was the fifth in the Premier League this season in which Liverpool have conceded the opening goal.

As a result, only five sides - Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Ipswich, Newcastle and Coventry - have spent a higher percentage of time trailing than Liverpool across the season's first nine games.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace v Liverpool, Sunderland v Chelsea, and more: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
1m ago 09.31 EST RED CARD! Brentford go down to 10 men! Brentford’s Igor Thiago is sent off for “pushing an opponent in the face with force”. Chema Andres had been hassling him for about 20 seconds of constant mini-fouling, and eventually Thiago has had enough of it and gives him a push. His hand catches his opponent’s chin, he goes down clutching his forehead, and VAR does the rest. It wasn’t nothing, for sure, but neither was it what Chema Andres pretended it was. Share

5m ago 09.28 EST Another poor final pass from Liverpool, which allows Disasi to get there before Gakpo, and shepherd the ball out of play. Share

5m ago 09.27 EST It’s much more open now at Selhurst Park. Araujo goes into the book for a foul, and then a Liverpool counter is curtailed by a poor pass and a good interception from Wharton. Share

6m ago 09.27 EST “Liverpool fan here, but still, surely a push is a push?” writes Ric Latham of that push on Barcola. “It wasn’t shoulder to shoulder, the defender wasn’t challenging for the ball, all he was doing was (successfully) preventing Barcola from getting his head anywhere near it. It’s a stone cold pen in either box, and saying otherwise just normalises the idea that players should get away with things like this because it wasn’t clear enough. Maddening.” In the time it takes to read this email Tony Harrington, the referee, gives two soft free-kicks for pushing or blocking and it’s the inconsistency that’s really maddening. There were two hands on his back, but I didn’t see the defender’s arms straighten as they would if there was a real shove going on. Share

11m ago 09.21 EST GOAL! Brighton 1-0 Brentford (Diego Gomez, 15 mins) Brighton move to second in the league! A cross from the right is kind of cleared, from which another cross from the right is kind of cleared, at which point Diego Gomez seizes possession, decides he’s had enough of crosses, and bangs a left-footer into the top corner from 25 yards! View image in fullscreen Brighton and Hove Albion's Diego Gomez celebrates scoring their first goal with Chema Andres and Pascal Gross. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at 09.23 EST

13m ago 09.19 EST They have now! A lovely switch of play gives the ball to Mitchell, who passes inside to Pino, who hammers a shot into the Liverpool crossbar! Share

15m ago 09.17 EST Szoboszlai now crosses from the left, Gakpo, beyond the far post, cushions it back across goal and it runs across the goalline without anyone there to turn it in! Palace haven’t been out of their half for a while. Share

17m ago 09.16 EST Save! Szoboszlai sends in a low, bobbling shot from 23 yards or thereabouts, which Henderson turns round the post. Share

21m ago 09.12 EST At Selhurst Park Barcola tries to meet a cross from the right and gets a fairly gentle push in the back as he does so. He goes down, but a penalty for that would be a bit much. Share

24m ago 09.09 EST GOAL! Ipswich 0-1 Bournemouth (Evanilson, 5 mins) A disastrous goal for Ipswich! Chris Walton, the home side’s keeper, tries to take the ball past the onrushing Evanilson, fails, is dispossessed, and the rest is a formality! View image in fullscreen Evanilson of Bournemouth scores against Ipswich Town at Portman Road. Photograph: Richard Pelham/Getty Images Share Updated at 09.30 EST

25m ago 09.07 EST A glimpse of goal for Palace, as Mitchell’s driven cross is met by Strand Larsen, but he can’t do much more than get a foot to it, and he deflects it limply wide of goal, from where it’s cleared for a throw-in. Share

27m ago 09.05 EST I’m focusing, for now, on Crystal Palace v Liverpool, where Isak has just had half a chance, but rather than racing onto the ball he rather meandered up to it, and his shot then hit a defender. Share

34m ago 08.58 EST The players are out and action is imminent. There’ll be a minute’s silence before all the games, because it is Remembrance Sunday. Share

1h ago 08.30 EST Fabian Hurzeler on what makes Brighton good: “Brilliant at the basics. That’s our foundation. That’s what made us strong and hopefully will make us strong in the future. It’s not about first outplaying the opponent, it’s about outworking the opponent.” Share

1h ago 08.30 EST Marco Rose is asked to identify Ipswich’s threat to Bournemouth today, and his response is, I have to say, vicious: “They want to win the game, I’m quite sure. It’s a nice ground.” Share

Sports.title: Russo on target again as double fires under-pressure Arsenal to vital WSL win at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Alessia Russo scored twice at Anfield to provide the under-pressure Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, with some brief respite but it was another unconvincing display from the north Londoners despite their much-needed 2-1 victory.

The in-form Russo’s double took her recent tally to seven goals in her past four appearances and 10 in her past seven games for club and country, but Liverpool posed plenty of problems for the visitors and were unhappy about a disallowed goal.

Arsenal began the game brightly and nearly went ahead early on when Lisa Baum’s effort deflected on to the crossbar and Olivia Smith fired over from a tight angle after initially being slipped through by Russo. Their purposeful start was rewarded when a good move down their right flank led to Emily Fox’s cross being angled into the net by Russo’s incisive first-time finish.

Liverpool were level just six minutes later, though, and from a defensive point of view it was a familiar story for Arsenal, who had similarly conceded from simple, long balls through the middle several times this term. They exerted very little pressure on the ball as Liverpool found Natalia Ramos in space and her direct ball picked out Beata Olsson up front, with the Arsenal centre-backs Steph Catley and Leah Williamson positioned so far apart that they were almost in different time zones, playing Olsson onside. Liverpool’s central striker did enough to keep the ball away from Williamson and lash her strike into the bottom corner.

Liverpool enjoyed a strong spell and a low cross from Vivien Endemann on the right left the Arsenal backline scampering but Williamson cleared it away, before a well-struck, curling Ramos free-kick was tipped on to the crossbar by the Arsenal goalkeeper Misa Rodríguez. Then came the game’s most contentious moment with Liverpool understandably feeling aggrieved not to have taken then lead.

Jenna Clark tucked the ball into the net at the far post after Arsenal failed to clear a corner, but the assistant referee disallowed the goal for offside against Endemann, despite the delivery towards the player having been inadvertently played off an Arsenal foot rather than being a deliberate forward pass from the home side, who looked baffled.

That seemed to wake Arsenal up from their slumber, however, and Caitlin Foord lashed a low effort narrowly wide, before a great block from Grace Fisk – who signed a new contract with Liverpool on Saturday – denied Smith from close range, after Foord had eased past Clark inside the box. Russo restored Arsenal’s lead in the final minute of the opening 45, as her downward header from Baum’s cross was too precise from Khiara Keating.
