After what had been a very watchable first half for neutrals, the second was comparative less entertaining, but still tense, as Liverpool fought to try to force an equaliser. They almost found it in the 89th minute but Gareth Taylor had his head in his hands in disbelief after Cornelia Kapocs volleyed wide from a glorious, unmarked position in front of goal. Kapocs had a shot blocked moments later, as Taylor’s team began to apply heavy, late pressure, but Arsenal clung on.

Sports.title: Julián Alvarez’s Atlético redemption arc in full focus for visit of Barcelona
Sports.content:
Julián Alvarez said sorry but forgiveness must be earned on the field and Sunday would be the perfect place. At 9pm at the Metropolitano, Atlético Madrid play Barcelona. It is the biggest match in Spain right now, a place at the top of the table awaiting the winner; it is also the game the striker they call the Spider planned to play on the other side. That, Alvarez said in Dallas, was his “dream”. Denied that, he must defeat the men he wanted to join to win back the supporters he wanted to walk out on, no better opportunity than now.

He has beaten them before. Last season, Atlético knocked Barcelona out of the Copa del Rey and Champions League. Alvarez scored both times but beneath the surface something had shifted in him and by the time the World Cup came round he admitted his desire to leave for Catalonia. That day, after Argentina beat Algeria, he didn’t name Barcelona and he didn’t need to; everyone knew. “It’s not the time to talk about this but nor can I hide,” he said. “I spoke with the people I needed to and the best thing for everyone is a transfer.”

Turned out that wasn’t true. Atlético didn’t agree then, refusing to sell; Barcelona, so open in their pursuit at the time, may not agree now. In week two of the new season, Alvarez was still in Madrid, whistled and booed by his own supporters, invited to walk off up the tunnel alone while his teammates turned the other way to applaud the fans who had abused him. One chant had started: “Tell him to go,” to which Alvarez probably thought: I’m trying. He had cut a lonely, distant figure, and if that was partly a public staging of his discontent, one more attempt to force his way out, if the fact he didn’t turn up for training over the next two days was as well, it didn’t work: when the transfer window shut six days later, he was still there.

They were still whistling too. Stuck, Alvarez had some making up to do, if only out of convenience, if only for a little while. He left Fernando Hidalgo, the agent whose exit strategy had failed, whom Atlético’s chief executive accused of having led Alvarez astray and who responded by calling the club “liars”. That helped, handing over someone to blame. He also played a bit more and a bit better, if not much to begin with. He at last scored a goal against Stuttgart on 20 October and four days later did it again, this time at home in a 1-0 win over Deportivo A Coruña. “I would like to apologise to our people for my words at the World Cup,” he said after.

Alvarez didn’t deny the way he felt and didn’t say that he no longer wanted to depart, but he did say he had made a mistake in the how and when. “I understand the anger; as a fan I would have been angry too, especially after all they had done to support me,” he said. The coach, Diego Simeone, was relieved. “I am very respectful of those who say sorry because it is not easy to say sorry,” he said. “I am sure Julián is more at peace now.”

It was about time, most fans felt, the least Alvarez could do – four months had passed since that day in Dallas, six weeks since he definitively realised he was staying – but he had waited until there was a goal, a peace offering to go with it. They had cheered it of course, but that didn’t mean embracing him. They also knew, though, that he was probably their best player. “We need lots of goals from Julián to be up there,” Jan Oblak had said in Stuttgart. “He has the quality to score a thousand goals,” Álex Grimaldo said.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha has reinvented himself as a No 9 since the start of the season for Barcelona. Photograph: Javier Borrego/AFP7/Shutterstock

He hasn’t yet but it is getting better, if slowly. Having started one of the first seven games, and without getting a goal, he has started five out of eight since, scoring twice. Meanwhile Barcelona, who thought they needed his goals, haven’t.

The summer in which they lost Robert Lewandowski, Marcus Rashford and Ferran Torres, and lost out on Alvarez, led to the reinvention of Raphinha as a No 9 and he is Europe’s top scorer with 19. Nor is it just him: people asked who was going to get the goals; the answer was everyone. Lamine Yamal has 13 goals and 11 assists. Thirteen different players have scored. Barcelona are on course to get more than 150 in the league alone, the chances of them returning for Alvarez receding. Barcelona are all right without him. The clásico reverse was their only domestic defeat after nine straight wins, although that same week they lost in Paris too, and the way it happened revealed a vulnerability.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Hope too for Atlético, for whom things were falling into place. Simeone had to accept Bayern Munich were superior on Tuesday, a step above that they cannot take yet, but in La Liga they have won seven in a row, including victory over their city rivals, Real. There is an assuredness about them, a variety too, optimism. Their record is better than it was at this stage the last time they won the league, the same question bringing the same answer. Who is going to get the goals? Everyone. Alvarez has scored one in the league, but Álex Baena has five, Álex Grimaldo four, Jonathan David and Giuliano Simeone three.

And here they are, ahead of Madrid, and just behind Barcelona. They have done it without the best Alvarez, the Spider’s powers weakened but slowly returning as he accepts that this is his place, begins a mission to make amends. Diminishing dependency may be no bad thing, the striker recast instead as an addition, the final, recovered piece in a functioning team, imagination allowed to take flight. Imagine if they can get him back; imagine if he can win them back too. Imagine if it happened on Sunday, with the win that takes Atlético to the top, redemption and rise in one, reconciliation too. “If the club wants to be in the places the fans dream of, we’ll need Julián,” Simeone said, no time like now.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca rues Manchester City’s lack of desire after defeat at Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca blamed his side’s lack of desire and the way they were outgunned in duels for a third successive Premier League defeat. After winning their first seven games of the season, Manchester City’s 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest extended their poor run.

Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle.

“You need desire and intensity to win second balls and duels. You require intensity or you struggle and we didn’t match their intensity. The second and third goals are copy and paste, lost duels first in the middle of pitch then at the edge of the box.”

City’s 100% record came to an end with a 2-1 defeat away by Aston Villa, and they followed that up last week with a 1-0 home reverse against Brighton. “They are all different,” said Maresca. “But if you look at chances, possession, chances inside box, in all of them we were much, much better but we lost all of them. We’re going to use this international break to clarify what we can do better. We know we need to improve things and avoid this kind of game.”

After his frustrated reaction to last week’s defeat at Brentford, Oliver Glasner was understandably delighted that his reset, ending what he had referred to as compromises, had paid off.

“The way we play football I think we’ve had many better games,” he said. “But how we defended, how passionately we defended, how tactically smart we defended, it was one of our better games.

“You should control everything and if you want to control it, you have to run because you have to be so quickly aware – they’re so good, such great players, such a good structure and they move the ball so quickly. Of course, you can just defend but you also need to go forward and this is what we did today in the right moments.”

Sports.title: There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title?

Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes.

Imagine being the manager who does sort it out. Imagine following in that brief lineage of United title winners: Ernest Mangnall, Matt Busby, Alex Ferguson … me? United remain the eighth wealthiest club by revenue in the world; imagine the resources that would be available if they were actually any good.

That is an allure that very few clubs in the world can match, no matter how good they were in the 1890s, and no matter how much the Villa owner, Nassef Sawiris, may dislike the fact. This is a point that cannot be made too strongly. Villa’s threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher was an outrageous attack on free speech. There is no way Carragher’s comment about the food chain of football could be construed as defamatory and, while it’s true he might have made the comment in less provocative terms, swearing is not a crime. This was a classic case of a legal threat being used to quell criticism and those fans – and, worse, journalists – who cheered it on should be thoroughly ashamed. The partisan blindness and persecution complex shared by fans of so many clubs is one of the most depressing features of the modern game.

But it’s also true United’s allure has come to look distinctly tarnished. No matter how bullet-proof a manager’s self-confidence, it would represent a remarkable risk to make the leap from Villa to United at this juncture. In almost every facet, from infrastructure to personnel, the modern Villa are better run than the modern United. And from Emery’s point of view, it’s not just that Villa are well run, it’s that they’re well run in his way.

He has the coaching staff he wants, while the president of football operations, Roberto Olabe, and the director of football operations, Damian Vidagany, are people he trusts and has worked with before. Emery would not have the degree of autonomy he has at Villa at many other clubs. United’s win over Roma on Tuesday may have eased the most immediate pressure on Michael Carrick, but nobody surely thinks that one good half against a depleted Serie A side cures all ills. (The question, obviously, is slightly absurd: nobody surely thinks Carrick is really the problem at United; it’s just that executives tend to get rid of managers because it’s what you do when there’s been a slump in form; it’s how a director acknowledges that he’s recognised there is a problem, while hoping desperately to deflect attention from his own shortcomings).

It doesn’t help that there is a clear precedent from five years ago, when a popular former United player saw his team come from two down to beat a Serie A side managed by Gian Piero Gasperini; Ole Gunnar Solskjær was sacked a month later.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick applauds the fans after Manchester United beat Roma in dramatic fashion. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

The United crisis may have eased, but it is far from over. While Sir Jim Ratcliffe shows off architects’ plans and begs for public money to build a new stadium, Villa get on with building the new North Stand. While United’s squad sags under the weight of its many contradictions, a weird mismatch of ill-fitting parts, Villa’s begins to take shape despite making 11 signings in the summer – even if the 3-0 defeat by Barcelona in midweek suggests there is still work to be done. They probably wouldn’t ideally have made such radical changes and would have preferred to keep Morgan Rogers and Ezri Konsa but, equally, there was an admirable sense of realism at Villa – a recognition of their place in the food chain, you might say – that when Chelsea or Arsenal come calling and offering huge contracts, there’s not much to be done other than to drive the price as high as possible.

Youri Tielemans is another player Villa might have liked to keep, but once United matched his release clause, the deal was done. Although Tielemans probably appreciates his new contract, it’s far from clear it’s been a good move for him from a football point of view, not least because United’s is a midfield that exposes his lack of mobility. Carlos Baleba was signed from Brighton to address that lack of dynamism in the United midfield but there were concerns about his tendency to drift in and out of games even before he suffered a hamstring injury on Tuesday.

It even feels as though Villa have been smarter about using United players than United have. Victor Lindelöf was brought in on a free transfer in summer 2025 and has excelled since and while Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho had less of an impact, Villa only signed them on loan. Rashford’s time, which featured four goals in 17 appearances in all competitions, was probably the more eye-catching, but Sancho made 39 appearances in his season at Villa.

In both cases, Villa got value out of a players whose futures were uncertain but without committing to having to take them on full-time.

It’s pretty hard to imagine at the moment, but at some point, United will start heading in the right direction. It may even be that Tuesday’s win prompts a surge of adrenaline that takes them into the top half of the table. For now, though, Villa look by far the brighter prospect, a club on the up, while United are in barely managed decline.

Sports.title: John Aloisi’s Chengdu choke to blow title chances on final day of Chinese season
Sports.content:
John Aloisi’s Chengdu Rongcheng let the Chinese Super League title slip from their grasp on the last day of the season, losing their fourth consecutive game as rivals Dalian Yingbo pipped them to the trophy following their fifth straight win.

Dalian completed a remarkable comeback by overhauling Chengdu’s lead, which once stood at 12 points, with Aloisi’s side picking up just one point in their last five matches. On the league’s final day, Chengdu lost 3-2 to Shandong Taishan, while Dalian’s 3-1 victory over Tianjin Tiger earned Li ⁠Guozu’s side ​the trophy.

The results saw the two teams finish level on 52 points, ​with Dalian winning the title on ‌a better head-to-head record ‌after recording a pair of wins over Chengdu, including in the penultimate ‌round of matches.

Dalian still needed to win on Sunday while hoping Chengdu lost, and Aloisi’s side went two goals down in Jinan when Raphael Merkies and Guilherme Madruga struck in the 15th and 23rd minutes respectively.

Felipe Silva pulled one back for Chengdu with seven minutes remaining ‌in the first half and, while Cryzan restored Shandong’s two-goal advantage in the 63rd minute, Wellington Silva’s 79th minute strike ​set up a tense finish.

View image in fullscreen Chengdu Rongcheng let a 12-point lead slip after losing their final four games of the season. Photograph: Shutterstock

Wang Ziming’s shot from close range was deflected over the bar in the third added minute as an increasingly desperate Chengdu ran out of time.

That left Dalian to secure the title in front ⁠of their own fans after Yang Mingrui gave the home ​side a fifth-minute lead.

Xadas’ ​50th minute penalty levelled ​the scores for Tianjin but Liao Jintao netted from the ​edge of the ‌area with 20 ​minutes left ​to restore Dalian’s advantage.

Huang Shan then struck from three yards out in the fourth minute of stoppage time to seal the win for Dalian and send the packed-out Dalian Suoyuwan Football Stadium into raptures.

It concludes an historic collapse for Australian Aloisi’s side who began the season with an unusual head-start as one of the only CSL clubs on zero points, while a series of points deductions were made to several rival sides which saw them start their campaigns in the negative.

Sports.title: Messi claims second straight Golden Boot as Nashville set points record on MLS Decision Day
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi won his second consecutive MLS Golden Boot award on Saturday, but Inter Miami squandered a three-goal lead in a 3-3 draw with Charlotte on the final day of the regular season.

The Argentinian superstar failed to score but set up Miami’s first two goals from corners at Nu Stadium as the defending champions secured second place in the Eastern Conference and home-field advantage for the first two rounds of the playoffs.

Messi’s 26 goals made him the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards. Dallas forward Petar Musa finished second with 22 after failing to score in his team’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado.

Ian Fray, Luis Suárez and Rodrigo De Paul scored first-half goals for Miami before Liel Abada struck twice shortly after the break to spark a Charlotte comeback, completed by Rodolfo Aloko’s 90th-minute equalizer.

Nashville broke the MLS single-season points record with a 2-0 victory over Cincinnati, finishing with 77 points to surpass the previous mark of 74 set by Miami in 2024.

Nashville finished atop the Eastern Conference with 23 wins, three defeats and eight draws, while Miami took second place with 60 points. Third-place New England missed a chance to overtake Miami after suffering a surprise 1-0 defeat at Orlando, leaving them on 58 points.

Miami will face Columbus in the opening round of the playoffs. Elsewhere in the East, New England will meet Philadelphia, Charlotte will take on Chicago and top-seeded Nashville will face the winner of the wild-card matchup between Orlando and Cincinnati.

Columbus secured seventh place and avoided the wild-card round with a 4-3 victory at Chicago.

At Nu Stadium, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, whose attempted clearance popped up for Fray to open the scoring.

Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suárez unmarked at the near post, where the Uruguayan glanced a header into the net to double Miami’s advantage.

De Paul made it 3-0 before half-time, but Abada pulled one back for Charlotte shortly after the restart and struck again in the 55th minute.

Aloko completed the comeback in the 90th minute, reacting quickest after Smalls’s shot rebounded off the post.

A visibly frustrated Messi struck the woodwork in stoppage time before Aloko came within inches of an improbable winner with a thunderous shot into the side-netting.

Seattle and Real Salt Lake advance in West

Western Conference champions Vancouver defeated Canadian rivals Montreal 2-0 to finish second in the overall standings, securing home-field advantage should the Whitecaps face Inter Miami in a rematch of last year’s MLS Cup final.

Six teams entered Decision Day fighting for the final three Western Conference playoff places, with all 30 MLS clubs in action.

Portland, Colorado and the LA Galaxy each needed only a victory to secure a playoff berth, but only the Timbers delivered, winning 2-0 at Austin.

Real Salt Lake defeated the Galaxy 2-1, while Colorado fell 3-1 at Dallas, allowing Salt Lake to claim a postseason place.

Seattle secured the other remaining berth with a 2-1 home victory over Los Angeles FC. Albert Rusnák scored in the opening minute and set up Sebastián Gómez’s 31st-minute goal before Eddie Segura pulled one back for LAFC in the 82nd minute.

Minnesota defeated visiting San Jose 3-1 but, like the Galaxy, finished a point behind Real Salt Lake and missed the playoffs.

The opening Western Conference playoff matchups pit Vancouver against the winner of the wild-card meeting between Seattle and Real Salt Lake, Dallas against Portland, LAFC against St Louis and Houston against San Jose.

Sports.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
Sports.content:
As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.

Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents.

“To the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach,” said Arteta. “I need to praise the players and all the staff for the work that they are doing because it’s been very, very demanding. We have a very short time to recover from games but despite that the mentality and the quality of the team has shown: it’s incredible.”

Jakirovic had promised beforehand that his side would go on the front foot. “If you are passive, they will destroy you,” said the Bosnian. But while his bold 5-3-2 formation caused Arsenal’s much-vaunted defence some issues, Hull remain without a league victory since the end of August. “It’s a big experience for us,” was Jakirovic’s post-match assessment. “We can take some big lessons from this but we have shown we can compete at this level.”

View image in fullscreen Martin Ødegaard scores the decisive goal from close range. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

Hull made the brighter start as John Egan headed wide from a corner. After losing to Brighton before the last international break, Arteta was taking no chances and reverted to the side that won at Liverpool last weekend. There was no William Saliba on the bench, with the France defender set to play for the under-21s on Sunday instead as he continues his comeback from a back injury.

Quick Guide How do I 

Yet aside from a set piece that resulted in Gabriel Magalhães just failing to connect with Ezri Konsa’s flick-on, the visitors’ low block frustrated Arsenal and they continued to cause problems on the break. Elliot Stroud forced David Raya into a save after Riccardo Calafiori surrendered possession cheaply.

Havertz’s failure to take a shot after being played in by a slide-rule pass from Ødegaard drew groans of frustration. A toiling Arsenal thought all their prayers had been answered just before half-time when the referee, Farai Hallam, was sent to the big screen by the VAR. Nobel Mendy was clearly pulling Havertz’s shirt inside the area yet the German was offside so the penalty was not awarded, even though it probably should have been according to the rules. They state that Havertz must be “attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball” to be penalised and because Mendy’s offence came first, that should have taken precedence, as it did when Newcastle’s Fabian Schär was awarded a penalty against Bournemouth in February 2024.

View image in fullscreen Kai Havertz is pulled back by Nobel Mendy but no penalty was awarded. Photograph: Simon Dael/Shutterstock

Pro Ref has yet to make a statement on the incident and Arteta admitted he had been left confused by the whole episode. “I don’t know what the interpretation is, I’m sure they will make that clear to understand,” he said.

The Arsenal manager’s annoyance levels continued to rise when Havertz could only head straight at Konstantinos Tzolakis on the stroke of half-time. Hull came out for the second half with a similar attitude and Jakirovic picked up a yellow card for protesting against another decision that went against his team. Declan Rice was withdrawn early, although Arteta insisted he was fine afterwards. Noni Madueke found space after a flowing Arsenal move but again his effort was straight down the throat of Tzolakis.

The feeling of desperation was growing. But Ødegaard has made a habit of coming to Arsenal’s rescue this season and the captain was quickest to react when Tzolakis spilled Madueke’s shot to finally break Hull’s brave resistance.

Sports.title: Premier League legend David Silva, 40, makes emphatic return to football with man-of-the-match performance - three-and-a-half years after retiring
Sports.content:
David Silva made his mark in his first game since coming out of retirement after scoring on debut in a man-of-the-match display for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin on Saturday. Last month, the Manchester City icon revealed he was lacing his football boots in a professional sense again for the first time since 2023. The 40-year-old started for Sha Tin and broke the deadlock against HK Rangers from the penalty spot in the 56th minute. Silva stepped up and coolly passed the ball into the bottom left-hand corner - sending Hong Kong Rangers goalkeeper Ka-Yu Yip the wrong way. The playmaker's goal sparked mass celebrations from his team-mates and the fans in the stands - with many taking their phones out of their pockets to record the moment. However, Silva's debut didn't go as smoothly as planned as the visitors equalised in the 65th minute through Ibrahim Yakubu Nassam. Some Spanish guy just scored a penalty for Sha Tin#DavidSilva #hkpl #hkfootball pic.twitter.com/JCbiYZEKE0 — Football in Hong Kong (@offsideHK) November 7, 2026 David Silva scored for Hong Kong outfit Sha Tin with this penalty in their 1-1 draw on Saturday The 40-year-old celebrates with his team-mates after scoring against Hong Kong Rangers Silva was named man-of-the-match, in what his first competitve match in over three years With 11 minutes remaining, Silva was then booked before he was substituted in the 84th minute with his side down to 10 men following Maxwell Ansah's 81st-minute red card for a second bookable offence. Despite failing to take all three points, Silva did collect the man-of-the-match award after the full-time whistle. Sha Tin currently sit 10th in the Hong Kong Premier League with five points from their opening seven matches. They sit one point and place above bottom-placed Eastern AA, who occupy the sole relegation spot, and 14 points adrift of table-toppers North District. Silva called it a day on his playing career back in 2023 when he tore his anterior cruciate ligament while playing for Real Sociedad. He is most famed for spending ten years at Manchester City between 2010 and 2020, where he won 11 major honours; four Premier League titles, two FA Cups and five League Cups. Much of that time period, though, is now under scrutiny. He also has a statue outside the Etihad Stadium, and won the 2010 World Cup with Spain, as well as Euro 2008 and Euro 2012. Upon joining Sha Tin, ex-Valencia midfielder Silva said in an Instagram video: 'I'm so excited to go to Hong Kong and enjoy the local culture, the food in Sha Tin and, of course, football in Hong Kong.' Silva will hope to lead his side to victory when they take on Southern District in the Hong Kong League Cup Losers play-offs on Saturday. Sports.title: Manchester Re-United! Legends join forces to toast Sir Alex Ferguson on 40th anniversary of his appointment at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester Re-United! Legends join forces to toast Sir Alex Ferguson on 40th anniversary of his appointment at Old Trafford

Manchester United legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his anniversary of being named manager of the club on Saturday night.

In a decision that ushered in the most successful period in United's history, Ferguson was poached from Scottish club Aberdeen 40 years ago on Friday – with the iconic manager lifting 37 pieces of silverware during his spell at Old Trafford.

He also played a significant role in shaping the careers of a litany of stars who graced the club during his 27-year tenure, with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and David Beckham hugely benefiting from his mentorship.

And a handful of players who shared a dressing room with Ferguson were on hand to toast the iconic manager during a celebratory evening in Manchester on Saturday night.

Diehard United fan and actor James Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside current United boss Michael Carrick.

Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea also joined their old mentor at the bash.

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez

Ferguson ushered in the most successful period in the club's history during his 27-year stint

Carrick has namechecked Ferguson as a crucial ally as he looks to transform United's fortunes amid the club's worst ever start to a Premier League season.

The Red Devils dropped into the relegation zone on Saturday night following Nottingham Forest's win over Manchester City, and Carrick's stint in the dugout appeared all but over following a 3-0 thumping by Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

But he was handed a reprieve by the United hierarchy and there were green shoots of optimism following a rousing 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

United host Unai Emery's Aston Villa at Old Trafford today, and Carrick has admitted he has been given no guarantees on his future.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night,' he said.

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

What a fantastic evening at Old Trafford celebrating 40 years of Sir Alex taking the reign at @ManUtd. Catching up with the boys and some great speeches about how he achieved to leave such a mark on this club! pic.twitter.com/kgoNfzfPWJ — Edwin van der Sar (@vdsar1970) November 8, 2026

Ferguson unveiled as new manager of Manchester United in 1986

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

Sports.title: This is how Enzo Maresca's tactics have left Elliot Anderson exposed with too much to do, writes JACK GAUGHAN... and why £125m Enzo Fernandez must step up and offer much more to solve midfield riddle
Sports.content:
Manchester City spent £320million on overhauling their midfield over the summer. In doing so, they twice broke their own transfer record. This marked the most aggressive focus on a specific need since the lavish outlay on full backs nine years ago.

All signed weeks before the independent commission’s guilty verdicts were announced, Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi heralded a new era in the City engine room. More energy, vibrancy, dynamism.

Two of them were ready-made replacements for Rodri and Bernardo Silva, with Bouaddi only 18 at the time and purchased as a potential superstar after shooting to global prominence at the World Cup.

But as Enzo Maresca heads into the second international break of the season on the back of three consecutive Premier League defeats, his midfield is the primary area of concern. And has been for a while.

A big fortnight lies in store for City’s manager, whose midfield has been wide open all year. Fine when outscoring opponents – see the 5-3 victory over Sunderland – and it makes for great entertainment yet an obvious gaping chasm when the goals dry up slightly.

The balance has not felt right and Maresca, who has gently batted away persistent questions about the midfield for weeks, must know this.

Elliot Anderson is being asked to do too much and it cost City in the 3-1 defeat at Forest

While studying tapes of all three defeats over the coming days, before City come back after the internationals to host Fulham and then go to Arsenal, he needs to determine a plan moving forward and that will include some tough decisions on individuals and shapes.

Nottingham Forest could have driven a bus through the middle of the park on Saturday night, two goals from counter-attacking situations engineered between the width of the centre circle. Twice the ostensible holding midfielder Anderson tried to nick possession, beaten to it, and City were turned around.

Noises coming from the dressing room suggest that Anderson is effectively being asked to operate as both a No6 and No8 when picked as the deepest of the three, to go and join play high up the pitch. That is Maresca leaning into the England international’s Action Man, everything to everyone style. That also relies on somebody covering for him.

That somebody does not exist in this current setup, Fernandez always too high and wide elsewhere.

So when they lose duels as happened at the City Ground, something the manager openly bemoaned, City are not stable enough to recover.

Liam Delap's fierce finish put Forest 2-0 ahead - and City were left playing catch-up

Club analysts have sat down with Anderson to go over video clips on how best to follow these instructions to the benefit of the team. Watching him, it’s hard not to conclude that this is a quality midfielder being asked to do too much as a single deep midfielder.

It will produce moments of sheer class – that lung-busting run up the right in Leipzig on Wednesday that bore hallmarks of Kevin De Bruyne, a perfect cross for Erling Haaland’s winner – while also leaving the defence exposed.

An exposed defence lends itself to a heightened chance of individual errors, plenty of those around at the moment, and it was noticeable at Forest that the opening goal came from uncertainty in possession. Josko Gvardiol made the error, eased off the ball by eventual goalscorer Jair Cunha, but the plan cannot be to have the left back with his back to goal and no viable passing options.

When Marc Guehi’s ball went into Gvardiol, Anderson was higher and wider on the right – deep in conversation with Abdukodir Khusanov about how they’d failed to move possession well enough earlier in the sequence – and Rayan Cherki was belatedly trotting back to offer himself.

Fernandez never once enters the frame, even when Cunha is in the box and subsequently wheeling away in celebration. Maresca rejected the suggestion that there is an issue with the team’s build-up on Saturday night.

As Man City look to build from the back in the third minute, Anderson (No 5) is busy delivering instructions to Khusanov (out of shot)...

... it means that when Guehi plays the ball to Gvardiol, he has his back to goal and nobody in midfield to pass to - and is already under pressure

... and with no support, three Forest players swarm and Jair Cunha dispossesses him, leading to him scoring the opening goal

What is clear though is that there is not yet that balance, that this is not yet a unit. Maresca moved to include Bouaddi with Anderson and Fernandez against Brighton – a one-goal defeat – but that acted as detrimental to creativity. If nothing else, Brighton proved that City require either Cherki or Phil Foden on the pitch at all times.

Over the past two games, Fernandez has lurked more menacingly at the back post, offering an additional goal threat than just relying on Haaland. That ghosting late run saw him score in Leipzig but for a joint-British record £125million needs to offer so much more. There will be growing calls for Bouaddi’s inclusion as a genuine deep-lying midfielder but it’s unlikely that the teenager can manage the league’s physicality as a single pivot.

The Moroccan has more chance of stamping his authority when alongside somebody else, dovetailing with an Anderson as a two. That leaves Fernandez, whose barnstorming league debut at Old Trafford feels like a long time ago now.

To persist with him, he either dislodges Cherki as the No10 on the promise of far more goals or Maresca drops him back into a more conventional role that allows Anderson to flourish properly.

Something has to give because the unevenness of City’s three is giving the rest of the team uncomfortable jitters.

Sports.title: Rodrigo Muniz's baby joy after miscarriage heartbreak: Premier League star reveals wife is pregnant again after off-field agony last season in emotional interview
Sports.content:
Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz has opened up on his 'really difficult' off-field issues, with the Brazilian revealing he and his wife suffered a miscarriage last year.

Muniz, 25, earned the Cottagers a point in Saturday's draw against Newcastle, with his 83rd minute strike his first Premier League goal since August 2025.

The centre forward, speaking with club media after the Craven Cottage game, spoke candidly of the difficulties he has faced with wife Jady - who are now expecting again after a turbulent year.

'Last season was really difficult for me because, now I can say, I had surgery, my wife was pregnant last season but unfortunately we lost the baby,' he said.

'But God is good all the time and now she is pregnant again. The goal was for my baby and I hope this season will be different to last season.'

Fulham star Rodrigo Muniz opened up on his personal agony after scoring on Saturday

Muniz revealed his wife Jady suffered a miscarriage but they are now pregnant again

Muniz has not been afforded a start by new Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa, making all eight of his Premier League appearances off the bench so far this season.

He hopes that his contribution against the Toon has done enough to earn his manager's trust after the international break.

'I train hard every week to get opportunities to play and I want to play more,' he said.

'I cannot control that but I showed to the gaffer I want to play more.

'And I have to keep training hard for him to say, 'okay, now is your time', and then I'm ready.

'To be a striker, you need to be ready to play five or ten minutes. Of course, I want to play more. And I want to start as well.

'We have a lot of players in the national team. We train with, I think, ten players.

'It's really important because we cannot stay out for too long.

'And when we have time to work it's really good – because it's really important that the gaffer can show us what he wants and we have time to do it.'

Sports.title: New mum and ex-Lionesses star Mary Earps names baby boy Xander after announcing her partner's secret birth in heartwarming Instagram video
Sports.content:
Euro-winning Lionesses goalkeeper Mary Earps has named her son Xander after becoming a mother for the first time, having revealed this week that her partner has given birth to a baby boy.

Earps, 33, was a hero of England's Euro 2022 victory at Wembley and starred at the World Cup in 2023, saving a penalty in the final. She won BBC Sports Personality of the Year but later lost her England place to rival Hannah Hampton and retired in acrimonious circumstances.

She moved to France with Paris Saint-Germain but returned to England earlier this year - and has now welcomed her first child with her partner, Kitty Forrest.

'Welcome to the world, Xander,' she posted on Instagram, with a photograph of her newborn's hand.

In a video released on Friday, Earps said: 'I've been keeping a little secret from you all. And I don't think I can talk my way out of this one. So, I think I'm going to have to show you.

'I can't quite believe I'm writing this, but yesterday Kitty and I welcomed our beautiful baby boy into the world!

'We're absolutely over the moon and still trying to take it all in. It's been such an emotional journey getting to this point, and we couldn't be more excited to start this next chapter of our lives as a family of three.'

Mary Earps has revealed the name of her baby boy following his secret birth: Xander

Earps and her partner Kitty (second right) revealed news of welcoming a baby boy (YouTube/Mary Earps)

Earps says she will not be able to take maternity leave due to the rigors of the football season. Her team, London City Lionesses, are eight games into the new Women's Super League season and sit third behind Chelsea and Manchester City.

'I do have one eye sort of on football, which is super weird,' she said.

'In any other job, you would just be like, "Okay, bye. Taking maternity leave, whatever. Um, and you just do what you need to do." But that doesn't really work in football, because you've got games and then, if you take the day off, then you got to think about what that looks like and how that works into sort of your training schedule and the fixture calendar.

'So, it's a little bit more complicated. You can't just take annual leave whenever you want without consequence. You know, it's going to be interesting to see what the next days and weeks bring.'

Earps first revealed that she was in a same-sex relationship in September of last year but largely kept partner Kitty out of the spotlight.

Kitty is a physiotherapist who worked as the lead in her department at Manchester United Women, Earps's former club.

Earps is pictured kissing the trophy after England won Euro 2022 at Wembley Stadium

Earps won BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2023 following her Euro heroics

In a statement at the time, Earps said: 'I've always tried to keep my personal life separate from my professional one, but it would have felt inauthentic not to include something so important to me in this book. I'm in a really happy relationship.

'The people closest to me have always known, and I feel ready and happy to share that with everyone else now.'

Earps retired from England duty in May last year after the release of her autobiography dragged up a storm with Hampton, the Chelsea goalkeeper who overtook her from understudy to become England No 1.

Earps revealed she told Sarina Wiegman that 'bad behaviour was being rewarded' after Hampton was recalled to the England squad.

Sports.title: Premier League star's career criminal brother beats Home Office bid to deport him to Africa - as he awaits trial for kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery
Sports.content:
Premier League star's career criminal brother beats Home Office bid to deport him to Africa - as he awaits trial for kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery

The street criminal brother of a Premier League star has beaten a Home Office attempt to deport him to Africa - by citing his own human rights.

The gang member and aspiring rapper, now in his twenties, was the subject of a concerted four year attempt by the government to send him to his family's country of origin in West Africa because of his shocking criminal record.

The young man, who has never held down a job, is currently in prison for dangerous driving and carrying a knife - while awaiting yet another court case accused of kidnap, false imprisonment, aggravated burglary and robbery.

During his teens he had played academy football for several Premier League teams but while his brother went on to make it and is now a multi-millionaire, the man instead got sucked into street crime.

And he has been involved in so much anti-social and criminal behaviour since then that he has even incurred a number of gunshot wounds.

But the wannabe rapper has managed to win a long-running deportation bid by the Home Office to kick him out of Britain as an undesirable - arguing that this wouldn't be fair as all his significant ties are here.

A Premier League footballer - who cannot be named for legal reasons - has seen his career criminal brother living in Britian beat a Home Office attempt to deport him back to West Africa

The Home Office first targeted him for deportation in 2022 after he was sentenced to 20 months in jail having been caught with a sword in his waistband, which in turn meant had breached an existing order about his criminal behaviour.

They lost that attempt to get him out of Britain but appealed - and have now lost that appeal too.

The gang member is 'healthy and capable' according to a judge but has never worked - in stark contrast to his hugely successful brother, a full international footballer who has made countless top flight appearances.

A court heard the foreign national has a 'sustained history of criminal offending involving repeated breaches of Criminal Behaviour Orders, possession of offensive weapons, breaches of licence conditions, recalls to custody, and recent charges. He has a history of offending with knives since the age of 17'.

Totaling his various jail terms together he has spent three of the last eight years prison.

But despite his ongoing recurrent criminality, the Home Office has failed in its latest attempt to deport him after a judge ruled he is 'socially and culturally integrated' into the UK and a return to his home country would leave him 'very much an outsider'.

The immigration tribunal decided he would face 'very significant obstacles to integration' in his home country and prevented the government from deporting him by ruling it would breach his human rights.

That decision came despite it emerging that he has an uncle in the country and grew up with a familiarity of the country, including its culture and food, while his mother maintains links to the country and visited as recently as 2024.

But the judge said the 'significance of these ties should not be exaggerated' because he has never been there.

They said his social and cultural identity 'has been almost entirely formed in the UK and by British culture' - even though he was born overseas and his family come from West Africa. The Home Office is appealing the decision and so the brother could still face deporation.

The knife criminal first arrived in the UK in 2006 after being born in another country where he doesn't have nationality.

He is in a relationship with a British woman with whom he shares a baby.

Their child was born in February but the rapper has only met them twice because he remains incarcerated.

There is no evidence that having a partner or child has reformed his criminal ways, a court heard.

The Home Office argued he is a healthy young adult capable of work who has a familiarity with the culture of his home country and has family ties in the country who could provide guidance and support.

But the judge concluded it would breach his human rights because he has never lived or visited and would be an outsider if returned.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino left sweating as Arsene Wenger urged to rival FIFA chief for job
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino left sweating as Arsene Wenger urged to rival FIFA chief for job

Gianni Infantino could face a battle to hold onto his FIFA presidency with Arsene Wenger being urged to provide a genuine challenge

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger already has a role within FIFA (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

There are growing calls for Arsene Wenger to challenge FIFA president Gianni Infantino as he bids to retain his role at the top of football.

‌



‌



Wenger, who has not been involved in management since leaving Arsenal in 2018, has emerged as a surprise threat to Infantino in his bid for re-election. The 57-year-old's stock has plummeted since the World Cup following his controversial plans to sell off stakes in future tournaments.

‌



Infantino has remained defiant in the wake of the backlash to said plans and wants to keep his job, but senior executives, including some from Europe, have been urging Wenger for weeks to put his hand up as the next FIFA president.

‌



The Frenchman, as well as a mystery candidate, are seen as the two men who could apply the most pressure to Infantino, reports The Telegraph. The upcoming week will be crucial with November 18 the deadline for candidates to come forward.

Should Wenge, who is now FIFA's chief of global football development, opt against running then UEFA, who have publicly called out Infantino, will back Kozo Tashima, the head of the Japan Football Association. Tashima has been on FIFA's ruling committee since 2015 has said his candidacy is “not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built”.

The Football Association have stated that they believe Infantino is no longer the right man to lead FIFA.

‌



Wenger publicly condemned Infantino’s controversial World Cup plan, describing its abandonment as “absolutely necessary and beyond question”. The issue is whether the former Arsenal boss, now 77, thinks he would be too old to run for the presidency.

Despite mass criticism, the Caribbean Football Union has confirmed it would endorse Infantino for another term after he visited the region. Support from Qatar and Saudi Arabia is aiding Infantino in his bid to secure the 106 votes he needs to be re-elected.

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has come under criticism (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

However the FIFA boss has faced another difficult week after it emerged his presidential office requested VIP treatment for his daughters and their dogs on a personal trip from Miami airport to Qatar. It has raised further questions over his personal conduct and an possible abuse of his position.

Infantino was also under major scrutiny during the World Cup, with the major flashpoint being FIFA's decision to take the unprecedented step of suspending Folarin Balogun's red card after Donald Trump put in a call to Infantino.

Sports.title: Arsenal legend, 53, becomes dad for a fourth time two years after splitting from wife
Sports.content:
Arsenal legend, 53, becomes dad for a fourth time two years after splitting from wife

A former Arsenal star has announced the birth of his daughter on Instagram, with the Gunners legend becoming a father for the fourth time at the age of 53

View 2 Images Arsenal legend Robert Pires has some exciting news (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal legend Robert Pires has announced the birth of his fourth child at the age of 53. The former France international shared the news with his followers on Instagram on Saturday, revealing that he and his new partner had welcomed a baby girl named Olivia.

‌



‌



Pires posted a touching black-and-white photograph of himself holding his newborn daughter's hand, alongside the caption: "Olivia Pires 31/10/2026. Welcome my baby girl."

‌



He followed it up with another monochrome image showing his partner, whose identity has not been made public, cradling her pregnant bump while sitting in front of him. A third photograph showed Pires leaving hospital with Olivia secured in a baby carrier.

‌



The announcement comes two years after Pires ended his relationship with French model Jessica Lemarie. The couple had been together for 21 years and married for 11, before going their separate ways.

Thomas Tuchel reveals why Eberechi Eze kept England place and names star he apologised to READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

They have three children together, including 19-year-old Theo, who has followed in his father's footsteps by pursuing a career in professional football. The teenager is a former youth captain at Arsenal and currently plays for Metz - the club where his father began his professional career.

‌



Pires was previously married to his first wife, Nathalie, for six years. The pair met during his time at Metz before divorcing in 2003, while the midfielder was playing for Arsenal. They did not have any children together.

A host of Pires' former team-mates and footballing colleagues were quick to congratulate him following the announcement.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Former Arsenal midfielder Gilberto Silva responded with three heart emojis, while ex-Chelsea and Gunners goalkeeper Petr Cech wrote: "Congratulations, Robert!" Sol Campbell also sent his best wishes, commenting: "Love and happiness!"

‌



Other former professionals to share their congratulations included Luis Figo, Roberto Carlos, Franck Ribery and ex-Arsenal defender Emmanuel Eboue.

Pires enjoyed a hugely successful six-year spell at Arsenal after arriving from Marseille in 2000. He made 284 appearances for the Gunners, scoring 84 goals and helping them secure two Premier League titles and two FA Cups.

‌



View 2 Images Pires (R) won four major trophies at Arsenal, including two Premier League titles (Image: Getty)

The Frenchman was also a key member of Arsene Wenger's legendary Invincibles side, which went through the entire 2003/04 Premier League campaign without suffering defeat. He formed a formidable attacking partnership with the likes of Thierry Henry and Dennis Bergkamp during his time in north London.

‌



His final appearance for Arsenal came in the 2006 Champions League final defeat to Barcelona, after which he moved to Spanish side Villarreal.

Pires returned to English football in 2010, joining Aston Villa, but his time at Villa Park proved brief. He made just nine Premier League appearances during a single season with the club. He officially retired in 2016, having enjoyed a final playing spell with Indian Super League side Goa in 2014.

Sports.title: What Michael Carrick knows about Man Utd future ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
What Michael Carrick knows about Man Utd future ahead of crunch Aston Villa clash

Michael Carrick is a man under pressure and continues to be in the dark regarding his future as Manchester United look to avoid dropping into the bottom three

View 2 Images Michael Carrick remains a man firmly under pressure (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has been given no assurances that he will remain as Manchester United boss after their clash with Aston Villa on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



Ahead of kick-off the Red Devils do find themselves in the bottom three following Nottingham Forest's win. Incredibly they are just two points off being bottom of the Premier League.

‌



They still have just one win to their name, that coming over Ipswich back in August, and they're in the midst of a poor run that could be extended by Unai Emery's side. As a result Carrick's future has come under serious threat and the United board know they could be forced into acting.

‌



This is already United's worst ever start to a Premier League season but it could reach new lows if they find themselves in the relegation zone come November's international break.

The upcoming pause in the domestic game is also traditionally when clubs would opt to make a change in the dugout, given the extended time to prepare for their next game. Carrick has continued to field questions over his future, but insists he's been given no assurances, nor does he need any, reports The Sun.

In midweek United calmed the noise somewhat, although only after coming back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2. Questions have been raised over whether that can be a turning point, or whether it simply covered the cracks that have been exposed all season.

‌



Carrick, who was only given the job permanently in the summer, could yet be the third man axed by the Ineos hierarchy, who themselves have come in for huge criticism. The United boss though has maintained he doesn't need any kind of refresh despite the upcoming break.

View 2 Images If Man Utd are to make a change in the dugout then the international break is seen as the ideal time (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"I think international breaks are always a time when, talking about the players that aren’t going away and for the staff, I think there is a little bit (of time) to re-energise and freshen up," he said.

"I think some of the players that go away in internationals, they get freshened up in a different environment, so there is an element of that, but I don’t really need it. I’m fine as I am."

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher's row with Aston Villa exposed a painful truth about Man Utd's new reality
Sports.content:
It was the sort of innocuous, run-of-the-mill opinion football fans hear all the time.

The dismal form of Manchester United this season has seen all sort of names bandied around as possible replacements for Michael Carrick and Jamie Carragher, in his role as a Sky Sports pundit, suggested Unai Emery.

Cue a gigantic - and understandable - backlash from Villa fans and a ridiculous and over-the-top response from the club and Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris, who threatened Carragher with legal action for his "unacceptable insults".

The row is still bubbling away in the background, via Emery's firm suggestion that Villa can challenge for the Champions League after Carragher revisited the topic in his weekly newspaper column.

‌



Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat READ MORE :

JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move READ MORE :

Carragher said it was "beyond doubt" that United eclipse Villa on every conceivable metric. "It did not strike me as controversial to suggest that when a club of United’s size wants Aston Villa’s managers or players, traditionally they get them," he wrote.

That, of course, is true. The financial power of the Premier League's traditional elite, their history and offers of playing in European competitions and winning trophies do usually tempt prospective targets.

But what Carragher perhaps fails to gauge is that his viewpoint is now out of date. Like a jar that has been forgotten about at the back of the fridge, it needs chucking out and replacing with something fresher.

United are no longer the powerhouse of their Sir Alex Ferguson glory days. And they don't have their pick of the best players and managers from the Premier League and beyond.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 4 Images Michael Carrick's side are far from what they once were (Image: Getty Images)

This summer, they spent £155million to sign Youri Tielemans from Villa, Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Carlos Baleba from Brighton. They didn't exactly have to fight off rival clubs for their signatures - and we've seen why in the last few months.

These are middle-shelf players at best. Premium, top-shelf ones are heading elsewhere. With the Glazers piling up debts and Sir Jim Ratcliffe slashing costs wherever he can, United are unwilling or unable to shop at the same stores as their rivals.

‌



It's a similar picture when it comes to managers. Since Ferguson retired in 2013, they have had 11 permanent or interim bosses. Five, including Carrick, have been former United players. Just two, Louis van Gaal and Jose Mourinho, could be described as proven, elite managers.

View 4 Images Unai Emery has big ambitions at Aston Villa and is not interested in joining Manchester United (Image: Javier Borrego/Getty Images)

The last two permanent bosses before Carrick show United's current level: Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim were hired after encouraging form with Ajax and Sporting Lisbon respectively. As the connection with Emery - who is about to sign a new contract with Villa - shows, United are simply unable to cherry-pick the best in the business.

In 2024, United chiefs spoke with Thomas Tuchel and Gareth Southgate as they pondered replacements for Ten Hag. Neither wanted the job.

‌



The list of prospective replacements for Carrick showed the situation clearly. Emery and Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler are unattainable. Julian Nagelsmann is at a career lull after a World Cup exit with Germany. Antonio Conte is a nuclear option not many other clubs are willing to take.

View 4 Images Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada have been unable to hire a top-tier replacement for Michael Carrick (Image: Getty Images)

In the Goldilocks analogy, Eddie Howe - a former Bournemouth and Newcastle boss - is just right. If they had managed to woo an elite manager then the truth is that Carrick would be long gone.

This harsh reality will be visible to all on Sunday at Old Trafford when Emery takes his Villa side to play United. Villa may arrive on the back of a 3-0 mauling by Barcelona, while United are buoyed by a 3-2 comeback win over Roma.

‌



But as the odds show, nobody would be surprised to see Villa follow in the footsteps of Bournemouth by leaving with all three points. Emery is perfectly happy where he is with good reason.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury goes public and demands fight on Anthony Joshua undercard is cancelled
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury goes public and demands fight on Anthony Joshua undercard is cancelled

Tyson Fury reignited his rivalry with Deontay Wilder with some choice words about the American boxer

View 2 Images Tyson Fury had quite the statement to make ahead of his blockbuster bout against Anthony Joshua (Image: getty images)

Tyson Fury claimed Deontay Wilder's upcoming bout against Jai Opetaia is "silly" and that his former foe should have already retired from boxing. The 'Gypsy King' is approaching the biggest fight of his career when he takes on fellow Brit, Anthony Joshua, at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on December 11.

‌



‌



While fight fans across the world will be treated to the long-awaited main event, the undercard fight of the 'Bronze Bomber' taking on the undefeated cruiserweight champion promises a tasty clash.

‌



However, Fury is placed firmly in the camp of those thinking the fight is a mismatch given Wilder's decline in recent years and the Aussie's reign of dominance. Fury and Wilder provided a heavyweight rivalry for the ages that began in 2018 when the pair fought to a spectacular draw.

‌



They battled two more times after that as Fury got his hand raised in both bouts and ended their trilogy with a stunning 11th-round knockout victory over the Olympic bronze medallist in 2021.

Wilder last entered the ring in April earlier this year when seeing off veteran Derek Chisora in a split-decision win. It's been quite the fall from grace for the 41-year-old, who has lost two of his last four fights.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



When discussing Wilder's fight against Opetaia on the undercard, Fury said his knockout of the Alabama-born boxer should have been the last time he ever entered a boxing ring. Fury told FightHype: "It’s silly, really, on Deontay’s part.

"He shouldn’t be in the ring; he should be nowhere near a ring. It is a dying shame that this man has to continue to fight after he is shot to bits. He should have never fought again after I beat him the last time; that should have been the end of it, but needs must.

‌



View 2 Images Tyson Fury said Deontay Wilder should walk away from boxing (Image: Getty Images)

"If you are getting knocked out by people that you probably should have knocked out yourself, then you should walk away. Him and Chisora looked shockingly terrible when they fought.

Article continues below

"Chisora is like 145 years old. And he was taking Wilder’s knockout-power shots – that are not there anymore – flush in the face, not even budging him."

Fury's last fight saw him stop Mariusz Wach in the seventh round in July, while Joshua came back from a shocking early knockdown to score a second-round knockout of Kristian Prenga the day after Fury's win.

Sports.title: Non-league clash postponed as ex-Forest starlet rushed to hospital in warm-up
Sports.content:
Non-league clash postponed as ex-Forest starlet rushed to hospital in warm-up

Truro City's National League South clash at Folkestone Invicta was postponed when City player Yassine En-Neyah suffered a medical emergency in the warm-up

View 3 Images The ambulance drove on to the pitch to take En-Neyah to hospital (Image: Tom Sandberg/PPAUK)

Truro City's trip to Folkestone Invicta was postponed due to a medical emergency for one of the visiting players.

‌



‌



City star Yassine En-Neyah, a Nottingham Forest youth product, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after the episode prior to the National League South clash.

‌



The 26-year-old is said to have collapsed on the pitch before the ambulance drove on to the playing surface in order to take him to hospital.

‌



Both sides released a short statement confirming the postponement, before a further post from Truro confirmed En-Neyah was the player involved and that he was receiving further treatment.

“Truro City can confirm that this afternoon’s match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed," they said.

"Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment. We will provide a further update in due course.”
