Sports.title: Hutchinson Targets Bivol-Smith Winner After Beating Buatsi
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson grabbed the vacant WBC light heavyweight title off Joshua Buatsi and went straight to calling out whoever wins between Dmitry Bivol and Callum Smith. Going for all the belts sounds great on the microphone, but the loose, free-wheeling style that worked against Buatsi will get him picked apart against either of those two.

Against Buatsi, Hutchinson relied on speed bursts, weird angles, and flipping between orthodox and southpaw to completely baffle a rigid, predictable opponent. Try that against Bivol, though, and it turns into a disaster. You cannot switch stances right in front of a technician like Bivol without squaring your feet up and losing balance. The second Hutchinson gives away his stance, Bivol will drill him down the middle with a straight right.

“We’ll go for undisputed, isn’t it? I want to beat the best, be the best, beat the best. And I’m one of the best now. Got one of the belts,” Hutchinson said after the fight.

Hutchinson likes the idea of the Bivol vs. Smith winner, but his biggest bad habit will be an open invitation for Bivol. Whenever Hutchinson throws his lead left hook, he leaves his chin in the air and pauses to admire his handiwork. Bivol thrives on that exact mistake. He takes a clean step back, makes the shot miss, and snaps back with a check-hook or a 1-2 before his opponent can even tuck their chin. Hutchinson cannot showboat his way out of trouble against a guy who controls the ring that well.

Smith presents a totally different kind of danger. Hutchinson loves throwing wide, flashy flurries, but Smith is deadliest when backed up to the ropes, waiting to uncork a short inside left hook. Trading hooks at mid-range with Smith is asking to get caught. To beat Smith, Hutchinson would have to abandon the circus act, use a stiff jab to keep range, target Smith’s tall body, and make Smith come forward so that counter hook stays locked away.

Then there is the Ben Whittaker option. Hutchinson shrugged and said he would take the fight, but it makes zero sense for his career right now.

Whittaker hates fighting on his back foot, and Hutchinson has the hand speed and awkward angles to give him nightmares. Still, both guys rely on athletic reflexes instead of solid defense. Taking on Whittaker is pure risk. If Hutchinson slips up, he blows his new WBC belt on a domestic scrap and waves goodbye to massive unification paydays in Saudi Arabia.

It ultimately comes down to boxing politics. If mandatory defenses or rematch clauses hold up the Bivol vs. Smith winner, Hutchinson will have to decide whether to stay busy with a simple defense or risk it all in a domestic clash.

Hutchinson finally has the belt he wanted. Keeping it means figuring out that the wild, erratic showmanship that worked on domestic rivals will get him dismantled against the elite at 175.

Sports.title: The Hold And Hit Trap That Wrecked Chris Billam-Smith
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke stopped Chris Billam Smith in the seventh round at London’s Copper Box Arena, crediting former heavyweight champion Wladimir Klitschko for the tactical blueprint that unraveled the former cruiserweight belt holder.

Asked about grabbing on to mess up Billam Smith’s timing, Clarke gave full credit to Klitschko’s old tactics.

“I learned that one from Klitschko. So, shout out Klitschko. That was a Klitschko special right there,” Clarke stated at the post-fight press conference.

The maneuver served as far more than basic stalling. Inside the ring, holding functions as an offensive exit strategy. A fighter stepping back after launching an attack enters counterpunching range. Smothering the reply by stepping forward eliminates that hazard, outsourcing the retreat to the referee.

That approach neutralized Billam Smith, who relies on sustained pocket combinations to do damage. Getting inside accomplished nothing when every entry resulted in wrapped arms. Each intervention by the referee forced Billam Smith to reset, handing Clarke another opportunity to score before initiating the next clinch.

Beyond killing the return fire, Clarke used his upper torso to press his full weight downward across Billam Smith’s neck. Forcing a fighter to carry dead weight round after round burns out their legs. By the middle rounds, Billam Smith was flat-footed, lacking the spring in his lower body required to absorb contact or dip away from incoming punches.

Clarke pushed the referee’s patience to the limit, later admitting he was warned about losing a point. A verbal warning means nothing to the fighter trapped in a headlock, though. Billam Smith needed to solve the problem himself instead of waiting on the official.

All that holding set the trap for the seventh round knockout. Clarke spent six rounds getting Billam Smith used to being grabbed after every punch. When Clarke stepped in during the seventh, Billam Smith dropped his hands to brace for another clinch. Clarke did not grab him this time. He ripped hard shots straight through the open guard, dropping Billam Smith twice before the referee stopped it at 1:24.

For the rematch, Billam Smith has to stop the clinch before Clarke gets both arms around him. He needs to fight for inside control, keeping one hand free to dig hard hooks into Clarke’s ribs. Timing an uppercut right when Clarke ducks forward would also make him think twice about diving in to grab. Once Clarke has both arms locked, trying to wrestle him off just burns energy without landing punches.

Billam Smith wants an immediate rematch, but running it back without fixing that flaw will lead to the exact same result. He has to hit Clarke on the way in before Clarke grabs him and forces the referee to step in.

Sports.title: Abraham Perez Drops Yankiel Rivera, Wins Unanimous Decision
Sports.content:
Abraham “Hammer” Perez scored a second-round knockdown and defeated Yankiel “El Doctorito” Rivera by unanimous decision over 12 rounds Saturday at Kiva Auditorium in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

Perez (16-0, 7 KOs) retained his IBF Intercontinental flyweight title by scores of 118-109, 118-109 and 120-107. Rivera (8-2-1, 4 KOs), a southpaw who represented Puerto Rico at the 2021 Olympics, had stretches of success, but the judges favored the hometown champion by wide margins.

A right hand to the nose dropped Rivera in the closing seconds of the second round. Referee Tony Weeks administered the count, and Rivera continued with blood coming from his nose.

Rivera fought his way back into the contest, opening a cut over Perez’s left eyebrow with a right hook in the final minute of the fourth. He then outlanded Perez in the fifth and sixth rounds before Perez rocked him with a right to the chin near the end of the seventh.

Perez landed a three-punch combination late in the ninth, while Rivera answered with a competitive tenth and outworked him in the eleventh. Both fighters had their moments during an active final round, although the scorecards showed Perez had built an insurmountable lead.

The DAZN card was promoted by Legacy Promotions, King’s Promotions and Salita Promotions.

IBF minimumweight champion Pedro Taduran (21-4-1, 14 KOs) retained his title with a unanimous decision over Brandon Moreno (16-1, 5 KOs). The judges returned widely differing scores of 120-106, 115-113 and 115-113 after 12 rounds.

In the light heavyweight co-feature, unbeaten southpaw Atif Oberlton (18-0, 14 KOs) defeated Dean Nicholson (23-2, 19 KOs) by split decision in a scrappy 10-round contest. Two judges scored it 98-92 for Oberlton, while the third favored Nicholson 96-94.

The taller Oberlton used his jab to establish an early advantage. Nicholson struggled to get inside and developed swelling around his left eye after catching an elbow in the seventh round.

Nicholson continued having difficulty closing the distance in the eighth and ninth, but found some success with looping right hands in the final round. Oberlton said afterward that he had injured his left arm.

Heavyweight Pryce Taylor (14-0, 8 KOs) claimed the NABF title with a split-decision victory over Tsotne Rogava (13-2, 8 KOs). Two judges scored the 10-round bout 96-94 for Taylor, while the third had Rogava ahead 97-93.

Rogava’s jab gave him the better of the opening three rounds before Taylor increased his work rate through the middle rounds. Both men slowed in the ninth, but Taylor produced a strong finish, staggering Rogava with a left hook midway through the tenth.

Albuquerque’s Jose Luis Sanchez (15-7-2, 4 KOs) defeated Josh Torres (31-8-2, 17 KOs) by unanimous decision over 10 rounds. Sanchez won by scores of 98-92, 99-91, and 99-91.

Unbeaten heavyweight southpaw Sardius Simmons (11-0, 6 KOs) earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Cesar Navarro (15-5, 13 KOs). The judges scored it 78-74, 77-75, and 77-75.

Navarro started aggressively, pinning Simmons in a corner during the opening round. Simmons worked his way into the fight and outlanded Navarro through much of the middle rounds. Navarro rallied in the seventh, but Simmons finished with a competitive eighth to secure the decision.

In a four-round super middleweight bout, debutant Parminder Pannu (1-0) defeated Peter Balderas Jr. (2-4, 2 KOs) on referee David Rios’ scorecard, 40-36.

Sports.title: Dana White’s Shakur Split Weakens His American Boxing Plan
Sports.content:
Dana White dismissed talk that Conor Benn’s reported purse triggered Zuffa Boxing’s sudden split with Shakur Stevenson. Yet the real damage is far more practical: Zuffa lost its premier American headliner before ever using him to anchor a broadcast or sell the rest of its roster to domestic fight fans.

During Saturday’s post-fight press conference in London, White revealed that he initiated the separation during a phone conversation with Stevenson’s team.

“We were on a call one day, and I said, ‘Maybe it’s better if we all just go our separate ways.’ And everybody agreed,” White said. “That just didn’t work out. You win some, you lose some.”

When asked if Stevenson pushed for parity after seeing Benn’s reported $15 million payday for the Regis Prograis bout, White shut it down immediately.

“That’s completely not true. Completely not true,” White said.

Asked what Stevenson actually demanded, White clamped down on specifics.

“That’s between us. That’s business behind the scenes. If you want to ask Shakur that question, ask him that. I’m not going to talk about it,” White said. “We all decided to go our own ways, and everybody’s happy with the decision.”

White’s comments shoot down the rumor mill while keeping the financial mechanics under wraps. Without figures on the table, it remains impossible to tell whether Stevenson overplayed his hand or if Zuffa attempted to impose an MMA-style pay structure that elite boxing champions routinely reject.

The structural fallout for Zuffa is unmistakable. In modern boxing promotion, an expensive main event star operates as an engine for the entire evening. Fans tune in for the proven name, creating a massive captive audience for developmental talent on the undercard. Without Stevenson delivering eyeballs, Zuffa cannot expose its lesser-known prospects to large-scale viewership. The company must now shoulder the expense of building interest in raw talent from scratch.

Stevenson also presented an awkward commercial equation for White’s promotional philosophy. White sells high-octane violence and ruthless aggression. Stevenson delivers surgical, defensive brilliance that purists appreciate but casual fans rarely rush to purchase. If Stevenson sought superstar guarantees without bringing explosive mass appeal, the balance sheet became an uphill battle.

Replacing that caliber of stateside talent presents an immediate hurdle. Reporters pressed White on established American draws like David Benavidez, Jaron Ennis, and Jesse Rodriguez, pointing out that nearly every top-tier domestic fighter is locked into commitments with rival outfits.

“We’re like eight or nine months into this thing. We’ll see how it all plays out,” White said.

Patience works in matchmaking, but broadcast partners look for immediate, dependable fixtures on the calendar. Television executives commit serious capital to showcase proven stars, not to finance protracted rebuilding phases. Walking away from Stevenson avoids an untenable contract, but it strips Zuffa of its flagship American asset before the company staged its first major domestic show.

Sports.title: Umar Dzambekov Punishes Zach Parker To Stay Unbeaten
Sports.content:
Umar Dzambekov brought Zach Parker’s comeback to a sudden halt, dropping the former British super middleweight champion with a ferocious left hook downstairs in round four at London’s Copper Box Arena. The undefeated southpaw spent the early minutes testing Parker up top before digging deep to close the show.

The fight ended at 1:47 of the fourth round during their scheduled ten-round light heavyweight clash on the Zuffa Boxing 12 undercard. Dzambekov (15-0, 11 KOs) drove a pinpoint shot right into Parker’s solar plexus. Parker collapsed, unable to beat referee Kieran McCann’s ten-count.

Parker (26-3, 18 KOs) stepped into the ring determined to rebound from a controversial majority-decision loss to Joshua Buatsi in November 2025. What he got instead was a brutal reminder of Dzambekov’s punch selection, suffering back-to-back defeats for the first time in his career.

Trouble surfaced just sixty seconds into round one. Dzambekov ripped a heavy left to the temple, visibly wobbling the 32-year-old Brit. Parker steadied himself, answering back with stiff straight rights to the ribs to keep the advancing puncher honest.

Still, landing punches never masked Parker’s defensive lapses. Dzambekov’s looping left kept sneaking past the guard, giving Parker fits as he tried to anticipate where the blows were coming from.

Momentum broke momentarily early in the fourth when Parker hit the canvas, but referee McCann correctly ruled it an accidental tangle of feet. Moments later, there was zero ambiguity. Dzambekov shifted levels, sinking that same lethal left hand square into the body. Parker went down in pure agony, completely out of time.

Changing levels proved to be the masterstroke. Dzambekov primed Parker to guard his jaw, only to explode into the midsection and end things instantly.

For the 28-year-old Russian, taking out a seasoned veteran in such quick fashion serves notice to the entire 175-pound division. Parker faces a tough road ahead after another crushing setback, while Dzambekov heads home with the most impressive scalp of his rising career.

At his age, Dzambekov does not have the luxury of spending another two years feasting on fringe operators and faded names. The clock is ticking, especially in a division as punishing as light heavyweight.

Putting away Parker in four rounds looks sharp on paper, but Parker was coming off a loss and never belonged among the elite at 175 anyway. If Dana White and Zuffa Boxing intend to run their own private ecosystem where house fighters pad records against in-house roster depth, Dzambekov will look like a wrecking ball forever without proving a thing.

The trouble comes if they harbor genuine ambitions of competing with the unified champions and top-tier sanctioning body contenders. You cannot groom a fighter on soft touches until he is 30 and then toss him into the deep end against world-class punchers expecting him to swim. The defensive habits Dzambekov gets away with against Parker—dropping hands, relying purely on head movement, leaving himself open when he loops that power hand—get exploited instantly against top-ten talent.

If Zuffa wants credit for building a legitimate world champion rather than just protecting an investment, they have to throw him into the fire right now. A genuine contender who fires back with venom would tell everyone immediately whether Dzambekov is the real deal or just another carefully managed project.

Sports.title: Elif Nur Turhan Defends Her IBF Title Against Alycia Baumgardner
Sports.content:
On Sunday night, November 8th, in the Most Valuable Promotions main event, the IBF lightweight world champion Elif Nur Turhan (14-0, 8 KOs) will defend her title against Alycia “The Bomb” Baumgardner (18-1, 7 KOs).

The champion is making a third title defense, while the challenger is making her debut at lightweight. The action is set to take place at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, with the event airing live on ESPN.

Back in December 2025, it was a battle of unbeatens, as Beatriz Ferreira defended her title against Elif Turhan. The challenger Turhan instantly put her power on display as she dropped Ferreira twice in the opening round.

At the midway point of the 5th round, Turhan stopped Ferreira when she landed a flurry of power shots. With the victory, the Turkey, Istanbul native Elif Turhan became a first-time world champion.

Turhan would go on to have two successful title defenses. Now the undefeated IBF world champion Elif Turhan is on the verge of taking the biggest test of her career when she faces a boxer who has had an incredible five-year run.

In November 2021, Alycia Baumgardner traveled to England, stopped Terri Harper in the 4th round, and won her first world title. Within a two-year span, Baumgardner collected all the belts.

After earning the undisputed super-featherweight crown, Alycia Baumgardner went on to successfully defend her titles on multiple occasions. Now her immediate goal is to become a two-division world champion.

Elif Turhan is a pressure fighter who has knockout power in both hands. Alycia Baumgardner is a boxer-puncher who is athletic, has excellent footwork, she’s sharp, and she has good timing.

This 10-round, three-minute-per-round fight features Baumgardner’s boxing skills versus Turhan’s punching power. The contrast in styles is the recipe for an action-packed bout.

If Baumgardner wins, she adds to her legacy, and if Turhan wins, she will have officially placed the other elite female boxers on notice. Airing live Sunday night on ESPN, the Turhan vs. Baumgardner clash is a fight you don’t want to miss.

Sports.title: Hutchinson Wins WBC Title, Rea Stops Taylor
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson defeated Joshua Buatsi by unanimous decision to win the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, building an early lead and surviving a late scare in their rematch at Manchester’s AO Arena.

The judges scored it 117-112, 115-113 and 115-113 for Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs), whose switching between orthodox and southpaw gave Buatsi problems throughout the DAZN main event promoted by Queensberry. Buatsi (20-2, 13 KOs) finished strongly but left himself too much ground to recover.

Hutchinson had the better of the opening six rounds, changing stance and landing enough to keep Buatsi chasing the fight. The Scottish fighter continued to hold a narrow edge through the tenth, putting the pressure on Buatsi to produce something decisive over the final two rounds.

Buatsi finally had Hutchinson in trouble during the last minute of the eleventh. It was the opening he needed, but Hutchinson survived the round and used the ring in the twelfth, working from southpaw and picking his moments to jab.

Buatsi pressed forward and may have taken the final round, but his late rally could not overturn Hutchinson’s earlier work. Referee Victor Loughlin oversaw the contest.

Jack Rafferty (28-0-1, 18 KOs) earned a narrow unanimous decision over Hovhannes Martirosyan (20-2, 12 KOs) in the co-feature, with a controversial final-round knockdown proving crucial on two scorecards.

Martirosyan’s greater activity gave him the edge through much of the opening eight rounds. Rafferty suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the tenth but fought back to take a close eleventh, leaving the contest heading toward a tense finish.

With blood running down his face, Rafferty caught Martirosyan with a right hand in the closing seconds of the twelfth. A push followed as Martirosyan went halfway through the ropes, but referee John Latham ruled a knockdown and administered a count as the bell sounded.

Two judges scored the fight 114-113 for Rafferty, while the third returned a wider 116-111 card. The knockdown supplied the winning margin on the two closer cards.

Gully Powar (14-1-1, 2 KOs) defeated Zack Miller (17-2, 3 KOs) by technical decision after their vacant British featherweight title fight was stopped at 1:32 of the tenth round.

Powar controlled the opening six rounds and continued to get the better of Miller, who developed swelling on his forehead following a clash of heads in the seventh. Referee Mark Lyson consulted the ringside doctor several times before the contest was halted and sent to the scorecards.

Bradley Rea (23-2, 12 KOs) delivered an emphatic finish against Ezra Taylor (13-2, 9 KOs), scoring two knockdowns to win the WBA Intercontinental light heavyweight title at 0:58 of the second round.

Rea dropped Taylor with a left hook to the chin, prompting a count from referee Michael Alexander. Taylor regained his feet, but Rea immediately attacked with a flurry that sent him down again and brought the stoppage.

Unbeaten middleweight Stephen Clarke (11-0, 2 KOs) controlled all eight rounds against Harley Collison (3-10-2). Referee Steve Gray scored the contest 80-72 for the Liverpool prospect.

Nineteen-year-old southpaw John Joe Carrigan (5-0, 5 KOs) maintained his perfect stoppage record, finishing Cheikh Diop (6-2, 4 KOs) at 1:50 of the fourth round of their scheduled six-round contest.

Javokhir Ummataliev (3-0, 1 KO) outlanded Atacayte Santana (4-4-2, 1 KO) throughout their six-round light heavyweight bout. Referee Mark Lyson awarded Ummataliev every round for a 60-54 victory.

Tumi Phillips (7-1, 1 KO) defeated Angelo Dragone (10-17-1, 1 KO) on points over four rounds. Dragone looked to hit and hold in the opener, but Phillips became more assertive in the second and third before an even final round. Lyson scored it 40-37.

Tony Yoka (16-3, 12 KOs) earned a six-round points victory over Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko (10-22-1, 7 KOs). The 2016 Olympic super heavyweight gold medalist outlanded Dovbyshchenko through the first five rounds before the Ukrainian increased his activity in the sixth. Gray scored it 59-55.

Alex Arthur Jr. (6-0, 1 KO) completed a comfortable six-round win over Jose Aguirre (2-32, 1 KO). The Edinburgh southpaw controlled the contest throughout, winning 60-54 on Gray’s card.

Sports.title: Cheavon Clarke Overwhelms Chris Billam-Smith In London
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke punished Chris Billam-Smith with cleaner punches before dropping him twice for a seventh-round TKO on Saturday at London’s Copper Box Arena. The finish came at 1:24, giving Clarke the biggest victory of his professional career and handing the former WBO cruiserweight champion his first stoppage defeat.

Clarke (13-2, 10 KOs) was ahead on our card entering the seventh, but Billam-Smith (22-3, 14 KOs) had just produced his strongest round. A well-timed right hand abruptly ended that recovery, sending Billam-Smith down for the first time as a professional. He beat the count, only for Clarke to attack again and force a second knockdown that brought the referee’s intervention.

The scheduled 10-round main event at Zuffa Boxing 12 carried personal history. Clarke had beaten Billam-Smith twice in the amateurs, including in the 2016 National Championships final. Billam-Smith wanted to settle that old score, but instead suffered a more damaging defeat against the same opponent.

Clarke’s accuracy was the difference from the opening round. The fight began with holding and short bursts of action, but he found the cleaner punches, including a right hand just before the bell. Billam-Smith improved in the second, closing the distance and landing heavier shots while absorbing another solid right.

That success did not become a sustained pattern. Clarke took control in the third with combinations, then edged a tighter fourth through two late right hands. Billam-Smith remained competitive, but his forward movement too often failed to produce enough clean offense.

The difficulty was getting close without paying for the journey. Billam-Smith needed to bring his hooks and body punches into range, yet Clarke repeatedly found him before he could establish that position. Following Clarke around left openings for counters and allowed the more accurate fighter to decide when to engage.

A heavy right in the fifth supplied another warning. Billam-Smith took it without visibly wilting and answered with effective punches late, but Clarke was still landing the more damaging shots. The former champion’s durability kept him competitive without solving the problems that were costing him rounds.

The sixth offered Billam-Smith a route back. He increased his output and connected with hooks to the head and body, finally making his close-range work more consistent. We had Clarke ahead 58-56 after six, with Billam-Smith having won the second and sixth rounds.

Then Clarke turned a points advantage into a decisive finish. His right hand in the seventh broke through with enough force to put Billam-Smith on the canvas. Once the former champion rose, Clarke gave him no opportunity to settle, following up until the second knockdown ended the contest.

Both fighters had entered after June stoppage victories, with Billam-Smith beating Ryan Rozicki and Clarke overcoming two knockdowns to stop Jack Massey. Those results suggested danger on both sides, but Clarke delivered the sharper work here.

For Billam-Smith, the defeat was more severe than another missed opportunity for amateur revenge. His pressure worked in spells, but Clarke’s timing prevented him from building on it. Clarke now has a stoppage victory over a former world champion, earned after controlling much of the fight rather than relying on one isolated punch.

Ghana News.title: T-bills auction: Government records 41% oversubscription; but yield on 91-day bill increases
Ghana News.content:
The government exceeded its treasury bills target by 41% to GH¢5.01 billion, according to the Bank of Ghana auction results.

This follows the government borrowing of about GH¢14 billion through short-term instruments in October 2026.

The bids accepted by the government were GH¢4.10 billion, higher than the targeted amount.

A little over GH¢3.0 billion of the bids came from the 91-day bill, representing 59% of the total bids. The uptake was about GH¢2.9 billion.

The 182-day bill also received bids of about GH¢1.6 billion. However, GH¢934.50 million was accepted.

About GH¢388 million of the bids were tendered for the 182-day bill. A little above GH¢243.15 million of the bids were accepted.

Meanwhile, interest rates were mixed along the yield curve.

The yield on the 91-day bill went up by 2.0 basis points to 4.56%.

However, the 182-day bill declined to 6.20% from the preceding week’s 6.26%.

Also, the yield on the 364-day bill decreased by 12.0 basis points to 9.48%.

Ghana News.title: GMA urges gov’t to intensify Ebola preparedness after detection of Bundibugyo strain in Nigeria
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Medical Association (GMA) has urged the government to intensify preparations against a possible Ebola outbreak following the reported detection of the Bundibugyo strain of the virus in neighbouring Nigeria.

The Association says Ghana must strengthen its disease surveillance and emergency response systems to prevent a potential outbreak and ensure that health facilities are adequately prepared to manage suspected cases.

Speaking at a press conference to mark the close of the GMA’s 68th Annual General Conference, the Association’s President, Professor Ernest Yorke, described the development in Nigeria as a serious public health concern and called for urgent preventive measures.

He warned that the spread of the Bundibugyo strain, which has been associated with high mortality, required Ghana to strengthen its preparedness rather than wait for an outbreak before taking action.

“The threats of Ebola virus disease, in particular the Bundibugyo strain, which has spread rapidly in Central and East Africa with very high mortality, are now imminent with the detection of the virus in our sister country, Nigeria,” he said.

Professor Yorke acknowledged the initial response by the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service, particularly efforts to educate health workers and the public and strengthen surveillance at the country's ports of entry.

However, he said that more comprehensive measures were needed to protect the country against the possibility of an outbreak.

The GMA is calling for intensified public education to ensure that citizens understand the risks associated with Ebola and the preventive measures required to limit its spread.

It has also urged the government to designate quarantine and isolation facilities, strengthen preparedness for the management of suspected and confirmed cases, and improve disease surveillance within communities.

The Association further wants the government to make advance financial provisions to support the country's response in the event of an outbreak.

According to Professor Yorke, adequate funding and preparedness are essential to ensuring that health authorities can respond quickly and effectively if cases are detected.

"The GMA calls for intensified public education, designation of quarantine and isolation sites, case management readiness, as well as strengthening surveillance within communities. We further call on the government to proactively set aside funds to finance the response to any possible outbreak," he said.

The GMA has also appealed to the public to observe proper hygiene practices and take precautions to reduce the risk of infection.

It has particularly encouraged regular handwashing with soap under running water and the use of alcohol-based hand sanitisers.

The Association also advised the public to avoid physical contact with people suspected or confirmed to have Ebola, dead bodies of infected persons, and objects that may have been contaminated.

It further urged people experiencing symptoms associated with the disease to seek immediate medical attention at the nearest public health facility.

The symptoms include high fever, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, general weakness, vomiting, and unexplained bleeding from any part of the body.

The GMA also called on members of the public to promptly alert health authorities if they notice anyone in their communities displaying similar symptoms.

Ghana News.title: GMA proposes dedicated emergency care fund; urges gov’t to explore NHIS, vehicle insurance contributions
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Medical Association (GMA) is demanding a dedicated and sustainable funding mechanism for emergency healthcare to ensure patients receive life-saving treatment without financial barriers.

The Association says hospitals must have an assurance of reimbursement for emergency services to prevent patients in critical condition from being denied or delayed treatment because of their inability to pay.

The proposal forms part of seven system-wide interventions outlined by the GMA to address persistent gaps in emergency healthcare delivery and tackle the 'No-Bed-Syndrome '.

General Secretary of the Association, Dr Richard Salomey, speaking to JoyNews at the end of the 68th Annual General Conference, said the government must identify a specific funding source to support the proposed arrangement.

He suggests that portions of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) could be repurposed for the fund, while a percentage of private vehicle insurance premiums could also be allocated towards financing emergency treatment.

Dr Salomey says the arrangement would guarantee hospitals payment for services provided while removing the financial burden from patients requiring urgent medical attention.

“Patients who require emergency care must receive the necessary treatment, with hospitals assured that the fund will reimburse them. This will ensure that patients are not burdened with financial barriers when seeking emergency care,” he explained.

The GMA says it is open to contributing to discussions on the proposed financing arrangements, leaving the government to determine the most appropriate mechanism.

The Association believes dedicated funding will strengthen emergency healthcare delivery by ensuring that financial constraints do not prevent patients from accessing timely and appropriate treatment.

Ghana News.title: New DVLA office in Ada to ease vehicle registration, improve road safety
Ghana News.content:
The Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) has commissioned a new office at Kasseh in the Ada East District of the Greater Accra Region to bring vehicle registration and licensing services closer to residents.

The facility is expected to reduce the challenges residents face in travelling outside the district to access services such as vehicle registration, licence renewals and roadworthiness inspections.

The commissioning ceremony also provided an opportunity for the Authority to educate stakeholders on its proposed Radio Frequency Identification (RFID)-enabled smart number plates, designed to strengthen vehicle identification and address the growing problem of registration plate duplication.

Kwesi Bona Otuo-Srebour, Acting Director of Vehicle Inspection and Registration at the DVLA, said the current vehicle registration system had vulnerabilities that made it susceptible to the cloning of registration plates.

He said the introduction of RFID-enabled number plates would improve vehicle identification, enhance security, and make it more difficult for criminals to duplicate registration numbers.

“The new plates incorporate electronic identification technology that allows vehicle registration information to be verified digitally, supporting efforts to detect counterfeit plates and improve the tracking of vehicles,” he explained.

Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the DVLA in charge of Services, Foster Akwasi Asante, said the establishment of the office formed part of the Authority's efforts to decentralise its operations and improve access to services.

“The stress and the traffic discourage motor and vehicle drivers from registering,” he said, adding that the new office would provide services including vehicle registration, licence renewals and roadworthiness inspections, among other services, to residents of Ada and surrounding communities.

He explained that the proposed identification system would link vehicle registration data directly to registered owners and allow ownership records to be updated whenever vehicles changed hands.

Mr Asante added that the system would include mechanisms for detecting cloned registration plates, while the Authority also planned to introduce an electronic learning platform to refresh drivers' knowledge of road signs, traffic regulations and other road safety requirements.

Mr Mordzifa Tanihu Jerry John Foreigner Mills-Nkrumah, District Chief Executive for Ada West, welcomed the establishment of the office, describing it as a significant development that would make DVLA services more accessible to residents of the two Ada districts.

Kenneth Kabu Kofi Kanor, District Chief Executive for Ada East, said the project was made possible through the efforts of the area's Member of Parliament and assured the Authority of the Assembly's support to ensure the smooth operation of the facility.

Madam Comfort Doyoe Cudjoe-Ghansah, Member of Parliament for Ada, pledged to support the enrolment and renewal of licences for 100 drivers under the new system and the registration of 100 commercial motorcycle operators, popularly known as okada riders.

She also appealed to the DVLA to prioritise the recruitment of qualified residents of the area to create employment opportunities for the local population.

Ghana News.title: Mahama targets $9bn investment to drive economic transformation by 2030
Ghana News.content:
President John Mahama says his government plans to invest $9 billion in Ghana’s economy between 2027 and 2030 as part of efforts to transform the country’s economic fortunes.

He said the investment would be channelled into initiatives aimed at driving economic transformation over the four-year period.

"Next week, the Minister of Finance will present on my behalf the 2027 budget. In this presentation, we will outline our plan on what we call the new economy. This is a bold initiative that will seek to invest over nine billion dollars ($9b) in sectors of the economy between 2027 and 20230," the president said.

President Mahama announced the plan at the 2026 Hogbetsotso Festival in Anloga in the Volta Region on Saturday, November 7.

The announcement comes ahead of the presentation of the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy by Finance Minister Cassiel Ato Forson next week.

The proposed investment is expected to outline the government’s economic priorities and development agenda, especially job creation for the period, the president noted in his address at the durbar.

Ghana News.title: GMA calls for nationwide expansion of electronic bed management system to end ‘No Bed Syndrome’
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Medical Association (GMA) has called for reforms to Ghana’s emergency healthcare system, including the nationwide expansion of the electronic hospital bed management system, to address the persistent problem of patients being turned away from hospitals because of a lack of available beds.

The Association says the current pilot of the electronic bed management system must be extended to all health facilities, supported by dedicated hospital bed management teams with the authority to coordinate patient transfers and ensure the efficient use of available beds.

It also wants the government to introduce a sustainable financing arrangement for emergency healthcare, expand hospital bed capacity, strengthen ambulance services, and equip district hospitals to improve access to timely emergency medical care.

Speaking at a press conference marking the close of its 68th Annual General Conference, GMA President, Professor Ernest Yorke, acknowledged efforts by the Ministry of Health to address the No Bed Syndrome but insisted that isolated interventions would not provide a lasting solution.

He said Ghana needed a coordinated emergency healthcare system that ensured patients could access medical attention, receive initial treatment and be transferred to appropriate health facilities without financial barriers.

“While the GMA acknowledges some commendable efforts by the Ministry of Health to mitigate the No Bed Syndrome, there's a need to move from fragmented interventions to a coordinated reform that directs every medical patient: how care is accessed, stabilised and transferred appropriately without any financial barriers,” he said.

To address the challenges confronting emergency healthcare delivery, Professor Yorke outlined seven major interventions the Association believes are necessary to establish an effective emergency response system.

The first is the expansion of the ongoing national electronic hospital bed management system, with the establishment of hospital bed management teams that have clearly defined responsibilities and the authority to coordinate patient movement.

The Association also wants all health facilities to expand their bed capacity and introduce spillover arrangements to accommodate patients when existing facilities reach capacity.

It further called for the implementation of multidisciplinary, hospital-wide patient flow strategies to ensure that patients are directed to the appropriate departments and facilities without unnecessary delays.

On financing, the GMA proposed a dedicated and sustainable funding mechanism for emergency care to guarantee that patients receive the full range of services they need, including ambulance transfers, regardless of their financial circumstances.

The Association also wants the government to strengthen pre-hospital and emergency care services, particularly ambulance operations, while improving the training of emergency medical technicians.

Other recommendations include providing district and other hospitals with essential emergency equipment and diagnostic facilities, as well as investing in continuous training and orientation for healthcare workers.

Professor Yorke said that staff attitudes must also be addressed through fair accountability measures, particularly in cases involving poor treatment of patients.

Beyond the challenges facing emergency healthcare, the Association has urged the government to strengthen Ghana’s preparedness against Ebola virus disease following the detection of the Bundibugyo strain in neighbouring Nigeria.

Professor Yorke warned that the development posed a serious public health concern and required Ghana to intensify its surveillance and emergency response measures.

He commended the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service for their initial efforts to sensitise health workers and the public, as well as strengthen surveillance at the country's points of entry.

However, he said more needed to be done to prepare the country for a possible outbreak.

“The threats of Ebola virus disease, in particular the Bundibugyo strain, which has spread rapidly in Central and East Africa with very high mortality, is now imminent with the detection of the virus in our sister country, Nigeria,” he said.

The GMA is calling for intensified public education, the designation of quarantine and isolation facilities, improved case management preparedness and stronger disease surveillance within communities.

It has also urged the government to proactively allocate funds to support the country's response in the event of an outbreak, warning against waiting until cases are detected before mobilising resources.

The Association has also advised the public to maintain good personal hygiene and adopt preventive measures to reduce the risk of infection.

These include regular handwashing with soap under running water, using alcohol-based hand sanitisers and avoiding physical contact with infected persons, dead bodies and potentially contaminated objects.

The GMA further urged people experiencing symptoms associated with Ebola to seek immediate medical attention at the nearest public health facility.

The symptoms include high fever, headache, muscle pain, sore throat, general weakness, vomiting, and unexplained bleeding from any part of the body.

It also encouraged the public to promptly alert health authorities about anyone in their communities displaying similar symptoms to ensure early assessment and an appropriate public health response.

Ghana News.title: You should probably be eating more whole grains. Here’s what to do
Ghana News.content:
The secret is out: Eating whole grains is good for you.

Extensive research in the past two decades has shown that a diet rich in whole grains is associated with lower risks of heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and type 2 diabetes, and helps people maintain a healthy weight.

In a new analysis, researchers reviewed dozens of studies to drill down on how whole grains contribute to cardiovascular and metabolic health at a molecular level — and how much you have to eat to make a difference.

The results, published Tuesday in the European Heart Journal, suggest that the benefits start at about 90 grams, or three servings, per day — about as much as you’d get from two slices of whole wheat bread and a bowl of oatmeal. Eating four to six servings per day is even more powerful, according to the study.

The researchers found evidence that people who ate three to six servings of whole grains for a prescribed period of time — as little as two weeks and up to two years — had slightly improved levels of about a dozen markers of health, including total cholesterol, LDL (low-density lipoprotein or “bad”) cholesterol, blood pressure, body weight and waist circumference, all of which are associated with a greater risk of cardiovascular disease. Though the effects were small, taken together, the findings back up what large population studies have found, said Dagfinn Aune, a coauthor on the meta-analysis.

Therefore, there is “likely a causal effect” from eating whole grains, and “this may translate into a reduced risk of cardiovascular disease,” Aune, a research fellow in the department of epidemiology and biostatistics at the Imperial College London’s School of Public Health, concluded.

But that doesn’t mean you can add two pieces of whole wheat toast to your morning bacon and eggs and expect to improve your heart health.

Taking results with a (whole) grain of salt

Doctors recommend choosing whole grains over products made with refined grains for heart health.

Whole grain foods — such as oatmeal, brown rice, whole wheat bread, farro, popcorn and quinoa — include all the parts of a grain as it exists in nature. Refined grains (think white rice and anything made with white flour) are processed to remove the less palatable parts, which are also where most of the fiber and other nutrients are found.

Eating whole grain food is important, but a single dietary swap is not going to prevent heart disease, Alice Lichtenstein, a professor at the Friedman School of Nutrition Science and Policy at Tufts University in Medford, Massachusetts, told CNN.

“If you eat a cinnamon bun made of whole grain, as opposed to a cinnamon bun made with refined grain, I’m not sure you’re going to see a benefit,” said Lichtenstein, who was not involved in the new meta-analysis.

And just adding more carbs to your diet to achieve a whole grain target could lead to weight gain, she added.

Up your whole grain IQ

Most people in the United States don’t eat the two to four servings of whole grains a day suggested in the federal government’s latest Dietary Guidelines for Americans. A serving could be a single slice of whole wheat bread, or half a cup of cooked oats, brown rice or quinoa.

The American Heart Association recommends eating foods made with whole grains, but it doesn’t specify a target amount to aim for each day. That’s because there’s no one amount that’s clearly most effective or that is right for every person’s body, genetics and lifestyle, said Lichtenstein, who was lead author of the nonprofit’s dietary guidelines published in March. Rather than nail down a magic-bullet number of any particular good-for-you food, “we’re trying to keep the focus on the dietary pattern.”

In addition to whole grains, the guidelines emphasize eating a variety of vegetables and fruits and limiting saturated fat, added sugar and salt, ultraprocessed foods and alcohol.

If it helps to have a goal in mind, replacing three servings of refined grains with whole grains every day could be a good place to start.

“My suggestion is as items run out in the pantry, replace them with whole grain versions,” Lichtenstein said.

That’s not always as easy as it sounds, she warned. Dark brown breads and products labeled as “multigrain” or “made with whole grain” may be predominantly made up of refined flour.

“Turn the package over and look at the ingredient list,” she said. “The first ingredient should be a whole grain.” If it’s not, she advised, leave it on the shelf.

Ghana News.title: GJA Awards: Afenyo-Markin calls for repeal of two laws restricting free expression
Ghana News.content:
Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has called for the repeal of Section 208 of the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), and Section 76 of the Electronic Communications Act, 2008 (Act 775), saying that the provisions are being used to criminalise free expression and suppress dissent.

Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards held at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, November 7, Mr Afenyo-Markin said the two laws had no place in Ghana's democracy, insisting that citizens and journalists should not face criminal prosecution for expressing opinions, criticising public officials or publishing information.

He acknowledged that freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly but maintained that criminal prosecution should not be the default response to false publications, criticism or disagreements.

“Let me be clear, our purpose as a Minority is not to defend irresponsible speech. We do not defend lies. We do not defend hate speech. We do not defend incitement. We do not defend reckless publications that destroy reputations, endanger lives or undermine public peace. Freedom of expression is not a licence for irresponsibility,” he said.

The Minority Leader said that cases involving defamation, libel and false publications could be addressed through civil remedies, including court proceedings, retractions, apologies and compensation, rather than criminal prosecution.

He warned that resorting to criminal law to punish disagreements, political commentary, criticism or honest mistakes could create fear and discourage citizens and journalists from freely expressing their views.

Referencing former President John Agyekum Kufuor's position on media freedom, Mr Afenyo-Markin reiterated the need for responsible expression within established rules of engagement.

He further argued that addressing misinformation and irresponsible speech required a stronger emphasis on truth, factual reporting, ethical journalism and public education, with civil remedies applied where necessary.

“The answer to bad speech must not always be the criminal law. The answer to falsehood must be truth. The answer to propaganda must be fact. The answer to hate must be ethical journalism, public education and, where necessary, civil remedies. The answer must never be a return to the politics of fear,” he said.

Mr Afenyo-Markin also cautioned against the use of strategic lawsuits to intimidate journalists and ordinary citizens, warning that influential individuals should not exploit costly and burdensome legal processes to silence critical voices.

“We will not accept a system in which the powerful use burdensome lawsuits not to protect their reputation, but to bankrupt journalists, exhaust editors and frighten citizens into silence. Justice must never become an instrument of intimidation,” he added.

Section 208 of the Criminal Offences Act criminalises the publication or reproduction of false statements, rumours or reports likely to cause fear and alarm or disturb public peace, where the publisher knows or has reason to believe that the information is false.

Section 76 of the Electronic Communications Act, 2008, addresses the knowing transmission of false or misleading electronic communications likely to prejudice life-saving services or endanger safety.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final to Claire Liu in straight sets
World.content:
Philippine’ tennis star Eala was left stunned after a 6-3, 6-0 loss to the 102-ranked American in Hong Kong.

Share Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final in search for second WTA title on social media

Tennis trailblazer Alex Eala from the Philippines burst into tears as she reflected on a “life-changing” season after falling agonisingly short of a second WTA Tour title in Hong Kong.

The second seed was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Claire Liu in the final of the Hong Kong Open as the American, ranked 102nd, won her first tour title on Sunday.

Eala is at a career-high 17 in the world after a breakout year in which the 21-year-old clinched her maiden title, in Washington, DC, in August.

That victory made her the first player from the Philippines to win a tournament on the WTA Tour.

Eala, set to rise to world number 15 next week, started the year ranked 50th.

“This season has changed my life; it’s changed my life for the better,” Eala, who finished the final with heavy strapping on her right leg, told the crowd afterwards.

Becoming emotional as she addressed her team in the stands, she said: “I’m incredibly proud of the work we’ve put in this year.

“We’re the only ones that truly know what it took to arrive to this point in our journey.

“This is only the beginning.”

World.title: US task force to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know
World.content:
Share US aims to cut off Iran’s transport of advanced weapons: What we know on social media

As the threat of renewed war grows, Washington is expanding efforts to choke Tehran’s military supply networks, including through Task Force Iron Gate – a unit targeting land routes and the Caspian Sea.

With it, the US military ⁠⁠⁠⁠is trying to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials, the United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announced on Saturday.

The same day, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced ambitious plans for underground complexes capable of sustaining missile and drone production under bombardment. That announcement came amid reports of ongoing construction near Iranian missile bases, based on satellite imagery and previous claims by Tehran that US strikes failed to destroy its underground facilities.

Here’s what we know about the US task force:

What is the purpose of the task force?

Task Force Iron Gate will aim to find out where “weapons systems are coming in, how they could potentially be cut off” and how “Iran is transporting its energy”, Michael Mulroy, a former US deputy assistant defence secretary for the Middle East, told Al Jazeera.

It expands on the US blockade of Iranian ports to cover Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea and will reportedly be run by 20 civilian and military personnel.

Iran shares borders with seven countries – Afghanistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Pakistan Turkiye and Turkmenistan.

Based in Tampa, Florida, the unit will coordinate with other US government agencies “on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illegal revenue streams across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea”, CENTCOM said. Task Force Iron Gate will reinforce “the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea”, CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said.



If US President Donald Trump ramps up the war, there will likely be attacks on this “series of targets”, said Mulroy.

“Unlike Operation Epic Fury, which primarily (focused) on military targets, I think these targets will be focused on economic and infrastructure targets, as part of this comprehensive plan to cut the regime off from its ability to fight and ability to fund itself,” Mulroy said. “It’s primarily a coordination body that’s looking for how the US can increase its economic strangulation strategy by going after the ground routes as they’ve already covered a majority of the maritime routes.”

How has Iran responded to CENTCOM’s announcement?

The IRGC dismissed the US military plan as “just a play on words”.

“The Americans cannot achieve their goal through this, which is to apply severe economic pressure to collapse and disintegrate the Iranian economy,” said IRGC spokesman Sardar Mohebi, as reported by the Fars news agency.

Washington previously “claimed that Iran will suffer an economic collapse within two weeks, but we witnessed that this did not happen”, he added.

Is the task force a response to reports of Russia-Iran weapons ties?

While CENTCOM’s announcement did not explicitly identify Iran’s weapons trade with Russia, analysts say the unit could be seen as an attempt to disrupt supply networks that include Russian connections.

US media have reported that Russia has sent drone components and explosives to Iran via the Caspian Sea. There are also claims that Russian technology could be helping Iran develop advanced supersonic cruise missiles.

Mahjoob Zweiri, a professor of contemporary history and politics at Qatar University, told Al Jazeera that reports of military equipment imported via Russia are a “real concern” for the United States.

The task force therefore could “cause a confrontation with Russia”, he said.

Rami Khouri, a public policy fellow at the American University of Beirut and a non-resident senior fellow at the Arab Center in Washington, said of the new unit: “The US really doesn’t quite know what to do about Iran as we’ve seen, and it’s doing things off the cuff” – a strategy that has led to little success.

Can the US really choke off Iran’s supply lines?

Khouri pointed to Iran’s history as a trading nation for thousands of years as evidence that the US mission is near impossible.

“There’s an enormous web of contacts that Iran has had for thousands of years with traders and partners and allies all over the region, especially in Asia – it’s virtually impossible for the US to seal off every one,” he said.



While the US can impose a blockade or sanctions on Iran, it cannot control the behaviour of everyone from the Russians, to the Chinese, to the Emiratis and beyond, said the analyst.

“There are people all over the region who have links with Iran, some very close, some just commercial,” he said.

A lot of the materials that go into Iran’s weapons systems are bought from some other countries, – some even from the US or Europeans – and then they are channelled through companies in Asia, Khouri added.

Could this change the course of the war?

Former Trump aide and top counterterrorism official Joe Kent, who resigned in March due to the US’s war on Iran, said the new task force is an attempt by CENTCOM to subvert ongoing diplomatic efforts.

“This is CENTCOM inviting Iran to escalate while the vice president is attempting to negotiate with the Iranians,” Kent posted on X. “This is, as CENTCOM calls it, ‘policy by CONOP’, when the military finds a way to subvert the White House without blatantly disobeying the President, by taking actions that will ensure a war escalates or perpetuates.”

According to The Wall Street Journal, CENTCOM chief Cooper is among the many officials, alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, pressing Trump to renew attacks on Iran.

The task force may also just be symbolic because the US has no military presence on the Caspian Sea, said Zweiri.

“America has no access to the sea, unless some of the neighbouring countries like Azerbaijan or Armenia or others collaborate [with them] … And they’re not collaborating on this because they don’t want to upset Russia,” he said. “It will require … troops on the ground, and this is unlikely to happen.”

Zweiri also said that the Caspian Sea’s contribution to Iran’s economy is just 11 percent, so the task force’s actions won’t have much negative impact on Tehran.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify this figure but the Caspian Sea accounts for only a fraction of Iran’s overall maritime trade, according to the Soufan Center based in New York City.
