World.title: At least 21 dead as small boat sinks off Senegal
World.content:
Senegalese Interior Ministry says one person rescued as search operation continues after migrant vessel capsized.

Share At least 21 dead as small boat sinks off Senegal on social media

A small boat carrying migrants and refugees has sunk off northwestern Senegal, killing at least 21 people.

The Senegalese Interior Ministry said in a statement on Sunday that one person had been rescued in addition to the 21 bodies recovered.

The ministry said the death toll was “provisional” as of late Saturday, adding that the search was still ongoing and the families of the victims were being helped.

Media reports said the pirogue-type flat-bottomed boat capsized on Saturday off the Loumpoul dunes in the Kebemer department, between Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis.

Le Soleil newspaper said that most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.

Thousands ⁠of people have ⁠died in recent years attempting to reach Spain’s Canary Islands from West Africa, including ‌635 in the first five months of this year, according to ‌migrant rights ‌group Walking Borders

Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro declared an emergency on Saturday after a surge in migrant boat arrivals. Since the start of November, El Hierro authorities said more than 3,300 people had arrived aboard around 30 boats.

World.title: Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya
World.content:
Former rivals in Libya are pushing for a unity government to end years of conflict.

Share Egypt’s reopening of its embassy in Tripoli signals regional shift on Libya on social media

The reopening of the Egyptian embassy in Tripoli marks a fundamental political shift, both domestically and regionally, for Libya, analysts say.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty inaugurated the historic embassy building on Saturday, which had been closed for 12 years due to security concerns.

Libya has been politically divided since the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, with rival administrations formed in Tripoli in the west and Tobruk and Benghazi in the east.

Egypt was widely considered to be backing the eastern authority, effectively led by strongman and renegade military commander Khalifa Haftar, and his self-styled Libyan National Army (LNA), until recent regional developments led Cairo to rethink its approach.

Libyan political analyst Hazem al-Rayes said the reopening of the embassy in Tripoli – which was the seat of the internationally recognised government that Haftar was fighting – is a sign of this.

“I can consider that what Egypt is doing in its recent moves towards the capital, Tripoli, is an attempt to readjust its behaviour in the Libyan file … [for] five years, no Egyptian foreign minister visited the capital,” he told Al Jazeera.

Elias al-Barouni, a political science professor at Libya’s Nalut University, also believes the move goes beyond the resumption of regular consular services in Tripoli.

“We are facing an indicator of a shift in Cairo’s method of managing its relations with the Libyan parties, and a rearrangement of its priorities in dealing with the Libyan crisis,” al-Barouni told Al Jazeera.

There have been several significant political and regional shifts that have somewhat stabilised the volatile situation in Libya, where thousands have been killed in fighting between militias attached to rival political authorities.



In July 2026, Ankara and the LNA reached unprecedented coordination, spearheading agreements to develop military facilities, advanced surveillance systems, and training programmes in Turkiye for eastern Libyan officers.

The deputy commander of eastern Libyan forces and Haftar’s son, Saddam Haftar, has also paid visits to regional capitals, including Turkiye and Qatar, which have supported the United Nations-recognised Government of National Accord (GNA) in Tripoli.

In Libya, rivals recently signed the so-called “4+4 agreement” that sets out a roadmap for possible presidential and legislative elections over the next two years.

Badr Hassan al-Shafei, a professor of African studies and conflict resolution at Cairo University, told Al Jazeera that Egypt came to revisit its policy towards Libya after realising that its reliance on eastern forces, led by Haftar, was not conducive to its overall strategic interests.

“It is clear that Cairo … found that relying on one party or leaning towards one party in Libya, which is Haftar’s party, may not be the right bet perhaps at the present time or even for a while, since the Turkish intervention several years ago,” al-Shafei told Al Jazeera.

“Consequently, perhaps Egypt wants to create a balance or also send a message to Haftar that he should not act unilaterally and that acting should be in coordination with Cairo, so it worked to extend bridges of cooperation with Libya also …”

Egypt has also become more concerned about developments to the south of its border, particularly the expansion of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan, which had allegedly received support from Haftar.

“Today, Egypt is no longer the Egypt of five years ago when its policies and relations were limited only to the [eastern] authorities in Benghazi,” al-Rayes told Al Jazeera.

It is “convinced today that its ally [LNA], which it supported throughout the past years at the expense of the legitimate government in Tripoli … has distanced itself from it today, and it needs to readjust its political behaviour with Tripoli and with the legitimate government”, he said.

Maritime border disputes

During Abdelatty’s visit to Tripoli, he discussed critical economic files with Libyan officials, including the 2019 maritime border memorandum of understanding signed between Tripoli and Ankara.

According to the Facebook page of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Abdelatty reaffirmed the importance of addressing Egyptian concerns regarding maritime demarcation between Libya and Turkiye in light of international law. The eastern parliament recently ratified the maritime agreement, which it initially opposed.



“Consequently, perhaps Cairo is trying to prevent the ratification of this agreement from causing damage to its interests in gas and oil exploration in the Eastern Mediterranean, and from that it wanted to extend bridges to Tripoli as well,” al-Shafei said.

“Instead of limiting itself to political and diplomatic objection from outside Tripoli, Cairo has become negotiating directly with the Libyan government that signed the agreement.”

Egypt might also be attracted to opportunities that reconstruction and the revival of Libya’s oil industry might bring.

“Perhaps with the reconstruction process, the incoming Egyptian labour will have priority, or even the currently present one will have its living conditions improved, not to mention the idea of the possibility of Egyptian investments and companies entering the reconstruction process,” al-Shafei said.

Push for settlement

After years of backing rival sides, a new regional consensus means there is a greater likelihood of rivals in Libya reaching a comprehensive agreement to end the war, al-Rayes told Al Jazeera.

But al-Barouni cautioned that there is still a plethora of issues facing Libya, and only a comprehensive solution can end the divisions within Libya.

“The Libyan problem is not merely a dispute over the name of the head of government, but rather it is a dispute over the nature of power, the distribution of influence, control over institutions and resources, the future of the military institution, and the conditions for reaching elections,” al-Barouni said.

“If Cairo, Ankara, Washington, and other capitals agree on the necessity of ending the division, that is a development that can be built upon, but the success of any settlement remains linked to the ability of the Libyans to formulate an independent national project. Libya needs a settlement that ends the division, not a deal that redistributes the division.”

World.title: CCTV captures streets shaking as 5.7-magnitude earthquake hits Japan
World.content:
NewsFeed CCTV captures streets shaking as 5.7-magnitude earthquake hits Japan

A 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan, injuring more than 20 people. Surveillance video captured streets and apartments shaking, causing windows to break and trains at Nagoya Station to be delayed.

World.title: Could Iraq’s Kurdish region return to two separate administrations?
World.content:
A political impasse between the KRG and PUK threatens to break up the semiautonomous northern region into zones of governance.

Disagreements between the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) over the formation of a new government have led to the threat of two rival administrations emerging in the Kurdish region of northern Iraq, analysts say.

The dispute between the two dominant political forces in the semiautonomous Kurdistan Regional Government, which traditionally has operated under a power-sharing agreement, escalated after a parliamentary session was held last week in Erbil without the PUK’s participation.

PUK leader Bafel Talabani responded by withdrawing his party from the government, and a threat is growing that a rival administration could be formed in the party’s Sulaimaniyah base.

Independent Kurdish politician Yasin Aziz said the latest developments have deepened the historical divisions between the KDP and PUK.

“I believe the spectre of two administrations in Kurdistan is now very close, and the outlines of such a scenario are becoming clear. … The events have been painful and rapid. The differences between the two parties were significant and have now led to a breakdown in relations,” Aziz told Al Jazeera.

“There had been hopes that the two sides would reach an agreement, but activating parliament without the PUK deepened the divisions between the KDP and PUK.”

The KDP, which is led by Massoud Barzani, is the biggest party in the region, and its strongholds are in Erbil and Dohuk.

Two powers

Since the first Gulf War in 1990 and 1991 and the establishment of a US-led “no-fly zone” in northern Iraq, Iraq’s Kurds have largely governed themselves, separate from the national government in Baghdad.



The Iraqi Constitution enacted after the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq recognised the northern Kurdish region as a federal entity with its own legislative, executive and judicial powers.

There is a historical precedent for the possible separation of powers in this region between two rival authorities. When a conflict erupted between elements of the KDP and PUK in the 1990s, the two parties formed separate local governments in Erbil and Sulaimaniyah, respectively.

While there have been no recent violent flare-ups between the two parties, political distrust remains deep.

During the sixth parliamentary elections in the region on October 20, 2024, the KDP won 39 seats and the PUK 23. This left a 16-seat gap between the two parties.

But the KDP’s ability to form a new government was still dependent on reaching an agreement with the PUK and other parties, such as the New Generation Movement, which secured 15 seats in the last election.

The PUK has so far refused to collaborate, so after a two-year wait, the KDP reactivated the regional parliament on Wednesday without its rivals.

Divisions but no conflict

Although the rivalry between the two parties is longstanding, Aziz argued that the current crisis is more serious and deeply rooted than previous political disputes.

“Given the political stubbornness of both parties, I do not expect an agreement or understanding to be reached soon,” he said. “Both sides must make concessions to each other. The party willing to make greater concessions will demonstrate greater concern for the Kurdistan region.”

Aziz was clear in laying blame for the deepening divide.

“The responsibility for deepening this conflict lies with the leaderships of Kurdistan’s two main parties,” he said. “Their failure to recognise the risks posed by continuing these disputes is one of the reasons we have reached this point.”

Subhi Mandalawi, a member of the KDP, blamed the current impasse on the refusal of the PUK to form a new government with the KDP.

“Following the Kurdistan parliamentary elections, the PUK delayed the formation of the new government. They were counting on the KDP being unable to secure the legal quorum needed to convene a parliamentary session,” Mandalawi told Al Jazeera. “But we held a parliamentary session without the PUK in 2018 as well, and they subsequently joined the government and parliament.”

Mandalawi insisted that the door remains open for the PUK and other political parties but warned that prolonged divisions would lead to deeper problems for the Kurdish region.



“Continuing to obstruct legislative institutions two years after the elections is unacceptable and harms the Kurdistan region domestically, regionally and internationally,” he said.

“Threatening to divide the Kurdistan region is a hasty, ill-considered and unrealistic decision. No party leader can take such a step, and the PUK would be the biggest loser if it went ahead with it.”

Despite the differences, there is little risk of a return to conflict between the two parties. “We are brothers, and there can be no fighting among us,” Mandalawi said.

Separation threats

Mahmood Khoshnaw, a senior PUK official, said the KDP’s decision to convene parliament without his party has worsened political tensions in the region.

“Activating parliament without the PUK represents a departure from the principle of partnership and from political realities, and there will be consequences. If a prime minister is appointed in Erbil, we will take the same step in Sulaimaniyah. Whatever the KDP does, we will do the same in Sulaimaniyah,” Khoshnaw warned.

“The situation in the Kurdistan region is heading towards chaos unless the crisis is addressed rationally and realistically. Activating parliament without reaching an understanding with the PUK has had a negative impact on relations between the two parties.”

Despite this, there are questions about whether Sulaimaniyah could legally separate from the Kurdish regional government.

Ramadan Albadran, an independent political analyst and constitutional affairs expert, said the dispute is not a constitutional issue about the KDP’s convening of parliament but a deep political crisis with the potential to create security repercussions for the region.

The Iraqi constitution also provides no mechanism for dividing the region into zones of influence between the KDP and PUK.

“If the PUK moves to separate Sulaimaniyah from the Kurdistan region, that would not be a legal or constitutional act,” Albadran said.

“If it takes place without a mandate from the elected Kurdistan Regional Government, it would be closer to an act of rebellion since there is no legal provision permitting withdrawal from or the dismantling of a region in this manner.”

World.title: Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe
World.content:
‘Terrorism’ investigation launched after government officials say suspect likely influenced by far-right ideology.

Share Poland mourns six killed in attack as authorities launch ‘terrorism’ probe on social media

Poland has begun two days of national mourning after an armed man killed six people in central Krakow, as the national prosecutor’s office opened a “terrorism” investigation.

The 24-year-old Polish suspect opened fire on Saturday in the heart of Krakow’s historic city centre. A British national was among those killed, according to police, and nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia were among the 15 wounded, authorities told the PAP news agency.

Three more bodies were later found at the suspect’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, about 150km (93 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.

The suspect was also wounded during police action and is in critical condition in hospital.

Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said on social media on Sunday it had “launched an investigation today into yesterday’s attack in Krakow”, adding it was probing “the killing of six people … using a firearm, and the attempted murder of many others, including police officers, this act constituting a terrorist offence”.

Daniel Prokopowicz, a spokesperson for the office, said it was “highly likely” that the killings in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski and Krakow were carried out by the same person, but that investigations were ongoing.

According to media reports, the suspect, Michal O, had a valid gun licence and no prior criminal record.

Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski stated the attacker was influenced by far-right and ultranationalist ideologies and views.



Meanwhile, Krakow’s main market square and ⁠the surrounding streets remained closed on Sunday, with police allowing only essential service workers.

Many nearby cafes were closed and flags ⁠at the city hall were at half-mast. Mourners placed candles in several locations in the area.

The traditional hourly trumpet call from St Mary’s church on the square was suspended for 12 hours to commemorate the dead, the first time this has happened since 1939, the Polish Press Agency reported.

World.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
World.content:
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in central Krakow. Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and his sister, who was 21-years-old.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.

Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur MoraÅski.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

In an update on Sunday, police spokesperson Katarzyna Cislo told Radio Krakow two women who were sent to hospital following the incident had been released and the remaining individuals in Krakow's hospitals are in a stable condition.

She said this included the two police officers who were injured.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

World.title: Houthis say at least 33 killed in Saudi air strike
World.content:
Media linked to the Houthi movement in Yemen say at least 33 people, including women and children, have been killed in air strikes by Saudi Arabia.

There has been no comment from the Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government in Yemen.

Live video footage on Al Masirah - a television station run by the Houthis - has shown rescuers pulling bodies out of the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.

The bodies of young children can be seen among those dug out from the ruins.

The television station has also shown a number of injured people being carried on stretchers to hospital.

Saba news agency, which is also run by the Houthis, said the attack was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Saturday. It added that 39 people had been injured.

The Saudis have led a coalition that has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government.

The war in Yemen had been dormant for several years but reignited as a result of the Iran war.

A truce began to fall apart when Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Sanaa - which is controlled by the Houthis - to prevent an Iranian plane landing there.

The Tehran-backed Houthis subsequently targeted Abha airport in Saudi Arabia, then began hitting Saudi ships that have been using the Red Sea off the coast of Yemen as an alternative oil export route to the Strait of Hormuz.

Major fighting has since resumed in Yemen between the Houthis and forces fighting for the Saudi-backed government of Yemen.

On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province, which has been the focus of much of the recent fighting, is reported to have killed 30 people.

The Houthis accused the Saudis of carrying out the strike, while government forces accused the Houthis of having fired a missile at the site.

The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

The Saudis have regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has fired multiple missiles at targets inside Saudi Arabia, including airports and oil facilities.

Hours before the strike that hit al-Shariyah, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a missile heading towards Riyadh.

The Saudi Ministry of Energy later said the Aramco tower had been hit by falling shrapnel in what it said was an attempted attack.

The state-owned oil company's building suffered minor damage.

A Houthi leader, Mahdi al-Mashat, has vowed that the group will take revenge for the latest attacks in Yemen.

World.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
World.content:
New Zealand voted in a new government as fog choked the capital, Wellington, on Saturday - and the mood was as palpable as the grey weather.

"It's pretty flat," 21-year-old Imogen Vlutger says. "There's this kind of apathy and a bit of dread."

"Tired. I think we're all tired," Symone, 28, admits.

"I didn't even vote," one man in his 40s sheepishly confesses. He couldn't bring himself to tick any of the boxes, he explains, declining to chat further.

"Wellington's a bit of a bubble," another voter says, expressing a caveat I heard often, before describing feeling disillusioned.

But polling shows this is a pervasive sentiment across the country: the national mood is low and faith in politics is even lower.

More than half the country no longer sees it as a land of opportunity, a recent study found, while a similar portion fears that the future looks even worse.

Many Kiwis feel the economy is in ruins, there are no jobs, the cost of living has become sky high, the sense of community that used to be a source of national pride is breaking down and there's no sense of genuine progress on policy solutions.

A record number of them are abandoning ship in search of brighter futures elsewhere.

Saturday's election also saw a record number of voters desert the two major parties, giving neither a clear mandate.

But it brought new highs for parties across the spectrum: the left-leaning Greens, the right-wing libertarian Act Party and the centrist Opportunity Party â the latter of which had never won a seat in parliament before but could now hold the balance of power with seven.

World.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
World.content:
Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.

Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.

A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.

Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.

The president has broad discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition and does not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

World.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
World.content:
A US State Department statement about its multi-million dollar reward said it was offering the money for information about the Iranian programme, including "facilities, equipment and associated personnel".

It said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA [the International Atomic Energy Agency] on safeguards obligations has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like [nuclear] centrifuges".

Centrifuges are needed to produce enriched uranium, which can be used to make reactor fuel for civilian use but also for nuclear weapons if enriched to around 90% purity or higher.

There had been mounting speculation that the US might resume significant strikes in Iran after the midterm elections, though Trump told reporters, prior to the polls, that he was in "no rush" to do so.

In an interview with Fox News on the eve of the midterms, the president also said the US "might need to go after Pickaxe [Mountain]", an underground site linked to Iran's nuclear programme.

This was "not a big deal" and could be done in "one hour", Trump said.

The president has repeatedly threatened to bomb the suspected underground site on previous occasions.

However, both Trump and Vice-President JD Vance have said public opposition to the war on Iran fuelled heavy losses for their Republican Party in this week's midterm elections, which has led to speculation the White House may no longer seek an escalation in the conflict.

On Friday, Trump insisted that Iran was keen to end the eight-month conflict with the US, stressing the damage to Tehran's economy and military.

"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman said on Tuesday that both sides were "reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented" and that it remained hopeful of a deal being agreed.

Iranian negotiators had discussed with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days once the US met its seven conditions.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

World.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
World.content:
The EU's former Brexit negotiator has warned that the UK cannot "cherry pick" which elements of the single market to which it subscribes, after Andy Burnham said he wanted to explore closer economic ties with Europe.

The prime minister has said rejoining the bloc's internal market was among options he could pursue as part of a reshaping of ties since the UK's exit from the EU nearly six years ago.

But Michel Barnier told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that EU members would insist on the UK readopting certain conditions, such as the free movement of people, to gain access.

He said there was not a "single market Ã la carte" menu from which the UK could pick and choose what elements it wanted to adopt.

Barnier - who led the EU delegation during Brexit talks between 2016 and 2021, and had a three-month spell as French prime minister in 2024 - said the "door is open" within Europe to the UK rejoining as an EU member.

But he insisted that any move to rejoin the single market - which allows for goods to be freely traded without border controls - would require the UK to follow the same terms as other members.

He added that this included compliance with regulations designed to promote the circulation of goods, services, capital and people, referred to collectively within EU institutions as the "four freedoms".

"There will be no possibility to have one freedom and not the other. The four freedoms are clearly the four conditions to be inside a single market."

Since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham has suggested he could commit Labour to pursuing a much closer future relationship with Europe, including asking to rejoin the organisation as a full member, though he has ruled out major changes before the next election.

His predecessors have struck a series of deals with the EU on different aspects of how the UK and EU interact post-Brexit.

Both sides are hoping to use a meeting in Brussels in 10 days' time to unveil deals on food standards, youth visas and re-linking British industry to the EU's carbon trading regime.

World.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
World.content:
Prosecutors in Paraguay have charged former president Santiago PeÃ±a over his alleged role in a banking scandal that led to his impeachment.

He has been accused of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

PeÃ±a, who denies any wrongdoing, was forced from office after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

He was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down but rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached PeÃ±a and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

PeÃ±a, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to PeÃ±a's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

PeÃ±a's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, AsunciÃ³n.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

PeÃ±a's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," PeÃ±a said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio NÃºÃ±ez said PeÃ±a was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

World.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America he is "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru, which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.

"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts; I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.

"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," Pope Leo confirmed.

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

On Friday, he arrived in Monetevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.

In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".

He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia the care he received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.

He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.

Pope Leo will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

On Sunday he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis who did not return during his own papacy.

The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

World.title: Why reelecting Tinubu is mandatory – Jigawa speaker
World.content:
The Speaker of the Jigawa State House of Assembly, Haruna Aliyu, has stated that supporting President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 general elections is a binding duty for residents of the state.

Mr Aliyu made the remarks on Saturday during the inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential and governorship campaign council in Dutse, the state capital.

He framed backing Mr Tinubu’s re-election as a religious obligation and an act of reciprocity, asserting that the President has consistently supported Northern political aspirations throughout his career.

Recalling Mr Tinubu’s instrumental role in the emergence of former President Muhammadu Buhari, the Speaker argued that Northern Nigeria owes him reciprocal loyalty.

“President Tinubu is a devout and dedicated Muslim leader who has the best interests of Jigawa State at heart,” Mr Aliyu said.

He added that although Jigawa was not initially listed on the President’s campaign itinerary, Mr Tinubu chose to visit because of his confidence in the state’s leadership and its people.

“That is why we must vote for him and support the APC at all levels,” he urged party faithful.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reflecting on the party’s readiness, the Speaker expressed confidence in its electoral strength, pointing to the presence of former governors, senators, and federal lawmakers at the event as proof of the APC’s broad grassroots appeal across Jigawa.

Mr Aliyu, who also coordinates the pro-Tinubu support group City Boy Movement in Jigawa, announced plans to ramp up house-to-house mobilisation ahead of the polls.

“We will mobilise the City Boy Movement across Jigawa, going from household to household to showcase the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi,” he said.

“We will mobilise the City Boy Movement across Jigawa, going from household to household to showcase the achievements of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Umar Namadi,” he said.

World.title: Nigerian Army regains control of X account two months after hacking
World.content:
The Nigerian Army said it has regained control of its official X account more than two months after it was hacked.

The military said the account had been successfully restored following efforts to resolve the “unauthorised access” reported on 29 August.

In a statement on Sunday, Appolonia Anele, a colonel and acting spokesperson for the army, said administrative control of the account had been fully reinstated.

She said the account was now secured and would resume regular updates on the army’s activities, operations, achievements and institutional developments.

“The successful recovery underscores the Nigerian Army’s commitment to safeguarding its digital communication platforms, protecting the integrity of information and ensuring the continued use of credible and secure channels for public engagement,” Ms Anele said.

The army thanked Nigerians, media organisations and other stakeholders for their patience and support during the period the account was inaccessible.

It also acknowledged their cooperation in helping sustain access to credible information through its alternative official communication platforms.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

ALSO READ: Nigerian Army investigates sexual abuse allegation against serving officer

The military urged members of the public to follow the restored account for timely and verified information about its activities.

It reaffirmed its commitment to strategic communication, public engagement and strengthening trust between the military and Nigerians.

The army did not explain the process of restoring the account, nor did it mention those responsible for the hacking.

World.title: NDLEA arrests Ugandan woman with 87 cocaine wraps at Lagos airport
World.content:
A 34-year-old Ugandan woman has been arrested at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Lagos, with 87 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.15 kilogrammes, the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has said.

The suspect, Farida Nansubuga, was arrested on Tuesday, 3 November, as she prepared to board a flight to Uganda at Terminal 2 of the airport.

In a statement on Sunday by the agency’s Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, the cocaine was strapped around her pelvic region and concealed beneath two layers of underwear.

The NDLEA said operatives became suspicious during a joint passenger screening exercise with aviation security personnel. A subsequent body search raised concerns that she had concealed something around her pelvic region, prompting officers to take her to a private search room, where they recovered the 87 wraps.

During questioning, Ms Nansubuga noted that she arrived in Nigeria on 29 October with members of her church for a prayer session at the Synagogue Church of All Nations (SCOAN), in the Ikotun-Egbe area of Lagos.

She told investigators that the other members of the delegation had returned to Uganda after the prayer session, but she stayed behind to collect the cocaine for a friend, identified as Joy, who lives in Uganda.

According to the NDLEA, Ms Nansubuga noted that Joy linked her with a contact in Nigeria, who arranged a vehicle to take her to a hotel on the morning of her departure. The contact allegedly handed over the drugs and instructed her to conceal them beneath her clothing to avoid detection at the airport.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She reportedly said they had not agreed on a specific payment, but she expected to receive at least $1,000 after delivering the consignment.

The arrest comes amid other reported attempts to smuggle cocaine out of Nigeria using body concealment, mirroring Nigeria’s role as a transit bub in the global cocaine menace.

In May 2025, NDLEA operatives arrested a woman at the Port Harcourt International Airport over an alleged attempt to smuggle 2.523 kilogrammes of cocaine to Iran.

Other seizures at Lagos airport

In a separate operation at the Lagos airport, the NDLEA intercepted 750,000 tablets of Tapentadol 250mg, weighing 526 kilogrammes and valued at N900 million.

The consignment arrived from Ahmedabad, India, on 3 November aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight. It was declared as Paracetamol 500mg tablets.

The agency said officers placed the shipment under surveillance after becoming suspicious of its declaration. They later examined it jointly with officials of the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies on Friday, 6 November.

The tablets were packed in 11 cartons inside two wooden structures. Ten cartons contained Tapentadol, while the remaining carton held paracetamol tablets.

The seizure follows earlier large-scale opioid interceptions at Lagos ports. In September 2024, the NDLEA reported recovering 25 million Tapentadol tablets and 350,000 bottles of codeine-based syrup at the Tin Can Island Port. It valued the Tapentadol at N13.725 billion and the entire consignment at about N16.1 billion.

The agency also intercepted 32 parcels of Loud, a strain of cannabis, weighing 16.15 kilogrammes at the Lagos airport.

The drugs were concealed inside two wooden sofas in a consolidated cargo shipment from Houston, Texas, which arrived aboard a Turkish Airlines flight on Wednesday, 4 November.

A freight agent, Ibrahim Abdulwaheed Adewale, was arrested when he came to clear the consignment. Two days later, a 34-year-old caterer from Ibadan, Oyo State, Adeoye Sarafa Ojo, was arrested while attempting to collect the package.

Mr Ojo reportedly told investigators that a friend, Taiwo Anuoluwapo Olusegun, had sent him.

Suspected Colorado chemical import network

The NDLEA said it had also uncovered a suspected network importing chemicals from the United Kingdom for the production of Colorado, a synthetic cannabis.

The investigation began with the interception of nine parcels concealed in two cartons of snacks labelled “Michael Tea Guy”. The shipment arrived aboard an Air Peace flight from the UK on 23 October.

Two parcels contained 1.20 kilogrammes of cannabis, while forensic analysis showed that the other seven contained chemicals used in producing synthetic cannabis.

A 51-year-old freight agent, Afolabi Abiodun Wale, was arrested when he came to clear the shipment.

Two additional cartons addressed to the same recipient later arrived from the UK aboard an Allied Air flight. A sting operation between 26 and 28 October led to the arrest of another 51-year-old suspect, Okwuite Benjamin Ojone, when he came to collect the four cartons.

A search of the additional cartons uncovered three parcels weighing 3.30 kilogrammes, concealed in detergent packs, and 11 plastic bottles containing mostly liquid substances weighing 16.25 kilogrammes.

The NDLEA said the operation resulted in the seizure of 1.20 kilogrammes of cannabis and 28.65 kilogrammes of chemicals suspected to be used in producing synthetic cannabis.

The agency has previously reported uncovering a laboratory allegedly used to produce Colorado in a residential building in Ajao Estate, Lagos, in November 2025. The operation followed months of intelligence gathering.

Seizures across states

At courier companies in Lagos, NDLEA operatives intercepted 46 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.2 kilogrammes in two cartons destined for the United Kingdom on Tuesday, 3 November.

Earlier, on 30 October, they intercepted 296 tablets of Swinol destined for Australia.

The agency also reported three tramadol shipments bound for the UK. They included 20 capsules from Benin City and 96 capsules from Sapele, Delta State, both concealed in vitamin C containers, as well as 600 tablets of Tramadol 225mg from Asaba hidden in female headwear.

In another Lagos operation, operatives arrested a 32-year-old man, Abubakar Ali, at Marine Beach, Apapa, on Friday, 6 November.

The agency said officers recovered drugs from a small store he had built inside his sitting room. The substances included 1.06 kilogrammes of Tramadol 250mg, 1.27 kilogrammes of Tramadol 225mg, 400 grammes of pregabalin capsules, 355 grammes of diazepam, 200 millilitres of codeine and 6.07 kilogrammes of cannabis.

In Ondo State, operatives recovered 148 bags of cannabis weighing 1,818 kilogrammes during a raid on Odofin Road, Uso, on 6 November.

Earlier that day, officers raided a cannabis farm in Board Forest, destroyed a one-hectare plantation, recovered 242 kilogrammes of cannabis and arrested a 36-year-old suspect, Itoro Linus Akpan.

In neighbouring Ekiti State, a 53-year-old man, Agbo Paul Peter, was arrested at Osin Forest, Osin Ekiti, on Thursday, 5 November, with 216 kilogrammes of cannabis and cannabis seeds.

In Edo State, officers intercepted a Volkswagen Golf saloon car carrying 19 bags of cannabis weighing 201 kilogrammes along the Auchi-Ibillo Road in Akoko Edo Local Government Area on 6 November.

The driver, Abdulmumid Isah, 39, and a passenger, Danako Godwin, 25, were arrested.

In a separate operation, officers raided a drug joint on Ihama Road, GRA, Benin City, where they arrested Emmanuel Sunday, 25; Samuel Bala, 31; and Loveth Momodu, 20. The suspects were found with quantities of Colorado, Loud and cannabis.

In Taraba State, officers arrested three men with 283 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 226.255 kilogrammes over two days at an NDLEA checkpoint in Lankaviri, Yorro Local Government Area.

On Thursday, 5 November, Ibrahim Abdullahi, 45, was arrested with 156 blocks weighing 149.275 kilogrammes, while Kabiru Usman, 25, was arrested with 80 blocks weighing 40.07 kilogrammes.

The following day, officers arrested Babangida Babayo, 32, with 47 blocks weighing 36.91 kilogrammes.

In Enugu State, a 57-year-old man, Celestine Uzochukwu Ejiakor, was arrested at a checkpoint in Eke Obinagu on Tuesday, 3 November, with 44 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.5 kilogrammes.

At another checkpoint in Ugwuoba, officers arrested Godwin Shaapera, 40, with 24,000 capsules of tramadol weighing 13.4 kilogrammes and 697 grammes of ketamine.

In Delta State, operatives arrested Edugua Othuke, 30, at Ozoro, Isoko North Local Government Area, on Saturday, 31 October, with 10.54 kilogrammes of skunk, 9.4 kilogrammes of cannabis seeds and 4.3 grammes of methamphetamine.

Another suspect, Akpofure Tobore, 34, was arrested at Upper Agbarho, Ughelli, on 4 November with quantities of skunk, tramadol, Rohypnol and laughing gas.

Drug abuse campaign

Meanwhile, the NDLEA said it continued its War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) campaign in schools, religious centres, workplaces and communities across the country.

During the week, the agency held sensitisation sessions for students and staff of St Andrew Basic School, Oyo; Government Technical College, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State; Sa’ad College, Kano; and Inland Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra State.

Its Zone 1 Command also paid an advocacy visit to the Emir of Bauchi, Rilwanu Sulaiman Adamu, at his palace.

The NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Buba Marwa, commended officers of the MMIA and the Lagos, Ondo, Ekiti, Edo, Delta, Taraba and Enugu commands for the arrests and seizures.

He said the Ugandan woman’s arrest showed how drug cartels exploit religious gatherings and travel opportunities to recruit couriers.

Mr Marwa, a retired brigadier general, urged officers to sustain efforts to disrupt drug supply networks and reduce demand.

World.title: 2027 Politics Watch: From Asaba rally’s death to Obi’s subsidy challenge
World.content:
One person was killed and five others injured during an opposition procession in Asaba on Saturday, according to police, who said they had received a warning of possible violence. Organisers disputed aspects of the police account of security arrangements before the gathering.

In Port Harcourt, President Bola Tinubu accused Atiku Abubakar of using public resources to establish a private university. Atiku denied the allegation, saying his investment in education began in 1993. The university’s published history, however, dates the academy he cited to 2002.

Peter Obi also challenged Tinubu over subsidy savings and borrowing. Official financial records provide a basis for examining his claims, including the distinction between estimated additional federation revenue and the debt accumulated by successive administrations.

Tinubu received a pledge of electoral support from Rivers Governor Siminalayi Fubara under a coalition coordinated by Nyesom Wike, whose allies were also involved in a separate PDP leadership dispute. In Bauchi, Seyi Makinde launched his presidential campaign with a programme containing specific fiscal, education, and security commitments.

Police and organisers dispute Asaba security arrangements

The Delta State Police Command said the violence occurred at about 12.15 p.m. on Nnebisi Road during a procession organised by the Obidient/OK Movement, a group supporting Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso on the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) platform.

In a statement reported on Saturday, police spokesperson Bright Edafe said the command had received intelligence about possible violence and invited the organisers to a security meeting.

Police said they recommended holding the gathering at a designated venue where they could provide protection, rather than conducting an open-road procession. According to the command, the organisers proceeded despite that advice.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Delta State coordinator Favour Emerure disputed aspects of the police account. He said the organisers had notified the command and complied with instructions not to assemble at Inter-Bua Junction. He questioned why officers were absent when participants came under attack.

His account did not clarify whether the organisers had agreed to abandon the road procession altogether.

Reports from the scene described damaged campaign vehicles and attacks on participants.

NDC accused people associated with the All Progressives Congress (APC) of involvement. Delta APC spokesperson Valentine Onojeghuo rejected the allegation, saying no evidence linked his party to the violence.

Police said officers evacuated injured participants, reinforced security and opened an investigation. Their published account identified neither the victims nor those responsible.

The investigation must establish who carried out the attack and what protection was available after police received advance intelligence. Any Organisers’ failure to follow security advice would not, by itself, establish responsibility for the violence.

AUN records date Atiku’s ABTI Academy to 2002 amid funding row

President Tinubu made his allegation during an APC campaign rally at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt.

The State House account records his assertion that Atiku used public funds to establish a private university while serving as vice-president between 1999 and 2007. It provided no financial documents supporting the accusation.

Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, rejected the allegation through Phrank Shaibu, director of strategic communication of his campaign council.

He said he began laying the foundation for ABTI Academy in 1993, six years before becoming vice-president, and linked that investment to the subsequent establishment of the American University of Nigeria (AUN).

The university’s official history dates the establishment of ABTI Academy, a private primary and secondary school, to 2002.

According to the institution, the later university project was licensed as ABTI University in 2003. Construction began in October 2004, and the first 124 students were admitted during the 2005–2006 academic period.

The university’s licensing and construction therefore occurred during Atiku’s vice-presidency. Its records do not exclude preparations beginning in 1993, but his published response provided no dated documents supporting that earlier account.

Neither the chronology nor the statements exchanged on Saturday establish the source of the university’s construction funds. President Tinubu’s allegation that public resources were used remains unsupported by the financial evidence made available in the exchange.

Atiku also referred to Mr Tinubu’s 1993 United States civil forfeiture case. The proceeding was not a criminal conviction, a distinction the presidency previously emphasised while responding to separate litigation concerning access to US investigative records.

The former vice-president also renewed his proposal for a production-based fuel subsidy linked to domestic refining, promising lower petrol and diesel prices.

In a September statement, the APC Presidential Campaign Council challenged him to explain its cost, legal basis, and funding arrangements, including how support to refiners would translate into lower prices for consumers.

The council questioned whether the proposed arrangement would comply with the Petroleum Industry Act, which provides for market-based petroleum pricing. Atiku’s Saturday response reiterated the proposal but did not address those specific questions.

Official figures put Obi’s subsidy and borrowing claims in context

The debate over fuel subsidy policy also featured in Peter Obi’s criticism of Mr Tinubu’s economic record, although the NDC presidential candidate approached it from a different direction.

Rather than proposing a new intervention in petroleum pricing, Obi challenged President Tinubu to explain what Nigerians had gained from ₦15.8 trillion in subsidy savings and more than $100 billion he claimed the administration had borrowed.

He demanded measurable improvements in poverty reduction, school attendance, primary healthcare, electricity supply and security, questioning how increased government revenue had affected living conditions.

His subsidy figure closely matches an estimate published by the Federal Ministry of Finance, although the calculation covers resources attributed to different tiers of government.

An August 2026 fiscal analysis estimates ₦15.827 trillion in additional federation resources associated with subsidy removal between June 2023 and December 2025.

The ministry arrived at the figure by comparing actual net Federation Account revenue with a hypothetical revenue path had the pre-reform trend continued. That calculation uses an eight per cent annual growth assumption.

The amount is therefore an estimate of additional resources associated with the reform, not a cash balance accumulated in a single federal account.

In its detailed distribution, the ministry attributes ₦5.007 trillion of the estimated additional resources to the Federal Government, ₦6.525 trillion to states, ₦3.876 trillion to local governments and ₦419 billion to other statutory allocations, including the Federal Capital Territory.

The summary combines the Federal Government and other allocations into ₦5.426 trillion.

Any accounting of how those resources were spent must consequently cover federal, state and local governments, rather than treating the entire ₦15.827 trillion as money retained by the presidency.

The ministry lists wage adjustments, infrastructure, electricity support, and increased debt service costs among additional expenditure associated with the reforms.

Those expenditure categories do not establish how much reached individual projects or beneficiaries. Payment records, contracts, audited accounts and evidence of functioning public services would provide a more complete picture.

The borrowing claim is less straightforward.

The Debt Management Office’s June 2026 report records approximately $120.93 billion in outstanding domestic and external public debt across federal, state and Federal Capital Territory liabilities.

That stock includes debts accumulated over successive administrations. It cannot be equated with the amount Mr Tinubu’s government borrowed after assuming office in May 2023.

Determining borrowing attributable to his administration requires new loan and repayment records over a defined period, with adjustments for currency movements and other changes in the debt stock. Obi’s reported statement did not provide a calculation reconciling his figure with those records.

The government’s own fiscal scorecard describes household welfare as weak, although beginning to improve.

Fubara pledges three million votes through Wike-led coalition

At the Port Harcourt rally, Rivers Governor Siminalayi Fubara pledged to mobilise at least three million votes for Mr Tinubu under the leadership of Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike.

He also promised support for candidates adopted by the Rainbow Coalition, which brings together politicians from the APC and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) without formally merging the parties.

The arrangement allows participating politicians to campaign for President Tinubu while supporting selected candidates on different platforms in governorship and legislative elections.

Mr Tinubu praised the reconciliation between Fubara and Wike after their prolonged struggle for political control in Rivers. Fubara, in turn, committed himself to the coalition coordinated by his predecessor.

His three-million-vote pledge was a mobilisation target, not a verified measure of electoral support.

Tinubu also urged young Nigerians to collect their permanent voter cards and defended the economic reforms introduced by his administration.

The presidency reported that he presented his 2027 manifesto at the event, although its account did not reproduce the detailed proposals.

President Tinubu also said his government was clearing inherited pension and gratuity arrears. Payment schedules, disbursement records and beneficiary information would show how much of the backlog had been settled.

The coalition’s support for candidates across party lines has also caused disagreements within the APC, where some leaders insist that members should campaign for their party’s candidates at every level.

Makinde sets fiscal and education targets at Bauchi campaign launch

In Bauchi, Seyi Makinde launched the Allied Peoples Movement’s (APM) presidential campaign at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa Stadium alongside his running mate, Musa Daura, whose name appears on INEC’s final presidential candidate list.

Bauchi Governor Bala Mohammed endorsed Makinde, calling for appointments that reflect Nigeria’s diversity without sacrificing merit.

Governor Makinde urged Nigerians to support his proposed national reset and told voters to accept campaign money but vote according to their conscience.

The launch followed Wednesday’s manifesto presentation in Abuja.

His 74-page Reset Nigeria Manifesto contains quantified economic and education targets, alongside proposals for security coordination, federal-state relations and public accountability.

On fiscal policy, the document sets two targets for the end of the administration’s third year.

The first is to bring the actual federal fiscal deficit within three per cent of gross domestic product, except where departures are expressly permitted by law, and they are disclosed.

The second is to reduce the actual federal debt-service-to-revenue ratio to no more than 50 per cent. The manifesto cites a 67.22 per cent benchmark from the Federal Government’s third-quarter 2025 budget implementation report.

For primary education, the programme promises that at least 50 per cent of Primary Three learners will meet the national minimum literacy standard and 65 per cent the corresponding numeracy standard within three years.

It also targets a reduction of at least 25 per cent in the proficiency gap between the five highest- and five lowest-performing states.

Those education targets would be assessed against an independently administered baseline established in the first year, with federal support provided to participating states.

The security programme proposes a Threat-to-Action Standard under which authorities would identify the agency responsible for responding to credible threats, supporting institutions, command arrangements and deadlines for action.

Serious incidents or failures to respond would trigger operational reviews examining what information was available, how agencies acted and what corrections followed. Public accounts of findings would be issued while protecting sensitive intelligence.

The manifesto also promises a consolidated implementation plan within the first 100 days, identifying responsible institutions, legal requirements, milestones and the evidence needed to establish completion.

Quarterly scorecards would disclose progress, delays and corrective action, with significant results subject to independent verification.

Achieving the education targets would require sustained cooperation with state governments. Some proposed changes to security coordination and the distribution of government responsibilities would also depend on legislative action and inter-institutional agreements.

PDP candidates urge Supreme Court challenge over leadership ruling

In Abuja, governorship candidates aligned with the Kabiru Turaki-led PDP group urged a Supreme Court challenge to a Court of Appeal judgment favouring the rival leadership backed by Mr Wike.

The candidates made the demand during a solidarity visit to the Turaki group’s Interim National Working Committee in Abuja, PREMIUM TIMES reported.

Their representative, Sunday Biggs, also called for reconciliation, improved communication and stronger party organisation ahead of the 2027 elections.

On Wednesday, the Court of Appeal dismissed an appeal brought by the Adolphus Wabara-led Board of Trustees seeking to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise Mr Turaki’s interim leadership.

The appellate court upheld the lower court’s decision favouring the rival PDP leadership chaired by Abdulrahman Mohammed and supported by Mr Wike.

Mr Turaki told the visiting candidates that lawyers had been instructed to review the judgment and advise on the nextstepsn.

He expressed confidence that his group would eventually secure recognition and places on the ballot, despite the ruling.

Biggs urged the leadership to pursue a Supreme Court challenge urgently. However, the available reporting confirmed a legal review and a demand for an appeal, not that an appeal had been filed or that a subsequent court order had changed the judgement’s effect.

World.title: Truck overturns in Lagos, kills passenger
World.content:
A man has died after a truck overturned around the TREM axis of Gbagada, inward Oshodi, Lagos State.

The accident occurred on Sunday and involved a Mercedes-Benz six-tyre truck loaded with assorted goods, including sealed bags and newly branded event chairs.

The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said one of the truck’s front tyres burst while the vehicle was travelling at high speed, causing the driver to lose control and overturn.

In a statement shared on X by its Director of Public Affairs and Enlightenment, Adebayo Taofiq, the agency said an elderly male passenger seated in the front cabin was thrown out of the truck.

LASTMA stated that he hit his head against a sharp object and died at the scene.

The agency said its Night Rescue Team arrived at the scene, cordoned off the area and evacuated the deceased from the road into a Lagos State Emergency Medical Services ambulance.

Personnel of the Pedro Police Division and the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service also took part in the rescue operation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

LASTMA said it could not remove the truck immediately because of the volume of goods it was carrying. He said it’s officers had to transfer the goods to another vehicle before they could recover the overturned truckovered.

The agency’s General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, described the incident as an avoidable loss and urged operators of heavy-duty vehicles to observe speed limits and regularly check their vehicles for faults.

He said excessive speed makes it harder for drivers to control their vehicles when mechanical problems occur.

The crash is one of several involving heavy-duty vehicles in Lagos in recent months.

In April 2026, LASTMA reported that 69 people died and 246 others were injured in road crashes across the state between January and March.

It also recorded more than 900 traffic violations involving trucks and other articulated vehicles during the period.

In April 2025, a container truck crashed along Cele Expressway, inward Oshodi, killing a pedestrian and injuring five others. LASTMA attributed the accident to brake failure while the truck was travelling at high speed.

Also in October, four people died when a truck carrying a 20-foot container overturned onto an interstate bus at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway.

World.title: NPFL Matchday 12 Preview: Rangers, Rivers United face crucial tests
World.content:
The race for supremacy in the 2026/27 Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) season is gathering momentum, with Matchday 12 offering another chance for the leading contenders to strengthen their positions and the chasing pack to close the gap.

The latest round of fixtures began on Friday at the Dan Anyiam Stadium in Owerri, where Kano Pillars were forced to settle for a 1-1 draw against Kun Khalifat despite taking the lead through substitute Sikiru Alimi.

Alimi, introduced alongside Ahmed Musa in the 57th minute, made an immediate impact on the contest and fired the visitors ahead in the 76th minute with a fine effort from outside the penalty area. However, Kano Pillars’ hopes of claiming their first away win ended as the 9 chances ended Pillars’ unbeaten run to four matches and moved them to 19 points from 12 games, keeping them firmly involved in the battle near the top of the table. Kun Khalifat, meanwhile, will take encouragement from their late response as they continue their fight to move away from the lower end of the standings.

With that encounter out of the way, attention now shifts to Sunday’s fixtures, followed by two more matches on Monday and Tuesday. There is plenty at stake, particularly for the teams competing for the top positions, with Enugu Rangers, Rivers United and the chasing sides all facing important tests.

Rangers look to consolidate their position against Kwara United

Rangers International will have the opportunity to strengthen their grip on the top spot when they welcome Kwara United to the Awka Township Stadium on Sunday (today).

The Flying Antelopes moved to 21 points from 10 matches following their hard-fought 1-0 victory over Bendel Insurance in a rescheduled fixture on Wednesday, with Chidozie Iwundu’s controversial second-half header settling the contest.

That result put Rangers three points clear of the chasing pack, although they have played fewer matches than several of their closest rivals. Their impressive start has put them in a strong position, but Fidelis Ilechukwu’s men cannot afford to take their foot off the pedal with the season still in its early stages.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Kwara United, on the other hand, arrive in Awka needing a response after suffering a 2-1 home defeat to Bendel Insurance in their previous outing. The Harmony Boys have struggled to maintain consistency and will know another setback could leave them further adrift of the leading contenders.

Rangers will be favourites, particularly with their home advantage, but Kwara United will believe they do have enough motivation to make this an uncomfortable afternoon for the league leaders.

Bendel Insurance seek response against Niger Tornadoes

Bendel Insurance will be eager to return to winning ways when they host Niger Tornadoes at the Samuel Ogbemudia Stadium in Benin City.

The Benin Arsenal suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to Rangers in their rearranged Matchday 9 encounter, a result ending their potential chance to overtake the league leaders. They remain among the leading contenders, however, and will see Sunday’s fixture as an important opportunity to get their campaign back on track.

Niger Tornadoes will not be travelling to Benin merely to make up the numbers. The Ikon Allah Boys have been one of the competitive sides in the early weeks of the campaign and remain within touching distance of the top positions.

With both teams separated by just a few points, the encounter carries significant importance in the battle for early-season supremacy. Bendel will look to make home advantage count, while Niger Tornadoes will be hoping to frustrate their hosts and take something back to Minna.

Barau FC and Shooting Stars Set for Kano Battle

Barau FC welcome Shooting Stars to the Sani Abacha Stadium in what promises to be one of the most interesting fixtures of the weekend.

The Kano-based side have remained competitive in their first campaign at this level and will be keen to use home advantage to strengthen their position in the top half of the table.

Shooting Stars, meanwhile, head into the contest with renewed confidence after one of their most convincing performances of the season, thrashing Abia Warriors 4-1 in Ibadan.

The Oluyole Warriors showed their attacking potential in that encounter and will hope to carry the same energy into Kano. Their challenge, however, will be to reenact that level of performance against a Barau side determined to protect its home ground.

With both teams looking to climb the standings, the outcome could hsignificantly affecttheir respective ambitions.

Nasarawa United face Plateau United in top-half clash

Nasarawa United and Plateau United will renew their rivalry at the Lafia City Stadium, with both sides looking to strengthen their positions among the leading teams.

The Solid Miners suffered a 2-0 defeat to Kano Pillars in their last outing, bringing an end to their positive run. They will be determined to respond in front of their supporters and avoid allowing another result to affect their momentum.

Plateau United also dropped points in their previous fixture, playing out a 1-1 draw against Warri Wolves in Jos. The Peace Boys have shown flashes of quality this season but will need greater consistency if they are to sustain a challenge near the top of the table.

With Nasarawa United sitting on 17 points and Plateau United on 16 before the weekend’s fixtures, there is little separating the sides. A victory for either team could provide a valuable boost in the race for the top positions.

The encounter is expected to be closely contested, with both sides aware of the importance of avoiding another setback.

Warri Wolves and Katsina United target maximum points

Warri Wolves will host Katsina United at the Southern Delta University Stadium, with both clubs seeking an important result as the campaign progresses.

The Seasiders earned a point in their previous match after holding Plateau United to a 1-1 draw in Jos. While the result offered some encouragement, they will be looking to turn that resilience into a home victory.

Katsina United arrive with confidence after defeating Sporting Lagos 2-1, thanks to another influential performance from Luis Dadong, who has been among the team’s important attacking contributors.

The Katsina-based side have collected 16 points and remains within reach of the leading pack, while Warri Wolves will be eager to improve their position after a mixed start to the campaign.

Katsina United will fancy their chances of getting a result, but the home side will be determined to make life difficult for their visitors.

Abia Warriors must respond against Doma United

Abia Warriors face another important test when they welcome Doma United to the Enyimba Stadium in Aba.

The Umuahia-based side are coming off a disappointing 4-1 defeat to Shooting Stars in Ibadan, a result that exposed their defensive weaknesses and left them needing an immediate response.

They will hope that returning to familiar surroundings provides the lift required to rediscover their winning form. However, Doma United will present a difficult challenge.

The Gombe-based side shared the points with Ikorodu City after a 2-2 draw in their previous outing and have remained competitive despite a number of demanding fixtures.

With Doma United sitting on 15 points and Abia Warriors on 10 in the relegation places, the hosts have plenty of work to do to close the gap. They will need a much-improved defensive display and greater efficiency in front of goal to claim maximum points.

For Doma United, the objective will be to take advantage of Abia Warriors’ recent struggles and strengthen their position in the top half.

Ranchers Bees and Enyimba battle for crucial Points

Ranchers Bees will welcome Enyimba to the Bako Kontagora Stadium, with both sides desperate to build momentum and move away from the lower end of the standings.

Ranchers Bees played out a 1-1 draw with Inter Lagos in their previous match, a result that offered some relief but did little to change their position in the bottom half.

Enyimba, meanwhile, secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Kun Khalifat through Tobi Iyanda’s early goal, giving the Aba giants a much-needed boost after a difficult start to the season.

The People’s Elephant will hope that the victory marks the beginning of a stronger run, but they must be prepared for a difficult away assignment against a Ranchers Bees side that will be desperate to make home advantage count.

For both clubs, the importance of this fixture goes beyond three points. Another positive result could provide the confidence needed to turn their respective campaigns around.

Ikorodu City host Inter Lagos in Lagos Derby

The Matchday 12 action continues on Monday when Ikorodu City welcome Inter Lagos to the Mobolaji Johnson Arena in Onikan.

The Oga boys will be looking to return to winning ways after sharing the points in a 2-2 draw against Doma United last time out. The Bright Ozagbe-tutored side have shown they can com of the league’s established sides, but they will need to convert more of their opportunities if they are to climb further up the table.

Inter Lagos, meanwhile, remain at the foot of the standings following a difficult start to life in the top flight. They played out a 1-1 draw against Ranchers Bees in their previous outing, but their points deduction has left them with little room for error.

The Lagos derby offers a chance to deliver a statement performance, while Ikorodu City will be keen to avoid dropping points against their city rivals in the derby.

The fixture also carries local bragging rights, adding another layer of significance to an encounter both teams will be eager to win.

Rivers United fixture postponed

Rivers United will not be in action during the scheduled Matchday 12 programme after their fixture against Sporting Lagos at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena was postponed.

The Port Harcourt club had been among the early pacesetters and will be looking to maintain their challenge when the rescheduled encounter is eventually played.

Their absence from this weekend’s action gives the other contenders an opportunity to make ground in the standings, although Rangers remain in a strong position following their victory over Bendel Insurance.

READ ALSO: Bendel Insurance petition NPFL over controversial Rangers goal

The race for NPFL Supremacy intensifies

With Kano Pillars already held to a draw in Owerri, Matchday 12 has begun with another reminder of how difficult it is to collect maximum points in the NPFL.

The 1-1 result against Kun Khalifat took Pillars to 19 points, but the attention now shifts to Rangers, Bendel Insurance, Nasarawa United, and the other challengers as they seek to strengthen their positions.

Rangers have the opportunity to consolidate their advantage at the summit, while the chasing sides know that dropped points could make the gap increasingly difficult to bridge.

At the other end of the table, the pressure is also mounting on clubs struggling to find consistency. For them, every fixture is becoming increasingly important as they look to avoid being dragged into an early relegation battle.

With several compelling match-ups across the country, Matchday 12 promises another weekend of intense competition, crucial points and potentially significant movement in the 2026/27 NPFL standings.

World.title: 2027: Kwara APC rallies for Tinubu, local candidates in Ilorin
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State has staged a mega rally in Ilorin to canvass support for President Bola Tinubu, Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, and the party’s governorship candidate, Salihu Yakubu-Danladi.

The rally, described by its organisers as a 20,000-man march, attracted party faithful and supporters from Ilorin West, Ilorin East, Ilorin South, Asa and Moro local government areas.

Organised by the Governor’s Special Adviser on Political Matters, Suleiman Sai Kayi, the rally was aimed at demonstrating support for the APC leadership and its candidates ahead of the 2026 elections.

The procession began at the Kwara State University Teaching Hospital (General Hospital) Roundabout and moved through major streets in Ilorin, with participants displaying party colours and chanting solidarity songs.

Many supporters wore APC-branded uniforms and caps bearing inscriptions such as ‘My Vote is for APC’ and ‘#Iwaju LaNlo’ as they danced and marched through the state capital.

Speaking with journalists, Mr Sai Kayi said the rally was organised to appreciate Governor AbdulRazaq’s performance, particularly in infrastructure development, education and the welfare of workers and pensioners.

He described Mr Yakubu-Danladi’s emergence as the party’s governorship candidate as an agenda for continuity, anchored in fairness and justice, and said he was confident the incoming administration would consolidate the present government’s achievements.
