“The youth are more than any other age group in this rally. We are gathered to appreciate Mallam AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for giving us SYD. SYD is part of our own constituency,” he said.

Mr Sai Kayi added that the APC believed in sustaining the current development trajectory, arguing that Mr Yakubu-Danladi was part of the achievements recorded by the AbdulRazaq administration since 2019.

Also speaking, the Senior Adviser and Counsellor to the Governor, Sa’adu Salahu, urged voters not to be swayed by opposition political campaigns but to assess candidates based on their records and contributions to public service.

He expressed confidence that the administration’s people-oriented programmes and infrastructure projects would translate into electoral support for the APC and its candidates.

Mr Salahu said Governor AbdulRazaq’s leadership had discouraged political violence and promoted political tolerance, contrasting the administration’s approach with what he described as the style of previous governments.

“We can have political differences, but you will agree with me that Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq has never encouraged political thuggery, in contrast to the style of the past government,” he said.

He also ruled out the possibility of a rainbow coalition gaining political traction in Kwara, insisting that the APC remained confident of winning the 2027 elections across the state.

The governor’s aide urged party members to sustain peaceful mobilisation and intensify door-to-door campaigns to secure votes for the party.

Similarly, the Director-General of the APC Campaign Council (Central), Abdulrazaq Jiddah, commended party members for their turnout and urged eligible voters to ensure they collected their Permanent Voter Cards when the exercise commenced.

The General Manager of the Kwara State Social Investment Programme, Abdulwasiu Tejidini, said the turnout of men, women and youths reflected growing support for the APC and its development agenda.

“Today, Kwara Central has spoken. The whole Kwara has spoken, because the good work of His Excellency, the Governor of Kwara State, has really spoken for itself,” Tejidini said, drawing parallels between the development agenda of President Tinubu and that of the Kwara State Government.

READ ALSO: Jos stadium gets facelift in 38 years ahead of APC rally

A former APC House of Assembly aspirant for Share/Oke-Ode Constituency, Abdulrasheed Akogun, described the zoning of the party’s governorship ticket to Kwara North as a historic political breakthrough for the region.

Mr Akogun commended Governor AbdulRazaq for what he called his commitment to equity, fairness and justice, adding that the governor provided a level playing field for party members to pursue their ambitions during the primaries, irrespective of their political tendencies.

Other dignitaries at the rally included the wife of the governorship candidate, Sa’adat Yakubu-Danladi; lawmakers and candidates Fatima Arinola Lawal and Mariam Yusuf Aladi; Ghali Alaya; the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Bashir Adigun; council chairmen from the participating local government areas; and other APC chieftains.

World.title: “America ‘ll be back bigger, stronger’ – Trump vows after midterm defeat
World.content:
Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP.

President Donald Trump vowed Sunday to bounce back stronger from a massive midterm elections loss that he called a “giant step back in history” for the United States.

Democrats captured both chambers of Congress in last Tuesday’s midterms that dealt historic losses for Trump’s Republican Party in states they had dominated for decades.

“America took a giant step back in History with the results of the last Election,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social, saying that the stock market that had grown during his tenture took a loss after the vote.

“But have no fear, we will be back, BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!”

While Republican lawmakers have been licking their wounds over the setback, Trump has sounded defiant and on Friday appointed hardline advisor Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, signaling a bare-knuckle fightback.

Democrats have pledged to hold the Trump administration to account and fight “every step of the way” against Miller, architect of Trump’s tough immigration policy.

World.title: UK lists 4 conditions migrants must meet to qualify for permanent residency
World.content:
The United Kingdom, UK has introduced four mandatory conditions migrants must satisfy to qualify for permanent residency under its proposed earned settlement model, which will make obtaining indefinite leave to remain (ILR) dependent on applicants’ contributions and conduct.

Under the proposed reforms, migrants will no longer qualify for permanent residency almost automatically after five years in the country. Instead, the time required to secure settled status will depend on their earnings, contribution to society and immigration history.

The four non-negotiable conditions, which will apply to all applicants regardless of when they arrived in the UK, include:

1. Clean criminal record: Migrants must have a spotless criminal record, with the government proposing stricter requirements than the current rules, which allow some applicants with suspended sentences of up to 12 months to qualify.

2. High English proficiency: Applicants must demonstrate a high standard of spoken English, equivalent to A-Level English as a foreign language.

3. No outstanding government debts: Migrants must have cleared any debts owed to the UK government or taxpayer before qualifying for permanent residency.

4. Sustained National Insurance contributions: Applicants must provide evidence of sustained National Insurance contributions as proof of their economic contribution to the country.

Beyond these four mandatory requirements, the proposed model introduces different settlement timelines based on migrants’ earnings and contributions.

Under the arrangement, the highest earners could qualify for permanent residency after three years, while migrants earning more than £50,271 annually could become eligible after five years.

Certain public service workers, including doctors, nurses and teachers, would also qualify for settlement after five years.

Other migrants would be subject to a new standard settlement period of 10 years, while those who have breached immigration rules would have to wait at least 20 years before qualifying.

The government said the reforms recognise settled status as a significant privilege, granting migrants unrestricted access to the labour market, the National Health Service (NHS) and the welfare system.

The proposed changes are intended to make permanent residency a status migrants must earn rather than an entitlement granted after a fixed period.

World.title: Vote-buying won’t work in 2027, APM candidate tells Ondo voters
World.content:
By Dayo Johnson, Akure

The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Ondo Central, Hon. Sunday Falae, has urged voters in Ondo State to reject vote-buying and vote according to their conscience in the 2027 general elections.

Falae, who spoke in an interview in Akure, said financial inducements would not determine voters’ choices in the forthcoming elections, claiming that many Nigerians were dissatisfied with the state of affairs and wanted a change.

“They can bring all the money they want, it is not going to work. I am on the streets every day and the anger is there. Look at what happened in Osun,” he said.

He described what he called a “Rainbow Coalition”, a voting pattern in which individuals support candidates from different political parties for various elective positions rather than voting exclusively for one party.

Falae illustrated the trend with the example of a woman who reportedly told him she intended to vote for the APC presidential candidate, him for Senate, an ADC candidate for the House of Representatives and an SDP candidate for the State House of Assembly.

“People are angry and they want change. They will take the money and vote their conscience,” he said.

On the management of public funds, the APM candidate questioned the accountability of state governors over increased allocations, arguing that the funds received by state governments were not reflected in the level of development across the country.

“We are not holding them responsible. The amount of money they are getting does not correspond to the development we are seeing,” he said.

He cited the Owena-Alade-Idanre road, which he alleged was awarded and paid for but remained unconstructed.

“That road should have been constructed. That money today, we don’t know where it is. The road was not constructed and it was approved and paid. So the money went to somebody’s pocket,” he alleged.

Falae argued that accountability should not be limited to the Federal Government, saying state governors, senators and local government chairmen must also explain how public funds allocated to their respective jurisdictions were spent.

On the 2027 presidential election, he said the South-West should complete its eight-year presidential tenure, arguing that the contest should be between President Bola Tinubu of the APC and Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, whom he identified as the APM’s presidential candidate.

He explained that he did not join the African Democratic Congress because he did not want to campaign against Tinubu.

“In all sincerity, I didn’t join the ADC because I didn’t want to campaign against the President. I want us as Yorubas to finish eight years in office. Buhari finished his eight years,” he said.

Falae said he eventually joined the APM because Makinde, whom he described as a fellow Yoruba, could complete the remaining four years of the South-West’s presidential tenure.

“Tinubu deserves a second term. But if you give it to Governor Makinde, that is fine. Does he deserve it? Yes. Does Makinde deserve it? Even better. He has the energy and he has done well in Oyo State,” he said.

He also praised Makinde’s performance in Oyo State, arguing that his administration demonstrated the kind of leadership he believed Nigeria needed.

Explaining his decision to contest the Ondo Central senatorial seat, Falae said the district had been inadequately represented over the past four years.

He disclosed that he was a member of the APC from its formation until April 2026, but left the party over what he described as inadequate representation of the constituency.

“I am interested because I am under-represented right now. I was in the APC from inception until April this year. The person we have there now is not representing us the way he should. I have been to all six local governments and everybody is complaining,” he said.

Falae added that constituents felt abandoned and believed there was little to show for the outgoing tenure of their current representative.

World.title: Anglican Church warns Tinubu, INEC against 2027 election manipulation
World.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — The Church of Nigeria (Anglican Communion), Province of the Niger, has warned the Presidency, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) against manipulating the 2027 general elections or taking Nigerians for granted.

The church also cautioned against moves towards a one-party system, describing the alleged intimidation of opposition parties and their candidates as dangerous to the country’s democracy.

It urged Nigerians not to approach the 2027 presidential and other elections with indifference but to use their votes to hold political leaders accountable for unfulfilled promises.

The Coordinating Bishop of the Province of the Niger, Bishop of Aguata and Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka, Rt. Rev. Dr Samuel C. Ezeofor, gave the warning during the 2026 Anglican Prayer Rally of Anambra State (APRAS).

Ezeofor recalled that the province had, during its synod in May, warned Nigerians about the dangers of a one-party system and urged citizens to remain vigilant.

He said, “This is the time for us to come out to show that we are human beings, that we are not robots and so everywhere in the country, we are calling upon Nigerians to take their future, and destiny in their hands with the forthcoming presidential and other elections in the country.”

Addressing the Presidency, INEC, the APC and other political stakeholders, the bishop said Nigerians were increasingly dissatisfied with developments in the country and should not be taken for granted.

“If they take Nigerians for granted, it may come to a point where there may be a revolution. I don’t pray for that, but by my training, I am trained to believe the best but be prepared for the worst,” he said.

He urged those involved in the 2027 electoral process to respect the wishes of voters and ensure that the outcome reflected their choices.

“So both the Presidency, APC, INEC and all the people who are involved in the election that is coming in 2027, let everyone of them be careful and do what Nigerians said with their ballots and would want to be done with their votes,” he added.

On the internal challenges facing the Province of the Niger, Ezeofor acknowledged that some Anglican faithful might have become discouraged by the crisis within the church.

He, however, urged them to remain steadfast, saying that setbacks in the church’s human administration did not mean God had abandoned it.

“My message to our faithfuls is that as human beings, we may stumble, but God is still on his throne. This church belongs to God, yet it is human beings who run the church and it is also a human system,” he said.

He encouraged members to continue looking up to Jesus Christ, whom he described as the author and finisher of their faith, expressing optimism that the situation would improve.

The 2026 prayer rally, themed “Dwelling in the Secret Place of the Most High God”, was attended by six bishops of the province, including the retired Archbishop of the Province of the Niger, Most Rev. Prof. Godwin Okpara.

Others in attendance were Bishop Ephraim Ikeako of the Diocese of Amichi, Bishop Prosper Amah of the Diocese of Ogbaru, Bishop Ndubuisi Obi of the Diocese of Nnewi and Bishop Obiora Uzochukwu of the Diocese of Niger East.

Earlier, the preacher at the rally, Venerable Dr Emma Ezeugo, urged Christians to devote more time to prayer and fasting, particularly as December approaches.

He said prayer brought peace, protection and peace of mind, urging believers to seek God’s presence in their daily lives.

World.title: NDLEA arrests Ugandan woman with 87 cocaine wraps at Lagos airport
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arrested a 34-year-old Ugandan woman with 87 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.15 kilogrammes, allegedly concealed around her pelvic region, at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos.

The suspect, identified as Farida Nansubuga, was arrested on Tuesday, November 3, while preparing to board a flight to Uganda after allegedly travelling to Nigeria for a religious programme at the Synagogue Church of All Nations (SCOAN), Ikotun, Lagos.

According to the NDLEA, Nansubuga arrived in Nigeria on October 29 with members of her church for a prayer session but allegedly stayed behind after the other members of her delegation returned to Uganda.

The agency said she was intercepted at the screening point of Terminal 2 during a joint passenger screening exercise with aviation security personnel.

A body search reportedly revealed a substance concealed around her pelvic region, prompting officers to take her to a designated private search room for further examination.

The search led to the recovery of 87 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.15 kilogrammes, allegedly strapped around her pelvic region and secured beneath two layers of underwear.

During preliminary interrogation, the suspect reportedly claimed she stayed behind to collect the consignment on behalf of a friend in Uganda identified as Joy, who had linked her with a contact in Nigeria.

She allegedly said a man brought her to a hotel on the morning of her departure, handed her the drugs and instructed her to conceal them beneath her clothing to evade airport security.

The NDLEA said the suspect expected to receive at least $1,000 upon successful delivery of the consignment.

In another operation at the Lagos airport, operatives intercepted 750,000 tablets of Tapentadol 250mg, weighing 526 kilogrammes and valued at about N900 million.

The opioid consignment, which arrived from Ahmedabad, India, aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight on November 3, was allegedly declared as Paracetamol 500mg tablets.

The agency said the shipment comprised 11 cartons packed in two wooden structures. Following suspicions over the cargo declaration, officers placed it under surveillance before conducting a joint examination with the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies on November 6.

The examination revealed that 10 cartons contained Tapentadol tablets, while only the last carton contained paracetamol tablets.

Also at the airport, operatives intercepted 32 parcels of Loud, a strain of cannabis weighing 16.15 kilogrammes, concealed inside two wooden sofas in a consolidated cargo from Houston, Texas, United States.

A freight agent, Ibrahim Abdulwaheed Adewale, who reportedly presented himself to clear the consignment, was arrested.

In a follow-up operation on November 6, NDLEA operatives arrested a 34-year-old caterer from Ibadan, Oyo State, Adeoye Sarafa Ojo, who allegedly came to collect the package.

Ojo reportedly claimed he was sent by a friend, Taiwo Anuoluwapo Olusegun.

The agency also announced the dismantling of a suspected syndicate involved in importing chemicals used in producing Colorado, a synthetic cannabis, from the United Kingdom.

NDLEA said nine parcels of illicit substances concealed in two cartons of snacks bearing the label “Michael Tea Guy” were intercepted in a consolidated cargo arriving aboard an Air Peace flight from the UK on October 23.

Two of the parcels contained 1.2 kilogrammes of cannabis, while forensic analysis identified the contents of the remaining seven as chemicals used in producing synthetic cannabis.

A 51-year-old freight agent, Afolabi Abiodun Wale, who allegedly came to clear the consignment, was arrested.

The agency said two additional cartons for the same recipient subsequently arrived aboard an Allied Air flight from the UK.

A sting operation conducted between October 26 and 28 led to the arrest of another suspect, Okwuite Benjamin Ojone, 51, when he allegedly took delivery of the cartons.

A search reportedly uncovered three parcels weighing 3.3 kilogrammes concealed in two packs of detergent and 11 plastic bottles containing mostly liquid substances weighing 16.25 kilogrammes.

The total seizure from the operation comprised 1.2 kilogrammes of cannabis and 28.65 kilogrammes of chemicals allegedly intended for synthetic cannabis production.

At courier companies in Lagos, NDLEA operatives intercepted 46 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.2 kilogrammes in two cartons destined for the United Kingdom on November 3.

The agency also intercepted 296 tablets of Swinol destined for Australia on October 30, alongside three consignments of tramadol bound for the UK.

The tramadol consignments comprised 20 capsules from Benin City and 96 capsules from Sapele, Delta State, concealed in vitamin C containers, as well as 600 tablets of Tramadol 225mg from Asaba hidden in female headwear.

In a separate operation in Lagos, operatives arrested a 32-year-old man, Abubakar Ali, at Marine Beach, Apapa, on November 6.

The agency said officers recovered several drugs from a small store allegedly constructed inside the sitting room of his apartment.

Items seized included 1.06 kilogrammes of Tramadol 250mg, 1.27 kilogrammes of Tramadol 225mg, 400 grammes of pregabalin capsules, 355 grammes of diazepam, 200 millilitres of codeine and 6.07 kilogrammes of cannabis.

In Ondo State, operatives raided Odofin Road, Uso, on November 6, recovering 148 bags of cannabis weighing 1,818 kilogrammes.

On the same day, officers raided a cannabis farm in Board Forest, destroyed a one-hectare plantation, recovered 242 kilogrammes of the substance and arrested a 36-year-old suspect, Itoro Linus Akpan.

In neighbouring Ekiti State, a 53-year-old man, Agbo Paul Peter, was arrested at Osin Forest, Osin Ekiti, on November 5 with 216 kilogrammes of cannabis and cannabis seeds.

In Edo State, operatives intercepted a Volkswagen Golf saloon car conveying 19 bags of cannabis weighing 201 kilogrammes along the Auchi-Ibillo road in Akoko Edo Local Government Area.

The driver, Abdulmumid Isah, 39, and a passenger, Danako Godwin, 25, were arrested.

The agency also raided a suspected drug joint on Ihama Road, GRA, Benin City, where three suspects — Emmanuel Sunday, 25; Samuel Bala, 31; and Loveth Momodu, 20 — were arrested with quantities of Colorado, Loud and cannabis.

In Taraba State, three suspects were arrested with 283 blocks of compressed cannabis weighing 226.255 kilogrammes during stop-and-search operations at the NDLEA checkpoint in Lankaviri, Yorro Local Government Area, over two days.

The suspects were identified as Ibrahim Abdullahi, 45, who was arrested on November 5 with 156 blocks weighing 149.275 kilogrammes; Kabiru Usman, 25, arrested the same day with 80 blocks weighing 40.07 kilogrammes; and Babangida Babayo, 32, arrested on November 6 with 47 blocks weighing 36.91 kilogrammes.

In Enugu State, a 57-year-old man, Celestine Uzochukwu Ejiakor, was arrested at a checkpoint in Eke Obinagu on November 3 with 44 blocks of cannabis weighing 22.5 kilogrammes.

At another interception along the Ugwuoba checkpoint, operatives arrested Godwin Shaapera, 40, with 24,000 capsules of tramadol weighing 13.4 kilogrammes and 697 grammes of ketamine.

In Delta State, a 30-year-old suspect, Edugua Othuke, was arrested at Ozoro, Isoko North Local Government Area, on October 31 with 10.54 kilogrammes of skunk, 9.4 kilogrammes of cannabis seeds and 4.3 grammes of methamphetamine.

Another suspect, Akpofure Tobore, 34, was arrested at Upper Agbarho, Ughelli, on November 4 with quantities of skunk, tramadol, Rohypnol and nitrous oxide, commonly called laughing gas.

Meanwhile, the NDLEA said its commands and formations across the country sustained their War Against Drug Abuse (WADA) sensitisation campaigns in schools, worship centres, workplaces and communities during the week.

The activities included awareness lectures at St. Andrew Basic School, Oyo; Government Technical College, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State; Sa’ad College, Kano; and Inland Girls Secondary School, Onitsha, Anambra State.

The agency’s Zone 1 Command also paid an advocacy visit to the Emir of Bauchi, Alhaji Rilwanu Sulaiman Adamu, at his palace.

The NDLEA Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), commended officers and personnel of the MMIA, Lagos, Ondo, Ekiti, Edo, Delta, Taraba and Enugu commands for the arrests and seizures.

Marwa described the arrest of the Ugandan woman as a reminder that drug cartels were exploiting religious travel to recruit couriers.

He urged officers across the country to sustain efforts to reduce both drug supply and demand.

World.title: Hashim raises alarm over 3.68m IDPs, insecurity before US commission
World.content:
Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim

ABUJA — Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, has drawn the attention of the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) to Nigeria’s estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), calling for greater international intervention over insecurity, religious persecution and ethnic discrimination.

Hashim also called for the release of Hausa cultural activist, Maisango, whom he alleged was being unlawfully detained, and urged the international community to investigate reports of attacks and the burning of 11 villages in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State.

He made the appeal during an engagement with the commission on Friday, where he discussed Nigeria’s religious freedom and humanitarian challenges.

According to a statement on the engagement, Hashim acknowledged that Christians in Northern Nigeria face persecution but argued that religious freedom violations also affect Muslim minorities, including Shia Muslims and Hausa communities.

He said Nigeria’s religious freedom challenges extended beyond the conventional Christian-Muslim divide, alleging that ethnic identity and cultural affiliation also influenced religious and social acceptance in some communities.

The Accord candidate particularly raised concerns about what he described as the marginalisation of Hausa Muslims in parts of Northern Nigeria, arguing that some communities experience unequal treatment despite sharing the same Islamic faith with other groups.

On Maisango’s detention, Hashim alleged that the cultural activist had been held without trial despite reportedly being dismissed from his employment with the Department of State Services (DSS).

He called for his immediate release, emphasising the need to respect due process and fundamental human rights.

Hashim also cited an estimated 3.68 million internally displaced persons in Nigeria, referencing UNHCR figures as of October 2026, and argued that the humanitarian crisis cut across religious and ethnic boundaries.

He specifically highlighted reported attacks on communities in Shanga Local Government Area of Kebbi State, including Kalkami, Tungar Bori and Kawara.

According to him, reports of attacks in April 2026 indicated that suspected bandits killed residents, set buildings ablaze and forced inhabitants to flee their homes.

He said reports that 11 villages were burnt in the area deserved sustained international attention.

Hashim further alleged that some armed groups operating in the region were more interested in killing residents, destroying settlements and taking control of territory than in religious conversion.

He blamed what he described as the government’s failure to adequately protect vulnerable communities and decisively confront armed groups, warning that the country’s security and religious freedom challenges must not deteriorate further ahead of another political transition.

The presidential candidate also criticised what he termed insufficient accountability under the present administration, alleging that political considerations had weakened efforts to tackle terrorism and other forms of armed violence.

He recalled that the United States designated Nigeria a Country of Particular Concern in October 2025 over religious freedom concerns, following earlier recommendations by USCIRF.

He said the international community should recognise victims of religious and ethnic persecution across all communities rather than concentrate on one religious group.

Hashim called for a comprehensive approach that addresses the experiences of Christians, Shia Muslims, Hausa communities and other vulnerable populations, while ensuring that state institutions protect constitutionally guaranteed rights.

He commended the commission for its work on religious freedom in Nigeria and acknowledged US President Donald Trump’s interest in the issue.

He said religious freedom was “an intrinsic part of democratic right”.

World.title: Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara
World.content:
File image of bandits

By Idris Salisu, Gusau

Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State.

The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted.

A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers.

According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members.

Several other residents were also reportedly abducted during the raid, although the exact number of those kidnapped could not be immediately ascertained.

The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites.

The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals.

Residents condemned the killings, describing the incident as barbaric, and called on security agencies and the Zamfara State Government to intensify efforts to protect lives and property.

As of the time of filing this report, security agencies had yet to issue an official statement on the attack.

World.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
World.content:
By Egufe Yafugborhi

EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor.

The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days.

It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication.

The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023.

The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor.

It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit.

The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory.

Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement.

He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others.

“People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said.

Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications.

According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences.

She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case.

The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun.

However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie.

He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings.

According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. Nyekigbe, however, expressed sympathy with the families of the deceased.

World.title: 2027: Support Tinubu’s Re-election Bid, Danjuma Urges Adamawa Residents
World.content:
Daji Sani in Yola

General Theophilus Danjuma (rtd) has appealed to Adamawa residents to support the re-election bid of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 general election, rather than that of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

According to him, the Tinubu administration had appointed more Christians into key government positions, a development he said had contributed to the progress and development of the country.

He advised Christians to vote wisely in the forth coming general election as he also donated N250 million for the expansion of the Adamawa Government House Chapel and the construction of residences for its chaplain and deputy.

The donation was announced over the weekend in Yola during the 20th anniversary celebration of the Chapel, where Danjuma was represented by General Ishaya Bamaiyi (rtd).

The anniversary, themed ‘Thus far has the Lord helped us’ taken from 1 Samuel 7:12, brought together top government officials, former governors, religious leaders and other dignitaries from across the state.

Danjuma commended the founding fathers and organisers of the anniversary for their vision, commitment and sacrifices towards the establishment and growth of the Chapel over the past two decades.

Meanwhile, the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, urged youths, particularly Christian youths, to shun political thuggery and embrace peaceful conduct ahead of the 2027 general election.

Mrs Tinubu, who was represented by the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Professor Kaletapwa Farauta, advised young people not to allow politicians to exploit them for selfish interests, but to promote peace, tolerance and responsible participation in the electoral process.

Farauta, who also represented Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, said the governor wants the Chapel to remain a unifying platform for Christians across all denominations and not to be identified with any particular church.

Governor Fintiri urged members of the Chapel to sustain its spiritual activities and ensure that the fire on the altar continues to burn, adding that God’s presence would continue to guide the government and inspire development and peaceful coexistence.

“Adamawa belongs to all of us. We must all join hands to ensure that the state continues to move forward, while living together as one another’s keepers,” the governor said.

In his remarks, former Governor Boni Haruna who was the originator of the Government House Chapel, explained that the Chapel was established in 2005 to fulfil the original architectural design of the Government House complex, which provided for two places of worship, a mosque and a chapel, in line with equity and fairness, and to address historical imbalance.

He expressed hope that it would remain a symbol of unity for all residents irrespective of religious differences.

The Chairman of the Board of Trustees, and former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Mr Boss Mustapha, described the anniversary as a celebration of faith, courage, perseverance, unity and God’s faithfulness, urging the leadership to preserve its ecumenical character while respecting religious diversity.

The celebration also featured the presentation of awards to the First Lady, Governor Fintiri, founding fathers and past chaplains of the Chapel, as well as donations from dignitaries including Boss Mustapha, Boni Haruna, Bala Nggilari, Senator Amos Yohana and Dr Edgar Amos, among others.

World.title: Face of the World Nigeria Beauty Pageant Honours Okpebholo, Tenebe, Adeniyi, Others
World.content:
Edo State Governor, Senator Monday Okpebholo; state Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Emperor Jarrett Tenebe; and Dr. Ifetayo Adeniyi were among prominent personalities honoured at the 20th edition of the Face of the World Nigeria Beauty Pageant, tagged the ‘Akpakomiza Edition’ on Saturday.

The colourful ceremony, organised by the Chairman of Divine Smiles Foundation International, Prince Eric Odigie, featured glamour, cultural displays, entertainment and the recognition of distinguished individuals for their contributions to societal development.

Okpebholo, Tenebe and other award recipients were celebrated for their respective roles in leadership, community development and impactful service, while Adeniyi emerged Best Journalist of the Year 2026 in recognition of his outstanding contributions to journalism and humanitarian advancement.

Adeniyi’s award, which was received on his behalf by Patrick Ochoga, was presented under the ‘Megastar Man of the Decade Award CSR’ category in acknowledgement of his commitment to national development and giving back to society.

In his appreciation, Adeniyi expressed gratitude to the organisers for the recognition, describing the honour as a motivation to deepen his contributions to the journalism profession and humanitarian causes.

Other distinguished awardees included Dr. Paddy Iyamu, Chief Edobor Ozakpolor, Chief Ebipade Karl, Hon. Cyril Oshiomhole, Excalibur Hotel, Mr. Elvis Edoba and Mrs. Edesili Okpebholo.

Speaking during the event, Odigie commended members of his organising team for their dedication and resilience in sustaining the beauty pageant over the years, noting that the platform had continued to provide opportunities for discovering and nurturing talents.

He acknowledged that the journey had been challenging, but said the experiences and disappointments encountered in previous editions had provided valuable lessons for improving the quality and organisation of subsequent events.

“The experiences and disappointments of the past years have taught us valuable lessons, which have helped us shape subsequent editions and make each event better than the previous one,” Odigie said.

The organiser also expressed appreciation to Tenebe for hosting the team in South Africa and facilitating international contacts, which he said had opened new opportunities for the organisation.

Odigie further applauded the contributions of sponsors and partners, including Wells Carlton Hotel and Apartments, Modela Couture, Pure Gold Sparkle Cosmetics, Ebenezer Apartment, Andy Modu Global Vision, Megastar Life & Style Magazine and Well Hosa Farm, describing their support as instrumental to the success of the event.

The beauty contest’s major highlight was the crowning of Blessing J. Oaikhena as Face of the World, Osato Omozokpia as Face of Edo, and Ebuba Simon as Face of Tourism.

Other winners were Ebuba Ugonwa, who emerged Most Beautiful Girl in Edo State; Chiwen Anamanya, Miss Amity; and Amenaghawon Idemudia, Miss Hospitality.

The winners were applauded for their beauty, poise, talent and impressive performances throughout the competition.

The 20th edition also featured captivating cultural performances by different ethnic nationalities, musical renditions by contestants and other groups, alongside exciting entertainment that added colour and splendour to the occasion.

World.title: NAF Redeploys 41 Air Vice Marshals to Strengthen Command Effectiveness
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has redeployed no fewer than 41 Air Vice Marshals (AVMs) in a major strategic realignment of its senior leadership.

According to a statement by the Director of Public Relations and Information, Nigerian Air Force, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the postings and appointments are designed to strengthen command effectiveness, enhance institutional capacity and sustain operational readiness in support of national security objectives.

He noted that the exercise, approved by the Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, takes immediate effect.

Air Commodore Ejodame said: “The appointments span Service Headquarters, operational commands, Defence Headquarters, training institutions and other strategic establishments, reflecting a deliberate effort to align leadership competencies and professional experience with the Service’s evolving operational and institutional priorities.”

Air Commodore Ejodame, said that

at Headquarters NAF, AVM AK Ademuwagun has been appointed Chief of Transformation and Innovation; AVM IV Ajiboye as Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation; AVM PN Amadi as Chief of Air Intelligence; AVM NN Ananaba as Chief of Operations; AVM AH Bakari as Air Provost Marshal; AVM EE Efiom as Chief of Training; AVM MS Ibrahim as Chairman, Air Expo and International Liaison; AVM AG Kehinde as Chief of Civil-Military Relations; AVM MA Sulaiman as Chief of Communications and Information Systems; AVM S Peters as Coordinator, Project Implementation Team; and AVM AJ Laoye as Chief of Aircraft Engineering. Other strategic institutional appointments include AVM AY Dari as General Manager, Nigerian Air Force Investment Limited Group of Companies, and AVM NS Okoro as Director-General, AFRDI.

At the operational command level, AVM NI Ilo has been appointed Air Officer Commanding (AOC), Tactical Air Command, while AVM BR Mamman assumes command of Mobility Command. AVM OS Ogunsina becomes AOC, Logistics Command; AVM MN Onyebashi is appointed AOC, Special Operations Command; and AVM FCS Nwakara takes over as AOC, Ground Training Command.

In major institutional appointments, AVM PB Philips has been appointed Commandant, Armed Forces Command and Staff College (AFCSC), while AVM MC Ekwueme becomes Commandant, Armed Forces Resettlement Centre (AFRC). Other appointments in this category include AVM AO Akinbunwa as Commandant, Air Force War College; AVM A Idris as Commandant, Air Warfare Doctrine Centre; AVM JA Ekwuribe as Commandant, Regiment Training Centre; AVM OC Ubadike as Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM AI Sambo as Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management; and AVM M Yusuf as Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Defence Academy.

At the strategic defence level, AVM UK Abdullahi has been appointed Director of Defence Operations at Defence Headquarters (DHQ), while AVM EOE Ebiowe moves to the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA) as Deputy Coordinator, National Intelligence. Other appointments include AVM DDG Pwajok as Director of Technical Services, Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA); AVM I Sani as Deputy Chief of Defence Intelligence; AVM AA Shinkafi as Director of Liaison, DHQ; AVM AO Shogbamu as Director of Military Strategy; AVM RK Olanrewaju as Director of Search and Rescue; AVM J Usman as Director of Special Duties; AVM JJ Ijudigal as Director of Sports; AVM ZA Usman as Director of Cyber Operations; AVM EK Gabkwet as Director of Civil-Military Relations; and AVM GAA Bello as Director of Joint Warfare Doctrine, all at DHQ. Additionally, AVM AA Suleh has been appointed Deputy Chief of Defence Space Administration (DSA), while AVM OA Oyename becomes Director of Earth Observation and AVM SS Lazarus takes up appointment as Director of Launch Vehicles and Space Operations, both at DSA. AVM OT Salami has been posted to the Defence Space Command Centre (DSCC) as Deputy Chief, while AVM AI Hanidu moves to the Air Power Centre of Excellence (APCOE) as Director of Integrated Air Power Studies. Other appointments at APCOE include AVM OF Akinboyewa as Deputy Director-General and AVM MM Omar as Director, Museum/Hall of Fame. AVM DO Dickson has also been appointed General Manager, Operations, Defence Health Care Limited (DHCL).

Other appointments at Headquarters NAF include AVM AK Famuyiwa as Director of Coordination and Cooperation; AVM AK Bello as Director of Armament; AVM YA Katabiya as Director of Logistics; AVM EO Ashiegbu as Director of Policy; AVM GA Mbaka as Director of Aircraft Engineering; AVM AL Dakwat as Director of Research and Development; AVM SO Eyekosi as Director of Plans; and AVM AG Akinyimika as Director of Personnel Management.

To further strengthen operational command structures, AVM JI Ukeh has been appointed Commander, Nigerian Air Defence Corps (NADC). Other appointments include AVM OA Abu as Chief of Staff, Mobility Command; AVM I Subi as Chief of Staff, Special Operations Command; AVM NB Folaji as Chief of Staff, Tactical Air Command; AVM F Ekpah as Chief of Staff, Ground Training Command; AVM ES Odekina as Chief of Staff Logistics Command and AVM M Umar as Chief of Staff, Air Training Command. AVM GI Jibia has also been appointed Deputy Force Commander, Operation HADIN KAI. In other appointments, AVM CE Akubue has been appointed Managing Director, Aircraft Engineering and Technical Services Limited (AETSL), while AVM CE Akpa becomes Commander, Headquarters NAF Camp.

Other professional military education and training appointments include AVM SA Eyoma as Deputy Commandant, Air Force Institute of Technology; AVM FO Ankeli as Commandant, Air Traffic Services Training Centre; and AVM U Ariahu as Deputy Commandant, Nigerian Air Force College of Logistics and Management.

NAF spokesperson said the strategic realignment reflects the NAF’s commitment to continuous leadership renewal, stronger institutional accountability and enhanced operational effectiveness.

The CAS expressed confidence that the professional competence and wealth of experience of the newly appointed officers would further advance his Command Philosophy and strengthen the Service’s capacity to deliver decisive airpower effects in support of joint operations and national security objectives.

All affected officers are to assume their new appointments and complete the necessary handover and takeover formalities not later than 13 November 2026.

World.title: Akpabio, NDC Hail Flamingos’ Historic World Cup Triumph
World.content:
Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) have congratulated Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

Akpabio described the victorious players as Nigeria’s Golden Girls, saying their achievement had brought immense pride and honour to the country and made history for the African continent.

In a congratulatory statement issued on Sunday by his Special Assistant on Media and Communication, Anietie Ekong, the Senate President said Nigeria had become the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

He described the victory as more than a football achievement, noting that it represented a significant milestone for Nigerian sports and the entire African continent.

“By achieving this remarkable feat, you have made Nigeria the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. This is not just a victory for Nigerian football; it is a proud moment for the entire African continent,” Akpabio said.

He commended the players for demonstrating extraordinary talent, determination, resilience and the Nigerian spirit, attributing their success to the collective efforts of the players, coaches and other members of the technical crew.

According to him, their courage, discipline, teamwork and fighting spirit have brought joy to millions of Nigerians and demonstrated that talent, hard work and self-belief can make seemingly impossible dreams achievable.

The Senate President said the team had not only won a trophy but had also captured the hearts of Nigerians and inspired a new generation of young girls to pursue their ambitions.

“You have not only won a trophy; you have won the hearts of millions of Nigerians and inspired a generation of young girls to dream big, believe in themselves and reach for greatness. You are our pride, our champions and our Golden Girls,” he said.

Akpabio added that the team’s achievement had raised Nigeria’s flag high and encouraged young girls across Africa to aspire to greater accomplishments.

“You are more than champions; you are history makers!” he declared.

He congratulated the players, coaches, technical crew and everyone who contributed to the team’s historic success, adding: “The world has heard our victory song!”

Similarly, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) congratulated the Flamingos, describing their triumph over Japan as a remarkable demonstration of courage, determination and the resilience associated with the Nigerian spirit.

In a statement issued on Saturday by its National Campaign Council spokesperson, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, the opposition party said the young players had made the country proud and demonstrated the enormous potential of Nigerian youths, particularly women.

“Congratulations to our incredible Flamingos on their historic victory over Japan. What a remarkable performance by these young Nigerian women who have just won the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup,” the party said.

The NDC noted that defeating Japan was no small achievement, commending the players for their never-say-die attitude and commitment throughout the competition.

It said the victory had once again highlighted the abundance of sporting talent among Nigerian youths and reinforced the importance of investing in their development.

“The future is bright, and it belongs to you. NDC supports youth in Nigeria,” the statement added.

The party wished the players well, describing their accomplishment as a source of inspiration and national pride.

World.title: Alao, Fagbohun, Babalakin Call for Integrity, Accountability in Varsity Governance
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Professor of African Studies at King’s College London, Abiodun Alao, weekend, called on stakeholders in Nigeria’s university system to prioritise knowledge production over personal interests and wealth accumulation, warning that selfish motives have undermined the purpose of higher education institutions.

Alao made this call at a book presentation of the former Vice-Chancellor of Osun State University, Prof. Olabode Popoola, titled ‘Navigating Stormy Waters’, held at the University of Ibadan.

He stated that many stakeholders in the university system lacked a proper understanding of the fundamental purpose of universities, which he described as the pursuit and production of knowledge.

He said universities should be managed with a strong commitment to academic excellence rather than the pursuit of personal advantage by those entrusted with their leadership.

“People should realise that knowledge is more important than wealth because when you look after wealth, knowledge looks after you,” he said.

He said his experience in university administration had exposed him to the challenges confronting Nigerian universities.

Recalling the crisis that characterised Osun State University’s administration during the former vice chancellor’s tenure, Alao said it emerged from efforts by a determined governing council to curb alleged illegal activities and practices that had become entrenched in the institution.

He explained that the governing council, under the leadership of Prof. Yusuf Ali (SAN), was determined to dismantle what he described as a cash-and-carry economy operating within the university.

According to him, the process was difficult, but the council remained committed to confronting the practices and restoring accountability.

“I witnessed the crisis. Let me even say I witnessed the wild wind that led to the crisis. What actually happened was that the cash-and-carry economy that existed met a new, determined governing council under Prof. Yusuf Ali which was resolute and determined to curb all forms of illegal activities. It wasn’t easy, but we fought it,” he stated.

On preventing recurring crises in universities, Alao who is also the Co-chair, African Community of Practice, argued that conflicts were inevitable in human institutions and that university authorities should focus on building effective structures capable of managing disagreements.

He said rather than attempting to prevent every crisis, university managements should establish institutional mechanisms that would enable them to withstand contradictions and resolve conflicts without derailing their core responsibilities.

“You can’t stem incoming crises because you don’t know the form an impending crisis will take. What you should have are structures for withstanding contradictions. You must have structures that can make you address conflict,” he said.

He added that conflicts were an essential part of human existence, stressing that institutions must be adequately prepared to manage them.

Alao further cautioned that the pursuit of personal benefits by university administrators, governing council chairmen and other stakeholders had increasingly overshadowed the collective responsibility of advancing knowledge.

In his keynote titled, ‘Academic Leadership: The Realities and Ruptures of University Governance’, former Vice-Chancellor of Lagos State University (LASU), Prof. Olanrewaju Fagbohun, explained that effective university leadership required more than academic credentials, noting that vice-chancellors must possess resilience, a clear vision, empathy, courage and the ability to manage competing interests while pursuing institutional reforms.

He identified inadequate funding, strained relationships with staff unions, institutional politics and pressure from competing interests as major challenges confronting vice-chancellors in the management of public universities in Nigeria.

He said leading a public university was significantly different from managing a corporate organisation, as university administrators were often expected to deliver outstanding results despite inadequate resources and institutional constraints.

He recalled that barely three months into his tenure as vice-chancellor, a staff union had accused him of committing 175 offences, describing the experience as an indication of the intense pressures confronting university administrators.

According to him, “While corporate chief executives operate with clearly defined key performance indicators, vice-chancellors are often expected to perform miracles without corresponding resources or the freedom to make critical decisions.”

He explained that the pressures came from different quarters, including staff unions, students, government, university management and other stakeholders, each with competing expectations.

On industrial relations, Fagbohun said while some staff unions played constructive roles in university administration, others could make governance difficult by placing demands without considering the institution’s financial realities.

He recalled a situation in which he appealed to staff unions to give his administration one year to stabilise the university’s finances and generate additional revenue to address outstanding salary arrears.

He said although the unions initially agreed, some later demanded extended breaks for members on the grounds that workers needed time to rest, raising concerns about how the university would generate the revenue needed to meet its obligations if academic activities were disrupted.

The former VC emphasised the funding challenges confronting public universities, noting that administrators were expected to transform their institutions into world-class centres of learning despite restrictions on tuition fees and inadequate government subventions.

He, however, maintained that such challenges were not insurmountable if the university ecosystem operated harmoniously and stakeholders supported the management’s vision.

Fagbohun said his administration had explored partnerships with institutions and developed market-driven academic programmes to generate additional revenue, adding that strong relationships with deans and provosts helped sustain the university during difficult periods.

He cautioned vice-chancellors against allowing institutional politics, ethnicity, religious affiliations and factional interests to influence administrative decisions.

“University administrators must resist pressure to favour particular groups and ensure that appointments and other decisions are based on merit and institutional needs,” Fagbohun stated.

He advised vice-chancellors to avoid confronting every criticism or responding to every provocation, stressing that the ability to maintain focus amid hostility is essential to effective leadership.

“You need a thick skin. You cannot be responding to everything that happens,” he said.

He also identified empathy as an important leadership quality, urging vice-chancellors to understand the challenges confronting students and staff while being honest about what the institution could afford to provide.

In his remarks, the book reviewer and Vice-Chancellor of Edo State University, Iyamho, Prof. Victor Adetimirin, said Nigerian universities must confront the weaknesses, intrigues and institutional failures undermining their development if the country’s higher education system is to overcome its current limitations.

The book, he noted, chronicles the author’s experiences in university administration and the challenges of navigating institutional governance.

He described the publication as a courageous and forthright account of the realities of university leadership, noting that it provided insights into issues that often remain unreported by the print and electronic media.

“The author demonstrated courage by documenting uncomfortable experiences and setting the record straight on developments within the university system,” he stated.

He said the author recognised that sweeping institutional problems under the carpet would only worsen the situation, stressing that meaningful reform required an honest assessment of the weaknesses confronting Nigerian universities.

Adetimirin noted that despite the number of universities in Nigeria and the many vice-chancellors who had successfully completed their tenures, few had documented their experiences and the lessons learnt while navigating the challenges of university administration.

Earlier in his remarks, the Vice Chancellor of the University of Ibadan, Prof. Peter Olapegba, stated that the book offered valuable insights into the complexities, challenges and responsibilities associated with university administration, particularly the difficult decisions and competing expectations confronting institutional leaders.

He noted that leadership required vision, courage, wisdom, resilience and strategic thinking to navigate institutional challenges and remain focused on long-term goals.

According to him, the publication goes beyond documenting the author’s stewardship at the university, providing opportunities for reflection, learning and knowledge sharing among university administrators, scholars and others interested in the governance and development of higher education in Nigeria.

He said one of the enduring foundations of leadership was the accumulation of experiences, including trials, lessons and occasional disappointments, adding that documenting such experiences would provide valuable lessons for others.

“As one who appreciates the demands and responsibilities of university administration, I recognise the courage it takes to lead an institution and the willingness required to reflect honestly on that experience and share insights with others,” he said.

The VC commended the author for the contribution, expressing confidence that the book would encourage discussions on institutional leadership, university governance and the future of education in Nigeria.

In his remarks, the chairman of the occasion and Chairman of Bi-Courtney Group, Wale Babalakin (SAN), urged academics and university administrators to uphold integrity, discipline and objectivity in the discharge of their responsibilities, saying those committed to institutional excellence must be prepared to confront resistance.

He also stressed the importance of documenting professional experiences and knowledge in books to guide younger generations and preserve lessons that could strengthen institutions.

He said individuals who pursued genuine reforms in the academic environment often faced opposition from people who presented themselves as scholars but were more interested in undermining institutional progress.

He described the university environment as one that required intellectual depth, hard work and absolute integrity, noting that the ability to distinguish serious-minded scholars was essential to building enduring institutions.

Commending the author for documenting his experiences, Babalakin said knowledge gained through years of service should be committed to writing so that others could learn from it.

According to him, “The purpose of life should include guiding others through the experiences and lessons acquired over the years.”

In his response, Prof. Olabode Popoola, said his five-year administration rescued the institution from imminent collapse, rebuilt its structures and strengthened its financial sustainability, accountability and academic culture.

He added that his administration was driven by a commitment to the development of the institution, Osun State, Nigeria and humanity.

The Professor of Forest Economics and Sustainable Development explained that he accepted the appointment because he believed he had something meaningful to contribute to the university, adding that his ambition was to transform the institution and establish a system capable of sustaining its growth beyond his tenure.

He said: “The university was in a difficult situation when I assumed office, prompting me to initially adopt persuasion as a means of addressing the challenges and securing the cooperation of stakeholders.”

However, he said when persuasion failed, he had to take difficult decisions, even when such actions meant stepping on toes.

Popoola disclosed that he had documented his activities throughout his five-year tenure, explaining that keeping records of his stewardship had become a personal practice whenever he occupied public office.

“The book is an expanded account of my administration and the developments that took place at the university,” he stated.

World.title: Sack Your Special Adviser On Labour, Niger NLC Tells Gov Bago
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

The Niger State chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has told Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago to sack his Special Adviser on Labour Matters with immediate effect.

The Congress rose from an executive meeting held at the Labour House weekend where it made the request but did not give reason for making the demand.

The meeting was attended by veteran labour leaders and members of affiliate unions.

In a communiqué made available to the press after the meeting, the Congress also asked Governor Bago to begin immediately the implementation of the new N70,000 transport allowance recently approved for workers by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

The communiqué signed by the chairman, Comrade Idris Abdul-Kareem Lafene, and Secretary, Comrade Maria Musa, said the meeting also reached some resolutions which included appreciating the governor for the interest shown to workers in the state.

The meeting, according to the communiqué, however called on the governor to expedite action towards adopting and implementing those demands already reached with the Congress.

World.title: Obinna: Prospera Finance’s Partnership With Shakara Square is to Drive Wellness and Financial Freedom
World.content:
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Prospera Finance Limited, Dr. Joshua Obinna Umesegha, is a seasoned financial expert committed to bridging Nigeria’s financial literacy gap. Drawing from his extensive background as a financial analyst, relationship manager, and credit risk expert, Dr. Umesegha established Prospera Finance to offer tailored financial solutions that prioritize calculated risk management, customer confidentiality, and long-term financial health. In this exclusive interview, he discusses the driving vision behind the firm, navigating macroeconomic volatility, leveraging secure technology, and partnering with Shakara Square to promote the intersection of physical wellness and financial freedom.

Why did you start Prospera Finance? Other companies offer similar services, what specific gap did you set out to fill?

What brought us to this mission is the reality that many people lack financial literacy, even though they constantly handle money and interact with financial opportunities. Having gathered experience as a financial analyst, relationship manager, and credit risk analyst, I felt compelled to take the bull by the horns and guide people onto the right track—and that track is ultimate financial freedom. That is what we are building here at Prospera Finance Limited. Our goal isn’t just to provide financial solutions; it’s to improve our clients’ financial responsibility, heighten their awareness, and ultimately elevate their overall financial health. Health is wealth, not to sound cliché. We want the general public to be fully aware and deliberate about the financial decisions they make.

Looking back at your first two years, or one year officially on the books, what would you consider Prospera’s single biggest achievement?

If you’re counting off the books, it’s been two years; by the books, it’s one year. Looking back, our greatest achievement is earning the trust of our customers. Trust is something we are constantly building and improving. Judging by our current portfolio and the steady stream of referrals it generates, it speaks volumes about what we are doing, the vision of Prospera, and our future. I won’t focus on the physical assets we’ve acquired because trust is the one key that unlocks everything else.

Given Nigeria’s economic volatility and naira fluctuations, many people are sceptical about investing. How do you convince clients to commit their capital?

While we provide tailored financing, what sets Prospera Finance Limited apart is taking calculated risks. We stay strictly aligned with regulatory frameworks, we play by the books. But playing by the books doesn’t mean we can’t formulate our own innovative solutions. We learn from those who came before us in this industry and fine-tune our approach to stay fully compliant. When navigating market and currency volatility, calculated risk is our best strategy. We make sure we thoroughly understand every venture before entering it, ensuring we never overtrade or stretch beyond our capacity. As a risk analyst, I don’t look at risk from a purely defensive standpoint; we actively look for the opportunities embedded within that risk and manoeuvre accordingly.

You are also leveraging technology. What security measures have you put in place to protect customer data from cyber threats?

First, we are certified by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC), which binds us strictly to client confidentiality. We never disclose customer information for convenience. Second, we have established robust internal tools that safeguard data privacy while giving customers full transparency over their information. We engage them through regular newsletters, secure POS terminals, and soon, our new mobile app. By God’s grace, our mobile application will launch very soon. It will allow customers to make transfers, pay bills, and manage investments conveniently from their homes. To ensure absolute security, top-tier cloud engineers have secured both the front-end and back-end architecture. Our customers have nothing to worry about—we have never recorded a single data breach across our POS networks or financial services. We also avoid overspending on technology just because an expensive option is popular. We deploy technology that fits our budget, matches our system requirements, safeguards confidentiality, and builds customer trust.

Prospera recently partnered with Shakara Square for a major fitness event. Why did you choose to collaborate with them?

You can’t execute everything alone in business; you need strong partners and sponsors who bring unique strengths to the table. If a partner has a wider reach or specialized expertise, collaborating shows strategic strength. We partnered with Shakara Square because they have an exceptional audience outreach and share our core values: meeting people’s needs, encouraging healthy living, and building wellness awareness. This platform allows people from various sectors to engage with our brand and understand what Prospera Finance Limited stands for. Shakara Square has built a long-standing reputation around the concept that health is wealth. To guarantee financial freedom for the public, we must align with partners who share that exact philosophy. For us, this isn’t just about brand visibility; it’s about ensuring the longevity and impact of our core mission.

Is this partnership with Shakara Square a one-off campaign, or do you plan to sustain it long-term?

It is definitely a sustainable, long-term partnership. I have known the Shakara Square team for quite some time, and they are a fantastic force to work with. I admire their business ethics, how they treat their customers, how they serve the public, and their top-notch, highly professional media strategy.

If you want to build world-class solutions, you must collaborate with the very best, and Shakara Square fits that role perfectly.

World.title: Tinubu: Benjamin Kalu Is Indeed the President’s Chief Campaigner in Abia
World.content:
By James Nwachukwu

In Abia State, there exists no ambiguity as to who bears President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s message with the greatest passion, consistency, and courage. There is no uncertainty regarding who proclaims the gospel of the Renewed Hope agenda with the most unrelenting fervour. It is the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives and member representing Bende Federal Constituency, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu.

Kalu is, indeed, an ardent and unwavering supporter of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. This devotion is conspicuous to all who observe him. Every opportunity afforded him becomes an occasion to speak of Mr. President and his manifold legacies. From far-reaching economic reforms to the renewal of national infrastructure, from the student loan scheme to bold decisions which others evaded for decades, Kalu enumerates them with boldness and conviction, anywhere and everywhere.

What renders this even more remarkable is that Kalu does not merely speak of Tinubu in public. He speaks of him in private as well. One needs not be intimate with him to discern this truth. In small gatherings, in one-on-one conversations, on the corridors and quiet chambers where there is no crowd to impress and no cameras to perform for, Kalu has continued to speak of President Tinubu with the same undiminished passion. That is how one knows it is genuine, emanating from the very depths of his heart.

Of course, Kalu set out early. Long before many others found their voices, he established the Renewed Hope Partners (RHP) to carry the message of the Renewed Hope Agenda to the hinterlands of Abia State. He did not wait for the campaign season. The message was his concern just to announce to the people the remarkable feats and deliveries of the President. He traversed community after community, town after town, village after village and local government areas, ensuring that ordinary Abians understood what the President was doing and why it mattered for their future.

Interestingly, Kalu’s support for Tinubu extends beyond the shores of Abia as he has not confined this advocacy to the State alone. He has carried the President’s message across the entire South East, speaking for Tinubu in other States, defending his policies on regional platforms, and standing as the President’s foremost voice in the zone.

Remarkably, this is not new for Kalu. In the build-up to the 2023 campaigns, a similar episode unfolded. His campaign office was shot at, riddled with bullets, for campaigning for Tinubu against other presidential candidates in a zone he is adjudged less popular. It was intimidation in its rawest form, I must say. It was an attempt to silence him for standing with Tinubu when it was not popular to do so. Yet, he did not bow. He did not switch allegiance. He did not flee. He stood upon his convictions.

He later won his election, surviving the Obi wave in Abia and the South East. While the wave swept many others away, Kalu stood firm and emerged victorious, proving that courage and conviction can endure even the most formidable political storm.

The same fire was on full display recently during the inauguration of the APC campaign council in Umuahia, the Abia State capital. With the International Conference Centre filled to the brim, the hall was agog, and Kalu spoke so passionately, so clearly, and so fearlessly about Tinubu that no one in that hall was left in doubt.

Of course, it was not a rehearsed speech even though he has a speech before him. Those present noticed that he veered off his script and spoke extempore to his utter convictions and love for Mr. President. This has been in Kalu’s character. It has been his practice. It has been in his totems. It reveals his genuine love for the President. This is a loyalty that is not seasonal, not transactional, and not dependent upon any rented crowd. It comes straight from the heart.

Now, place this against the scenario in Aba on Saturday during the Item Cultural Day in Aba. Item is a large community with three electoral wards in Bende Federal Constituency. Kalu represents the Constituency at the National Assembly.

The indigenes of the community resident in Aba had invited him to the event, and Kalu honoured the invitation. Ordinarily, someone who was completely exhausted after spending his full day in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, for the APC Presidential rally on the same day with President Tinubu amongst a plethora of other dignitaries would have decided to go home to get some rest in his Bende country home. But for his love for his people, Kalu diverted his convoy to Aba to celebrate with his people.

And amid cacophonous noise from a mixed political background, Kalu still delivered Tinubu’s message of Renewed Hope head-on to the crowd. He did not retreat. He stood his ground and spoke for the President during the celebration. The video making the rounds showed that despite the attempt to drown his voice, the mandate anthem of the President permeated the air.

Among his imprint in Item is the attraction of the new University of Medical and Health Sciences for which the lawmaker pledged continued support and assured the people of its full establishment. This is outside the health centers, roads, primary and secondary schools block of classrooms Kalu has attracted to the Item.

Well, he has promised to do more for the people of Item where he also has more allies and appointees than any other place in the 13 electoral wards of Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State.

From the bullets in 2023 to the noise in Aba in 2026, the pattern is the same to try to silence him, but he has spoken even louder for Tinubu. This is what a true chief campaigner does. And that is Kalu, unrelenting, bold, convinced and loving.

While others whisper their support behind closed doors, Benjamin Okezie Kalu shouts it in the open. He did it in Umuahia. He did it in Aba. He has done it across the South East and everywhere.

For President Tinubu, Abia already has its voice for him, and that voice is Benjamin Okezie Kalu, the speaking Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, and come January 2027, President Tinubu will win Abia overwhelmingly, by God’s Grace and the vote of the people.

*Nwachukwu, a public affairs analyst and social commentator writes from Umuahia, the Abia State capital.

World.title: Steyn City property goes to auction as owner racks up R158 000 levy debt
World.content:
For some fortunate buyer, the search for a Steyn City home for sale will end with the bargain of the decade.

In Steyn City, where the average sale price is R4.7 million, and the cheapest flat on the market is R1.9 million, one property is heading to auction for less than R1 million of its market value.

Homeowner racks up 2 years of levies and rates debt

This flat could be a once-in-a-lifetime purchase for a buyer with the funds to bid at auction.



According to the Private Property listing, the homeowner has extensive rates and levies debt. The listing shows R88 611 in arrears on rates and taxes and a further R69 096 in levy arrears, for a total of R157 707.

On similar properties in Steyn City, rates, taxes and levies total R5 700.

This debt breaks down to roughly 27 months of non-payment, excluding interest.



Steyn City is home to some of Gauteng’s most expensive properties.

This particular flat is located at Oasis at Steyn City. Flats in this part of the development routinely sell for above R2 million.

But this flat, which goes to auction on 17 November, has a R1.9 million reserve.



Buyers willing to bid on this 99-square-metre ground-floor unit will get access to 2 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms, and 2 parking bays.

They could also get the home at a bargain.

If it breaks reserve and doesn’t get higher bids, a successful bidder may get the property for less than it sold for in 2023.



In 2023, the unit sold for R2.7 million, according to data from the South African Deeds Registry.

Since 2023, property prices in Steyn City have increased by 8.62%.

This means this unit would be worth R2.93 million today.



Sold for reserve, a bidder would get a 35% discount.

Living in Steyn City

Any buyer will be pleased to find a Steyn City home on sale for this price given the estate’s amenities.

Residents have access to restaurants, an upmarket shopping district, a spa, a championship golf course, horse riding and mountain bike trails.



The 2 000-acre estate has multiple fitness centres, a wellness hub, and a lagoon precinct.

Then there’s the private school, serving pre-primary grades to matric.

Buyers could also enjoy the property’s investment potential.



Ground-floor units in the same complex are let for R25 000. Fully furnished units are let for R30 000.

More Homes heading to auction

Currently, Absa is taking more than 80 homes to auction across the country, some with no reserves.

In Umhlanga Rocks, the bank is auctioning a luxury flat on Lagoon Drive where the owner has racked up R576 014 in rates arrears.



The bank is also selling a handful of repossessed properties.

In Sandown, Sandton, for example, the bank is selling a 4-bedroom home for R5.2 million.

Buyers wanting a bargain in Cape Town can also bid on a property 17 minutes from the City Centre with a R600 000 reserve. Sectional Titles in the area typically sell for closer to R1 million.



These listings come as South African homeowners fall on hard times.

According to the 2026 Old Mutual Savings and Investment Monitor, roughly one-fifth of middle-income South Africans have fallen behind on home loan repayments, up from one-sixth in 2025.

But the problem predates the recent economic stressors.



According to Experian data, in the first quarter of this year, R5.7 billion in new home loan default balances were recorded.

This is a 16.1% reduction compared to the same period last year.

World.title: LIVE | Carling Knockout Cup: Kaizer Chiefs vs Siwelele FC
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will be determined to keep their Carling Knockout Cup campaign on track when they face Siwelele FC in the quarter-finals on Sunday. Image: Kaizer Chiefs website

Kaizer Chiefs will be determined to keep their Carling Knockout Cup campaign on track when they face Siwelele FC in a quarter-final clash at the New Peter Mokaba Stadium in Polokwane on Sunday.

Kick-off is scheduled for 18:00, with Amakhosi chasing a place in the semi-finals and another step towards a record-extending 14th title.
