Kaizer Chiefs are the most successful club in the competition’s history, having won the trophy 13 times.



The Soweto giants booked their place in the last eight with a convincing 3-0 victory over TS Galaxy in the Round of 16.

Wandile Duba was the star of the show, scoring all three goals in a hat-trick that was the first by a Kaizer Chiefs player in the competition since 1987.

KAIZER Chiefs have recent advantage over Siwelele

Sunday’s encounter will be the fourth meeting between the two clubs, with their previous three clashes all taking place in the league.

Each team has recorded one victory, while the other meeting ended in a goalless draw last season.

Kaizer Chiefs won the most recent encounter, beating Siwelele 3-2 at home in September.

This will be their first meeting in cup competition.



Kaizer Chiefs have also avoided defeat in their two previous home matches against Siwelele, recording one victory and one draw.

Different routes to the last eight

Kaizer Chiefs reached the quarter-finals after their impressive win over TS Galaxy, while Siwelele had to negotiate a penalty shoot-out against Polokwane City.

The sides played to a 0-0 draw before Siwelele progressed from the spot to reach the Knockout Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

Duba will have another opportunity to make history. If he scores on Sunday, he will become the first Kaizer Chiefs player since Eric Mathoho in the 2015/16 campaign to score in the club’s opening two rounds of the competition.

KAIZER Chiefs’ impressive Knockout Cup history

Amakhosi have a long record of success in the competition’s knockout stages.

They have reached the semi-finals 22 times previously and will be targeting a 23rd appearance in the last four.

Their most recent quarter-final outing ended in defeat against Mamelodi Sundowns in 2024/25.

Kaizer Chiefs also reached the semi-finals in three successive tournaments between 2017/18 and 2019/20.

Their biggest quarter-final victory since 1996/97 was a 4-0 home win over Dynamos in 2004.

Kaizer Chiefs have also featured in 16 League Cup penalty shoot-outs since 1996/97, winning 13 and losing three. Four of their quarter-final ties during that period have been decided on penalties.

For Siwelele, Sunday’s match represents an opportunity to reach the semi-finals for the first time and continue an impressive debut run in the competition.

Tournament results

Mamelodi Sundowns and Orlando Pirates have already reached the semi-finals.

The fourth and final quarter-final clash will take place between Stellenbosch FC and AmaZulu, also on Sunday, 8 November at 18:00.

Prediction

Kaizer Chiefs to beat Siwelele FC

World.title: Moeneeb Josephs identifies Orlando Pirates’ biggest weakness
World.content:
Orlando Pirates legend Moeneeb Josephs has highlighted what he believes is the Buccaneers’ biggest weakness.

The retired goalkeeper feels the team is well-balanced and capable of conquering Africa, but believes they have one major problem.

Despite scoring more goals than any other team in the PSL last season, Pirates also missed the most chances.



Their inability to kill off matches has been a recurring concern in recent years.

Moeneeb not happy with Pirates in front of goals

Following their 1-0 win over Sekhukhune United in the Carling Knockout Cup, Josephs felt Abdeslam Ouaddou‘s men were wasteful in front of goal.

“For our own sanity, we should kill games off. If I look at this game against Sekhukhune, they thought they were going to be aggressive. In the first half, they were physical, but the way we controlled the ball, it was hard to catch us,” he said on SoccerBeat.



Moeneeb argued that Pirates players were more relaxed in front of goals when leading.

“We need to change our attitude. As soon as we notice our opposition feel defeated, our mindset changes as well. I think that is something that we can work on as well,” he added.

“We need to have a killer instinct and finish things off. It’s like we feel sorry for teams and would rather keep the ball away from them. I see the coach on the side losing his head as well.”



Moeneeb Josephs spent five years with Orlando Pirates, winning six trophies with the Soweto giants.

Do you agree with Moeneeb?

World.title: Former Knysna mayor murder: Alleged hitman arrested
World.content:
Former Knysna executive mayor Aubrey Tsengwa was shot dead in August 2026. Police have arrested a 44-year-old suspected hitman in connection with his murder. Image: X

Police have arrested a 44-year-old suspected hitman in connection with the murder of former Knysna mayor Aubrey Tsengwa, who was gunned down in August.

Detectives from the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT) tracked the suspect to Peddie in the Eastern Cape, where they arrested him during an operation on Friday, 6 November.

National police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe confirmed the arrest on Sunday.



Suspect faces murder charges

Mathe said the arrest followed an investigation into Tsengwa’s murder on 19 August 2026.

Tsengwa was sitting in his vehicle in Knysna with three other occupants when gunmen opened fire, killing him.

The three other occupants survived.

Police have charged the suspect with murder and three counts of attempted murder.

He remains in custody and is expected to appear in the Knysna Magistrate’s Court on Monday, 9 November.

Political killings under spotlight

The arrest comes as the United Democratic Movement (UDM) calls for the PKTT to investigate the murder of its Nelson Mandela Bay councillor, Luxolo Namette, who was shot dead in Motherwell, Gqeberha, on Saturday, 7 November.



The UDM fears Namette’s killing may have been politically motivated, although police have yet to establish a motive.

World.title: AWKWARD! Cyril Ramaphosa to attend Election 2026 results announcement
World.content:
President Cyril Ramaphosa will attend the announcement of the final results of South Africa’s 2026 Local Government Elections on Sunday. Image: X @myanc

President Cyril Ramaphosa will attend the announcement of the final results of South Africa’s 2026 Local Government Elections on Sunday, in what could be a politically uncomfortable occasion for the ANC leader following the party’s poor election performance.

The Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) will announce the results from 18:00 at its National Results Operations Centre at the Gallagher Convention Centre in Midrand, Gauteng.

The ceremony will be broadcast live.



Cyril Ramaphosa has led the ANC to its worst-ever election results this year.

VIDEO | DA emerges as the BIG winner from Elections 2026

ANC LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTION RESULTS SINCE 2000

Year Percentage 2000 59.39% 2006 64.82% 2011 61.95% 2016 53.91% 2021 45.59% 2026 30.77% *

* Not final

Will deliver brief remarks

According to the Presidency, Ramaphosa will attend in his capacity as President of the Republic of South Africa and deliver brief remarks.

However, the occasion comes against the backdrop of a significant setback for the ANC, which has recorded a sharp decline in voter support.

With 99% of votes counted nationally, the governing party was sitting at approximately 30.77% of the vote, compared with 45.59% in the 2021 Local Government Elections.



The result represents a loss of close to 15 percentage points and adds to the political pressure on the ANC leadership following the party’s loss of its national parliamentary majority in the 2024 general election.

Talking point

The ANC’s performance in KwaZulu-Natal has also been a major talking point.

With 99% of votes counted in the province, the uMkhonto weSizwe Party (MK) Party, led by former president Jacob Zuma, was ahead with 34.33% of the vote. The ANC was on 20.28%, narrowly behind the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) on 20.15%.

The ANC’s national leadership has acknowledged the scale of the election setback, with secretary-general Fikile Mbalula describing the outcome as “catastrophic”.

Ramaphosa’s appearance at the IEC ceremony is therefore likely to attract particular attention, as the President delivers remarks while his party faces questions about its declining electoral support and its future in local government.

South Africans went to the polls

South Africans voted on Wednesday, 4 November, to elect representatives to municipal councils across the country.

Special voting took place on 2 and 3 November.

Registered voters were given the opportunity to choose their local representatives and influence decisions affecting service delivery in their communities.

The final results will determine the political make-up of municipal councils across the country, including those where no party has secured an outright majority and coalition arrangements will be required.

World.title: Injury-hit France recall big-name veterans for Springbok Test
World.content:
France coach Fabien Galthie has recalled a clutch of experienced internationals for the country's Nations Championship fixture against South Africa. Image: AFP

France coach Fabien Galthie on Sunday recalled a clutch of experienced internationals for the country’s Nations Championship fixture against South Africa on Friday, 13 November in Paris.

Kick-off is at 22:10 (SA time).

Les Bleus thumped Fiji 54-17 on Saturday in Lyon, but have only won once in the last 10 meetings with the Springboks going back to 2009.



READ | Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicks his way up Springbok points scorers list

Five straight wins for the Springboks

South Africa have beaten France five straight times at the Stade de France, including a one-point quarter-final victory in 2023 on their way to retaining the World Cup.

Galthie recalled 31-year-old hooker Julien Marchand, who had been sidelined since injuring a thigh in early October.

He made his return for his club Toulouse on Saturday and could go straight into the starting line-up to face South Africa’s destructive front row.

France continue to face injury problems in the backs.

Flyhalf Romain Ntamack was forced off with a shoulder injury on his international return on Saturday. France were already without flyhalf Matthieu Jalibert and fullback and goal kicker Thomas Ramos.



Galthie also recalled 32-year-old centre Gael Fickou and 33-year-old winger Teddy Thomas as well as flyhalf Louis Carbonel and winger Gael Drean.

Carbonel has not featured in a France match-day squad since 2022.

Drean, 26, returned to action for his club, Toulon, and scored a try on Saturday, after a six-month lay-off following heart surgery.

World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns players in the CAF Champions League at Loftus Versfeld. Image: Sundowns media

Mamelodi Sundowns starting line up: Williams, Matuludi, Khoza, Ndamane, Modiba, Mokoena, Allende, Morena, Santos, Matthews, Leon.

CAF SUPER CUP: MAMELODI SUNDOWNS VS MC ALGER

The club known as Kabo Yellow qualified for the continental showpiece after winning the 2025/26 CAF Champions League. On the opposite side, MC Agler became the CAF Confederation Cup champions.

Both clubs will be chasing their second CAF Super Cup title, with the winner also set to receive a significant financial reward.



SUNDOWNS BANK ON HOME ADVANTAGE

Miguel Cardoso’s side head into the final in good domestic form, currently sitting at the top of the Betway Premiership standings.

However, Sundowns will be looking to respond after their disappointing early exit from the current CAF Champions League campaign.

Iqraam Rayners could be one of their biggest weapons after scoring five goals in his last five domestic appearances.



The Brazilians could also receive a timely boost from Ronwen Williams and Teboho Mokoena, who have both returned to training ahead of the encounter.

Playing at Loftus Versfeld gives Sundowns an opportunity to use home advantage as they pursue another continental trophy.

USM ALGER ARRIVE WITH CONTINENTAL EXPERIENCE

USM Alger travelled to South Africa early to acclimatise to Pretoria’s conditions ahead of the final. The Algerian outfit have previous experience of winning this competition, having lifted the trophy in 2023.



Coach Lamine N’Diaye will be counting on the experience within his squad, with Mohamed Amine Ramdaoui expected to lead the attacking threat as their leading scorer this season.

Sundowns have a positive record against USM Alger, having beaten the Algerian giants home and away during the 2019/20 CAF Champions League group stage.

However, the Brazilians cannot afford to underestimate their opponents.



USM Alger are expected to rely on a disciplined defensive structure and quick counter-attacks to trouble the hosts.

For Sundowns, the challenge will be turning their home advantage and attacking quality into another continental trophy.

World.title: MK Party demands eThekwini vote audit despite election lead
World.content:
Voting station signage in Cape Town during South Africa’s 2026 municipal elections. The image is used to illustrate the MK Party’s dispute over eThekwini election results. File photo. Image: Husskeyy / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0).

Jacob Zuma’s MK Party has challenged the 2026 municipal election results in eThekwini, demanding an independent audit even as it leads the vote count.

The party alleges that failures in the Electoral Commission of South Africa’s (IEC) results system caused discrepancies between electronically captured figures and voting-station records.

It wants the IEC to suspend processing disputed results and delay their final declaration until the concerns have been investigated.



Why is the MK Party disputing eThekwini results?

The party lodged a formal objection on Friday, 6 November, under Section 65 of the Municipal Electoral Act.

According to SABC News, the MK Party claims a system failure at the eThekwini Results Operations Centre disrupted the transmission and capturing of election results.

It also alleges that some electronic figures do not match the signed results slips completed at voting stations.



The party has requested an independent forensic examination of the affected records. It also wants the IEC to preserve the disputed electronic data and halt further processing while the figures are checked.

However, these remain allegations. The reported discrepancies have not been independently established as evidence of vote manipulation.

MK Party leads despite raising objections

The challenge comes as the MK Party maintains a lead in eThekwini, one of South Africa’s most closely watched municipalities.



The party was ahead of the Democratic Alliance and African National Congress in provisional results on Saturday, although the final outcome had not been declared.

Its objection therefore concerns the integrity of the counting process, rather than simply a demand to overturn an unfavourable result.

The dispute follows earlier tensions involving the party and the IEC. The South African previously reported that the MK Party lost a court challenge over the 2024 election results.



That earlier case is separate from the present objection and does not establish whether the latest allegations are valid.

Can the IEC delay the election results?

Section 65 of the Municipal Electoral Act allows interested parties to challenge irregularities that could materially affect an election result.

The legislation permits the IEC to investigate objections, request further information and hear submissions before making a decision.



If an objection succeeds, the commission may adjust affected results within its legal powers. Certain disputes can also reach the Electoral Court.

The IEC had set Friday, 6 November, as the deadline for objections, although the law allows late submissions to be considered where good cause is shown.

The commission has acknowledged challenges during results capturing in KwaZulu-Natal, including connectivity problems and recounts. However, those difficulties do not, by themselves, establish the irregularities alleged by the MK Party.



Final municipal election results were expected on Sunday, 8 November.

Whether the objection changes that timetable will depend on the IEC’s handling of the dispute.

Should parties be allowed to delay final election results due to disputed vote counts?

World.title: EFF's declining support raises questions
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Daily Maverick associate editor Ferial Haffajee has attributed the EFF’s declining electoral support to what she describes as patronage politics within the party.

The EFF has lost significant ground in the 2026 Local Government Elections, raising questions about its leadership and political strategy.

READ | Malema accuses ANC of empowering DA

Speaking about the party’s performance, Haffajee argued that the party’s involvement in other issues may have distracted it from its political responsibilities.

“We must look to another big occasion, which is the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry, which does show us that the party got engaged in patronage politics, and my view is that that's what's showing up now. You're distracted by other things,” she said.

World.title: ActionSA concludes round of ANC talk
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Post-election coalition negotiations are gathering pace.

ActionSA has confirmed it has concluded its first round of talks with the ANC.

The party's national chairperson, Michael Beaumont, said they held a productive, mutually respectful engagement.

Discussions focused on the principles needed to establish stable and effective coalition governments.

ActionSA said it remains committed to engaging all political parties on the same basis.

The party is poised to play a key role in coalition negotiations in Gauteng, particularly in Tshwane, Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni.
