World.title: Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands in Ukraine
World.content:
MOSCOW - Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure cut power to hundreds of thousands of homes in the Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, authorities and an energy provider said on Sunday.

Ukraine is bracing for a new harsh winter of war as Russia ramps up daily aerial barrages, raining down drones and missiles on the power network.

In the central Dnipropetrovsk region, "more than 600,000 residents of the region have been left without power," power company DTEK said on Telegram after a "night attack has damaged important energy facilities".

It said the company was working to restore electricity but the task was "complicated by repeated attacks".

In another strike, a Russian drone hit "a critical infrastructure facility" in the northeastern Kharkiv region, the mayor of Zlatopil city, Mykola Baksheyev, said on social media.

"Nearly 250,000 customers in the Kharkiv region were left without power," Baksheyev said.

Repair works were underway but "the exact time for restoring power supply is still unknown," he added.

The strikes came a day after Ukraine's energy ministry said a massive attack on energy facilities had plunged residents in five regions into darkness and significantly hampered electricity transmission in Kyiv.

President Volodymyr Zelensky has accused Russia of intensifying strikes to put pressure on Kyiv at US-brokered trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi scheduled for Tuesday and Wednesday.

Russia has battered Ukraine's energy grid and infrastructure throughout its four-and-a-half-year invasion and Kyiv was now entering another war-time winter with temperatures already hovering around freezing.

World.title: Bronkhorstspruit residents still waiting for clean water
World.content:
BRONKHORSTSPRUIT - The local government elections may be over, but for Bronkhorstspruit residents, the fight for clean drinking water continues.

After months of concerns over contamination, residents say they’ve lost faith in the City of Tshwane.

Residents are still without safe drinking water, weeks after contamination left hundreds of people ill.

Mayor Nasiphi Moya says water samples have been sent for testing, and pumping will resume once results confirm the water is safe.

But residents want to know when they’ll have clean water again.

As the new municipal administration takes shape, residents say they cannot afford more delays.

They want clean, safe drinking water and, above all, clear answers on when the taps will run again.

World.title: Electric auto rickshaws reshape India's roads
World.content:
She said adoption accelerated over the past two years as government subsidies, improving vehicle quality and falling operating costs combined to make ownership more attractive.

E-rickshaws first appeared on New Delhi's streets more than a decade ago, often assembled in roadside workshops using Chinese-made batteries fitted to modified pedal-powered tricycles.

But the sector has since eaten into the market for sturdier fossil-fuel-powered three-wheelers, becoming a major industry as manufacturers such as Mahindra expand their share.

The shift has altered the look and sound of Indian cities.

Across northern India, e-rickshaws now queue outside railway stations and bustling markets, replacing the thumping noise of traditional "tuk-tuks".

- Fuel savings -

Mahindra is one of 15 finalists shortlisted for the environmental Earthshot Prize, to be awarded in Mumbai by Prince William on November 17.

For many drivers, however, earnings outweigh environmental benefits.

"Money is coming straight into my pocket," said Afroz Alam, a 31-year-old driver in Hyderabad who switched from a gas-powered model to an EV this year.

The cost of charging his vehicle saves him several hundred rupees a day, helping repay the loan he took out to buy the more expensive electric version.

"It may seem expensive, but then it levels out with the gas money you no longer have to pay," he told AFP.

Analysts agree economics is the key driver of adoption, with falling costs of batteries and rising fuel prices widening the advantage of e-vehicles.

World.title: Can't cook or shower: Indonesians take aim at data centres
World.content:
BATAM - Cooking and bathing became difficult when taps ran dry in Batam, an Indonesian island where residents are protesting as data centres spring up to power the global artificial intelligence boom.

The area had suffered a "long drought" caused by low rainfall, the local water utility operator told AFP, as a strong El Nino cycle exacerbates dry weather.

But, as in other countries, anger has been directed at the data centres, warehouse-like facilities that keep apps and artificial intelligence tools running, with water often used to cool their humming servers.

Frustration is bubbling over in Indonesia and Malaysia -- especially in regions bordering Singapore that are seen as a prime location for new tech facilities.

At first the main reaction was, "thank God industry is coming" to Batam, 54-year-old tradesman Juniardi Adinda Sembiring Gurukinayan told AFP.

But severe recent outages hitting the municipal water service in some Batam communities meant "sometimes I skipped my shower".

"We cannot eat rice without water. We cannot cook vegetables without water," he said.

At the worst point, dozens of angry residents staged spontaneous protests outside Nongsa Digital Park -- a new cluster of data centres and other amenities, designated a special economic zone.

People in the district believe "that the water shortages... are related to the construction of data centres", Juniardi said.

The drought caused the nearby Nongsa Reservoir to run very low, and supply systems were further disrupted by an electrical fault, said Ginda Alamsyah, a spokesman for water utility operator Air Batam Hilir (ABH).

The tech park receives water from a different source, Duriangkang Reservoir, an industry source told AFP.

- 'Smelly, yellowish' -

Authorities in late September told developers they must build plants to desalinate seawater for cooling, to avoid straining local resources.

Companies behind operational or planned data centres at Nongsa Digital Park include the Singapore-headquartered BW Digital, DayOne, and Princeton Digital Group.

Another owner, Hong Kong-based Gaw Capital Partners, said it was "aware of the distress and frustration expressed by local residents in Nongsa and surrounding Batam communities" over water shortages.

To ensure sustainable operations, "our data centre facilities must deploy a combination of advanced engineering, efficient architectural designs, and renewable energy sourcing," it said.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses opposition divisions as 'polygamous family' rivalry
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County on November 8, 2026. [Peterson Githaiga, Standard]

Democracy for the Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed claims of divisions within the Opposition, describing the disagreements among its leaders as normal sibling rivalry in a polygamous family, while insisting that the coalition remains united behind plans to field a single presidential candidate in the 2027 General Election.

Gachagua said the Opposition leaders were committed to working together to challenge President William Ruto, despite their differing opinions on the timing of selecting a joint presidential flagbearer and occasional disagreements among their political camps.

Speaking during a church service in Isinya, Kajiado County, the former Deputy President likened the political differences to children from the same father competing for attention but eventually uniting whenever an external threat emerges.

“The Opposition is united to a man, and we have agreed that we will have a single presidential candidate. Everybody is committed, and we talk on a daily basis. The only challenge is normal petty problems,” he said.

He added that the disagreements should not be interpreted as a breakdown of the coalition, maintaining that such differences were healthy and expected in a broad political alliance.

“Ile shida kidogo ni ya boma, watoto wengi wa baba mmoja. Watoto huko ndani, oh, baba anakupenda kuliko mimi. Mbona ulinunua kiatu kabla mimi? Si hiyo ni kawaida kwa polygamous family?” he posed.

Gachagua said the bigger threat to Opposition unity was not necessarily disagreements among its principals but the conduct of their supporters, social media influencers and political bloggers, whom he accused of fuelling unnecessary tensions through insults and online confrontations.

He cautioned Opposition leaders against allowing overzealous supporters to dictate their political relationships, warning that unchecked political attacks could eventually weaken the coalition and undermine its common objective.

“If there is anything to separate us, it is our supporters and social media bloggers. Wanawakisha moto hakuna, watu wangu na wa Matiang'i wanatukanana na sisi tunakula breakfast pamoja,” he said.

He further claimed that some political influencers associated with his DCP party had been recruited and allegedly paid by individuals opposed to him to attack his leadership and the party.

Gachagua urged coalition principals to exercise restraint and avoid reacting to every provocation from supporters, insisting that political leaders must remain focused on the bigger picture.

“I want to ask leaders in the Opposition, be careful. Don't listen to overzealous supporters and influencers; they will lead you astray. Remain focused,” he warned.

On the question of selecting a joint presidential candidate, Gachagua revealed that differences remained over the appropriate timing, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka proposing that the flagbearer be identified before December, while Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna favoured February and Narc Kenya leader Martha Karua suggested May.

Gachagua, however, argued that selecting a candidate too early could expose the individual to political pressure and possible frustration from the government.

He proposed April next year as a more suitable time, maintaining that the coalition was united on the principle of having one candidate even if its leaders differed on the timing.

The DCP leader also dismissed arguments that academic qualifications, experience or political credentials should determine who becomes the coalition's presidential candidate, insisting that electoral numbers and the support of ordinary Kenyans would ultimately decide.

“As others say they have experience and an agenda in the Opposition, the deciding factor is the numbers. I'm with the people. You say you have capacity, but the person to decide is the voter,” he said.

He added: “Akili nyingi ni nzuri, but bila kura unaweza kaa nayo nyumbani.”

World.title: Mudavadi urges Western Kenya to unite, says region cannot remain on sidelines
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime CS Musalia Mudavadi. [File, Standard]

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi has urged Western Kenya to unite ahead of the 2027 General Election, saying the region must strengthen its political representation to have a greater say in national decision-making.

Speaking during a UDA delegates' meeting in Shitoto village, Mumias East, Kakamega County, he said Western Kenya could not afford to remain on the sidelines while decisions affecting the country were being made.

"2027 is the moment we must change the narrative. We must make sure that we are at the table where decisions are made. We cannot afford to remain spectators when the future of our country and our region is being determined," he said.

Mudavadi said parliamentary influence depended on numbers, arguing that electing more MPs would give the region a stronger voice in key parliamentary committees, including the Budget Committee.

"Parliament exercises authority in its own right. We want more MPs so that we can have a say in the Budget Committee and other important committees. These positions are secured through numbers, and numbers matter when decisions affecting the country are being made," he said.

Turning to the opposition, Mudavadi described its leaders as divided and challenged them to present clear manifestos outlining what they would offer Kenyans.

He said the divisions within the opposition would work in President William Ruto's favour as he seeks re-election in 2027, expressing confidence that he would win in the first round.

"We want Ruto to win without a petition. We want to thrash them in the first round," he said.

World.title: Family identifies two security officers involved in Abshir Abdi abduction
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

LSK president Charles Kanjama leads members in a protest over the disappearance of lawyer Abshir Abdi. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

The family of Nairobi lawyer Abshir Ahmedsadak Abdi has identified two security officers alleged to have taken part in their kin's abduction, even as his colleagues threatened mass protests to push for his release.

The Law Society of Kenya (LSK) said the two names have been forwarded to the police to aid in investigations and demanded that the office of the Inspector General of Police, Douglas Kanja, speed up the probe into the abduction.

"One is named Siad and the other is Hussein, and we want them released for investigation, arrest, prosecution, conviction, sentencing and imprisonment," said LSK.

The revelation came during a demonstration led by (LSK outside the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police and other towns yesterday .

Abshir was forcibly taken on November 1 along Muchai Road, his vehicle was pursued and intercepted by armed individuals in two vehicles before he was seized.

While state security agencies have denied holding him in custody, court filings and colleagues suggest his abduction may be connected to his professional work representing clients in high-profile cases involving senior police officers.

Furthermore, the LSK presented additional names of security personnel linked to the incident, demanding immediate legal action against Chief Inspector Vitalis Kibet, Inspector Kennedy Kimani Karanja, Siad Mohammed, Abdurahman of the Anti-Terrorism Police Unit (ATPU), and KDF officer Ali Hussein.

The leadership voiced their frustration over the state's inaction and the alarming pattern of extrajudicial actions targeting officers of the court. Representatives insisted that lawyers must be allowed to execute their duties without fear of intimidation, torture, or abduction.

"We demand that the officers involved be handed over, arrested, prosecuted, and convicted. We will stand in the courts, in the streets, and in the boardrooms until abductions come to an end," they said in a statement.

The LSK has issued a stern ultimatum to the police command, including the president, DIG Gilbert Masengeli, Inspector General Douglas Kanja, and senior commanders. If Abshir is not released safely and the identified suspects are not formally charged in court by Monday, the LSK warned it will initiate private prosecutions itself.

Furthermore, the society threatened to bring activities to a complete shutdown and demand the immediate resignation of Kanja, Masingeli and Minister for Security Kipchumba Murkomen, carrying their demonstrations to Parliament and State House if necessary.

As court proceedings continue under a habeas corpus application at the Milimani High Court, the legal fraternity remains resolute: the protest at Jogoo House is merely the beginning of an unyielding campaign for justice and the rule of law.

In Nakuru, lawyers protested within the Law Courts, calling for his production.

“It is shocking that one of our colleagues was picked and today we do not know where he is. Unless we voice our concern, there will be complete lawlessness in the country,” said LSK member Ekaterina Handa. “Our lives matter and silencing lawyers is silencing justice. we will not relent until we get justice.”

Rift Valley LSK Chair Wangari Mwangi said it was shocking that the alleged abduction was captured on CCTV.

She rubbished the narrative that the missing lawyer was involved in a crime syndicate, maintaining that he should have been arrested and charged in court. [Additional reporting by Daniel Chege]

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Kenyan cult leader sentenced to 200 years in prison over the deaths of 190 children
World.content:
A Kenyan cult leader has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murder of 191 people, all but one of them children, in a campaign of abuse and forced fasting.

Paul Mackenzie, founder of the Good News International Church, was sentenced Friday alongside more than two dozen others at the Mombasa High Court.

Mackenzie preached that the world would end in August 2023 and that followers needed to fast in order to reach heaven. According to a Kenyan Senate report into the deaths, his teachings were based on “doomsday or end-times” beliefs. Children were scheduled to die first, followed by young people and women. Men were expected to stay alive long enough to bury the bodies before dying.

Mackenzie’s sentencing comprised of 100 years’ imprisonment for the murder of those who starved and 100 years for those who died by direct homicide.

In her sentencing remarks, Lady Justice Diana Kavedza said she did not impose the death penalty because it could strengthen the convicts’ belief that dying would reunite them with Jesus, rather than deter them. She also wanted to leave open the possibility that they could help locate the remains of missing children.

“In the respectful view of this court, such a sentence (the death penalty) would therefore fail to achieve deterrence,” she said.

Kavedza said 161 of the victims were children aged 9 or younger. Twenty-two were between 10 and 13 years old, and five were between 14 and 16. The ages of two others could not be established. She also said that several of the convicts’ children remained missing and were presumed dead.

The judge added that 183 of the 191 victims died from starvation, including 182 children and one adult. The remaining eight victims, all children, were suffocated, strangled or beaten to death.

Mackenzie had persuaded followers to abandon their homes and move to Shakahola Forest, in eastern Kenya, promising that fasting there would bring them closer to God and prepare them for heaven.

The court found that religious teachings were used to enforce the fast. Guards controlled followers’ movements and prevented them from leaving. Those who resisted were forced to comply, while children were restrained, denied food and punished when they tried to eat or escape.

Mackenzie was convicted of murder last month. In her ruling, Kavedza described how he used sermons and written materials to convince followers that the outside world was evil and that salvation could only be found in the forest. Messages extracted from his phone, including WhatsApp exchanges, showed that he had communicated with followers before they’d moved to Shakahola Forest.

Kavedza said most of those convicted hadn’t shown any remorse for their actions. Mackenzie smiled several times during Friday’s sentencing.

Survivors testified that deaths in the forest were celebrated as “weddings to Jesus,” with those who died regarded as “heroes of faith,” Kavedza said.

Postmortem findings cited by the judge showed that starvation was not the only cause of death. Some victims died from suffocation, neck compression or head injuries.

Authorities began exhuming bodies from Shakahola in April 2023 after reports that people had died while following Mackenzie’s teachings. They have recovered more than 400 bodies so far. The 191 murder convictions relate to the victims in the case decided last month, while further charges could follow.

Stephen Mwiti, whose six children died in Shakahola, told Reuters that his wife had taken his family there to fast. She was among those convicted in the case.

Questioning the decision to make children fast, Mwiti said: “Even if the adults had agreed to fast, what about the children?” He said no outcome in the case could undo the loss of his family.

Rodgers Shibutse, a Nairobi resident who identified his mother’s remains among those exhumed in February 2024, told CNN after the sentencing Friday: “I cannot say that I am 100% satisfied. It (the verdict) is not enough to pay for the life of my mum, but we have no other choice. At least, he (Mackenzie) cannot finish the 200 years in jail and will die eventually.”

This story has been updated with developments.

World.title: AI nerves reinforce age-old investing lesson: Get diversified
World.content:
A $2.5 trillion wipeout for the Nasdaq Composite this week is reminding even the smallest investors just how reliant we’ve all become on the success of the artificial intelligence buildout.

As AI stocks tumbled Thursday, the major indexes dropped sharply, with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq each posting their worst day in 19 months. The Democrat sweep in the midterm elections is accelerating concerns that moratoriums and other public policy hurdles could slow the pace of AI data center construction.

The recent volatility is unnerving, but it reinforces the importance of diversification: Investing in a mix of stocks, bonds, commodities and other assets can help make sure a portfolio isn’t too reliant on a few blockbuster stocks — and can help you weather rough times.

Many portfolios and 401(k)s became increasingly AI-heavy as tech companies’ market values surged and grew to comprise larger portions of benchmark indexes like the S&P 500.

The recent tech-driven selloff “is a wake-up call for investors who may have drifted away from a well-diversified portfolio,” Arun Sundaram, senior vice president for investment strategy at CFRA Research, told CNN.

That wake-up call means it’s time for investors to put in some work to ensure they are diversified.

AI everywhere

Over the past four years, AI has become the dominant force in the stock market, boosting the share prices of technology companies, semiconductor chipmakers and other businesses involved in the data center buildout.

Chipmakers make up nearly one-fifth of the S&P 500’s market value. The top 10 stocks in the index — nine of which are tech stocks — account for almost 40 percent of the index’s market value. As tech stocks have soared in recent years, major indexes like the S&P 500 have become more concentrated, which can make it feel harder to diversify.

The AI boom sent the S&P 500 soaring 88 percent between November 2022 — when OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT for public use — and Thursday’s rout, lifting the value of portfolios and 401(k)s. Since AI supercharged much of the index’s gains, many portfolios are now heavily exposed to AI and underprepared if there were ever a severe decline in stocks tied to the buildout.

Seeing a lot of red in your portfolio can be unsettling, but it’s essential to remain calm and avoid selling in panic, portfolio managers said. It’s important to be disciplined about how you take action.

How to diversify

There’s no one-size-fits-all strategy for investing, and it largely depends on your age, time horizon and risk tolerance.

Trying to find the best time to buy and sell is considered a fool’s errand. Rather, investors can use different strategies so their portfolio is better diversified in the long run.

Investing in health care stocks, long-term bonds or buying specific exchange-traded funds can be a good bet when there are concerns about AI stocks declining, said David Bailin, founder and chief executive officer at the CIO Group.

Health care is one sector that can fare well regardless of what happens with AI. The bond market sell-off in recent months pushed yields upward to relatively attractive levels that can provide strong long-term income for investors. Bailin said he also likes active futures funds, which provide exposure to investing strategies that try to maintain a low correlation with stocks and bonds. That can help balance out losses when stocks decline.

Investors can be hesitant to dig into the weeds of their portfolio, but it’s critical to be proactive and to make sure you’re aware of what you hold, especially after such a strong run for tech stocks in recent years.

“Be mindful of the hidden concentrations in portfolios,” Bailin told CNN. “You can do something about them.”

Investors should be careful not to dump all their AI stocks. Tech stocks are high-growth stocks when times are good, contributing strong returns to portfolios. But investors should be thinking about how to hedge against their exposure by investing in industries that have less correlation to AI, like health care and consumer staples.

“Diversification doesn’t eliminate losses, but it reduces the extent to which a financial plan depends on any one part of the market,” said Tomas Geoghegan, founder at Beacon Hill Private Wealth.

Ultimately, make sure you are comfortable with what’s in your portfolio and that it matches your risk tolerance and lifestyle goals. Investing in commodities like gold, high-quality bonds and cash equivalents can also provide diversification.

“Diversification allows investors to feel more comfortable that their portfolios can weather volatility,” said Erin Kolo, manager of PWM equity and fixed income research at Baird.

World.title: Building owned by Saudi oil giant damaged in missile attack on Riyadh’s financial district
World.content:
A building belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco in the financial district in the capital Riyadh has been damaged in a missile attack.

The strike in King Abdullah Financial District was reported after Saudi Civil Defense issued ‌an early-warning ⁠alert of a potential threat to the city.

Video circulating on social media and verified by CNN shows damage to several floors of the Aramco building, with windows seen blown out. But Saudi authorities said the impact was minimal.

“An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack,” on Sunday, according to the official Saudi news agency, citing a source at the Saudi Energy Ministry.

“The incident resulted in falling shrapnel that caused minor damage to the building, with no injuries or fatalities reported,” the agency reported.

However, one witness said they saw ambulances heading to the area.

CNN has reached out to the Information Ministry by email for further details.

The Houthis, who have fired missiles and drones towards multiple targets across Saudi Arabia over the last three months, have not claimed responsibility.

Multiple loud booms were ⁠heard in the Saudi capital ⁠Riyadh early Sunday.

The Saudi led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed two cruise missiles in Riyadh and the southern region. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki wrote in a post on X that air defenses also “intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh.”

Saudi defense challenges

The missile attacks on Riyadh came a day after Yemen’s Houthi-run health ministry said Saudi airstrikes had ‌killed ‌at least ​33 ​people near the capital Sanaa, including women and children.

“We will punish the Saudi regime for its crimes against the Yemeni people,” said Mahdi al-Mashat, a senior Houthi official, on Saturday.

Last month, 13 people were killed in one missile strike on Riyadh’s international airport, and several more died in other strikes on the airport.

The Houthis have said they will continue firing missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia so long as the Kingdom carries out airstrikes against the parts of Yemen they control and enforces a blockade against its territory.

Saudi Arabia spent $83 billion on defense last year, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, putting it firmly among the top ten military spenders worldwide. It has acquired US fighter jets as well as Patriot and THAAD air defense systems, and a range of advanced weaponry from France and the United Kingdom.

But the Saudis have a lot to defend: a country roughly one-fifth the size of the US, with threats on three sides – from Iran, Iranian-backed militias in Iraq, and the Houthis.

The Saudis are intercepting many of the missiles and drones fired by the Houthis. But some get through. The defense ministry faces difficult choices in distributing the existing systems with so many installations vulnerable to attack.

The Houthis have learned to combine ballistic and cruise missiles with long-range drones to overwhelm Saudi defenses, according to analysts.

In Yemen, the Saudi-backed coalition is trying to prevent the Houthis from advancing further south towards the port of Aden, which is held by the internationally-recognized government.

The Houthis have frequently targeted Aden’s airport with missiles in recent weeks, after taking a stretch of Yemen’s Red Sea coast in September.

Hostilities between the Houthis, who are backed by Iran, and Saudi Arabia reignited in July, shattering a 2022 UN-brokered ceasefire that had largely halted fighting ⁠between the ‌two sides.

Ibrahim Dahman, Teele Rebane and Farida Elsebai contributed reporting.

World.title: National Bank of Egypt increases yield on Platinum certificates
World.content:
The National Bank of Egypt (NBE) has decided to raise the annual yield on its fixed-rate Platinum certificates of deposits.

The rate is now 18.75 percent for certificates with monthly interest payouts, and 18.85 percent for those with quarterly payouts – an increase of one percentage point for each, up from the previous rates of 17.75 percent and 17.85 percent respectively.

The CEO of the NBE, Mohamed al-Etreby, announced that the bank’s Asset and Liability Committee (ALCO) approved the adjustment to the interest rates on these certificates.

They are available to customers through all NBE branches and the bank’s digital applications, effective Sunday, November 8, he said.

Yield Rates

The increase applies to two types of Platinum fixed-yield certificates, which differ in the frequency of interest payouts.

The yield on the Platinum certificate with monthly interest payouts has increased from 17.75 percent to 18.75 percent, while the yield on the Platinum Certificate with quarterly interest payouts has risen from 17.85 percent to 18.85 percent.

Consequently, the annual yield for the certificate with monthly interest payouts has risen to 18.75 percent, while the certificate with quarterly interest payouts now offers 18.85 percent—a difference of 0.10 percentage points.

Return on LE 100,000

Calculating the return on an investment of LE 100,000 illustrates the difference between the two certificates, based on the announced annual rates:

Platinum certificate with monthly returns: The annual return is LE 18,750, equivalent to LE 1,562.50 per month.

The annual return is LE 18,750, equivalent to LE 1,562.50 per month. Platinum certificate with quarterly returns: The annual return is LE 18,850, equivalent to LE 4,712.50 every three months.

These calculations show that a certificate with a quarterly payout frequency offers an annual return that is LE 100 higher for every LE 100,000 invested, whereas a certificate with a monthly payout frequency allows for more regular receipt of returns throughout the year.

Interest Rate Hikes

The adjustment to the yields on “Platinum” certificates follows a decision by the Central Bank of Egypt’s Monetary Policy Committee to raise key interest rates by 100 basis points during its meeting on Thursday, October 29.

The CBE’s decision included raising the overnight deposit rate to 20 percent, the lending rate to 21 percent, and the main operation rate to 20.5 percent.

Additionally, the discount rate was increased to 20.5 percent.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Palestinian Civil Defense receives 1,500 distress calls from Gaza Strip amid heavy rains
World.content:
The Palestinian Civil Defense announced on Saturday that it has received over 1,500 distress calls since the onset of the current weather depression.

It warned of a worsening humanitarian situation across the Gaza Strip—a region already facing catastrophic conditions—as tens of thousands of tents housing displaced people have been flooded, residential buildings have sustained damage, and there is a critical shortage of resources needed to respond to the crisis.

In statements reported by the Palestinian news agency “Sanad,” the Civil Defense noted that heavy rainfall has caused the flooding of camps and tents in various parts of the Strip.

The agency urged the international community not to overlook the dire humanitarian conditions in Gaza.

Furthermore, the Civil Defense called upon the world to address the severe humanitarian plight faced by Palestinians in Gaza, requesting the provision of tents capable of protecting people from rain, wind, and cold, alongside the urgent delivery of essential relief supplies.

Ongoing field efforts

As part of its field response, the Palestinian Civil Defense deployed 30 teams across various areas of the Gaza Strip to address distress calls, drain floodwaters, rescue affected families, and secure buildings at risk of collapse.

These efforts are ongoing, though responding to every report has proven difficult due to a critical shortage of equipment, machinery, and fuel.

The Government Media Office reported that approximately 70,000 tents were flooded within the first 12 hours of the storm, with initial material losses estimated at around three million dollars.

The Gaza Municipality further reported that approximately 60 millimeters of rain fell on the city between Friday night and Saturday afternoon.

Devastating rainfall

The rainfall led to the collapse of residential buildings that had already been damaged by Israeli bombardment.

Collapses were recorded in Gaza City, the al-Bureij refugee camp, and the al-Nuseirat refugee camp, while two individuals sustained injuries when a wall of a building collapsed in the northern part of Gaza Strip.

The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned that heavy rainfall and the flooding of shelters pose immediate risks to displaced persons—particularly those residing in low-lying areas or damaged buildings.

The OCHA has called for the entry of winter supplies, heavy machinery, spare parts, and fuel to bolster the humanitarian response.

These developments unfold amidst a severe shelter crisis; the Government Media Office estimates that approximately 162,000 out of 270,000 tents are now unfit for use.

With the onset of winter, the territory is in urgent need of interventions to provide safe shelter for hundreds of thousands of displaced people.

World.title: Egyptian Football Association to dismiss Hossam Hassan
World.content:
Officials at the Egyptian Football Association (EFA) have decided to dismiss Hossam Hassan as the head coach of the Egyptian national team.

Al-Masry Al-Youm learned that EFA officials have resolved to part ways with Hossam Hassan and Ibrahim Hassan following various recent controversies.

The EFA has determined that the upcoming matches against Malawi, as part of the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, will be the final games for the current coaching staff.

Tarek Soliman will take charge of the team on the touchline for the matches against Malawi, as Hossam Hassan is currently serving a three-match suspension.

According to the source, the most likely successor to Hossam Hassan will be an Egyptian head coach, with several candidates under consideration—particularly Hossam al-Badry and Ali Maher.

The decision is expected to be officially announced following consultations with the EFA’s Technical Director, Shawky Gharib.

Malawi match

The final decision will be reached following the formal announcement of the coaching staff’s dismissal and the completion of the two matches against Malawi—especially given that some are calling for the appointment of a foreign head coach.

There were several suggestions to postpone the announcement of the decision until after the international window this November, so as not to affect the national team’s performance in the matches against Malawi.

The Egyptian national team will enter a closed training camp this November in preparation for their two matches against Malawi, which form the third and fourth rounds of the qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations.

The first leg will be hosted at Cairo International Stadium on November 13 at nine pm, while the return leg will take place on November 17 at Bingu National Stadium, at three pm (Malawi time).

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: FM reaffirms Cairo’s legal position on Turkish-Libyan maritime MoU
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty reaffirmed Egypt’s established legal position on the Turkish-Libyan maritime memorandum of understanding during a meeting on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with Libya’s Acting Foreign Minister Taher al Baour.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of taking Egypt’s concerns into account regarding maritime boundary delimitation, in light of the brotherly ties between the two countries and in accordance with international law and the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, in a manner that serves their shared interests.

The meeting also addressed ways to strengthen cooperation between the two countries, particularly in the economic, trade and energy sectors.

Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Ambassador Nader Zaki said Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s firm support for a political solution in Libya through an inclusive dialogue owned and led entirely by Libyans, based on broad national consensus and free from external dictates or interference, in a way that serves the interests of the Libyan people and preserves stability.

Abdelatty underscored Egypt’s keenness to further strengthen bilateral relations and build on their recent momentum. He also highlighted the importance of holding the next session of the joint higher committee to advance cooperation across various fields.

He further stressed the need to provide additional facilities for Egyptian students in Libya and improve arrangements for the Egyptian community residing there.

For his part, al Baour expressed his deep appreciation for the close ties between the two countries, praising the significant progress in bilateral relations.

He said Libya looks forward to benefiting from Egyptian expertise in various fields and supporting efforts to boost the Libyan economy, while commending the contributions of the Egyptian community and Egyptian companies operating in Libya.

World.title: FM discusses energy cooperation with Libyan counterpart
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty met on Saturday, November 7, 2026, with Libyan Acting Minister of Oil and Gas Khalifa Al-Sadiq at the newly established premises of the Egyptian Embassy in Tripoli to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in the energy sector.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of expediting the implementation of joint projects, including the construction and connection of gas pipelines between the two countries and expanding cooperation in petroleum products.

He also called for swiftly completing projects to refine Libyan crude oil in Egypt for re-export, rehabilitating Libyan refineries and finalizing electricity interconnection projects between the two countries as soon as possible.

For his part, Al Sadiq expressed appreciation for the ongoing cooperation between the two countries in technical fields related to energy, outlining current technical cooperation in oil, gas and electricity.

He affirmed Libya’s commitment to continuing the implementation of ongoing joint projects and announced plans to visit Cairo soon to continue discussions on technical cooperation with Egypt’s ministers of petroleum and electricity.

World.title: Liberia’s Billion-Dollar Bet: Boakai Sends Record US$1.54 Billion Budget to Lawmakers as Questions Linger Over Revenue Windfall
World.content:
Liberia’s proposed 2027 budget is the biggest in the country’s history, promising higher pay for teachers and police, more money for hospitals and a plan to repay nearly US$60 million owed to the state pension fund. But it rests on a revenue milestone that was lifted in part by a one-off mining payment, and the government has yet to explain how it will keep the money coming.

By Rodney D. Sieh

MONROVIA, Liberia – Liberia’s government on Friday asked lawmakers to approve a US$1.538 billion spending plan for 2027, the largest in the West African nation’s history, betting that a recent surge in tax collections can pay for higher wages, new hospital equipment and a long-delayed fix for public-sector pensions.



Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan delivered the draft budget and President Joseph Nyuma Boakai’s budget message to House Speaker Richard Nagbe Koon on November 6. The plan is about 18 percent larger than the current year’s revised US$1.302 billion budget.

Boakai titled his message “A Growing Budget for Bigger Impact,” tying the plan to the ARREST Agenda, his government’s development blueprint. He told lawmakers the budget was bigger not only in size but in its potential to change lives, and urged them to pass it quickly.

The pitch leans heavily on one number. In September, Liberia’s domestic revenue crossed US$1 billion for the first time in its 179-year history. How durable that figure is – and how much of it reaches ordinary Liberians – is likely to dominate the debate in the Capitol over the coming weeks.

The billion-dollar question

On September 16, the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) reported that collections for the year had reached just over US$1.005 billion. That is roughly 63 percent more than the government collected in 2023, the year before Boakai took office, when revenue stood at about US$612 million.

Boakai’s budget message presents the milestone as proof that the state can now finance its own development. Economists and opposition lawmakers are likely to ask how much of it will repeat.

A large share came from a single source. The 2026 budget counted a US$200 million signature bonus from steelmaker ArcelorMittal, part of a renegotiated iron ore deal. The company was the country’s biggest taxpayer this year, accounting for about US$270 million of collections. LRA Commissioner General James Dorbor Jallah has argued that Liberia would have neared the billion-dollar mark even without the bonus.

The underlying trend is more modest. Stripping out one-off payments, the LRA’s monthly collections ran at around US$88 million between January and July – a pace that would yield roughly US$1.06 billion over a full year. The 2027 budget asks for close to US$1.54 billion.

The Finance Ministry’s summary of the budget does not say how much of the 2027 total will come from domestic taxes, how much from donors, and how much from borrowing. Nor does it name new tax measures. Ngafuan disclosed in August that ministries and agencies had initially requested about US$1.92 billion for 2027, showing the pressure on the budget even before lawmakers add their own priorities.

The government is targeting US$1.3 billion in domestic revenue by December; the LRA’s own forecast is higher, at US$1.42 billion. Whether the 2027 plan is built on the target, the forecast or the underlying monthly pace is the first question lawmakers are likely to put to the finance minister.

At the clinic, the classroom and the payslip

For most Liberians, the budget will be judged less by its total than by whether hospitals have medicine, teachers are paid and pensions are honoured.

Health. Spending rises 22 percent, from US$110.9 million to US$135.8 million. The money is meant to staff and equip the New Redemption Hospital in Monrovia, buy dialysis machines and other equipment for the John F. Kennedy Medical Center (US$5.3 million), keep medicines flowing to rural clinics through a community pharmacy programme (US$1 million) and launch a national hepatitis B response (US$800,000). Even so, health takes under 9 percent of the budget, well short of the 15 percent African governments pledged in the 2001 Abuja Declaration.

Education. The sector gets US$163.5 million, up 13.9 percent from US$143.6 million. The headline item is US$7 million to continue renovating the University of Liberia. Public schools in Monrovia, where students have protested over conditions this year, get US$1.5 million for repairs.

The change teachers are most likely to feel is a new pay floor across government schools: US$650 a month for those with a master’s degree, US$400 with a bachelor’s, US$240 with an associate degree or B-Certificate, and US$200 with a C-Certificate.

Wages. The government says more than 17,000 people will benefit from pay changes – nearly 13,000 existing workers getting raises and about 4,350 new hires, including volunteers. They include 1,934 police officers, 616 staff of the Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency who will get a 15 percent raise, and 358 health workers. From January, no government director will earn less than US$500 a month.

Pensions. In one of the budget’s most significant admissions, Boakai confirmed the government owes nearly US$60 million to the National Social Security and Welfare Corporation (NASSCORP) in employer contributions it never paid. From 2027, the government says it will pay its full 6 percent share on time and clear the arrears in instalments – a promise retiring civil servants will watch closely.

Youth and women. The budget sets aside US$2 million for commercial motorcyclists, including roadside rest stops, and funds 1,400 new recruits for the army and police. It provides US$3 million for the national football team, the Lone Star, plus US$650,000 for former players. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection gets a 77 percent increase, while US$2.5 million is earmarked for small businesses, mostly run by women, and US$3 million for school feeding.

What lawmakers will want to know

The ministry’s summary leaves several gaps that the Legislature’s budget committee is likely to probe in hearings.

It does not give a dollar figure for the 77 percent rise at the gender ministry, or say how much of the total goes to salaries rather than roads, clinics and schools. It does not say over how many years the NASSCORP debt will be repaid. And it is silent on agriculture – the “A” in the ARREST Agenda – a sector that has received less than 1 percent of recent budgets despite employing a large share of Liberians.

The priorities themselves invite scrutiny. The football team’s US$3 million allocation is three times what the government plans to spend keeping essential medicines in rural clinics.

Liberia’s fiscal year now runs from January to December, so lawmakers have less than two months to pass the plan. Boakai has asked them to act quickly. The size of the budget, and the questions over how it will be paid for, suggest the debate will not be brief.

World.title: Liberia Pays £5.95 Million to IMO, Remains Top Financial Contributor to Global Maritime Body
World.content:
Annual contribution accounts for approximately 15 percent of IMO’s operating budget as Liberia reaffirms commitment to safe, secure and sustainable international shipping.

LONDON, United Kingdom — Liberia has paid £5,946,633 (approximately £5.95 million) in annual assessed contributions to the International Maritime Organization (IMO), reinforcing its position as the organization’s largest financial contributor and one of the leading voices in global maritime governance.

Liberia’s Maritime Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer, Cllr. Neto Zarzar Lighe Sr., presented a symbolic cheque for the amount to IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez during a ceremony in London on November 6, 2026.



Commissioner Lighe said the timely payment underscores Liberia’s commitment to the IMO, its institutional programs and the continued development of international shipping.

As the world’s largest ship registry, Liberia contributes approximately 15 percent of the IMO’s annual operational budget through its assessed financial contributions.

Speaking during the presentation, Lighe emphasized that Liberia considers its financial obligations to the organization a serious national responsibility, particularly given its influence in the international maritime industry.

“Liberia takes its obligations to the IMO as a serious national obligation. As a global maritime leader and Category-A member of the IMO Council, we remain firmly committed to fulfilling our responsibilities promptly and supporting the Organization’s vital mission of advancing safe, secure, efficient, and environmentally sustainable international shipping,” he said.

Receiving the symbolic cheque, Secretary-General Dominguez expressed appreciation to the Liberian Government for meeting its financial obligations on time and maintaining its longstanding commitment to the organization.

Dominguez also recognized that Liberia’s contribution to the IMO extends beyond financial support, highlighting the country’s active participation in the organization’s technical working groups, committees and Council deliberations.

He described Liberia’s representation as effective, efficient and highly engaged, noting its important role in advancing the IMO’s mandate and strengthening international maritime cooperation.

Liberia has consistently maintained an influential presence within the IMO, reflecting the country’s strategic importance to international shipping through its extensive ship registry.

Commissioner Lighe was accompanied at the presentation ceremony by Liberia’s Permanent Representative to the IMO, Ambassador Robert Wilmot Kpadeh; Alternate Permanent Representative, Dr. Harry Conway; and other officials of the Liberia Permanent Mission to the IMO.

The latest payment further reinforces Liberia’s standing as a responsible flag State, a dependable international maritime partner and a major contributor to global maritime governance.

World.title: Liberia: China Signals Readiness to Expand Agricultural Imports, Eyes Investment in Processing Sector
World.content:
Vice President Jeremiah Koung secures commitment from Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang on market access for Liberian cocoa, coffee and dried chili peppers, while Beijing pledges continued development support and encourages Chinese investment.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

MONROVIA — China has expressed readiness to increase imports of agricultural products from Liberia, including cocoa, coffee beans and dried chili peppers, as the two countries explore ways to expand trade, attract investment and strengthen economic cooperation.



The commitment was conveyed by Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang during bilateral discussions with Liberia’s Vice President Jeremiah Kpan Koung Sr. in Shanghai on November 5, according to a press release from the Office of the Vice President.

Vice Premier Ding identified the submission and approval of eligible Liberian exporting companies as the next practical step toward accessing the Chinese market. He explained that agricultural products such as dried chili peppers, coffee beans and cocoa from African countries, including Liberia, had been granted access under existing market arrangements.

He encouraged Liberia to submit a list of companies interested in exporting these products to China for the necessary approval procedures, after which successful applicants could begin trading.

The discussions followed Vice President Koung’s participation in the opening of the Ninth China International Import Expo, where he called for greater efforts to translate China’s zero-tariff policy into increased exports, domestic processing and employment opportunities for Liberians.

Ding also expressed China’s willingness to strengthen agricultural trade facilitation with African countries and encouraged Liberia to take advantage of the China International Import Expo and other commercial platforms to connect local producers with Chinese buyers.

Welcoming the opportunity, Vice President Koung identified rubber, cocoa, coffee and other agricultural products as priority areas for expanded trade cooperation.

He emphasized that Liberia wants foreign investment to go beyond the export of raw materials by creating opportunities for domestic processing, skills development and employment.

“Our objective is to create jobs, develop Liberian skills, and retain more value within our economy,” Koung said.

He invited Chinese businesses to explore investment opportunities in Liberia’s special economic zones, particularly in rubber processing, agro-processing and light manufacturing.

In response, Vice Premier Ding said China would encourage more Chinese companies to invest in Liberia and called for continued support to facilitate their operations.

He also identified iron ore mining as an important area of bilateral cooperation, expressing China’s readiness to strengthen policy coordination to ensure that investments generate greater benefits for both countries.

China Outlines Additional Development Support

Beyond trade and investment, the Chinese Vice Premier reaffirmed Beijing’s willingness to support Liberia’s development priorities through ongoing and proposed infrastructure and technical assistance projects.

Ding outlined continued cooperation involving the Congo Town overpass bridges, diagnostic laboratory facilities, agricultural machinery, government vehicles and road-related assistance.

He further disclosed that Chinese working teams would visit Liberia to assess proposed projects involving broadcasting facilities and the renovation of the Capitol Building.

China also pledged to continue providing scholarships and training opportunities for Liberian professionals as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s human resource and technical capacity.

Vice President Koung welcomed the assistance but stressed the importance of incorporating training, maintenance and technical support into development projects to ensure their sustainability.

He also highlighted reliable and affordable electricity as a major national priority, identifying opportunities for cooperation in solar energy, battery storage, hydropower and rural electrification.

Other areas raised by the Liberian delegation included clean water, healthcare delivery, digital connectivity and vocational training.

To move the discussions from commitments to implementation, Koung proposed the designation of focal persons and the identification of a shortlist of priority projects for further engagement between the two governments.

He assured the Chinese delegation that Liberia’s Embassy in Beijing and relevant government institutions were prepared to work with their Chinese counterparts to advance the proposed initiatives.

Liberia Seeks China’s Support at UN Security Council

The discussions also addressed cooperation on international affairs, particularly Liberia’s upcoming presidency of the United Nations Security Council in December.

Vice Premier Ding congratulated Liberia on its forthcoming presidency and expressed China’s readiness to maintain close communication and cooperation with Monrovia.

Vice President Koung, in turn, thanked China and other international partners for supporting Liberia’s election to the Security Council for the 2026–2027 term.

He outlined Liberia’s priorities during its tenure, including strengthening the participation of women and young people in peace and security initiatives, addressing the connections between climate change, conflict and natural resources, promoting regional security, and advancing Security Council reform and peacekeeping.

Koung also solicited China’s continued support for Liberia’s December presidency.

Both officials reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening the Liberia-China strategic partnership and translating diplomatic engagements into practical economic and development benefits for their respective populations.

The meeting was held at the Xijiao State Guest Hotel in Shanghai and attended by Shanghai Mayor Zhu Zhongming; Chinese Vice Minister of Foreign Affairs Miao Deyu; Liberia’s Ambassador to China, Dudley McKinley Thomas; and Executive Chairman of the Liberia Special Economic Zones Authority, Prince A. Wreh.

Other members of the Liberian delegation included Samuel Nagbe, Executive Director of the Rural Renewable Energy Agency; Deputy Chief of Staff for Administration Macdonald Metzger; Press Secretary Richmond Neufville; and J. Wesley Washington, Minister Counselor at the Liberian Embassy in China.
