World.title: Haiti gang leader killed as Bukele steps up war on gangs, and Belize watches closely
World.content:
Haiti gang leader killed as Bukele steps up war on gangs, and Belize watches closely

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Haiti’s National Police say they have “neutralised” Mathias Saintil, leader of the Boston gang in Cité Soleil, one of the poorest areas of the capital, Port-au-Prince.

Saintil was reportedly hit by multiple bullets during a police operation and later died in hospital. Haiti’s Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé celebrated on social media, writing, “One less gang leader,” and warning that gangs would not be able to sleep.

The killing comes as El Salvador’s President Nayib Bukele takes a more aggressive role in Haiti. After four Salvadoran aviation technicians serving with the international Gang Suppression Force were kidnapped on October 18, Bukele sent as many as 2,000 troops to Haiti and warned gang leaders that worse was coming if the hostages were not returned alive.

Belize has its own reasons to pay attention. National Security Minister Michel Chebat recently said he plans to visit El Salvador to study Bukele’s crime fighting strategies and see whether any lessons could apply here.

That approach has strong supporters, but also critics. Human rights groups say Bukele’s crackdown in El Salvador, including mass arrests and mass trials, has undermined due process and civil liberties.

At home, Belize is under a 30 day state of emergency in Southside Belize City and parts of the Belize and Cayo Districts, following the murder of four men on the Coastal Highway.

World.title: Armed gangs backing squatters
World.content:
An aerial view of Flamingo Beach, Trelawny, where some of the land has been overrun by squatters, stalling a proposed development that includes resort and entertainment facilities in addition to a residential component.

Well-known attorney Gordon Brown says armed gang members from outside the community are thwarting his six-year-long effort to curb squatting on sections of 167 acres of land he owns in Flamingo Beach, Trelawny. Even a private security firm, he said, has refused the job of protecting the property from being further overrun.

Brown has submitted plans to the National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) and the Trelawny Municipal Corporation (TMC) for an integrated development that includes resort and entertainment facilities in addition to a residential component, but he is unable to proceed as the land is littered with structures at various stages of construction.

In his view, apart from the TMC, which has publicly expressed concern about the stalled development, little has been done by State agencies to help him with his battle.

“Whilst I cannot say exactly how many acres have been squatted upon, what is unequivocal is that, since 2020, both personally and through the several attorneys who have assisted, I have made assiduous efforts to contain the festering squatting problem,” Brown said in a written response to the Jamaica Observer’s Real Estate on the Rock.

“In the supervening five years since filing suit I have respected the rule of law and complied with all orders of the court. Regrettably, my experience has proven yet again that, in our nation, those who abide by the law and show restraint are met with contempt or indifference. Those who flout it are given safe harbour by the authorities, especially if muscular action is visited upon them,” he added.

He listed a litany of failed attempts to arrest squatting taking place on the land, starting with his lawyers’ appeal to NEPA in early May 2020 to use its powers to “require the demolition of all illegal structures on the property”. He said NEPA posted warnings on all the structures on the site, but they were ignored and the squatting continued unabated.

According to Brown, in mid-January 2021, his attorneys served all the squatters with notices to quit, referencing NEPA’s May 2020 warning. In February, he said, his lawyers wrote to the superintendent of police for Trelawny, alerting him that his team may be needed if the squatters got rowdy after being served with notices to leave the property. Then in March 2021 he tried to hire private security to patrol and protect the land in an effort to move the process along.

“They carried out investigations and declined to accept the assignment, as their checks revealed the credible presence of armed gang members from other communities who were in place to resist any efforts to impede the illegal construction,” said Brown.

He said his lawyers then appealed to the commissioner of police, in late March 2021, alerting him to “rampant suspected criminality” in the area and the impact it was having on his property.

“This was copied to several parties, including the chief of defence staff, member of parliament and others, but we received no response, save from the TMC,” said Brown.

“Early April 2021 I met with the TMC to present the estate’s case and its need for coordinated action by the municipality and the police to curtail and demolish the structures. Subsequent to a meeting with the deputy superintendent of works of the TMC on-site, the property caretaker was ambushed by armed thugs who warned him not to erect the signage that we had agreed with the TMC should be put in place to advise the squatters of imminent action,” he added.

Brown then sought help from the courts, filing a suit in May 2021 in which he named all the then-known squatters

— about 10 of them

— and provided a “generic description” of a handful of others who were not known. In the suit, he sought an order for possession of the property. According to Brown, he was “granted an injunction restraining the squatters from damaging the site’s ecology, carrying out further construction activity upon the premises, and other relief”.

However, that did nothing to rein in the squatters, some of whom claim to own the land they occupy.

“Since that time there has been an explosion in the number of occupants. The injunction has been renewed pending final determination of the matter by the court. The occupants have falsely claimed that they have been in occupation of the premises for a period that would give them a possessory title to the parts of the premises occupied by them, but produced no evidence to support their claim. I have tendered video, aerial and geospatial evidence of the state of the premises as of the date of the court action [and before] which prove their claims untenable,” said Brown.

In explaining his claim to the land, he said he was the administrator of the estate of the late Carl Fei, an American who owned several parcels of land in Jamaica, including “approximately 167.25 acres at Flamingo Beach, Trelawny, near to the border of St James”.

“I was registered as the proprietor on November 11, 2005, but have been engaged with the affairs for the estate for many years prior to that date,” Brown told the Sunday Observer.

The Flamingo Beach land issue came to public attention in September when Falmouth Mayor C Junior Gager raised an alarm during the TMC’s regular monthly meeting. He cited Flamingo Beach as one example of the growing problem of squatting in Trelawny which has resulted in the municipal authority being inundated with complaints from frustrated landowners.

“There is a submitted plan here for that property that will help to build Trelawny, but we cannot proceed because there is this problem of squatting,” Gager said of Flamingo Beach, naming Brown as the owner of the land.

During the meeting the mayor also referenced significant squatting on sections of 344.5 acres of land in an area called Tilston, Hague, where one acre has been informally settled; and Hague Cave Island, where four acres of the property have similarly been occupied. He also pointed to Cooper’s Pen in Trelawny

— where approximately 12 acres of the property had been informally occupied

— which had made news headlines following an August 11 early-morning demolition of about 20 structures by the private owner.

There is also a major development planned for Cooper’s Pen and the landowner has been fighting a legal battle for years to get squatters off the land. Brown pointed to similarities between that case and his struggles at Flamingo Beach.

“This débâcle bears all the portents of another Cooper’s Pen, only with more visible, painful results,” he said.

He outlined the ways in which State agencies have failed to act effectively.

“The police have been given statements by parties duped into ‘purchasing’ lots at Flamingo Beach by unscrupulous persons and received necessary information to investigate and prosecute same. No one has been charged,” Brown said.

“I have made several overtures to the police in Trelawny and at the level of the high command for their assistance to address the burgeoning criminality, but with only token support, limited to police escorts whenever court orders are posted on-site. Even equipment bearing insignia and markings of the Jamaica Defence Force has been observed on the site, engaged in illegal activity,” he alleged.

Insisting there can be no excuse for squatting, Brown lay the blame at the feet of successive administrations who have skirted around the issue. He said there has been a “collective refusal” to craft plans to install basic infrastructure on the 550,000 acres of land believed to be in the Government’s possession; pursue transparent divestment methodology and pricing; and put in place the technical staff and enforcement personnel needed in municipal corporations across the country to review and inspect building sites.

Pointing out that the bulk of the country’s housing stock is informal but it is “futile” to demolish them because of non-compliance, Brown argued that many squatters genuinely want to be legitimate owners of property, but the State has failed to put the necessary channels in place.

“Many squatters pay for lands which they occupy

— just not the legitimate owner. Squatters spend large sums for palatial homes on lands they do not own. There is clearly no issue of their ability to afford land, which represents 10 per cent or marginally more of the cost of overall development,” he argued.

“Given an opportunity to acquire lands owned by Government legitimately, those in search of lands [who become squatters] would do so. However, the State must make lands affordable, while ensuring that both the subdivisions and intended development of them are orderly and comply with structural integrity for the safety and health of the intended inhabitants. Formal infrastructure in the form of paved roads and electricity are never a feature of communities that have been squatted,” Brown said.

“These services typically follow after an informal settlement has been established and there is pressure on a member of parliament to support it. These become far more costly to implement because there is no planning of these communities; service roads are twice as long, etc. It is therefore only logical for the State to lead with low-cost, basic infrastructure

— serviced lots in locations with sufficient proximity to main/arterial roads, etc,” Brown added.

He made it clear, however, that he was not excusing the behaviour of those who have stalled his plans at Flamingo Beach.

“These [plans] cannot exist nor be pursued in the context of lawlessness and criminality,” Brown told the Sunday Observer.

World.title: Nurse offers land for proposed Portland hospital
World.content:
Public health Nurse Elaine Linzi making the offer to give up five acres of her land as a site for a new hospital in Portland, last Thursday at the opening of Katus Blakey Dental Clinic in Manchioneal. (Photos: Everard Owen)

MANCHIONEAL, Portland — Hearing Health and Wellness Minister Dr Christopher Tufton saying Government was scouting land on which to house a hospital planned for Portland, United Kingdom citizen and public health Nurse Elaine Linzi last Thursday offered up unused property she owns in the parish. She now works at Manchioneal Health Centre in Portland.

“There seems to be a challenge re identifying a suitable area for the hospital and I’m offering you my land. I have five acres,“ she told Tufton as guests, gathered for the opening of Katus Blakey Dental Clinic in Manchioneal, listened keenly.

”Think out of the box and not always think [about only] Port Antonio. We have wonderful places right here in the east — flat, accessible, cool. All you need is electricity, water, and staff. It is between Kensington and Rural Hill,” Linzi added.

The health minister welcomed the offer, and asked for a round of applause for Linzi.

“It’s a good offer. Send us a note and… all of the team will look at it. The truth is, there’s a lot that goes into building a facility, recognising the needs of the parish in its totality. It’s not necessarily the capital; it could be anywhere on the outskirts… I’m just thinking of a convenient location” said the minister.

“Government is committed and have started a process with land identification. Over the next year we’ll give an update as to where we are to give you a hospital commensurate with the development of the parish,” he promised.

As Tufton noted, the existing hospital in Port Antonio is no longer able to meet the needs of the parish. He pointed out that earlier in the week, Member of Parliament for Portland Eastern Isat Buchanan had raised the issue in the House.

“The truth is, the demand on the facility is higher than the facility’s capacity to deliver. The location of the facility is a problem, because it has no space for expansion. The access to the facility is a challenge, especially when you have an emergency,” he said.

Tufton also pointed to the challenge being faced by many expectant mothers who now have to seek medical care at Annotto Bay Hospital in St Mary.

“We have to find a way to ensure that we develop our health services in keeping with what is required and the growth and the future prospects of the parish,” said Tufton.

Ahead of Linzi’s offer he indicated that talks are under way with Port Authority of Jamaica, which has plans for a development that is being worked on. He said there have also been discussions with the North East Regional Health Authority, National Land Agency, and “the Urban Development Corporation because they are the largest repository of land”, and there has been a suggestion that he should have a discussion with the College of Agriculture, Science, and Education “because they have a lot of land”.

“We’re going to do some sort of comparison to see what is available and what is the most suitable,” said Tufton.

He added that the Government would draw on lessons learned from projects such as Cornwall Regional and the Children’s Hospital in Montego Bay, as well as work done at Black River, Spanish Town, Falmouth, and Kingston Public hospitals.

“I’m here to announce to you that we appreciate and understand what is coming for Portland. We know that health services have to be improved, and we’re making provisions; we will keep you and your representatives abreast as to the progress. I’m hoping that during the course up to the end of this financial year, maybe sometime in the new year… we should at least have some idea as to where that is,” Tufton shared.

World.title: Romain Virgo bares his soul on My Woman & I
World.content:
Virgo’s latest single, My Woman & I was released on Friday, October 30, 2026Contributed

For Romain Virgo, vulnerability has never been something to shy away from. Whether through his music or in his personal life, the reggae singer believes there is value in allowing people to see the person behind the performer, even when the emotions being shared are difficult.

That openness is at the heart of his new single, My Woman & I, a deeply personal offering inspired by a period of uncertainty in his own relationship and a reminder that committed love is not necessarily love without struggle.

Written about a year ago, the song emerged at a time when Virgo and his wife, Elizabeth, were navigating some of the challenges that can arise in any relationship.

Rather than suppressing those feelings, the singer turned to music to process them, recording what was on his heart.

“Relationships and everything that comes with it, those moments when it feels like things aren’t going to work, that’s how I was feeling about my personal relationship in the moment,” he told the Jamaica Observer. “Relationships are like a roller-coaster ride and sometimes, as musicians, the best way to handle these things is to put it in the music. I put pen to paper and I just wrote how I was feeling and recorded it.”

For Virgo, the decision to draw on such a personal experience speaks to his commitment to authenticity. He wants listeners to recognise themselves in his music, particularly those who have experienced the uncertainty that can accompany a relationship while still believing in the possibility of working through it.

“The world, by now, knows me and knows that I am not afraid to show the real side of me. Whether through music or in real life, I am authentic always,” he said.

That willingness to be candid extends to the conversations surrounding the song at home.

When Virgo first played My Woman & I for his wife, her response was not quite the enthusiastic reception he might have hoped for.

“If I’m going to be as vulnerable as possible, the first time she heard this song, she hissed her teeth while laughing at the same time,” he recalled. “I would trouble her and tell her this is the song that she will probably hate the most.”

The reaction, however, appears to have softened. Virgo recently caught her singing the song, prompting a laugh when she remembered that she had supposedly disliked it.

For him, the moment reflects a growing understanding of how music allows him to work through his experiences, including those that are deeply personal.

His creative process, he explained, means drawing on what he is feeling in the moment rather than shying away from difficult emotions. More importantly, the song is not about presenting a relationship as perfect. Instead, Virgo hopes it will resonate with people who understand that commitment is sometimes tested by circumstances that cannot be resolved overnight.

“I hope this single will give people who look to music for their peace and to express themselves. I hope it gives them a sense of belonging,” he said. “I hope they hear someone who has been through some tough times when it comes to relationships and now that it just something that comes with the territory.”

His message to listeners is simple: Difficulty does not have to mean defeat.

“When you’re committed to something, you have to find ways to work through issues and keep showing up, don’t give up on love,” he said.

Though written a year ago, My Woman & I is only now making its way to listeners. Virgo explained that the timing was not right for its release earlier, particularly in the aftermath of Hurricane Melissa, when he delayed the release and promotion of several songs already in the pipeline.

With the time now right, the single will also serve as a precursor to a larger project currently in development. Sources suggest a 2027 release on Ineffable Records.

“This track will lead into something bigger. We working on a project that we can’t give too much details on just yet. Just know this single is a part of a bigger picture,” he said of the track produced by Mr G and revives the classic Dub Fire rhythm made famous on Dennis Brown’s Promised Land.

For now, My Woman & I offers listeners an intimate look at an artiste willing to turn his own experiences into music, with a message that extends beyond romance. Love, as Virgo presents it, is not simply about the moments when everything falls into place, but also the willingness to keep showing up when it does not.

My Woman & I was released on Friday, October 30, and is available on all digital platforms.

World.title: The 15-year challenge
World.content:
Inter Miami’s Lionel Messi (second left) deftly scores past Cavalier’s goalkeeper Vino Barclett (#1) as Jeovanni Laing (left) looks on during the Concacaf Champions Cup second-leg round-of-16 match at the National Stadium on Thursday, March 13, 2025. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

When Mount Pleasant FA and Cavalier FC represented Jamaica in the Concacaf Champions Cup it was a proud moment for local football. However, their participation also highlighted the gap between Jamaican clubs and the region’s top teams.

Clubs in Major League Soccer (MLS) and Mexico’s Liga MX have far greater financial resources, with budgets exceeding US$10 million (over $1.5 billion). This puts them well ahead of teams in the Legend Jamaica Premier League (JPL).

The difference is not just about players’ salaries. It also comes down to facilities, technical support, sports science, preparation, and the cost of competing internationally.

Mount Pleasant have done more than most Jamaican clubs to improve their operations. Under owner Peter Gould, the St Ann club has built its own training academy, hired experienced technical staff, and established itself as one of the leading teams in the Caribbean.

However, even with that investment, Mount Pleasant still have work to do to compete with the best in Concacaf.

Mount Pleasant Sporting Director Paul Christie says the club has made significant progress since 2022, but is still some way from achieving its continental ambitions.

“In 2022, when we were given the privilege of carrying out the mandate by owner Peter Gould, Mount Pleasant was 172nd in Concacaf’s club rating and 35th in the Caribbean,” Christie told the Sunday Observer. “Since then, we’re on the cusp of breaking into the top 50 in Concacaf, and we’re the #1 team in the Caribbean. Until we are able to satisfactorily compete at the Concacaf level, there’s still a lot of work to be done.”

The challenge extends beyond individual clubs. Professional Football Jamaica Limited (PFJL) Chief Executive Officer Owen Hill says the league must address several problems if Jamaican teams are to compete more regularly at the regional level.

One of the biggest challenges is the lack of stadiums that meet Concacaf’s requirements. This often forces clubs to play home matches overseas, increasing their expenses and taking away the advantage of playing in front of their supporters.

Hill pointed to Portmore United’s Caribbean Cup campaign as an example of the problem. He explained that the reigning JPL champions had to play a home match in Trinidad because suitable venues were unavailable in Jamaica.

“That was a home game – in Trinidad, why?! Trinidad is not even close to Jamaica, but the reason they played in Trinidad is primarily because of the economics of it. It’s cheaper to play in Trinidad than Jamaica,” Hill told the Observer.

Hill explained that the National Stadium was booked for the Independence Gala period, while Sabina Park was being used for the Caribbean Premier League. He said Portmore had no other suitable venue available and had to travel to Trinidad to fulfil the fixture.

Playing home matches overseas means clubs miss out on ticket sales and other income that could be used to improve their operations. It also limits the support they receive from local fans.

Hill wants clubs to eventually have their own stadiums that meet minimum Concacaf standards. This would not only give them a suitable home venue for international matches but also allow them to build stronger connections with their communities and generate income.

The PFJL is also working with Concacaf and the Jamaica Football Federation to adjust the domestic calendar around international competitions. However, Hill says clubs must also plan their training programmes and squad depth because fixture clashes cannot always be avoided.

The financial demands of international football are another concern. Hill says the PFJL supports clubs that qualify for regional competitions, while Concacaf subsidies have increased. However, the cost of travel, maintaining squads, and preparing for matches remain major challenges.

“Our clubs and, by extension, our economy, are not about to sustain that consistently, so what we try to do is incentivise the opportunities but also ensure that education happens very early,” Hill says.

The PFJL also wants Jamaican clubs to become stronger brands that can attract investment from the Diaspora and international sponsors. Hill admits that the response from overseas Jamaicans has so far been limited, but believes clubs can become more attractive to investors as the professional product improves.

The league has already reached some important milestones, including an expanded sponsorship agreement with Legend Beer, 360-degree broadcast coverage, and venue partnerships with Independence Park Limited.

Hill also sees the proposed redevelopment of Montego Bay Sports Complex as a model for future projects. He believes Jamaica needs at least 10 stadiums of a similar standard over the next decade to improve the facilities available to clubs and other sporting events.

However, better stadiums alone will not close the gap. Hill says clubs also need proper gyms, recovery facilities, and technical analysts who can study opponents and help coaches prepare their teams.

He believes the lack of those resources also affects how Jamaican football is viewed internationally. While the country’s players are recognised for their speed and athleticism, tactical preparation remains an area that needs improvement.

The long-term plan is to build clubs that can generate enough income through sponsorship, commercial activities, and player transfers to reinvest in their operations.

“When I talk about the vision, I’m saying no less than 10 to 15 years of building and toiling before we see some actual results, such as players being sold for solid amounts of money; transfer fees are now back into the club’s ecosystem to develop the club’s infrastructure at a minimum standard,” Hill says.

World.title: Loyalty At Heart
World.content:
In Citizen Magazine Issue 005, award-winning actress Sheryl Lee Ralph shares the spotlight with her daughter, stylist Ivy “Coco” Maurice, for “Loyalty at Heart”. (Photo: Rasaan Wyzard)

Plus…

For Sheryl Lee Ralph, style is a family affair. The Emmy, Critics Choice and Independent Spirit Award-winning actress joined her daughter, stylist Ivy “Coco” Maurice, for a striking fashion moment in Citizen Magazine Issue 005. Photographed in Kingston, Jamaica, in March, the mother-daughter duo wore designs by Bianca Saunders and Diotima, respectively, for ”Loyalty at Heart”, an editorial styled by Mecca James-Williams. Curated in the wake of Hurricane Melissa, the visual tribute turns its lens on Jamaican families, celebrating the bonds that endure and a shared allegiance to one another and home. A sentiment captured in its central message: “Loyal to one another, home in Jamaica”.

World.title: Man suspected of drowning in Alligator Pond
World.content:
People enjoying the river and sea at a beach in Alligator Pond. A no swimming sign is seen in the background. (Photo: Kasey Williams)

MANCHESTER, Jamaica — A man is suspected to have drowned in Alligator Pond, south Manchester on Saturday.

Police identified him as Simon Newman, a resident of Downs near the Manchester/ St Elizabeth border.

Preliminary reports are that about 4:00 pm Newman was swimming in a river when he got into difficulty and went underwater. His body was later removed from the river. Police were called and he was pronounced dead at hospital.

The area, known as River, has been the scene of numerous drowning incidents over the years, especially on holidays.

In August 2023, two people drowned at the location. A local community hero, who saved people from drowning at the same location, also drowned upstream in the river in Alligator Pond, a week after rescuing several people.

READ: Alligator Pond warning

READ: Alligator Pond hero found dead in river

A police source said in January 2025 Newman’s twin brother was one of two people who died in a crash on the Buttup main road in south Manchester.

READ: Two motorcyclists killed in head-on collision in Manchester

— Kasey Williams

World.title: Manning Cup quarterfinalists decided
World.content:
In this file photo, Kingston College’s Deshawn Byfield (left) and Mona High’s Jermaine Morgan vie for the ball during the ISSA Walker Cup final at Stadium East. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Former champions Jamaica College (JC), Mona High and Wolmer’s Boys were the last three qualifiers to the ISSA Manning Cup quarterfinal following the final set of games in the round of 16 on Saturday.

JC drew 1-1 with Eltham and finished second on five points in Zone 4. Eltham won the group with seven points. Norman Manley defeated Tivoli Gardens 4-2 and grabbed third place with three points. Tivoli Gardens ended with a point.

In Zone 1, defending champions Excelsior came from behind to beat St George’s College 2-1 and consolidated their position at the top with nine points. The Light Blues finished at the bottom with a point.

Mona High booked their spot with a comprehensive 4-0 win over St Catherine High and finished with six points and second spot in Zone 1 as St Catherine were eliminated with a point in third spot.

Wolmer’s Boys blanked Hillel Academy 2-0 and finished second in Zone 3 with six points and into the last eight. St Andrew Technical High School (STATHS) topped the group with maximum nine points after whipping St Jago High 5-0.

Kingston College defeated Calabar 1-0 to top Zone 2 with maximum nine points. Calabar, who had already qualified for the quarterfinal, were second with six points.

The quarter final pairings have been decided with Group A consisting of Excelsior high, Eltham High, Wolmer’s Boys and Calabar High while Group B will have KC, STATHS, Mona and JC.

–Howard Walker

World.title: NWC customers miss out on $50m
World.content:
SOME National Water Commission (NWC) customers missed out on hundreds of dollars in compensation as the utility paid only $23.76 million of the $73.78 million potentially available for breaches of its Guranteed Standards during the 2025–2026 financial year.

The shortfall of approximately $50 million is outlined in the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) 2025–2026 Annual Report, tabled in Parliament on Tuesday.

The report shows that the NWC committed 14,817 breaches of its Guaranteed Standards during the period April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.

But the utility paid just 32 per cent of the potential compensation its customers should have received.

Among the reasons cited for the non-payment were customers failing to submit the required claim forms and NWC receiving relief from the Guaranteed Standards following Hurricane Melissa in October 2025.

The OUR excused the utility from meeting certain service requirements between October 24 and December 31, 2025, because of the disruption caused by the Category 5 storm.

This meant the utility could avoid paying compensation for breaches covered by that relief during the period.

The report also disclosed that, in March 2026, the NWC requested a further six months of relief, beginning January 1, 2026. At the end of the reporting period, that request was still under review, with the OUR indicating that a decision would be issued in the next financial year.

The Guaranteed Standards are service requirements that utility providers are expected to meet. Where a provider breaches an applicable standard, affected customers may qualify for compensation, subject to the relevant conditions and procedures.

The NWC’s compensation figures form part of wider concerns about customer service and unresolved complaints recorded by the OUR during the financial year.

The OUR said it received 3,558 contacts from consumers about utility services during the period, of which 1,168 related to the NWC. These included complaints, enquiries, and other matters brought to its attention.

At March 31, 2026, the NWC also accounted for 251 of the 625 complaints that remained open across all utility providers, representing 40 per cent of the outstanding cases.

The report found that billing disputes and service interruptions were the leading reasons consumers contacted the OUR, accounting for 48 per cent and 18 per cent of all contacts, respectively.

The regulator also noted that it had secured approximately $21.34 million for customers through investigations of appeals and complaints during the financial year.

The NWC accounted for the largest share, paying approximately $9.45 million for consumers, or 44 per cent of the total. The OUR said it would continue reviewing the NWC’s request for additional relief in the following financial year.

The utility recently applied for a 51 per cent tariff increase which is to be considered by the OUR.

World.title: Europe will be represented in Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine, French foreign minister says
World.content:
“In recent weeks, Europeans have made their voices heard, expressing to the American mediator that no discussion concerning the future of the continent can disregard our expectations and demands,” Barrot told RTL.

European Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said Friday the EU executive didn’t yet have details to share, but added that “it’s obviously up to the European Union to decide on matters which affect its security and on matters which are of its competence.”

The EU has scrambled to agree on who should represent it at the peace talks and who, if anyone, should be in contact with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni urged European Council President António Costa to settle the issue in a letter this week, prompting Costa to put it on the agenda of the Nov. 13 leaders’ summit. Meloni’s letter was partly prompted by a phone call Finland’s Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Jonas Gahr Støre made to Putin on Oct. 27, which took some European leaders by surprise.

Meanwhile, the European Commission hosted talks on Ukraine’s reconstruction on Wednesday, bringing together representatives from Ukraine, the U.S., U.K., Germany, France, NATO and the World Bank.

U.S. President Donald Trump spoke late Thursday of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.” The plan has brought anxiety among EU officials, who fear it risks sidelining the continent and emboldening Putin.

“We already have a European security architecture in place — NATO and European Union both have their respective roles,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Friday in response to the U.S. plan. “We must make sure Ukraine is integrated into this architecture. The problem remains that Russia keeps breaking the treaties that underpin it … Putin does not have a veto over European security.”

World.title: Russian strikes leave 600,000 in the dark in eastern Ukraine
World.content:
“Power company workers are already working to restore electricity. Their efforts are being hampered by constant Russian shelling,” said the region’s governor Oleksandr Hanzha, adding that hospitals and critical infrastructure are now relying on generators for power.

The blackout follows shelling in the region on Nov. 3 that damaged infrastructure in a key industrial region bordering active combat areas, and a wider attack the same day across Ukraine targeting energy facilities.

The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant also lost power overnight, with the International Atomic Energy Agency saying on Sunday morning it is now relying “on emergency diesel generators for reactor cooling and other essential nuclear safety and security functions.”

The attack comes as Kyiv and Moscow gear up for another round of US-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week. Following the new wave of attacks on Saturday night Zelenskyy called on international partners to ramp up sanctions on Russia to hamper its capability to acquire or build more missiles.

“It is very important that they be synchronized across Europe and G7 jurisdictions. If the world does not have enough anti-ballistic capabilities to protect Ukrainian skies, then the missiles must be stopped on the production lines,” he said.

World.title: Security Sunday: Die neue Front der Bundeswehr in Litauen – mit Robertas Kaunas
World.content:
Eingeklemmt zwischen Kaliningrad und Belarus liegt die verwundbarste Stelle der NATO. Genau hier entsteht mit der Panzerbrigade 45 das wohl wichtigste Projekt der deutschen Zeitenwende. Bis 2027 sollen fast 5.000 deutsche Soldaten dauerhaft in Litauen stationiert werden.

Doch die Bedrohung durch Russland ist längst nicht mehr nur theoretisch: Drohnen, Desinformation und brennende Infrastruktur zeigen, dass der hybride Krieg Litauen bereits erreicht hat. Im Gespräch erklärt der litauische Verteidigungsminister Robertas Kaunas, wie real die Gefahr einer Invasion ist.

Die Folge beleuchtet, wie sich die baltischen Staaten wappnen und was Europa tun muss, falls die USA als Schutzmacht ausfallen. Eine präzise Einordnung, warum die Abschreckung an der Ostflanke über das Schicksal des Kontinents entscheidet und die Sicherheit in Vilnius letztlich die Sicherheit in Berlin bedeutet.

World.content:
Share on LinkedIn

Die Welt spielt verrückt, doch im Präsidium des Bundestages herrscht überraschende Einigkeit. Bundestagsvizepräsident Bodo Ramelow (Die Linke) gibt im Gespräch mit Gordon Repinski einen seltenen Einblick in die überparteiliche Zusammenarbeit, auch bei Nachtschichten. Dabei wird deutlich, mit welcher Strategie das Gremium den Provokationen der AfD begegnet.

In seiner eigenen Partei brodelt es derweil gewaltig. Ramelow findet deutliche Worte zur Antisemitismus-Debatte innerhalb der Linken und kritisiert das taktische Lavieren einzelner Abgeordneter. Warum er trotzdem eine Gesinnungsprüfung ablehnt, aber klare rote Linien beim Existenzrecht Israels zieht, offenbart die tiefe Zerrissenheit seiner Partei.

Zudem verrät er, warum die Wahrnehmung der Linken im Bundestag derzeit auch von der Gruppe der „Silberlocken“ abhängt, wie sich die Silberlocken regelmäßig absprechen und warum er sich trotz aller Krisen nicht verrückt machen lässt.

Mit den Linken, aber auch der SPD und den Grünen beschäftigt sich auch der neue Podcast von POLITICO und WELT. In „Inside Links“ geht es jede Woche darum, wie in Deutschland womöglich eine neue linke Mehrheit entsteht, zu welchem Preis und wer künftig dabei möglicherweise am Regierungstisch sitzen könnte. „Inside Links“ gibt es auf den Podcast-Plattformen zu hören und zu sehen, unter anderem auch hier.

World.title: Merz’s conservatives poised to nominate Germany’s first woman president
World.content:
President of the Bavarian parliament Ilse Aigner arrives at the Christian Social Union party congress in Munich, on Oct. 23, 2026. | Alexandra Beier/AFP via Getty Images

BERLIN — Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is set to become Germany’s next president, making her the country’s first woman to hold the office, according to two senior conservatives with knowledge of the matter.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative bloc and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) will nominate Aigner to succeed outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the officials told BILD, which, like POLITICO, is part of the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network. Both officials were granted anonymity to discuss internal party matters freely. Aigner’s nomination will officially be announced Monday, according to the officials.

Aigner, who previously served as agriculture minister under former German Chancellor Angela Merkel from 2008 to 2013, is currently president of the Bavarian State Parliament. She is also a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

World.title: Trump’s ‘big, beautiful’ European security plan isn’t convincing Europe
World.content:
The latest U.S. proposal underscores growing anxiety around Trump’s fresh rapprochement with Russia as he ramps up pressure on Ukraine and his administration attempts to revive long-stalled talks to end Moscow’s full-scale war against Kyiv.

POLITICO spoke to 12 NATO diplomats, EU envoys and European government officials, all of whom were granted anonymity to speak freely on the sensitive issue. NATO allies were not briefed about the American plans in advance, according to three alliance diplomats, and many remain skeptical of the idea.

U.S. President Donald Trump late Thursday talked of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.”

“Our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment,” Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner added soon after.

Kushner said the arrangement would have five goals: “Permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.”

“It is a bit obscure what Kushner meant,” said one NATO diplomat. “The general sentiment in Europe is that any discussion with Russia on the future architecture at the moment will just be used by Moscow to legitimize their arguments ... it will not fly with the European allies.”

World.title: NATO faces €7B shortfall on military aid pledge to Ukraine
World.content:
The shortfall comes ahead of an alliance meeting on Nov. 17 where European capitals are expected to examine ways to boost funding and increase the transfer of critical weapons to Ukraine. While new NATO funding pledges are still expected, it’s possible that allies may fail to meet this year’s target, the diplomats said.

A NATO official speaking on behalf of the organization said that “allies continue to provide essential military support to Ukraine” to fulfill the pledge and “are working to ensure that Ukraine has the support it needs now and into the future.”

The target combines bilateral contributions throughout the year and €30 billion drawn from the EU’s €90 billion loan to Ukraine.

Kyiv has repeatedly urged allies to step up their funding as Russia continues its devastating air assaults; more than 40 people were reportedly killed after a school bombing this week.

During a closed-door meeting with allies Thursday, Ukraine’s ambassador to NATO Alyona Getmanchuk “emphasised the importance for Ukraine of NATO Allies fulfilling the commitment made at the Ankara Summit to provide €70 billion in military support this year,” according to a statement by the Ukrainian mission.

“It is essential to mobilise all partners to the fullest extent, accelerate new decisions, and translate previously announced commitments into concrete deliveries of equipment or transfers of funds,” it added.

World.title: Wave of bomb threats target Irish media outlets and more European flights
World.content:
“We have expected a rise in hybrid threats to Ireland because of our hosting of the EU presidency, and the EPC meeting will be by far the biggest set-piece event of that presidency, so one must presume it’s no coincidence that we’re experiencing this spike in hybrid activity now,” the Irish official said.

The Irish government said the threats against media outlets were probably part of a European-wide pattern of threats that have targeted dozens of airlines this week, including Irish carriers Ryanair and Aer Lingus. Hackers also targeted supermarket refrigeration systems in at least seven European countries.

“It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralized or coordinated effort,” the Irish government said in a statement. “However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a coordinated campaign of disruption.”

Bomb threats also targeted at least 18 European flights Friday, after at least 22 the day before, raising concerns that the hoaxes may be part of a coordinated campaign to disrupt air traffic.

Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares told Spanish public broadcaster TVE on Friday that the bomb threats affecting flights could be “an attempt at hybrid aggression and war in some psychological way.” He added that “it cannot be a coincidence that so many identical events occur with the same modus operandi throughout Europe.”

Luis Gallego, CEO of airline group IAG, said: “It is clear that what they [the perpetrators] are looking for is to create chaos and disruption in the different airports.”

World.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave 850,000 without power as Zelenskyy reports drone attack on Komyshuvakha
World.content:
Russian strikes on Ukraine overnight reportedly left more than 850,000 people without power across the country.

 

Ukrainian energy firm DTEK said Russian forces had launched a "massive attack" on Ukraine's energy sector, targeting key facilities in the eastern Dnipropetrovsk region.

"Over 600,000 residents of the region in the Pavlohrad, Samar, Kamianske and Dnipro districts, as well as in the city of Dnipro itself, have been left without power," the company said. Power is gradually being restored in the region, authorities later announced.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy added that there were widespread power outages across the nation, including in Kharkiv Oblast in the northeast and the Zhytomyr in the northwest, where he said 140 apartment buildings were without heating following a Russian strike.

Local authorities in Kharkiv reported that around 250,000 customers in the region had been left without power but that it had since been restored.

Russia has once again begun to ramp up attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure as winter draws nearer, capitalising on Kyiv's shortage of interceptor missiles as it seeks to break Ukraine's resistance.

Over the past week, Zelenskyy said Russian forces have fired 115 missiles, almost 1,900 guided aerial bombs, and more than 3,000 attack drones against Ukraine.

Komyshuvakha

On Sunday morning, Zelenskyy said Russia had also launched a drone strike on the site of a recent attack on Komyshuvakha, where rescuers have been carrying out search operations following a bombing that killed at least 55 people on Monday.

"Unfortunately, more people may still be under the rubble. Absolute cynicism and brutality," the Ukrainian leader wrote on X.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service said Russia had "deliberately attacked" emergency service workers at the site but that no one had been injured.

The Monday strikes, which hit a school Kyiv said was used for humanitarian purposes, followed a rare localised truce between Kyiv and Moscow that had allowed evacuees to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in Ukraine's southern Kherson region.

One person was also killed and three others were injured in a strike on a residential area of Dnipro on Sunday, per Oleksandr Hanzha, the head of the regional military administration.

"A fire has broken out. At least one private house has been destroyed. It is believed that people may be trapped under the rubble," he said.

Zelenskyy has accused the Kremlin of intensifying attacks in a bid to put additional pressure on Ukraine's negotiating position ahead of planned trilateral talks between Kyiv, Moscow and Washington in Abu Dhabi.

World.title: Europeans to join Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, says French FM Barrot
World.content:
European countries, including France, will be involved in the talks between Russians and Ukrainians due to open on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi under US mediation, the French foreign minister has announced on RTL and Public Sénat.

 

"The Europeans will be well represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to take part in these talks", Jean-Noël Barrot said, specifying that he would not personally be at the negotiating table.

"I cannot yet tell you who will represent France on this occasion, but it will definitely be there", he added.

"In recent weeks Europeans have made themselves heard. They have explained to the American mediators that no discussion concerning the future of this continent can ignore our expectations and our demands", he said.

After meeting the Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev on Thursday, Donald Trump predicted, in front of the press, the imminent conclusion of a "major agreement" with Russia on Ukraine which, according to him, "could cover all of Europe" and "everyone will be delighted with", without providing any further details.

Jean-Noël Barrot said on Sunday that he did not know what the US president had in mind, stressing that no agreement with "consequences for the European security architecture" could be "designed, or even discussed" without the Europeans.

Until now, the talks scheduled for 10 and 11 November had been presented as trilateral negotiations bringing together Ukrainian, Russian and American officials. However, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky had clearly expressed his wish for Kyiv's European allies to be involved.

Mélenchon, 'mouthpiece of the Kremlin'

Asked about the positions taken by Jean-Luc Mélenchon on a settlement of the war in Ukraine, during his rally at Le Bourget the previous day, Jean-Noël Barrot described the leader of hard left La France Insoumise as a "mouthpiece of the Kremlin".

While the LFI programme, "L'Avenir en commun", unveiled this week, devotes little space to the war in Ukraine, unlike the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Jean-Luc Mélenchon advocated holding a referendum on the status of the Donbass, largely occupied by the Russian army, stating that "it is for the people to decide".

"We do not accept the idea of peace involving territorial concessions in Ukraine without asking the populations concerned whether they agree to find themselves on this side of the border or the other", he told thousands of supporters.

Moscow has already staged sham consultations in annexed Crimea and in the four regions of south-eastern Ukraine it partially controls, procedures rejected by Kyiv and the international community.

"All over the world the Kremlin is trying to convince heads of state and government that, basically, the Donbass is Russian and that the war of aggression is a war to liberate the Donbass", Jean-Noël Barrot said. "This is obviously of unprecedented seriousness and, in my view, definitively disqualifies him [Mélenchon] from holding the offices he aspires to", he added.

The war in Ukraine has already been a source of controversy in the 2027 presidential campaign, where Marine Le Pen, well ahead in the polls, and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, currently in second place, have taken positions seen as favourable to Putin.

The far-right candidate said in mid-October that she would end French financial aid to Ukraine, which she estimates to be 6 billion euros a year, if she were to win the 2027 presidential election.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy then responded that "Madame Le Pen does not have a very good grasp of certain details" of French-Ukrainian military cooperation, defending a "win-win" partnership that he said was also beneficial to France's security.

World.title: Egypt reopens Tripoli embassy after 12 years and raises concerns over Turkey-Libya maritime deal
World.content:
Egypt reopened its historic embassy building in the Libyan capital, Tripoli, on Saturday during a visit by Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty for talks on trade, energy and a disputed maritime boundary.

 

Libya’s acting foreign minister, Taher al-Baour, joined Abdelatty at the ceremony. Egypt closed the building in January 2014 after gunmen kidnapped five embassy staff. Its diplomatic mission resumed work in Tripoli in May 2021.

Cairo has long backed Khalifa Haftar, the military commander whose forces dominate eastern Libya, where a rival government is based. In Tripoli, Abdelatty met Abdulhamid Dbeibah, the prime minister of Libya’s internationally recognised Government of National Unity.

The two discussed ways to make trade easier. Dbeibah praised the role Egyptian companies and workers have played in rebuilding Libya, according to Egypt’s foreign ministry.

Abdelatty also met Libya’s acting oil minister at the reopened embassy. He called for faster progress on gas pipelines between the two countries and on plans to refine Libyan crude in Egypt for export. The Libyan minister said he would travel to Cairo for further talks, Libya’s state news agency reported on Sunday.

Why the maritime deal is disputed

In his talks with Dbeibah, Abdelatty raised Egypt’s objections to a 2019 agreement between Turkey and Libya’s then government in Tripoli. He said Egypt’s concerns should be taken into account when maritime boundaries are drawn, according to his ministry. Dbeibah told Egyptian broadcaster Al-Qahera News that officials from both countries would discuss the maps and their respective claims at their next meeting.

The agreement draws a boundary between Turkish and Libyan maritime zones in the eastern Mediterranean, where several countries claim rights to explore for oil and gas. Greece says the boundary ignores the rights of Greek islands, including Crete, which lies between the Turkish and Libyan coasts. Egypt and Cyprus also oppose the deal.

Libya’s eastern-based parliament ratified the agreement on 20 October after opposing it for years. The EU said the next day that the deal infringed on other countries’ rights and could have no legal effect on them. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan defended it as “an entirely legitimate agreement, both from a legal and a political perspective”.

World.title: Condolences and solidarity: European and world leaders react to Krakow shooting.
World.content:
News of the events in Krakow reached the public around the world within a short time. Representatives of European governments as well as leaders of individual states reacted to the tragedy.

 

In their statements they mainly expressed solidarity with those affected, offered condolences and firmly condemned all forms of violence.

"The events that took place in Krakow have deeply moved me. My thoughts are with the victims and their families. Germany, as a friend and partner of Poland, stands by its side in this difficult time. I wish all the injured a speedy recovery," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote.

"Shock and emotion after the tragic shooting that took place in Krakow. All our solidarity, sincere condolences and sympathy to Poland, to the victims, their families and loved ones," French President Emmanuel Macron wrote.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed deep sadness and her sincerest condolences to Poland for "the cowardly and unacceptable act of violence that has struck the city of Krakow".

"My thoughts, as well as those of the Italian government, go to the families of the innocent victims, to the injured, to whom I wish a swift and full recovery, and to the entire Polish nation. We will always defend our security and our freedom against every form of terror and violence," she added.

Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened" by the events in Krakow. "My thoughts are with the families of those who lost their lives, all the injured and everyone affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the Polish people," he wrote.

"Today Spain stands with Poland and with the victims. I wish the injured a speedy recovery," Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wrote.

Latvian President Edgars Rinkēvičs wrote: "Terrible news of the shooting in Krakow. I extend my deepest and sincerest condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims, wishing a swift recovery to all those injured. Latvia stands in solidarity with our Polish friends and allies in this tragic hour."

"In the face of this tragic attack my thoughts and my heart are with those affected, their loved ones and all the residents of Krakow. I offer my sincerest condolences to the families of the victims. I thank the heroic police officers for acting at the risk of their lives. Europe joins Poland in pain and solidarity," wrote European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

Kaja Kallas said it was "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland's borders".

"My thoughts are with the victims and their families and with the emergency services. Poland's strength lies in the resilience of its people. In this moment of mourning Poland does not stand alone," added the head of EU diplomacy.

European Parliament President Roberta Metsola stressed that "with great sadness she learned of the shooting at the Main Market Square in Krakow".

"My thoughts are with the innocent victims and their families. I wish all the injured a swift and full recovery. I thank the police and emergency services for their rapid intervention and for bringing the situation under control," she added.

All EU institutions are flagged at half mast.

President of Lithuania Gitanas Nausėda wrote that he was deeply saddened by the tragic shooting in Krakow. "Sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of those who lost their lives. I wish a swift and full recovery to all those injured. Lithuania expresses its full solidarity with President Karol Nawrocki and the Polish people in this difficult time," he added.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote of "the shocking crime in Krakow".

"On behalf of the Ukrainian people and personally, I extend my most sincere condolences to the families and loved ones of the victims. There is no justification for this attack and we trust that the perpetrator will face justice.

We wish strength and a speedy recovery to the injured and to everyone affected by this tragedy. Ukraine expresses solidarity with Poland and the Polish people. People have the right to safety," he stressed.

United States Ambassador to Poland Tom Rose stressed that "America stands by Poland in this dark hour, just as Poland stands by its beloved citizens of Krakow".

"May the blessed memory of those who passed away today ease the grief of those who mourn," he noted.

"I am deeply saddened by the tragic shooting in Krakow, and my thoughts are with the victims, their families and everyone affected by this situation. Romania expresses its full solidarity with Poland and its people in this difficult moment," wrote Romanian President Nicușor Dan.

Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban wrote on X that she was "deeply saddened by the tragic shooting in Krakow".

"I extend my sincere condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and wish a swift recovery to all those injured. Hungary stands in solidarity with Poland and the Polish people," she added.

World.title: Egypt announces new Mediterranean gas field discovery estimated at 200 billion cubic feet
World.content:
Egypt has announced a new natural gas discovery in the Mediterranean Sea, with initial estimates pointing to around 200 billion cubic feet in the reservoir of the exploratory well "Nasim-1X".

 

Cairo hopes the discovery will help support domestic gas production and reduce reliance on imports.

The Egyptian Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources said on Friday that drilling and appraisal work at the well, located in the Taiba concession area, had revealed a gas-bearing layer with a net thickness of around 15 metres, featuring distinct geological and petrophysical characteristics.

Technical and reservoir studies are still under way to determine the volumes that can be produced, assess possible daily production rates and evaluate the commercial viability of the discovery.

The ministry has not announced a date for the start of production.

Pipeline planned to speed up use of the discovery

Egypt plans to connect the well to existing production facilities via a pipeline about 22 kilometres long, linking it to the Abu Madi - El Gamil pipeline. This is intended to make use of the available infrastructure and shorten the time needed to begin production.

Italian company Eni is operating the Taiba concession in partnership with Australian company Woodside, while Egyptian firm Petrobel carried out the drilling work on behalf of the partners.

The Ministry of Petroleum attributed the positive results to higher investment and exploration activity, noting an improved investment climate and progress in settling overdue financial receivables owed to foreign companies working in the energy sector.

Egypt is seeking to increase its domestic natural gas production after a decline in output in recent years led to greater dependence on gas imports to meet market demand.

Cairo is relying on the development of new discoveries and faster exploration work to strengthen local supplies, amid strong gas demand from the electricity and industrial sectors.

World.title: US forces strike commercial vessel in Gulf of Oman after crew 'ignored repeated warnings'
World.content:
The US military said on Saturday that its forces had "disabled" a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman after its civilian crew "ignored repeated warnings" and made a number of attempts to "violate" the naval blockade of Iran.

 

"A U.S. military aircraft fired precision munitions at the stern of St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda, disabling the ship after CENTCOM forces directed the crew to abandon targeted spaces. The cargo vessel tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement, adding that it was continuing to "strictly enforce" the blockade against Iran.

According to the military command, since July, US forces have redirected 147 commercial vessels that complied with the blockade, while disabling five merchant ships that refused.

"Additionally, CENTCOM has previously destroyed another 10 Iranian commercial oil tankers that were part of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps’ multibillion-dollar shadow network," it added.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency said late on Saturday that it had received a report of an incident involving a bulk carrier and military forces in the Gulf of Oman, around 18 nautical miles east of Khor Fakkan on the east coast of the United Arab Emirates.

The UAE National Guard announced early on Sunday that 22 people had been rescued from a cargo ship in the gulf.

IRGC: Two tankers strike mines around Strait of Hormuz

At the same time, Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) navy claimed in a statement that two oil tankers, one to the east of the Strait of Hormuz and the other sailing in the strategic waterway, had caught fire after hitting mines.

The Guards said they had been using an "unauthorised" route.

"These two tankers, through multiple violations and by switching off their navigation and positioning systems, intended to transit the Strait of Hormuz via an unauthorised route. After hitting a mine, they exploded and are burning," the IRGC navy said in a statement.

The Guards also accused CENTCOM's commander of "fantasy" and warned that any ship or vessel that cooperates with the US military, "disobeys Iranian regulations for the Strait of Hormuz and enters the unauthorised area, will inevitably hit a mine."

Tensions between Tehran and Washington over the Strait of Hormuz have flared once again in recent days following the end of the US midterm elections.

On Friday night, reports emerged of explosions on Qeshm Island, and the Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck the area.

A few hours later, US President Donald Trump confirmed that US forces had targeted an Iranian air defence system.

Iranian news agencies reported on Saturday night that further explosions had been heard in Qeshm, Sirik, Jask and Bandar Abbas.

World.title: Latest news bulletin | November 8th, 2026 – Midday
World.content: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond in this Euronews news bulletin. In just a few minutes, our newsroom brings you the latest news and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, with the context you need to make sense of a fast-moving day. Reported with the independence and the European perspective that define Euronews, this regular round-up gives you a clear and reliable overview of the stories shaping our world right now, wherever you are watching from.

World.title: Canary Islands demand urgent government action amid surge in migrant arrivals
World.content:
The president of the Canary Islands has announced that Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has agreed to convene an emergency meeting of the Interministerial Commission on Immigration on Tuesday to address the growing pressure facing the island of El Hierro following a recent surge in migrant arrivals.

 

Fernando Clavijo said he had briefed the prime minister on the severity of the situation on the island and the mounting discontent among residents.

The El Hierro Island Council has declared a social emergency following the arrival of more than 8,000 migrants over the last five weeks.

Between 1 and 6 November, 49 boats carrying a total of 4,587 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands, according to the regional government.

Of these, 35 reached El Hierro, where authorities say the pressure on local resources is "extraordinary."

Clavijo said the Canary Islands have been calling for months for additional resources, better planning and a coordinated governmental response to deal with the situation.

"This meeting must serve to agree, between both governments and the relevant ministries, on a joint action plan, with specific, responsible measures and deadlines for implementation," Clavijo wrote in a post on social media. "We cannot continue to act only when the situation worsens."

He said he had also requested "urgent meetings" with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen as well as European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, Magnus Brunner.

"The Canary Islands cannot continue to face, practically on their own, a situation that requires the involvement of the Spanish government and Europe," Clavijo added.

World.title: At least 21 killed after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
World.content:
The incident occurred near Kebemer off the coast of northwestern Senegal. Authorities on El Hierro in the Canary Islands have declared an emergency after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.

At least 21 people were killed after a small boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of northwestern Senegal, Senegalese authorities said.

Thousands have died in recent years after embarking on boats from the Senegalese coast in order to reach Spain's Canary Islands through the perilous Atlantic route.

According to the Senegalese Interior Ministry, only one person was rescued from the capsizing, and 21 bodies were recovered.

The ministry added that the toll was "provisional" and that search operations were still ongoing.

The incident occurred near Kebemer, some 180 kilometers (around 112 miles) north of the capital, Dakar.

On Saturday, the ministry stressed the government's "determination to combat people smuggling networks, notably through strengthened cooperation with neighboring countries."

Senegalese authorities said they intercepted 142 migrants on a similar boat aimed at reaching Spanish territory on Friday. The boat included nationals of multiple West African countries.

Authorities on the island of El Hierro have declared an emergency due to increased migrant arrivals Image: Jesus Cabrera/REUTERS

El Hierro island declares emergency over migrant arrivals

Authorities on El Hierro Island in the Canary Islands declared an emergency on Saturday after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.

El Hierro officials say that over 3,300 people have arrived on around 30 boats since the start of the month.

"We are very concerned... by this sharp increase in arrivals," Alpidio Armas, head of the El Hierro regional council, told Spanish television.

"This is precisely what has led us to declare an emergency in order to ensure a framework of cooperation with higher-level institutions," he added.

Armas said that conditions at the island's hospital have become "undesirable."

El Hierro is home to about 11,400 residents.

Migrant arrivals reached a record high of 46,000 in 2024. Afterwards, arrivals have fallen sharply due to increased surveillance and cooperation with African countries.

World.title: Iran: US strikes ship after Hormuz blockade breach
World.content:
The US military said a vessel trying to leave an Iranian port was hit due to the naval blockade on the country. On its part, Iran said three "non compliant" oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

The United States struck a commercial ship attempting to breach its naval blockade on Iran, the US military said Sunday.

According to the US Central Command (CENTCOM), the cargo vessel "tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port," before its stern was struck by "precision munitions" shot from a US military aircraft.

In a video posted by CENTCOM, an explosion can be seen on the M/V Huda's stern as a result of the shooting, with the ship's civilian crew ignoring "repeated warnings."

The authorities in the UAE said 22 people had been rescued due to a fire on a vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

What's the situation in the Strait of Hormuz?

The US naval blockade on Iran, intended to pressure the country into lifting its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, has been in force for months.

Iran's own blockade of the waterway, through which a fifth of the world's oil and gas supplies flowed before the war started in late February, saw energy prices spike around the world.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three "non-compliant" oil tankers caught fire while going through the Strait. Tehran has regularly attacked vessels going through the Strait of Hormuz without its approval.

Aramco building hit after rocket attack

Elsewhere in the Middle East, the escalation between Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi Arabia continued to rage.

Saudi Arabia said it had intercepted incoming missiles shot in the direction of the capital, Riyadh, on Sunday.

Debris from the interception damaged a building belonging to state-owned oil company Aramco. No casualties were reported, but some of the building's floors were heavily damaged, witnesses told AP.

Saudi Arabia accused Yemen-based militant group Houthisof launching two ballistic missiles and two cruise missiles.

While Houthis carried out such attacks in the past, the rebels have not claimed responsibility for the attack yet.

According to the Houthis, 33 people were killed in Saudi-led attacks on Yemen's rebel-held capital, Sanaa, on Saturday.

World.title: Gaza: Rains add misery to humanitarian catastrophe
World.content:
With most homes damaged or destroyed by the war, Gazans are facing worsening humanitarian conditions due to heavy rain.

Heavy rains sweeping across parts of the Middle East this week have flooded tens of thousands of tents in Gaza's displaced persons' camps.

According to authorities in the enclave, at least 70,000 tents have been flooded over the past day, where tens of thousands of people took shelter.

No fatalities had been reported, although some people were injured.

Some of the tents have been washed away due to the weather, with mattresses and blankets soaked with water.

Around 1 million Palestinians live in camps that lack proper shelter, water and sanitation Image: Dawoud Abu Alkas/REUTERS

Majority of houses destroyed

More than 1.6 million residents of Gaza's 2.1-million population now live in tents or other makeshift shelters due to Israel's war in the enclave.

UN data says some 80% of the enclave's structures have been damaged during the war, with two-thirds destroyed, leaving Gaza's residents — many of whom were displaced multiple times during the war between Israel and Hamas — to either live in tents or risk their lives and seek shelter in buildings that could be on the verge of collapse.

The Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs in Palestine released a statement appealing for humanitarian aid for the Gaza Strip due to the situation.

Tents were flooded as a result of the heavy rains in the region Image: Dawoud Abu Alkas/REUTERS

According to the committee, some 950,000 people are living in areas "vulnerable to flooding," with more than 400,000 living in areas of "high levels of risk."

"Heavy rainfall is compounding an already catastrophic humanitarian situation, leaving displaced families and those who have lost their homes exposed to the elements and deprived of the most basic necessities of life," the statement said.

Israel accused of genocide

Some 74,000 people have been killed in the Gaza Strip since October 7, 2023. The war was triggered when Islamist Palestinian organization Hamas and its affiliates launched a terrorist attack in Israel's south, killing some 1,200 Israelis, most of whom were civilians. The militants also kidnapped 251 hostages.

The UN, EU, US and Israel, among others, consider Hamas to be a terrorist organization.

A UN commission of inquiry, as well as many leading human rights organizations, have accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza. Israel has rejected the accusation, saying its army is acting in accordance with international law.

World.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
World.content:
Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

Young people pose inside a crematorium oven at the Buchenwald concentration camp memorial, laughing while they give the Nazi salute and take pictures of each other. "In a sense, they're trophies to post on social media for them to boast about — breaking the ultimate taboo," Jens-Christian Wagner, director of the Buchenwald and Mittelbau-Dora Memorials Foundation , told DW.

"Incidents like this have become more frequent in recent years. We have seen memorial trees planted in honor of concentration camp victims cut down. When something like this happens — and it happens regularly — I find it particularly despicable because, because it ultimately kills these people a second time," added Wagner.

Jens-Christian Wagner reports on rampant disrespect at the Buchenwald Memorial and warns against the distortion of history Image: Markus Schreiber/AP Photo/picture alliance

Wagner is part of the curatorial team behind the exhibition "Never Again! Against Forgetting the Crimes of the Nazi Regime " in Bonn's Bundeskunsthalle, or the Art and Exhibition Hall of the Federal Republic of Germany. Wagner said Holocaust remembrance is under pressure, and the subject of intensifying attacks.

Critics have dismissed remembrance as a "cult of guilt" or "national masochism." With right-wing populism on the rise and historical revisionism becoming more common, Wagner worries about how Germany will remember the victims murdered by the Nazi regime. He is also concerned about the future of democracy. And soon, there will be no Holocaust survivors left to tell the true story of what happened.

This new exhibition tackles this concern head-on with numerous works of art and historical artifacts.

Moralizing doesn't help people learn

"I hope that perhaps even some people who don't already believe it's important to confront Nazi crimes will find their way to the exhibition," Wagner said. Memorial sites also attract visitors who aren't necessarily convinced of the need to confront these parts of history. Many of them are students.

"Let's not kid ourselves: When a teacher says 'We're going there,' it's always a mandatory visit," he said.

For today's young people, the Nazi era seems like the distant past, Wagner explained. "When you tell them to remember something that their grandparents didn't even experience, it naturally feels like an emotional burden. They can practically see the finger being wagged at them, and that doesn't exactly encourage learning."

Visiting a Holocaust memorial site is a required part of the curriculum at many schools Image: Peter Gercke/dpa/picture alliance

A two-hour lecture won't have much of an impact if pupils aren't even paying attention. Instead, Buchenwald organizes full-day programs that allow students to explore historical sources together and make sense of history for themselves.

The next step, Wagner said, is to show young people that this chapter of history isn't closed. Visitors are encouraged to make connections between the past and current events like migration, for example.

"For the longest time, people have been discussing migration almost exclusively in terms of threats to public safety and crime. This broadly marginalizes certain groups — a mechanism that also worked for National Socialism," he said.

Holocaust survivor: 'The number tattooed on my arm was always there'

Eva Umlauf, 83, knows firsthand what it means to experience exclusion in its most extreme form. She is a patron of the Bonn exhibition.

In November 1944, Umlauf was just 2 years old when she, her pregnant mother and her father were deported by the Nazis from the Novaky labor camp in Slovakia to Auschwitz-Birkenau, the notorious Nazi concentration and extermination camp. She was saved from the gas chambers by mere days; the Nazis stopped using the chambers as the Red Army advanced, hoping to hide evidence of their crimes.

Germany's darkest chapter: Auschwitz and the Holocaust To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The camp was liberated on January 27, 1945. Three months later, Umlauf's sister Nora was born. But her father, her mother's siblings and her grandparents were all murdered. Eva barely survived herself. She suffered from tuberculosis, rickets and whooping cough, as well as edema caused by starvation. "Forget about the child. She won't survive," a doctor told her mother. But he was wrong.

Her mother returned to what was then Czechoslovakia with her two daughters, settling in Trencin. Eva Umlauf has no conscious memories of Auschwitz, but she carries her family's trauma deep within her.

Her mother never talked about what happened. Even so, Eva knew from an early age that she was a survivor. Her family rarely mentioned the camp by name, but one sentence came up again and again: "They stayed there." Eva knew that meant "they" were dead. And then, there was the number tattooed onto her arm: A26959.

Eva Umlauf has been president of the International Auschwitz Committee since 2025 Image: Alessandra Schellnegger/SZ Photo/picture alliance

Eva Umlauf: 'I cannot forgive'

Her mother taught her daughters not to draw attention to their Jewish identity — antisemitism was widespread throughout Czechoslovakia at the time. The small family managed to avoid harassment.

Eva Umlauf wanted to become a pediatrician, so she studied medicine. In the 1960s, she met her future husband, Jakob, who had also survived the Holocaust. He was an architect, active in Munich's Jewish community. They married in 1966, and she moved to Germany. She could hardly have imagined that she would one day live in the country of the perpetrators. "I don't hate Germans," she said. "But I cannot forgive. How can you forgive the deaths of 6 million people?"
