World.title: Tartu Peace Treaty talks table on display at Ministry of Foreign Affairs
World.content:
The historic negotiating table used during the Tartu Peace Treaty talks between Estonia and the Soviet Union (1919-1920) is now temporarily on display at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The table was used by the delegations to reach an agreement before the signing of the document on February 2, 1920, in Estonia's second-largest city, Tartu.

The treaty ended the Estonian War of Independence that had lasted for almost 18 months after Estonia declared independence. The agreement was one of the first major achievements in the field of international relations for the young state.

The treaty established Estonia's eastern border, and Soviet Russia recognized Estonian independence de jure, renouncing voluntarily "for ever all rights of sovereignty formerly held by Russia over the Esthonian people and territory".

The Treaty of Tartu was also the first international act recognizing the Soviet government.

"It certainly has enormous symbolic significance and value for us," said Rasmus Lumi, undersecretary for Administrative Affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Members of the Estonian delegation at the signing of the Treaty of Tartu. At center is Jaan Poska. Source: Muis/Estonian War Museum

"That is why we want it to be visible to all our guests, including foreign visitors, to whom we can tell the history of Estonia and the history of diplomacy. Of course, we will also try to find opportunities to hold signing ceremonies of greater symbolic significance at this very table," he explained.

The oval wooden table is on display at the ministry while the Tartu City Museum undergoes renovation. It was transferred to Tallinn as part of the Athens 2026 evacuation exercise to practice protecting valuable cultural heritage in a crisis situation.

The piece of furniture is unusually large – 3.4 × 2.4 meters –and was known as the peace table even before the negotiations. It was believed that those sitting around it would find common ground despite their differences.

Minister of Foreign Affairs Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said the treaty "reminds us that what seems impossible can become reality."

He added: "With the will to defend its freedom and the support of allies, even a small nation can defeat a far larger adversary. Estonia proved it."

The original Tartu Peace Treaty. Source: EV100

World.title: Demand for raw milk leading to supermarket shortages, farmers say
World.content:
Farmers have said there are no milk shortages in Estonia – despite gaps on supermarket shelves – but competition for raw milk has intensified as companies look for ways to make higher-value items, such as protein-rich products.

Earlier this week, ERR reported there were shortages of milk sold in plastic bags in some of Estonia's supermarkets.

Marta Palm, purchasing manager at Rimi Estonia, said around two weeks ago the producer of Rimi Smart milk told the supermarket there were supply difficulties.

"We have been in very close contact with the producer, and the producer has said that the transition to new feed had temporarily made raw milk production more difficult," she said.

One of the suppliers of milk in plastic bags, Maag Food, declined to comment on the issue to Saturday's "Aktuaalne kaamera" evening news show. But Lenno Link, head of dairy farming company Väätsa Agro, said changing feed generally does not affect production, which is usually "very stable".

Bagged milk in an Estonian supermarket. Photo is illustrative. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Raw milk production is actually increasing in Estonia by around 100 tons each year, as processors are competing for raw milk more than before.

"People are consuming more and more protein. This is largely also thanks to weight-loss drugs, and animal protein is being added everywhere, to various products. Whey protein powder, which is produced from raw milk, has become very scarce," Link said.

Prices on the European milk market have risen by around 10 percent in recent months. This gives dairy farmers hope of signing more favorable supply contracts with processors for next year.

The Estonian Chamber of Agriculture and Commerce said the tense period of contract negotiations may be one reason why supplies of milk in plastic bags have been disrupted in recent weeks.

"This competition means that raw material prices are rising, dairy processors have to pay more to obtain milk, and so they are looking for ways to process that milk into higher-value products to add more value to it. The question is rather whether milk in plastic bags can be sold in stores at a price that is also fair to producers," said Ants-Hannes Viira, head of agricultural policy at the chamber.

"Milk in plastic bags is certainly not going to disappear from the mainstream market anytime soon. I have been in the dairy industry for over 20 years, and there has been constant talk about milk in plastic bags disappearing, but today we still see that consumption of milk in plastic bags in Estonia is 100 tons per day," said Valio CEO Maido Solovjov.

According to Rimi's purchasing manager, Maag Food has promised to resume its deliveries of milk in plastic bags next week, and the retailer has pledged not to raise the product's price.

World.title: More migrants caught in Tallinn, 1 foreigner found dead in apartment
World.content:
A 21-year-old man from Pakistan was confirmed dead by police at an apartment in Tallinn on Saturday. Eight illegal migrants who said they had traveled from Latvia to Estonia were also found in the same location.

At around 4 p.m. on Saturday, foreign nationals staying in an apartment on Tehnika tänav called an ambulance for one of their companions. Paramedics who arrived at the scene confirmed the death of a 21-year-old man of Pakistani origin and informed the police. Officers responding to the scene found no external signs of violence on the body.

Inna Toater, operations manager at the North Prefecture, said there were eight other foreign nationals in the apartment, and checks revealed that they were staying in Estonia illegally.

"According to preliminary information, the men arrived in Estonia today from Latvia. According to the men themselves, they were involved in a traffic accident in Latvia last night, when the vehicle transporting them veered off the road. We are currently establishing how the men reached Estonia and under what circumstances one of them died," she said.

Toater said the health of the other foreign nationals in the apartment was also checked.

"Three men were taken to hospital for further medical examinations, while the remaining five were taken to a detention center," she explained.

The body of the 21-year-old man was sent for an autopsy to determine the cause of death. Police are continuing to investigate the exact circumstances of the incident.

According to preliminary information, the eight foreign nationals are from Afghanistan, Morocco and Ethiopia.

Thousands of migrants have crossed the Belarusian-Latvian border into the European Union without the correct documentation this year in what officials say is a "hybrid attack" orchestrated by the regime in Minsk.

The migrants, mostly from Africa and the Middle East, then travel on to other countries in western or northern Europe, using Estonia as a transit country. However, more than 400 people have been caught in Estonia this year after Poland and Germany boosted security checks on their borders, and smugglers changed their routes.

When apprehended, the migrants are usually returned to Latvia under EU rules.

World.title: Mystery orange 'fireball' over Estonia turns out to be aircraft contrails
World.content:
A bright orange object that appeared to fall towards the ground was reported over both in Tallinn and Lääne County on Thursday afternoon, Maaleht said .

However, Taavi Niittee of the Tõrva Astronomy Club said the photographs taken most likely captured planes, or rather their condensation trails lit by low-angle sunlight.

The effect occurs when a contrail left by a high-flying aircraft is lit by the sun low on the horizon, as it is at this time of year, turning a bright orange or red hue ahead of sunset and resembling a burning object.

Contrails consist of small ice crystals formed from water vapor in aircraft exhaust and can persist in the sky for some time depending on weather conditions.

If the aircraft is moving at certain angles relative to the observer, the glowing trail can look as though it is "falling" from the sky.

Niittee said there is nothing unusual about the sighting, describing it as relatively common on clear evenings at this time of year.

A meteor, by contrast, appears when a small body from space enters the atmosphere at high speed and begins to glow, typically lasting only a few seconds.

A contrail can remain visible for several minutes or longer, making this the simplest way to tell the two apart.

Niittee advised anyone seeing something similar to check air traffic, for example the Flightradar24 site, where you can see flights in real time, as well as all flights in the preceding 24 hours.

World.title: Rally car, sword fight and football: President Ülle Madise's Father's Day
World.content:
President Ülle Madise gets into a rally car, plays football with fathers and sons, joins a band rehearsal and takes part in a historical sword fight in a Father's Day show airing Sunday.

The broadcast is called "Isadepäev Vabariigi Presidendiga Mulgimaal" ("Father's Day with the President in Mulgimaa") and follows the president through the villages of Raasilla, Holstre and Mustla, where different generations work together and traditions pass from fathers to children.

Mulgimaa is a distinct historical region of South Estonia, primarily covering present-day Viljandi County and parts of Valga County. Its small villages, the show highlights, have an active community life in which generations take part in shared activities.

The show sees the head of state embark on a forest hike alongside the rally track and the other activities, taking part rather than simply observing.

It will close with a presidential address to fathers across Estonia. The show was pre-recorded, and highlights can be seen in the gallery above.

"Isadepäev Vabariigi Presidendiga Mulgimaal" airs on ETV at 8.30 p.m. on Father's Day, Sunday, November 8, with sign language interpretation on ETV2 and in Russian on ETV+.

World.title: Gallery: PÖFF presents lifetime awards on opening night
World.content:
The 30th Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) opened at Alexela Concert Hall in Tallinn Friday, with lifetime achievement awards given out to three people.

Animator Priit Pärn, composer Sven Grünberg, both from Estonia, plus Icelandic director Hilmar Oddsson were the recipients.

Oddsson, 69, is one of the film-makers who helped put Icelandic cinema on the world map in the 1980s. His most recent film, "Á Ferð með Mömmu" ("Driving Mum"), which involved Estonian film-makers, won PÖFF's grand prix in 2022. Awarding him is also a nod to the Nordic auteurs the festival began with in 1997 — Oddsson was one of them, and his film "Tár úr steini" ("Tears of Stone"), which brought him to Tallinn 29 years ago, screens again in the anniversary program "PÖFF tähistab" ("PÖFF celebrates").

Grünberg, who turns 70 shortly, was honored for his contribution to Estonian film music. He has scored nearly 130 Estonian and foreign films, seen by tens if not hundreds of millions of people. His credits include "Hukkunud Alpinisti hotell", "Leiutajateküla Lotte", and "Naksitrallid"," and the series "Wikmani poisid".

Pärn, who recently turned 80, was honored for his contribution to Estonian animation and is Estonia's most internationally known film-maker. This is his 13th lifetime achievement award. His 1987 film "Eine murul" remains one of the deepest portraits of the oppressive Soviet everyday, and his own teaching system has produced a generation of animators in Finland, Estonia and beyond.

The 30h annual PÖFF festival got underway on Friday and runs until Sunday, November 22, with 230 feature films and 259 shorts from 87 countries being screened during that time.

World.title: U.S. Envoy Barrack warns Iraq on faction arms as disarmament plan stalls
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – U.S. Special Envoy Tom Barrack concluded his second high-stakes diplomatic visit to Baghdad within a month, delivering blunt warnings to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi against allowing Iranian-aligned armed factions to drag Iraq into a regional military conflagration.

According to an investigative report published by Al-Mada newspaper, Barrack participated directly in a high-level phone conference between President Donald Trump and Al-Zaidi—attended by U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Steven Fagin—wherein Washington firmly cautioned against Iraqi militias reviving their “Unity of Fronts” operational doctrine.

The diplomatic pressure coincides with a severe domestic impasse surrounding Baghdad’s planned weapons-confinement initiative. Leaks obtained by Al-Mada confirm that several prominent armed factions formally notified Al-Zaidi of their refusal to surrender munitions at this juncture, citing the imminent risk of widespread conflict with Iran.

The fissures deepened following the collapse of talks within the Shia “Coordination Framework” and the failure of its four-party committee, prompted by Al-Zaidi’s decision to personally steer the negotiations based on advice from U.S. officials, including Barrack. This operational divide was underscored on the ground by Iraqi security forces intercepting and arresting three Hashd al-Shaabi affiliates transporting 35 surface-to-surface rockets through Latifiyah, just south of Baghdad near the faction stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhar.

Political analysts indicate that Washington is unwilling to accept Baghdad’s proposed compromise of “conditional disarmament,” which sought to store heavy weaponry within institutional depots in exchange for diplomatic guarantees regarding sovereignty and Turkish military presence.

Political scientist Aqeel Abbas noted that the Trump administration demands full, unconditional state control over arms, warning that mid-term election dynamics could incentivize the White House to accelerate regional military action against Tehran before the new congressional term begins.

Concurrently, foreign relations analyst Kato Saadallah highlighted that Barrack’s mission serves as an uncompromising gauge of the Iraqi cabinet’s capacity to uphold sovereign neutrality and restrain paramilitaries following the full withdrawal of U.S. military forces completed in late September.

World.title: US dollar edges higher across Iraq near 169,000 dinars
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar registered a slight upward tick across major parallel markets on Sunday morning, November 8, 2026, ending roughly a week of consolidation near 167,000 IQD per $100 and testing the 169,000-dinar ceiling in the capital.

According to morning market data, physical foreign exchange counters across major commercial hubs traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange desks recorded retail selling rates at 169,000 IQD against buying bids of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Selling rates settled at 168,500 IQD alongside purchase offers of 168,000 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange bureaus quoted retail sales at 168,750 IQD and buying rates at 168,250 IQD per $100.

The slight upward adjustment widens the spread between parallel market trading and the official benchmark established by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), which remains fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar). The modest shift highlights persistent friction in matching cash foreign currency supply with informal commercial demand across secondary markets.

World.title: Iraqi weightlifter Ali Ammar wins World Championship Title in Ningbo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi weightlifter Ali Ammar was crowned world champion in the super-heavyweight (+110 kg) division at the 2026 World Weightlifting Championships held in Ningbo, China, securing three podium finishes comprising two golds and one silver.

Ammar clinched gold in the snatch with a successful lift of 211 kilograms, followed by a silver medal in the clean and jerk at 255 kilograms. His combined score reached 466 kilograms, securing the gold medal in total lift and sealing the world championship title against an elite international field.

The triumph marks a landmark milestone for Iraqi weightlifting, reinforcing the country’s competitive standing in top-tier international athletics and elevating prospects for future Olympic cycles.

World.title: Iraq seeks to resolve diplomatic differences with Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said that the country is actively attempting to use frank discussions to tackle diplomatic and security issues with Saudi Arabia.

During a recent interview with Al-Jazeera, Hussein indicated that Baghdad has proofs that both local and foreign armed groups have been using Iraqi territory to carry out cross-border assaults against neighboring Gulf States.

Saudi Arabia has long accused Iran-aligned armed groups operating in Iraq of targeting its critical infrastructure. Baghdad acknowledged in September that the drones attacking Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline had come from Iraqi territory.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reassured Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that Iraq will not allow its territory to be used to attack neighboring countries.

The Iraqi government is in discussions with groups associated with Iran to bring their weaponry under the state’s control.

Hussein stressed that rather than using military action, Baghdad is trying to bring the firearms of armed groups under state control through diplomatic communications.

Powerful groups such as Kataeb Hezbollah continue to oppose arms control frameworks, whereas Asa’ib Ahl al-Haq has consented to them.

After regional warfare interruptions, oil exports through the vital Strait of Hormuz were suspended, costing Iraq an estimated $60 billion in revenue. To stabilize the country’s oil-dependent economy, strengthening connections with Gulf neighbors is considered crucial.

Hussein emphasized that Baghdad opposes any foreign interference in its internal affairs, notwithstanding the Iraqi leadership’s insistence that it desires a positive partnership with Tehran.

Baghdad is trying to prevent itself from turning into a proxy war zone while preserving its crucial diplomatic and economic connections in the Middle East by openly proposing communication to Riyadh.

World.title: Shia leaders launch urgent mediation to defuse standoff between Al Zaidi and armed factions
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Hikma Movement leader Ammar Al-Hakim and Islamic Supreme Council of Iraq (ISCI) head Humam Hammoudi have launched an urgent political mediation between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and Kata’ib Hezbollah, seeking to de-escalate tensions and avert potential armed confrontation.

Backed by the broader Coordination Framework, the diplomatic intervention aims to preserve internal security following a sharp confrontation between Baghdad and the armed faction.

The rift widened after Al-Zaidi directed security agencies to execute outstanding arrest warrants against faction-linked individuals and canceled three commercial contracts at Mosul International Airport—comprising Sky Plus (check-in counters), Sama Al-Matar (parking facilities), and Al-Faisal Al-Shamekh (taxi concessions)—citing affiliations with armed groups, with instructions to reassign operations to international ground-handling and management firms.

Kata’ib Hezbollah escalated its rhetoric against the administration, directing accusations at the prime minister’s brother, Hassan Al-Zaidi, and condemning what it described as hostility toward resistance factions.

Concurrently, the faction’s security official, Abu Mujahid Al-Assaf, criticized the government’s economic performance and accused political figures within the Coordination Framework of facilitating discounted oil sales and revenue splits amounting to 4.5 trillion dinars per month.

The crisis has also complicated disarmament talks. Members of the Shia “Four-Party Committee”—including Badr Organization leader Hadi Al-Ameri—expressed frustration over Al-Zaidi conducting unilateral discussions with factions that reject disarmament (notably Kata’ib Hezbollah, Harakat Al-Nujaba, and Kata’ib Sayyid Al-Shuhada), arguing that direct talks undermine the institutional committee’s roadmap slated for completion by June 2027.

The political dispute unfolds against backdrop pressures from Washington, where the U.S. State Department and the White House have reiterated backing for Al-Zaidi’s efforts to enforce the sovereign monopoly on arms and eliminate parallel military command structures.

World.title: Dubai-based restaurant AMAYA expands to Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dubai-based restaurant and lounge brand MYA, also known as AMAYA, has announced the opening of its new branch in Baghdad, expanding its presence in Iraq following its earlier launch in Erbil.

The new restaurant, on Al-Amirat Street in Baghdad’s Al-Mansour area, introduces the brand’s luxury dining and lounge concept to the Iraqi capital.

MYA, which debuted in Dubai Mall in 2022, specializes in worldwide fusion cuisine with Mediterranean influences, blending a varied menu with modern decor, quality service, and a luxurious lounge environment.

The Baghdad launch is part of the brand’s worldwide development via franchise agreements, which builds on its current operations in Dubai and Erbil.

The firm said that its growth strategy is centered on working with local franchise partners that can maintain its dining standards while adjusting to the tastes of each area.

The new Baghdad site is another step in MYA’s development in Iraq, reflecting the continuing entry of multinational restaurant and hotel brands into the country’s eating scene.

World.title: Habib Beirut to open second Baghdad branch at Iraq Mall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Lebanese restaurant chain Habib Beirut Group plans to launch its second branch in Baghdad in December 2026, strengthening its foothold in Iraq with a new site at Iraq Mall.

The restaurant will have two levels, seating for approximately 300 people, and views of the mall’s fountain.

The new location will provide traditional Lebanese food and hospitality, trying to recreate the ambiance of Beirut in Baghdad.

Edarat Hospitality Group-Iraq and the Iraq Mall Team are collaborating on the opening.

Habib Beirut already has a restaurant on the fourth floor of the World Heart Hotel in Baghdad’s Al-Jadriyah area, as well as sites at the Gulan Mall in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah.

The forthcoming Iraq Mall location will help the brand increase its footprint in Iraq’s burgeoning restaurant and hotel industry.

World.title: Iraq restricts airspace as United States calls for Iran border closures
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has issued temporary airspace restrictions from November 7 to 11, citing military operations, as Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein warned of rising regional tensions and the potential of fresh violence.

According to an aviation notification (NOTAM), the limitations will apply daily between 05:00 and 11:00 UTC, disrupting airplane operations throughout Iraqi airspace, including routes servicing Baghdad, Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, and Kirkuk.

The events came as Hussein stated that the US has officially demanded that Iraq block all border crossings with neighboring Iran, save two.

Hussein also stated that Iraqi authorities had evidence that foreign parties were exploiting Iraqi territory to conduct assaults on neighboring nations, creating worries about Iraq’s sovereignty and regional security.

He also cautioned that present conditions lead to the prospect of further conflict in the area, as Iraq is under growing strain from tensions between Iran and the US.

The issue underlines Iraq’s challenging position in the face of regional instability, as the government seeks to safeguard its sovereignty, maintain border security, and avoid becoming a battlefield for larger geopolitical disputes.

World.title: ‘Matter of personal faith’: Congress on Akhilesh Yadav’s proposed Ram Temple visit
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Congress on Sunday described Samajwadi Party (SP) president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Akhilesh Yadavâs proposed December 12 visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya as a âmatter of personal faith.

"

The two parties are allies in the state.

Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam questioned why any political leader should object to the SP chief's proposed visit.

âReligion is a matter of personal faith. Whether someone wants to visit a temple, mosque, gurudwara, church, Buddhist monastery, or Jain temple is entirely their personal choice,â he told ANI.

âOur Constitution gives everyone the freedom of religion and worship.



So why should any political leader have a problem with that?â the Congress leader asked.

Gautam's remarks came amid attacks by BJP leaders, including Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and deputy chief minister Brijesh Pathak, on Akhilesh Yadav over his proposed Ram Temple visit. They cited the 1990 police firing on "kar sevaks" (volunteers), which took place when Akhilesh Yadav's father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the chief minister.





This comes a day after SP leader Pawan Pandey claimed Akhilesh Yadav will visit Ayodhya with his family on December 12 to offer prayers at the Hanuman Garhi temple and seek blessings at the Ram Temple.

"On December 12th, the national president of the Samajwadi Party and former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Akhilesh Yadav, will visit Ayodhya along with his family," Pandey said, referring to the BJP-led government, currently in its second term.

World.title: ‘Why funding only for temples?’ Congress's Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury flags Bengal’s Rs 1,000-crore plan
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury on Sunday questioned the BJP-led West Bengal government's proposed Rs 1,000 crore spending over the next two years to renovate and restore ancient temples and monasteries across the state under the 'Tirthakshetra Circuit'.Speaking to reporters on the occasion of Kali Puja and Diwali, Chowdhury said the country did not belong to any one religion and that the government should adopt an inclusive approach."There are Gurdwaras and mosques, too; why is funding given only to temples? If resources are to be allocated, it must be done for everyone, for people of all religions. Our country does not belong to just one religion," he said.He added that resources should be made available to people of all religions and urged the government not to create divisions among religious communities.He also appealed to the government not to create divisions between communities and called for an approach that included everyone.Meanwhile, Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge extended Diwali greetings on Sunday, wishing people happiness, peace and harmony.In a post on X, Rahul said, "Warm wishes to you and your family for Diwali! May the lamps of joy and prosperity light up every home. May this sacred festival bring happiness, peace, harmony, and the light of new hopes to all of India."Kharge, in his Diwali message, wished for the darkness of injustice and ignorance to be dispelled and for the light of justice, equality and goodwill to reach every person."On my behalf, and on behalf of all Congress Party leaders and workers, I extend heartfelt wishes to all our fellow citizens for Diwali. May this sacred festival of lights spread the glow of happiness, peace, prosperity and joy in every home and courtyard. May the flame of love, brotherhood and harmony always burn brightly in our society. May the darkness of injustice, ignorance and discrimination be dispelled, and may the light of justice, equality and goodwill reach every person. May the lamp of hope burn in every heart, and may every life be greeted by a new dawn of happiness," said Kharge.

World.title: ‘Not a political book, but a personal one’: Sonia Gandhi ahead of memoir release
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two days before the India release of her memoir, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi on Sunday described it as ânot a political book but a personal one," emphasising that she wanted to portray her family "honestly," as people she knew and loved.

âThis is not a political book, itâs a personal one. Much has been written about my family, but rarely with real insight into who they were, their motivations, their struggles, their very human flaws. I wanted to portray them honestly, as people I knew and loved,â the Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson wrote on X.

She gave a detailed account of how the book, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love," came to be, in an article for The Hindu, which had published a

with her on Saturday.



"For most of my life, I kept my inner world to myself. Even after grief pulled me into politics, I held on to whatever privacy I could, and writing openly about my life felt almost unthinkable. Only after stepping back from the daily churn of public life could I see my own story clearly," Sonia Gandhi wrote in the article, referring to the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, who was India's youngest Prime Minister.





"When I did look back, one thread ran through all of it: love, and the loyalty that grows from it. It all began in England, where a 19-year-old woman from a small Italian town met a young Indian student (Rajiv Gandhi). It carried me into a new country and a new family, into a deep bond with my mother-in-law (Indira Gandhi), and through the years of raising our children," she added,

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"It also carried me through the unbearable, when I lost first my mother-in-law and then my husband to violence," the former Congress president wrote.

Published by HarperCollins India, Sonia Gandhi's memoir will be released in India on November 10, ending uncertainty over the book's domestic publication following an "impasse" between the author's representatives and Penguin Random House India.

The book covers major tragedies that impacted the Gandhi family, including the death of Sonia Gandhi's brother-in-law Sanjay Gandhi in a plane crash, Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984 and Rajiv Gandhi's assassination in 1991.

The memoir also delves into political events surrounding the Congress' victory in the 2004 elections, when Sonia Gandhi declined to become Prime Minister and instead led the party and its alliance, which governed India till 2014.

World.title: Evening Newswrap: PM Modi warns of 'Dimagi Naxals', Mamata joins Abhishek Banerjee's protest & more
World.content:
PM Modi warned "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated political parties despite armed Maoists being wiped out.

Mamata joined Abhishek Banerjee's protest after an overnight BJP-TMC clash; each side blamed the other.

Trump's offer of the press secretary job to UFC's Dana White sparked speculation he confused him with another Dana White.

Sensex ended at 80,999.40 and Nifty at 24,986.40 as Muhurat trading closed flat.

A US memo says officials believe Nvidia's Jensen Huang dated Alice Huang, suspected of spying for China.

Here are the top stories of the day

PM Modi warns of 'Dimagi Naxals' in political parties after armed Maoists wiped out

Addressing security personnel at a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar on Diwali, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the threat of Naxalism was not over even though armed Maoists had been eliminated from the forests.

He claimed "Dimagi Naxals" had infiltrated several political parties and organisations and were inciting people against the Constitution, and said the country needed to identify and defeat them.

Mamata joins protest at Abhishek Banerjee's residence after overnight clash with BJP workers

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee joined TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee in a protest at his Kalighat residence after an overnight confrontation between TMC and BJP supporters. Abhishek alleged BJP workers attacked his home after two days of reconnaissance and called it the seventh attempt on his life in six months, while the BJP blamed a birthday gathering held on a public road.



Mamata accused the BJP of hooliganism and said she had written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.

Did Trump mistake UFC boss Dana White for another Dana White while offering press secretary job?

US president Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that he had offered the White House press secretary's job to Dana White, the UFC president and CEO and a longtime ally, urging him to take it. The announcement sparked widespread speculation that Trump may have confused him with Dana W White, a former Pentagon public affairs official reportedly on a shortlist for the role.





The UFC chief eventually turned down the offer, CNN reported, after initially appearing to play along with an Instagram story captioned "On to the next chapter.

"

World.title: Watch: Sonia, Priyanka take a trip down memory lane, recall Diwali with Rajiv Gandhi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her daughter, Priyanka Gandhi, revisited memories of Diwali celebrations with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.

In a conversation shared on social media, Sonia Gandhi recalled her fondness for Diwali, describing the elaborate decorations, traditional rituals and festive gatherings that marked the celebrations.

"Oh, Diwali I loved. So, Diwali was always beautiful," she recalled in a video shared on her Instagram account.

Recalling the traditional rituals, Sonia said a Ganesh idol was placed at the entrance of the house, where the first diya of the celebrations was lit. She added that the idol is now kept at her residence.

"At the entrance, there used to be a Ganesh Murti, which is now in my house. And so, we would do the first lighting of the diya in front of Ganesh Ji's Murti.



And it was always decorated. In those days, we didn't have those little lights everywhere, but we had diyas everywhere - around the pond, all along the roof, veranda, and along the path, wherever there was a path. So, it was very pretty," she said.

Priyanka Gandhi, the MP from Wayanad, also recalled how festivals were celebrated with great enthusiasm, with people from different walks of life gathering in the Gandhi family's garden.





Sonia remembered how the family would sometimes get carried away with firecrackers, while Priyanka recalled how her father, Rajiv Gandhi, would take them to Chandni Chowk in Old Delhi to buy crackers.

"Papa used to take us to Chandni Chowk to buy crackers. We used to go to Old Delhi to buy crackers," Priyanka recalled.

Sonia also remembered phuljhadis, or traditional sparklers, saying she enjoyed them, although she was less enthusiastic about some of the noisier fireworks.

Beyond the lights and firecrackers, Sonia said the atmosphere during the festive season remained particularly memorable. Recalling the weather during those celebrations, she spoke about the clear blue skies that formed the backdrop to the festivities.

"Weather at that time was beautiful. Blue skies and all, which you hardly see now. Yeah, it was lovely," she said.

Sonia also recalled that festivals were marked by Kashmiri cuisine and a traditional sweet rice preparation, a culinary tradition that continues in the family.

"And then, on festivals, we always used to have Kashmiri food and that sweet rice, like that, which we still make, by the way," she said.

Sonia Gandhi has also documented several personal experiences and significant moments from her life in her memoir, titled *Belonging: A Journey of Love*. The book is scheduled to be launched on November 10.

The memoir chronicles Sonia Gandhi's journey, from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance that brought her to India to the personal losses that profoundly shaped her life and her relationship with her adopted country.

In the book, the 79-year-old Congress veteran, who holds the distinction of being the party's longest-serving president, revisits her childhood in Italy, her relationship with Rajiv Gandhi during their time at Cambridge, and the assassinations of her mother-in-law, former prime minister Indira Gandhi, and her husband, Rajiv Gandhi.

World.title: 'Jhola-picking-up time fast approaching': Congress takes swipe at PM Modi over 'Dimagi Naxals' remark
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Sunday slammed Prime Minister Narendra Modi for targeting political rivals during his Diwali address to security personnel at a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) camp in Chhattisgarh, accusing him of using a non-political occasion to launch a political attack.

In a post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh objected to

's remarks on "Dimagi Naxals", alleging that the prime minister had violated institutional norms by making political remarks while wearing the uniform of security personnel.

"The Prime Minister has not spared the nation even on Diwali day his trademark abuse. He has once again spoken of what he calls dimagi naxals. He has used a very solemn non-political occasion, donned the uniform of the security forces, and hurled invectives at his political rivals.



This is a brazen assault on all institutional norms but when has that ever stopped this man?" Jairam Ramesh said.

"It was on April 28, 2024 that he had said that those demanding a caste census were urban naxals. Later on April 30, 2025, he announced that a caste census will be carried out as part of Census 2027. Earlier, in Sept 2020, he had called those agitating against the three black farm laws as supporters of a naxal ideology.





Later, on Nov 19, 2021, he withdrew those very laws. The PM is clearly distraught, disturbed and desperate.

Jhola-picking-up time is fast approaching," he added.

Ramesh's remarks came after PM Modi said that although armed Naxalites had been eliminated from forests, the threat of Naxalism persisted, with "Dimagi Naxals" allegedly exercising influence over several organisations, including political parties.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Addressing security personnel at a CRPF camp in Karanpur in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, PM Modi said such elements were inciting people against the Constitution and democracy and needed to be identified and defeated.

"We must remember one thing. Naxalites have been eliminated, but the threat is not yet over. While armed Naxalites have been wiped out from the forests, 'Dimagi Naxals' have taken control of several organisations. Even today, they are inciting people against the country's Constitution and democracy. These 'Dimagi Naxals' have also infiltrated several political parties and different organisations. We must identify them, defeat them and ensure the security of the nation," he said.

The remarks came months after the Centre announced on March 31 that the country had been freed from the menace of Naxalism, following the elimination of several Maoist leaders and cadres and the surrender of hundreds of others.

World.title: 'Spreading propaganda against Ayodhya out of fear': Yogi Adityanath targets SP, Congress
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Sunday accused the

(SP) and the Congress of spreading "propaganda" against Ayodhya, claiming that the two opposition parties were "uncomfortable" with the development of the temple town and the infrastructure projects being undertaken across the state.

"People are now maligning Ayodhya out of fear. They are spreading propaganda against Ayodhya because they know that if this journey of heritage and development continues in the same manner, the politics of the Samajwadi Party and the Congress will be buried forever," PTI quoted the chief minister as sayiing. He was addressing a Diwali programme in Gorakhpur.

"Those who once created an identity crisis for the state will now face a crisis of their own political identity.



If this journey continues with the same strength and unity, the Congress and the Samajwadi Party will themselves face an identity crisis," he added.

Adityanath's remarks came a day after he took an apparent swipe at Samajwadi Party president and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister

over his proposed visit to the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.

According to SP leader Pawan Pandey, Akhilesh Yadav and his family will visit the temple on December 12 to offer prayers.





Also Read |

This would be the SP chief's first visit to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.

"Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathi-charge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions," Adityanath said in Ayodhya on Saturday without naming his predecessor.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Also Read |

"There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga," he added.

In 1990, Uttar Pradesh Police opened fire on "kar sevaks" (volunteers) marching towards the Babri Mosque, which stood at the erstwhile disputed site in Ayodhya. Akhilesh Yadav's father Mulayam Singh Yadav was Uttar Pradesh chief minister at the time.

The mosque was demolished on December 6, 1992.

In November 2019, a Constitution bench of the Supreme Court ruled in favour of the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.

World.title: 3 Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for staying without valid documents
World.content:
Three Nigerian nationals arrested in Delhi for overstaying without valid documents and sent to a detention centre

NEW DELHI: Three Nigerian nationals were arrested by the Delhi Police for allegedly staying in India without valid documents and subsequently sent to a detention centre, news agency PTI reported citing officials on Sunday.Following their arrest, they were produced before the foreigners regional registration office (FRRO) and later sent to Sewa Sadan detention centre in Lampur, officials said.The arrests were made on October 31 during a verification drive in southwest Delhi's Dwarka.The three men allegedly failed to produce documents authorising their stay in the country.Police identified the accused as Bartholomew Uwaebuka Iloegbunem, Konan Okocha alias Konan Brice Kousaai and Ndubuisi Charles Nwabufor.

World.title: 23 dead in clashes between South Sudan government, opposition forces
World.content:
Four weeks of clashes between South Sudan government and opposition forces in the north of the impoverished country have left 23 people dead while thousands have fled the conflict zone, authorities and police said Sunday.

Hundreds of people have died in clashes across South Sudan in recent weeks between forces loyal to President Salva Kiir and those of detained former vice president Riek Machar and other ethnic unrest, as the world's youngest country heads towards national elections scheduled for December 22.

Ruweng administrative area's information minister Tony Chol Ayat told AFP that fighters from Riek Machar's SPLA-IO force had entered Ruweng from neighbouring Unity state.

He said fighting between October 4 and Thursday this week had left 23 dead and 17 wounded. The toll was confirmed by two police sources.

Chol Ayat said that more than 100,000 people had fled the fighting while one of the police sources confirmed "thousands" had left the area.

A resident in Ruweng told AFP that SPLA-IO fighters had started fighting and that "the government built up forces on the front lines and the rebel armies were repelled".

Another Ruweng resident said there were fears of heightened conflict. Both spoke on condition of anonymity.

A South Sudan army spokesman would not comment on events, while Riek Machar's forces did not respond to an AFP query.

Independent since 2011, South Sudan is one of the world's poorest countries with widespread corruption. Saalva Kiir and Riek Machar's forces fought a civil war from 2013 to 2018 that left more than 400,000 dead.

The country's first presidential and legislative election has already been postponed several times and a UN human rights commission, which has accused the country's elite of siphoning off billions of dollars of oil revenues, has said an election in current tensions could unleash widespread new conflict.

World.title: Jean Drèze urges T.N. govt. to take strict action amid report of ‘fake book’ at Kalaignar Centenary Library
World.content:
Economist Jean Drèze on Sunday (November 8, 2026) said an English-language book attributed to him as the author and allegedly found in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu is “fake”.

The confirmation comes following a media report alleging that a title listed in Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library may not have been authored by Mr. Drèze. The book which lists him as the author was identified as the title ‘Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World’’.

“I am foxed and baffled to read on social media that a book called Democracy and Peoples Right in the Contemporary World, attributed to me, has surfaced in some public libraries of Tamil Nadu. If this book exists under my name, it must be fake, because I have never authored such a book,” he wrote in a clarification issued to The Hindu via e-mail.

Mr. Drèze urged the Tamil Nadu government to take “strict and swift action against the publishers of this fake book and other culprits”. “It is important to stem the rot before it spreads, all the more so if this book was AI-generated,” he added.

The economist also raised questions on procurement checks in place at public libraries and said: “The issue is not just that a fake book was printed but also how it was procured by a public library. Surely it would have taken little effort to ascertain the authenticity of this book.”

According to the media report, the book in question was allegedly procured from Phoenix Publishers and carries a valid International Standard Book Number. It also further alleged that the address of Phoenix Publishers is the same as that of Akal Vilakku Publishers.

The procurement date cited in the report is June 25, 2023 before the inauguration of the library. Madurai’s Kalaignar Centenary Library was inaugurated on July 15, 2023, by the then Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin.

World.title: Fire breaks out at factory in southwest Delhi's Najafgarh; 22 fire tenders rushed
World.content:
A fire broke out at a factory in the Najafgarh area on Sunday (November 8, 2026), prompting the deployment of 22 fire service vehicles, an official of the Delhi Fire Service said.

The blaze was reported at 4:21 p.m. at a factory in Nangli Sakrawati, in southwest Delhi, he said.

"Initially, two water tenders, two water bowsers and a quick response vehicle were rushed to the spot. The fire was upgraded to a medium-category blaze at 5:25 p.m., following which additional resources were deployed," the officer said.

So far, no injuries have been reported, he said.

World.title: Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water to be used for mist spraying in Kolkata; environmentalist slams move
World.content:
West Bengal Minister Agnimitra Paul says rose water will be mixed into mist spraying on special occasions, while environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh says the city’s air needs cleaning at the source

West Bengal Municipal Affairs and Urban Development Minister Agnimitra Paul has said that, on special occasions, rose water will be mixed with the water normally used for mist spraying to control air pollution in the city.

The move drew criticism from an environmentalist, who argued that the city’s air needed to be cleaned at the source rather than through such cosmetic interventions.

In a Facebook post in Bengali, Ms. Paul said the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) has regularly been spraying water mist at various locations across the city, particularly in areas where the Air Quality Index (AQI) is relatively high. This was being done under the direction of the State government to control air pollution in Kolkata and make the city’s environment cleaner.

The initiative is helping reduce the concentration of dust particles in the air and keep AQI levels somewhat under control, she said.

Alongside these measures, rose water will be mixed with the water used for mist spraying on special occasions and during various festivals, including Kali Puja, she said.

“This will not only help control dust particles in the air but also spread the pleasant fragrance of rose water throughout the surrounding environment... Our goal is to build a cleaner, fresher and fragrant Kolkata. We will continue our efforts to make the city more habitable,” Ms. Paul said in the post on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

“A few days ago, during my visit to London, I had observed that the AQI in several areas there was below 10, and in some places, even close to 1. This was truly astonishing. In contrast, Kolkata’s AQI rarely falls below 200 for most of the year,” she said.

This situation is a matter of concern for the health of all residents, and that is why the authorities are making continuous efforts, within their means, to improve the quality of air in the city, the Minister said.

Questioning Ms. Paul’s proposal, environmentalist Somendra Mohan Ghosh said on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that the city needs concrete measures to curb air pollution rather than cosmetic interventions.

“Spraying rose water might make the air smell pleasant temporarily but would do little to address the underlying pollution problem. Rose water won’t fix Kolkata’s air. But clean action will. With due respect to the minister, the fragrance will vanish within two minutes. Kolkata’s air does not need perfume; it needs cleaning at the source,” Mr. Ghosh said.

Mr. Ghosh also said ageing diesel and petrol vehicles were among the major contributors to PM2.5, PM10 and black carbon emissions. To make the air clean, he urged the authorities to stop the practice of coal-fired cooking stoves at roadside eateries and food stalls, suggesting a transition to cleaner LPG or electric cooking systems, with financial and logistical support for small vendors.

He further proposed deploying 100 water cannons across the city to wash roads, flyovers and dust-prone corridors, claiming that the measure would help settle suspended dust particles and remove accumulated dust from tree leaves.

On Sunday afternoon, ahead of Kali Puja and Deepavali, Kolkata’s average AQI stood at 165 (PM2.5), according to a Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) reading. This reading is described as “Moderate” (101-200) on the CPCB scale.

However, readings from individual monitoring stations operated by the West Bengal Pollution Control Board (WBPCB) indicated considerable variations in pollution levels across different neighbourhoods in the last few days.

The AQI had touched 232 on November 7, 2026, in the “Poor” category, with monitoring stations at Jadavpur and Bidhannagar recording particularly high pollution levels. Other monitored locations, including Ballygunge, Fort William, Rabindra Bharati University, Rabindra Sarobar and Victoria, reported moderate air quality.

World.title: West Bengal to institute 'Seema Mitra' award for BSF, SSB, police personnel from 2027: Suvendu
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 8, 2026) announced that his government would institute the 'Seema Mitra' award from 2027 to recognise exceptional contributions by BSF, SSB, and state police personnel in securing the country's borders.

A selection committee would be constituted to decide the awardees, he said, while addressing BSF personnel at a border outpost in Hingalganj in North 24 Parganas district, which shares a boundary with Bangladesh.

"We will give the 'Seema Mitra' award from next year for BSF, SSB and West Bengal police personnel," Mr. Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister visited the border outpost to greet security personnel on the occasion of Diwali and Kali Puja.

The BSF guards the India-Bangladesh border, while the Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) is deployed along the country's frontiers with Nepal and Bhutan.

Mr. Adhikari apologised to the BSF and CRPF personnel for what he described as derogatory remarks and behaviour by the previous State government.

"I, as the Chief Minister of the State, apologise to you for the derogatory remarks and behaviour of the previous regime towards BSF and CRPF," he said, targeting the erstwhile Trinamool Congress government.

He alleged that the previous Mamata Banerjee government had failed to provide the required land to the BSF for fencing nearly 600 km of the India-Bangladesh border in West Bengal.

Mr. Adhikari said the BJP government had handed over the required land to the BSF soon after assuming office and would provide any additional land needed for border fencing.

He said that his government will provide any additional requirement of land by the BSF in the border areas.

He claimed that the people gave their "appropriate retort" through the democratic process.

The Trinamool Congress lost to the BJP in the 2026 assembly elections in the State.

"We have to move ahead and ensure the security of the country," he said.

The Chief Minister said the State administration, BSF, and SSB were working in close coordination and that his government would work with the Centre to strengthen security infrastructure in the border districts.

West Bengal shares a border of over 2,200 km with Bangladesh, he said, adding that the government would facilitate the setting up of more police stations in frontier areas and provide the necessary infrastructure, logistics and manpower.

Mr. Adhikari asserted that every infiltrator should be identified and sent back.

"This country is for Indian citizens, and we are committed to them and the people of West Bengal," he said.

Referring to Union Home Minister Amit Shah's three-day visit to north Bengal in August, Mr. Adhikari said meetings had been held to strengthen border security and coordination between central and state agencies.

He said coordination meetings between border guarding forces and local police should be held not only at the district level but also at the police station level to address logistical and manpower requirements.

The Chief Minister, who also holds the Home portfolio, said the State had 105 police personnel per one lakh population, against the national average of 155.

His government would focus on creating employment opportunities for youths in border areas and had adopted the Centre's 'Vibrant Village' programme for their comprehensive development, he said.

The government would also ensure optimum utilisation of existing welfare schemes and development projects in the frontier districts, he added.

Mr. Adhikari said the State had started police recruitment and handed over appointment letters to more than 11,600 recruits.

The State cabinet had so far approved 29,000 police recruitments since May, he added.

He also announced that two India Reserve Battalions (IRBs) would be raised in the State with assistance from the Centre.

"Verbal discussion for this has been held, and official papers will be prepared soon," he said.

"It is my duty to come and greet you. When the whole country is celebrating Diwali, you are guarding the frontiers of the country," Mr. Adhikari said, addressing the BSF personnel.

He said he was inspired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who has been visiting border outposts on Diwali to meet security personnel since his tenure as Gujarat Chief Minister.

Mr. Modi celebrated Diwali this year with security personnel at a CRPF camp in Chhattisgarh's Bastar district.

Mr. Adhikari said there was close coordination between the BSF and State police, but some issues, including border fencing along the Icchamati river in North 24 Parganas, remained pending.

The State's Irrigation and Waterways Department would work on the issue, he said.

"After completing this portion, the borders here will be 100% secure," the Chief Minister said.

Mr. Adhikari said he had travelled on the last floating jetty towards the Bangladesh border and alleged that people on the other side were waiting to cross over whenever BSF personnel moved away from the area.

Claiming that several lakh infiltrators had been pushed back, he said combing operations were being conducted up to 15 km inside Indian territory to identify and deport illegal immigrants.

"The rest of the infiltrators will also be sent back," he said.

He also asserted that infiltrators would not be entitled to social welfare benefits, including the Annapurna Yojana, under which eligible women receive ₹3,000 per month.

Mr. Adhikari also wished former Deputy Prime Minister L. K. Advani on his birthday, crediting him with contributing to the country's development and the Ram temple movement.

"In his leadership and with the intervention of the Supreme Court, we got the Ram Mandir," he said.

Recalling his association with Mr. Advani, the Chief Minister said the BJP veteran had visited Nandigram two days after the March 14, 2007, firing incident in which 14 people were killed.

"He was then the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha; I am ever indebted to him," Mr. Adhikari, who was a Trinamool Congress leader then and was a pivotal figure in the anti-land acquisition agitation in Nandigram, said.

Mr. Adhikari said that after he became a Lok Sabha MP in 2009, Mr. Advani would ask him about Nandigram whenever he met the BJP leader in Parliament.

World.title: Europe will be represented at U.S.-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi: France
World.content:
Europe will be represented at the upcoming U.S.-mediated talks with Moscow and Kyiv in Abu Dhabi aimed at ending the Ukraine war, France said on Sunday (November 8, 2026).

"The Europeans will be represented and France will be in Abu Dhabi to participate in these talks," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told RTLradio.

His comment came after President Donald Trump stoked fears of a U.S. pivot toward the Kremlin by predicting a "very big" deal with Russia involving not only the Ukraine war but "all of Europe".

Up to now, the talks scheduled for Tuesday (November 10, 2026) and Wednesday (November 11, 2026) had been framed as a trilateral format at the level of officials, not leaders, from Ukraine, Russia and the United States.

The identities of who would take part have not been made public.

Although Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has made it clear that he wants involvement from European allies in the process, Russia has suggested there would be no place for European representatives at the table.

Mr. Barrot said that, in the past, "there have been discussions, sometimes without the Europeans and sometimes with," but "this time they will participate".

He said, "France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard."

On Thursday (November 5, 2026), U.S., European, Ukrainian and NATO officials met in Brussels ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.

A NATO spokeswoman said they "sought to advance a just and sustainable end to the war in Ukraine".

Jared Kushner, the U.S. President's envoy and son-in-law, participated in the Brussels meeting by videolink. He said the United States was working on "a broader European security architecture that can help establish the conditions for lasting peace".

The American approach is being treated warily by European allies, which have long rejected Moscow's desire to rewrite the European security architecture.

Before launching the war in Ukraine in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO which included a demand that the alliance's troops be withdrawn from eastern Europe.

That was rejected by the Western military alliance.

Mr. Kushner on Thursday (November 5, 2026) said that Washington will "consult closely with our European partners on the sidelines" of the Abu Dhabi talks and "if progress is made, aim to move toward a broader multilateral format with their direct participation".

World.title: Poland calls Krakow shooting rampage 'terrorist' attack
World.content:
Poland on Sunday (November 88, 2026) launched a terrorism probe as mourners brought candles and flowers to Krakow's Main Market Square in tribute to six people killed by a gunman who authorities said was "fascinated by far-right ideologies".

The 24-year-old Polish man opened fire at random on Saturday (November 7) in the historic centre of the country's second city, in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk called an act of "terrorism".

A British national was among the dead, according to police. Among the 15 wounded were nationals from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia, an Interior Ministry spokeswoman said.

Three more bodies were found at the suspect's home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, around 150 kilometres (95 miles) northeast of Krakow. Police said they were his parents and a sister.

The gunman was wounded in a shootout with police and is in critical condition in hospital. The National Prosecutor's Office said it had launched a terrorism investigation.

"I'm absolutely devastated," Weronika Filar, 27, a Krakow resident, told AFP on Sunday (November 8).

"It's one of the safest places on Earth genuinely... I did not expect anything like this to happen to us," she said. "Our city will never be the same."

"We've heard of various incidents of this sort happening elsewhere in Europe," Krzysztof Stepien, a 28-year-old part-time city guide told AFP.

"Nothing like this has ever happened here, and I hope it never will again," Stepien said.

Two police officers were wounded as they desperately chased the suspect, who was masked and dressed in military garb, including a bullet-proof vest.

The man left his car at an intersection and started shooting at the officers with a semi-automatic rifle, according to police.

Police hero

Social media images showed the two police firing at the gunman, with one managing to wound him despite his own injuries.

One police officer was in serious but stable condition, the interior ministry said, as quoted by PAP.

Police named him as "Jakub Kulik, who without hesitation confronted an armed attacker".

On Sunday morning, the usually busy site of the attack was sealed off with red-and-white tape.

People laid candles and police checked the bags of workers at the cafes and restaurants on the square.

Most of the souvenir shops remained closed.

Black flags and Poland's flags with black ribbons were seen in the city as Warsaw announced two days of national mourning for the victims from Sunday (November 8).

Relatives' bodies found

The suspect was named in the media as Michal O.

The three bodies found at the gunman's home were his parents and a sister, regional police said on social media.

The victims were a 53-year-old man and two women aged 52 and 21.

"Injuries were found on the bodies, which were preliminarily assessed as gunshot wounds... Seven firearms were seized from the flat," police added.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said police had also found weapons in the suspect's car.

According to investigators quoted in the Polish media, Michal O. had no previous criminal record.

He was a member of a shooting club, along with his father.

Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting".

World.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
World.content:
The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said.

Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition.

All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL.

One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day.

A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said.

A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement.

An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation.

Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said.

The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added.

The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person.

Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma were closely monitoring the situation, the PSU said on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Mr. Sonowal, who is the Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh, called OIL CMD Ranjit Rath to take stock of the situation.

CM Sarma has directed his principal secretary to be in touch with OIL chairman-cum-managing director to ensure the best possible medical care for the injured and adequate compensation for the families of those killed.

World.title: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives
World.content:
The administrative setup in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa plans to establish faceless anti-terrorism courts in the province as part of its initiatives to strengthen the fight against terrorism, according to a briefing by the officials televised on Sunday.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi was also present at the briefing, where KP Secretary Home Amjad Ali Khan outlined several measures planned to step up the fight against terrorism and explained that witnesses in terrorism cases feared coming forward.

“So, we have recently sent the amendment to set up faceless anti-terrorism courts. Through this, not just the protection of witnesses, but that of prosecutors and judges will also be ensured,” he said.

Moreover, he said the administrative setup planned to spend Rs70 billion on the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and police in a year, in order to increase their capacity.

Talking about dealing with terrorism in the policy domain, Khan noted that in the past there had been a “lack of political ownership” in the fight against terrorism in the province.

“Our armed forces and law enforcement agencies are making sacrifices in the war against terrorism; however, [..] the provincial government was not taking ownership for them.”

The Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.

Khan stressed the need for a “close liaison” on terrorism between the public, political leadership, and security forces. He further recalled that despite the Centre formulating an Afghan policy, “actions continued to be taken in the province contrary to that policy, leading to confusion among the people”.

He also noted that there was “propaganda against the security forces in attempts to sabotage the counterterrorism efforts in the province”.

The official then spoke of the “insufficient funding” for civil law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including police and CTD, particularly in the merged districts, where he said only 3.2 per cent of the budget was allocated for security.

He highlighted a shortage of over 10,000 personnel in the police, while also noting the lack of security infrastructure.

“Along with that, in the merged districts, most of the dependence regarding the police force is on former ex-Fata Khasadars and Levies,” he said, adding that the police personnel did not receive adequate training.

He further highlighted inadequate counter-drone protection, for which the available system was at a capacity of 12pc, noting that terrorists were using drone technology as well, “due to which we are suffering considerable losses”.

He also highlighted the lack of adequate Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) teams.

“Because of these issues [..] we have suffered significant losses over the past two or three years in which 1,003 personnel of the armed forces were martyred, 627 police personnel, and 808 civilian casualties occurred,” he stated.

Referring to the Centre’s Rs160bn package for uplift of KP, Khan said that the provincial set-up and the federal government were on the same page, expressing hope that “its effects will be seen in the coming days”.

He went on to outline plans to strengthen police capacity in the province, including fortifying sensitive police stations and check posts, extending the Safe City project, and establishing anti-drone systems in Dera Ismail Khan, Lakki Marwat, and Bannu as well as functionalising District Nerve Centres in ten districts.

Updated information will be available to LEAs from the centres, he added.

Under the legal interventions in policing, the official said that faceless ATC courts will be set up.

“Witnesses in terrorism cases are afraid to come forward due to their identity. So we have recently sent the amendment for these faceless courts. Through this measure, witnesses, prosecutors, and judges will have their protection ensured,” he stated.

Detailing the technical abilities of the police, the official said that satellite communication systems were being set up in areas with no prior communication system.

He added that the provincial administration was also deploying AI tools for social media monitoring to counter terrorists’ narrative.

Khan also stressed the need for increased public outreach, including strengthening District Dispute Resolution Councils as well as establishing tribal liaison committees.

“Regular jirgas will be held with notables, regular interaction will occur with the public, and community mobilisation will take place,” he stated.

He also outlined plans for police to be trained in modern technology such as anti-drone systems and sniping. He also recalled the provincial setup’s decision to revise packages for martyred police personnel.

Khan continued: “Kinetic operations will be scaled up so that militancy can be eliminated. In this regard, intelligence-based operations will be enhanced, area sanitisation will be carried out [..], terrorist facilitators will be arrested, and re-verification will also be carried out for people on the fourth schedule to ensure none of them is providing facilitation or support to terrorists.

He also added that the Rapid Response Force will be mobilised. Khan added that the provincial administration also planned to increase the number of police check posts.

He announced that the government was spending Rs70bn on CTD and police annually.

“In this regard, the police are being given Rs59.8bn, of which Rs33.4bn will be for their infrastructure and Rs26.4bn will be for procurement, while Rs10.3bn is being given to the CTD, of which Rs5.4bn is for infrastructure, and Rs4.9bn for procurement.”

He added that police surveillance capacity — at 15pc presently — will be increased to 60pc, while for CTD it will be enhanced by 70pc.

“The police’s counter-aerial threat capacity, which is currently at 1pc, will be taken up to 50pc. Our air strike capability is currently at 18pc and will be increased to 50pc, as well as night fighting capacity, with vehicle armour capacity of the police to be improved by 45pc,” the official said.

He added that “jammer availability was at 40pc but will be increased to 50pc while counter-drone capability — at 52pc presently — will be increased to 60pc”.

Protective gear and vehicle availability will be improved as well, while specialised training will be held in collaboration with the Pakistan Armed Forces.

The official also announced action against smuggling, narcotics, extortion and non-custom-paid vehicles.

“The purpose of all these measures is to provide a safe and secure environment to the people of KP where they can spend their lives, according to their codes and traditions,” Khan concluded.

Since the imposition of the governor’s rule in KP, the provincial administration has vowed to steer the province towards development and eliminate terrorism. Chairing his first apex committee meeting after taking charge of the province, governor Kundi promised to equip police and CTD with resources.

“Whatever weapons you want, whatever you need, we will get them to you. We will not compromise on our police officers and personnel. We will equip them well,” Kundi had said at the meeting.

Last month, he also announced an increase in the compensation packages for police officers martyred or injured in the line of duty.

Governor Kundi calls for ownership of war against terrorism

Speaking at the occasion, Governor Kundi said the provincial government’s priority was to restore peace and strengthen the police force, stressing that development would follow once security was ensured.

He said the police were at the forefront of the war against terrorism and needed to be adequately equipped to carry out their responsibilities. “Until we strengthen and facilitate [the police], how will they fight using just one Kalashnikov and a few bullets?” Kundi asked.

While the government had announced compensation packages for the families of police martyrs and was working on improving police salaries, it would also provide the force with weapons, ammunition and other resources, Kundi stressed during his speech.

“We talk a lot about merged districts, but as far as I know, not a single police line has been created in our merged districts, our former Fata. Look at their police stations, check posts, and facilities,” Kundi highlighted, adding that the government had directed the chief secretary and additional chief secretary to prepare a comprehensive package in this regard.

He said the plan also included solarising and equipping police facilities.

The governor pointed out the “lack of political ownership” previously with regard to the war against terrorism in the province.

“When something happened here, voices always came from the assemblies saying that this is ‘not our war’. We don’t own it,” Kundi said.

He questioned what the families of martyrs would say when political leaders did not take ownership of the war. “For whom did the martyr make this sacrifice? Was it for this soil, this country, or was it made under a specific agenda?” he asserted.

“If I have a gunman who is there for my protection, and I say that I don’t even own this gunman, how will he protect me?” Kundi asked rhetorically.

According to the governor, not owning the war indicated a lack of coordination.

Kundi referred to the security situation in parts of KP, adding that political leaders, including a former chief minister and JUI-F’s Maulana Fazlur Rehman, had acknowledged difficulties in moving freely in certain areas.

“If intelligence-based operations do not take place and the police and security forces do not conduct operations, how will these problems be resolved?” he asked.

Kundi said the current set-up’s stance was “clear” and that decisions and policies would be made in Islamabad rather than “Kabul, Kandahar or Jalalabad”.

The governor alleged that Afghanistan was facilitating India and Israel in using its territory against Pakistan. He referred to reports of drones entering Pakistan, saying some had crossed the border but were intercepted by Pakistani forces. He then criticised the lack of response by the previous government to statements by Afghan ministers threatening to take over Peshawar.

Kundi said Pakistan had repeatedly raised its concerns about Afghan soil being used to facilitate terrorism at international forums through the Foreign Office and the deputy prime minister and foreign minister, but Kabul had not budged an inch on addressing the issue.

“It is very clear that whoever does not accept our state, Constitution and laws cannot be engaged in dialogue. Anyone who takes up arms against the state cannot be offered dialogue; they will be responded to accordingly,” Kundi asserted.

During his speech, the governor stressed the importance of winning public trust, recalling that the province began its journey towards peace in 2008, when it was grappling with suicide bombings, target killings, kidnappings for ransom, among other problems.

He said public support had been crucial to previous military operations and would remain essential to counterterrorism efforts.

“You saw we cleared Swat; the world’s largest displacement occurred at that time, and we rehabilitated the people. People supported us for the operation.”

Reiterating that the government had a zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, Kundi said the fight against it remained its foremost priority, with development coming afterwards. “You can build roads, large underpasses and even turn the city into a garden, but what is the point if the people themselves are not safe?” he said.

He stressed that people needed to be assured that their children could go to school, college and playgrounds and return safely, while family members could travel to work or conduct business without fear. The governor also called for greater engagement of the province’s large youth population through “positive activities”.

World.title: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
World.content:
An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.

Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack. Aramco facilities and infrastructure have been repeatedly struck by the rebels in Yemen in recent months, with tankers, refineries, storage areas and the company headquarters all targeted by the group.

The energy ministry said in a statement that “an administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh was subjected to an attempted attack today”.
